facts.statement: Google's Search Status Dashboard lists these broad core updates since 2025: March 2025 (began 13 Mar 2025), June 2025 (began 30 Jun 2025), December 2025 (began 11 Dec 2025), March 2026 (began 27 Mar 2026) and May 2026 (began 21 May 2026). No core update is listed after May 2026 as of 3 Nov 2026. Judge ranking changes against these windows before blaming on-site work.
facts.source_title: Google Search Status Dashboard - Ranking incident history

facts.statement: Google ran four spam updates in 2026: March 2026 (began 24 Mar), June 2026 (began 24 Jun), August 2026 (began 18 Aug) and September 2026 (began 24 Sep, about two weeks long). The August 2025 spam update began 26 Aug 2025. A traffic drop starting in one of these windows points to a spam-policy issue, not a quality issue.
facts.source_title: Google Search Status Dashboard - Ranking incident history

facts.statement: Since 15 June 2026, 'back button hijacking' breaks Google's malicious practices spam policy. This means scripts, ad code or libraries that insert or replace browser history entries so users can't go back. Sites that do it can get manual actions or automated demotions. Announced 13 Apr 2026.
facts.source_title: Introducing a new spam policy for 'back button hijacking'

facts.statement: From 30 Aug 2026 Google enforces its site reputation abuse policy differently in the EEA, after talks with the European Commission. Outside the EEA, a manual action demotes the affected section of a site. Inside the EEA, the manual action's demotion doesn't apply, and the section may be separated so it ranks on its own. Hosting third-party content to exploit a trusted domain is still a policy violation everywhere. Announced 28 Aug 2026.
facts.source_title: Update to the Site Reputation Policy

facts.statement: In June 2025 Google started phasing seven structured data features out of Search results: Book Actions, Course Info, ClaimReview, Estimated Salary, Learning Video, Special Announcement and Vehicle Listing. By 8 Sep 2025 all but Book Actions were gone from results. From 9 Sep 2025 they were removed from Search Console reporting and the Rich Results Test, and API support ran through December 2025. Don't build new pages expecting these rich results.
facts.source_title: Simplifying the search results page

facts.statement: On 5 Nov 2025 Google said it is phasing out more rarely used search result features. From January 2026 Search Console and its API stop supporting the affected structured data types. Google lists specifics only in the Search documentation changelog, so check that changelog before adding niche schema types.
facts.source_title: Here's an update on our efforts to simplify the search results page

facts.statement: Google released its first Discover core update on 5 Feb 2026, for English-language users in the US, with expansion to all countries and languages planned over the following months. Its aims are less clickbait, more local content from sites in the user's country, and more in-depth, original, timely content from sites with topic expertise.
facts.source_title: Google's February 2026 Discover core update

facts.statement: Search Console's Performance report has a branded queries filter that splits data into branded and non-branded queries. An AI system classifies them, covering brand typos, all languages and product names. It was announced 20 Nov 2025 and has been available to all eligible sites since 11 Mar 2026. It works only for top-level properties with enough volume, and it doesn't affect ranking.
facts.source_title: Introducing the Branded queries filter in Search Console

facts.statement: Google's own guide to generative AI in Search says Google Search doesn't use llms.txt or similar 'special' files. Adding them neither helps nor harms visibility. No special schema.org markup is needed for AI features. To appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. Google calls optimizing for AI search 'still SEO'. Announced 15 May 2026.
facts.source_title: Google Search Central - Optimizing for generative AI features in Google Search

facts.statement: Google-Extended is a robots.txt control token, not a separate crawler. It decides whether Google-crawled content can train future Gemini models and be used for grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. It doesn't affect inclusion or ranking in Google Search. Google's crawler documentation says Google intends to support the AIPREF training-preference signal 'user-agent: __usage_ai-training' in early 2027.
facts.source_title: Google's common crawlers - Google Crawling Infrastructure

facts.statement: On 30 Oct 2026 Google announced it will support a shared AI-training policy token in robots.txt (IETF draft-kelley-aipref-training-preference-signal), alongside other AI providers, in 2027. If a site uses the shared token to opt out of training and doesn't name Google-Extended explicitly, Google will treat it as disallowing Google-Extended. Sites that explicitly allow Google-Extended stay eligible for Gemini Apps grounding and clicks from it.
facts.source_title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites

facts.statement: Search Console has dedicated Search generative AI performance reports covering impressions, pages, countries, devices and dates for AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover. They launched for a subset of sites on 3 Jun 2026 and reached all websites worldwide on 31 Aug 2026. This data is also still included in the overall Performance report.
facts.source_title: Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console

facts.statement: OpenAI uses separate user agents. OAI-SearchBot puts sites in ChatGPT search, and blocking it removes them from ChatGPT search answers (navigational links can still appear). GPTBot crawls for model training. ChatGPT-User makes user-initiated fetches, to which robots.txt may not apply. OAI-AdsBot checks the safety of landing pages submitted as ChatGPT ads. robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to apply to OAI-SearchBot.
facts.source_title: Overview of OpenAI Crawlers

facts.statement: Perplexity has two agents. PerplexityBot indexes and links sites in Perplexity search, follows robots.txt, and isn't used to train foundation models. Perplexity-User makes user-requested fetches and generally ignores robots.txt. Both publish IP ranges (perplexitybot.json, perplexity-user.json) for WAF allowlisting, and changes take up to 24 hours.
facts.source_title: Perplexity Crawlers

facts.statement: ChatGPT Ads launched in the US on 9 Feb 2026. On 21 Oct 2026 OpenAI expanded them to 26 more countries, for 89 in total, and said more than 100,000 advertisers had run campaigns. Ads show only on the Free and Go plans (Plus, Pro and Enterprise stay ad-free). They are labeled and separate from answers. OpenAI says ads don't influence answers and conversations aren't shared with advertisers. Advertisers can buy through partners or the self-serve Ads Manager.
facts.source_title: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform

facts.statement: On 28 Oct 2026 Google expanded ads in AI Mode to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. It also launched multiturn ads in the US, which can appear in AI Mode follow-up queries labeled 'Sponsored'. Brazil, Mexico and the UK are planned for Q4 2026.
facts.source_title: Ads in AI Mode expand to 10 new countries

facts.statement: Existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns qualify automatically for ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Advertisers can't target these surfaces separately or opt out of them separately from Search. The only controls are negative keywords and brand exclusions. Ads above or below AI Overviews can serve in all 200+ AI Overviews markets. Ads inside them are limited to English in a set of markets including the US.
facts.source_title: About ads in AI-powered experiences in Google Search - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Google is moving Search campaigns to AI Max. Campaigns using automatically created assets (now 'text customization') or campaign-level broad match were auto-upgraded starting September 2026. A 11 Jun 2026 update says the Dynamic Search Ads sunset and auto-upgrade to AI Max begin in February 2027. Review AI Max settings (search term matching, text customization, final URL expansion) in every Search campaign.
facts.source_title: We're upgrading Dynamic Search Ads to AI Max

facts.statement: The Google Ads channel performance report shows how Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns deliver across Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Maps, Gmail and Search partners, with status diagnostics. Data is available for any date range after 6 Jun 2025 (Campaigns > Insights and reports > Channel performance).
facts.source_title: About the channel performance report for Performance Max - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Google Marketing Live 2026 (20 May 2026) bidding news: journey-aware bidding is in beta for lead-gen Search campaigns using Target CPA. Smart Bidding Exploration was due in beta for Performance Max with product feeds and Shopping 'in a few weeks'. Demand-led pacing for Search and Shopping is coming 'in the coming months'. Campaign total budgets have launched for Search, Shopping and Performance Max.
facts.source_title: Google Marketing Live 2026: bidding and budgeting news

facts.statement: Microsoft Advertising: from 1 Oct 2026 you can't set a Max CPC when creating a new non-portfolio campaign with Maximize Conversions (Target CPA), Maximize Conversion Value (Target ROAS) or Maximize Clicks. Campaigns created before then keep the setting, and portfolio strategies still support it. AI Max for Search became generally available on 27 Aug 2026.
facts.source_title: AI Max for Search and other product news for August 2026

facts.statement: Microsoft Advertising updates for Performance Max on 28 Oct 2026: age and gender targeting is generally available, device targeting is rolling out, audience exclusions are in open pilot, search term and auction insights reporting are available, and search term landing page reporting rolls out from mid-November. The Microsoft Advertising Conversions API is generally available.
facts.source_title: Build, steer, and measure your campaigns with AI: What's new in Microsoft Advertising this October

facts.statement: The Microsoft Advertising SOAP API will be fully deprecated on 31 Jan 2027. Integrations must move to the REST API by then. Until that date, new features ship in both SOAP and REST; the earlier plan for REST-only features from 1 Oct 2026 was dropped.
facts.source_title: Less busywork, more growth: What's new in Microsoft Advertising this September

facts.statement: Meta's Marketing API has merged Advantage+ shopping and app campaigns into the Advantage+ campaign experience. You create OUTCOME_SALES, APP_INSTALLS or OUTCOME_LEADS campaigns with Advantage+ audience, budget and placements, and they get advantage_state ADVANTAGE_PLUS_SALES/APP/LEADS. From v25.0 the legacy ASC/AAC API can't create campaigns. At v26.0 legacy campaigns are blocked from edits, and those using existing_customer_budget_percentage are paused.
facts.source_title: Advantage+ Campaign Experience for Sales, App, and Leads - Meta Marketing API

facts.statement: Meta says its ad delivery now runs on three AI systems that need no setup: Andromeda (ad retrieval, now routing to expert models), GEM (generative ads recommendation foundation model) and GenRecs (an LLM-based generative recommender that helps new ads with little history perform sooner). Meta stresses that results still depend on the conversion goal, the quality of shared conversion data, and how much optimization advertisers hand to the models.
facts.source_title: Inside the Three New AI innovations in Ads Ranking Improving your Ad Performance

facts.statement: Meta announcements of 6 Oct 2026: generative AI video from static assets in Advantage+ creative is generally available, Customer Lifecycle Strategy for acquisition campaigns is available to all advertisers, expanded Meta ads MCP Server workflows are live, and AI-enabled audience discovery in Detailed Targeting is coming by end of 2026. Conversational campaign creation in the Meta AI business assistant is starting tests.
facts.source_title: Advertising Week New York 2026: New AI Capabilities to Guide Campaigns and Reach Customers

facts.statement: TikTok's upgraded Smart+ puts manual and Smart+ setup in one flow, from full automation to fully manual. Each ad works like an asset group with its own URL, product set and up to 50 creatives, and reporting is grouped by creative material ID. It covers the Traffic, Sales, Lead Generation and App Promotion objectives, but the help page says it may not be available to every account yet (last updated October 2026).
facts.source_title: Smart+ Upgraded Experience - TikTok Ads Manager Help

facts.statement: TikTok Search Ads campaigns powered by Smart+ show ads beside organic TikTok search results. They offer automated keyword expansion, negative keywords, Brand and Category Keyword Packs, and Search Ads Impression Share diagnostics, for the Traffic, Sales, Lead Generation and App Promotion objectives. They're available in the US and in testing in other markets.
facts.source_title: Introducing Search Ads Campaign Powered By Smart+

facts.statement: At TikTok World '26 (13 May 2026) TikTok announced three things. Smart+ Auto Selection picks the best-performing creative from creator, product and Symphony AI assets. Smart+ Asset Manager joins catalog, data connections and creative in one place. Search Hubs put brand-owned pages at the top of TikTok search. No rollout dates were given.
facts.source_title: TikTok World '26: Turning Discovery Into Business Growth with AI-Powered Innovations

facts.statement: LinkedIn Campaign Manager updates of 30 Jun 2026: campaign-level conversion lift tests, refreshed Brand Lift reporting, AI-generated ad drafts from a URL, AI copy variants, Flexible Ad Creation that builds and optimizes up to 64 creative combinations, real-time copy personalization by company name, industry and job title, and a Brand Kit for on-brand AI drafts.
facts.source_title: LinkedIn Marketing Solutions - Product Updates

facts.statement: Meta has stopped serving political, electoral and social issue ads in the EU since 6 Oct 2025. Google also stopped serving political ads in the EU before the TTPA regulation (EU 2024/900) took effect in October 2025. Both cite the regulation's broad definition and legal uncertainty, so ads touching social issues can be rejected in the EU on either platform.
facts.source_title: Ending Political, Electoral and Social Issue Advertising in the EU in Response to Incoming European Regulation

facts.statement: Since its 12-13 Mar 2026 update, Facebook's originality policy deprioritizes unoriginal content in Feed and Reels. That includes reaction or watch-along reuse, stitched clips, narrating existing footage, re-uploads, and minor edits such as borders, captions or speed changes. Accounts that post mainly unoriginal content can become non-recommendable and lose monetization. Creators can appeal.
facts.source_title: Rewarding Original Creators on Facebook

facts.statement: Meta reported (28 Jan 2026) that Instagram raised the prevalence of original content in the US by 10 percentage points in Q4 2025, and 75% of recommendations now come from original posts. Threads optimizations lifted time spent by 20%, and Facebook organic post views rose 7% from ranking changes.
facts.source_title: 2026: AI Drives Performance

facts.statement: Instagram's ranking explainer (2023, still the published rule) says Reels that are watermarked, low-resolution, muted, bordered, mostly text, or already posted on Instagram are made less visible. Main signals are activity (likes, saves, reshares, comments), history with the poster, information about the reel and poster, and predicted actions such as watching through and resharing.
facts.source_title: Instagram Ranking Explained

facts.statement: Since 24 Jul 2026, YouTube Partner Program creators can upload custom thumbnails for Shorts, and desktop users can pick from three suggested frames. YouTube plans to expand this to more creators over time.
facts.source_title: New thumbnail updates in YouTube Studio help creators customize their videos

facts.statement: Meta One subscription plans for businesses (announced 15 Sep 2026, rolling out gradually) bundle a verified badge and impersonation protection (Essential, $14.99/mo per profile). From Advanced ($49.99/mo) they add clickable links in organic posts and Reels, scheduling, exportable analytics and competitive insights. Expert ($149) and Max ($499) tiers add more. Pricing and availability vary by region.
facts.source_title: Introducing Meta One plans for businesses

facts.statement: Search Console 'platform properties' let owners track how their Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube posts perform in Google Search, Discover and Google News. They have been globally available to everyone since 29 Jul 2026, and Google published a guide on analysing social and video content performance alongside them.
facts.source_title: Platform properties roll out globally, plus a new social and video performance guide

facts.statement: Gmail sender requirements, in force since 1 Feb 2024. All senders need SPF or DKIM, valid forward and reverse DNS, TLS, RFC 5322 formatting, and a spam rate below 0.3%. Senders of 5,000+ messages a day to personal Gmail accounts also need both SPF and DKIM, DMARC (p=none is enough) with the From: domain aligned to SPF or DKIM, and one-click unsubscribe plus a visible unsubscribe link on marketing mail. DKIM keys must be at least 1024 bits; 2048 is recommended.
facts.source_title: Email sender guidelines - Google Workspace Admin Help

facts.statement: Gmail began ramping up enforcement in November 2025. Mail that fails the sender requirements can get temporary (4.7.x) or permanent (5.7.x) rejections or go to spam. New domains face a faster schedule. One-click unsubscribe must use List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers per RFC 8058, and a mailto link doesn't satisfy it. Unsubscribes should be honored within 48 hours.
facts.source_title: Email sender guidelines FAQ - Google Workspace Admin Help

facts.statement: Gmail calculates spam rate daily and advises keeping user-reported spam below 0.1%. Rates above 0.1% already hurt inbox delivery. Since June 2024, senders at 0.3% or more are ineligible for mitigation until they stay below 0.3% for 7 consecutive days. Postmaster Tools shows the daily rate.
facts.source_title: Email sender guidelines FAQ - Google Workspace Admin Help

facts.statement: Yahoo bulk sender requirements: SPF and DKIM, a DMARC policy of at least p=none that passes (relaxed alignment is fine, rua reporting recommended), From: domain aligned to SPF or DKIM, a working one-click List-Unsubscribe header (RFC 8058, POST highly recommended), a visible unsubscribe link, unsubscribes honored within 2 days, a spam rate below 0.3% (measured on inbox-delivered mail), and valid forward and reverse DNS.
facts.source_title: Yahoo Sender Hub - Sender Best Practices

facts.statement: Outlook.com (hotmail.com, live.com, outlook.com) requires domains that send more than 5,000 emails a day to pass SPF and DKIM and to have DMARC of at least p=none, aligned with SPF or DKIM. Per the 29 Apr 2025 update, from 5 May 2025 non-compliant mail is rejected with '550; 5.7.515 Access denied, sending domain does not meet the required authentication level'.
facts.source_title: Strengthening Email Ecosystem: Outlook's New Requirements for High-Volume Senders

facts.statement: On 17 Oct 2025 Google said Chrome will keep its current approach of offering users a choice on third-party cookies (there will be no deprecation). It is retiring most Privacy Sandbox technologies: Attribution Reporting API, Protected Audience, Topics, Private Aggregation and Shared Storage, IP Protection, Related Website Sets and others. CHIPS, FedCM and Private State Tokens remain supported. Don't plan measurement around Topics or Protected Audience.
facts.source_title: Update on Plans for Privacy Sandbox Technologies

facts.statement: Google consent mode has four consent types. ad_storage controls advertising cookies and analytics_storage controls analytics cookies. ad_user_data (consent to send ad-related user data to Google) and ad_personalization (consent to personalized ads) were added in November 2023 as consent mode v2. Google says it is strengthening enforcement of its EU user consent policy, so banners for EEA and UK users must set all four.
facts.source_title: Set up consent mode on websites - Google Tag Platform

facts.statement: California's CPPA regulations on CCPA updates, risk assessments, cybersecurity audits and automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) took effect 1 Jan 2026. Risk assessment duties started 1 Jan 2026, with attestations due 1 Apr 2028. ADMT rules for significant decisions apply from 1 Jan 2027. Cybersecurity audit certifications are due 1 Apr 2028, 2029 or 2030 depending on revenue (>$100M, $50-100M, <$50M).
facts.source_title: California Finalizes Regulations to Strengthen Consumers' Privacy

facts.statement: Under the CCPA, businesses must honor opt-out preference signals such as Global Privacy Control as a valid request to opt out of sale or sharing. California's Delete Request and Opt-out Platform (DROP) for data brokers is live, and data brokers must register by 31 January each year.
facts.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - California Privacy Protection Agency

facts.statement: The Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act (HB 15, signed 4 Apr 2024) took effect 1 Jan 2026. It gives consumers rights to access, correct, delete and port their data and to opt out of targeted advertising, sale of personal data and profiling. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority.
facts.source_title: Kentucky General Assembly - 24RS HB 15

facts.statement: After the Commission's April 2025 Digital Markets Act non-compliance decision on 'consent or pay', Meta committed (8 Dec 2025) to give EU users a choice between fully personalised ads and a less personalised ads option using less personal data. The option was presented to EU users in January 2026. Expect lower ad personalization and smaller addressable audiences for EU Meta campaigns.
facts.source_title: Meta commits to give EU users choice on personalised ads under Digital Markets Act

facts.statement: EU AI Act timeline: in force 1 Aug 2024. Prohibitions and AI literacy have applied since 2 Feb 2025, and general-purpose AI model obligations since 2 Aug 2025. Most of the Act, including the transparency rules, has applied since 2 Aug 2026. A ninth prohibition (non-consensual sexual content and CSAM generation) applies from 2 Dec 2026. The AI Omnibus (in force 27 Jul 2026) moved high-risk Annex III rules to 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I product rules to 2 Aug 2028.
facts.source_title: AI Act - Shaping Europe's digital future

facts.statement: AI Act Article 50 has applied since 2 Aug 2026. Deployers must clearly disclose deepfakes at first exposure. AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest must be labelled unless it had substantive human review and someone holds editorial responsibility (spell-checking doesn't count). The provider's machine-readable marks don't satisfy the deployer's duty. Providers of systems already on the market before 2 Aug 2026 have until 2 Dec 2026 for the Article 50(2) marking duty. Content made before 2 Aug 2026 doesn't need retroactive labels.
facts.source_title: Transparency obligations under Article 50 of the AI Act

facts.statement: The FTC's Consumer Review Rule (16 CFR Part 465, announced 14 Aug 2024) bans: fake or AI-generated reviews from people who don't exist or never used the product, reviews bought for a set sentiment, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled 'independent' review sites, review suppression by threats, and bought fake followers or views. On 22 Dec 2025 FTC staff sent warning letters to 10 companies, citing civil penalties of up to $53,088 per violation.
facts.source_title: FTC Warns 10 Companies About Possible Violations of the Agency's New Consumer Review Rule

facts.statement: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital on 12 Mar 2024. Google's 'good' targets are LCP within 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, and CLS below 0.1.
facts.source_title: Understanding Core Web Vitals and Google search results

facts.statement: The European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882) has applied since 28 Jun 2025. It covers e-commerce, banking services, e-books, electronic communications, passenger transport services, computers, smartphones, e-readers and self-service terminals sold in the EU. Online shops and checkouts serving EU consumers must be accessible.
facts.source_title: The EU becomes more accessible for all

facts.statement: The Commission's EAA page lists the services covered (e-commerce, banking, e-books, air/bus/rail/waterborne passenger transport, telephony, audio-visual media services) and products (computers and operating systems, ATMs, ticketing and check-in machines, smartphones, digital TV equipment). Member States had to transpose the Act into national law by June 2022.
facts.source_title: European accessibility act - European Commission

facts.statement: Since 13 May 2026, GA4's Default Channel Group includes an 'AI Assistant' channel, with medium 'ai-assistant', for visits from assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. Report AI referral traffic from this channel rather than custom regex groups.
facts.source_title: [GA4] What's new in Google Analytics

facts.statement: GA4 changes in 2026: custom conversion windows (engaged-view 1-30 days, previously fixed at 3; click-through 1-90 days) from 11 Aug 2026. A currency field is required for campaign cost data imports from 28 Jul 2026. Dashboards launched 9 Sep 2026. Hostname Include filters (allowlists) arrived 21 Sep 2026. A Source Group dimension (consolidating sources like Facebook, Instagram, TikTok) arrived 11 Jun 2026.
facts.source_title: [GA4] What's new in Google Analytics

facts.statement: Meridian is Google's open-source marketing mix model (github.com/google/meridian). It models video reach and frequency, uses search query volume to control for organic demand, supports budget optimization, and can be calibrated with geo experiments. Meridian GeoX, an open-source geo-experiment tool that feeds Meridian priors, is now available. Meridian Studio, an enterprise MMM platform on Google Cloud, was announced 5 May 2026.
facts.source_title: Meridian - Google for Developers

facts.statement: Google Ads measurement news (5 May 2026): a Data Manager map view of data flows (BigQuery, Drive, HubSpot, Shopify) was coming in the following months, Data Manager and its API will combine Google tags with extra data such as store sales, there is a no-code visual flow for upgrading existing Google tags, and Google Tag Manager is coming to all users.
facts.source_title: Google Marketing Live 2026: growth in the age of AI

facts.statement: From 31 Aug 2026, new apps and updates on Google Play must target Android 16 (API level 36). Wear OS and Automotive must target API 35, and TV and XR API 34. Existing apps must target at least API 35 to stay visible to new users on newer Android versions. Developers could request an extension to 1 Nov 2026.
facts.source_title: Meet Google Play's target API level requirement

facts.statement: From 16 Nov 2026, App Store Connect's age rating questionnaire adds two content descriptors: 'Shared Location' and 'Dating and Relationships'. Dating and Relationships forces a minimum 18+ rating, and Brazil requires A16 for Shared Location and A18 for dating. Every app must complete both declarations by 12 Jan 2027, and they are required with any update before then. Announced 2 Nov 2026.
facts.source_title: Upcoming: New age rating content descriptors in App Store Connect

facts.statement: Apple moved all App Store apps to its new age rating system (shown on iOS 26 and later). Developers had to answer the updated age rating questions in App Store Connect by 31 Jan 2026 or face interruptions submitting updates.
facts.source_title: Age Rating Updates - Upcoming Requirements - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Since 4 Jun 2026, Texas law SB 2420 applies to new Apple Accounts in Texas. Downloads, in-app purchases and significant app changes by under-18s need age assurance and parent or guardian consent, and parents can revoke consent. Developers must use the Declared Age Range API, the Significant Change API (PermissionKit), StoreKit's AppStore.ageRatingCode, and App Store server notifications for consent withdrawal.
facts.source_title: Update for Apps Distributed in Texas - Apple Developer News

facts.statement: The Google Content API for Shopping reached its sunset on 18 Aug 2026. Since 1 Sep 2026, requests without an approved extension fail intermittently with HTTP 410, and full shutdown is expected in early 2027. Feeds and integrations must use the Merchant API, generally available as v1 since July 2025. Platform-managed accounts are migrated by the platform partner.
facts.source_title: Deprecation and sunset - Content API for Shopping

facts.statement: Google Marketing Live 2026 shopping news (20 May 2026): Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) checkout in Universal Cart and in Direct Offers and YouTube Shopping ads is 'coming soon', with UCP rolling out to Canada and Australia, then the UK. Merchant Center AI performance insights (share of voice on AI surfaces vs similar brands) roll out in AU, CA, IN, NZ and the US. Conversational attributes for product descriptions are available now globally.
facts.source_title: How we're helping retailers thrive with new Universal Commerce Protocol features and AI tools on Google

facts.statement: Since 12 Nov 2025, Search Console 'Shipping and returns' settings are open to any site Google identifies as an online merchant, with no Merchant Center account needed, and these settings take precedence over structured data. Google added organization-level shipping policy markup so merchants can declare one site-wide policy. Product-level shipping markup still overrides it for those items.
facts.source_title: More ways to share your shipping and returns policies with Google

facts.statement: LinkedIn Conversions API now accepts MARKETING_QUALIFIED_LEAD and SALES_QUALIFIED_LEAD conversion types (version 202608, August 2026), feeding a qualified-leads optimization goal. Hashed first and last name identifiers and a 180-day attribution window were added in 202609 (September 2026). MAX_QUALIFIED_LEAD has been an optimization target for Lead Generation campaigns since 202602.
facts.source_title: Recent Marketing API Changes - LinkedIn

facts.statement: LinkedIn Marketing API operations: since 16 Mar 2026, new lead notifications (LEAD_ACTION webhooks) go only to validated webhooks. DMP segments are capped at 1,000 per ad account (since 202608; exceeding returns 429 SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). API versions sunset monthly, and version 202511 sunsets 16 Nov 2026.
facts.source_title: Recent Marketing API Changes - LinkedIn

facts.statement: Microsoft Advertising LinkedIn company lists can now hold up to 10,000 company names (up from 1,000), for LinkedIn targeting in Search and Audience campaigns. Microsoft Advertising is also live in HubSpot, connecting CRM data to campaigns and tracking which ads drive pipeline and revenue (announced 30 Sep 2026). LinkedIn Job Seniority targeting is generally available for Audience ads and Search.
facts.source_title: Less busywork, more growth: What's new in Microsoft Advertising this September

facts.statement: LinkedIn event and Boost updates (31 Mar 2026): Event Ads have a lead generation objective gated by Lead Gen Forms. Off-LinkedIn events can be promoted without a LinkedIn Event page. Event Analytics combines organic and paid performance. Boost turns an existing post, Page update or event into a feed ad without building a full campaign.
facts.source_title: LinkedIn Marketing Solutions - Product Updates

facts.statement: EU AI Act GPAI timeline (Commission GPAI guidelines page, updated 28 Apr 2026): obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models have applied since 2 Aug 2025 for models placed on the market after that date; the Commission's enforcement powers, including fines, apply from 2 Aug 2026; models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027. The GPAI Code of Practice is a voluntary tool to show compliance. Per the page, only providers that make significant modifications to a model need to meet GPAI provider obligations; minor changes do not trigger them.
facts.source_title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models

facts.statement: AI Act Article 99 fines: prohibited practices (Art. 5) up to EUR 35M or 7% of worldwide annual turnover; most other operator obligations, including Article 50 transparency, up to EUR 15M or 3%; incorrect or misleading information to authorities up to EUR 7.5M or 1% (whichever is higher). For SMEs and start-ups each cap is the lower of the two amounts. Use the 3% tier when sizing the risk of an unlabelled deepfake or undisclosed chatbot in a campaign.
facts.source_title: AI Act Service Desk: Article 99 Penalties

facts.statement: The Digital Omnibus on AI amended AI Act Article 4 (paragraphs 1-3; the Service Desk page reflects the EUR-Lex consolidated version of 27 Jul 2026): providers and deployers must take measures to support AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf, considering their knowledge, experience and context of use, but the obligation does not require guaranteeing any specific level of AI literacy of any individual. Keep a short record of AI training and usage guidance for everyone (including agencies and freelancers) who runs AI tools for the brand.
facts.source_title: AI Act Service Desk: Article 4 AI literacy (amended)

facts.statement: The Commission published the final Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content on 10 Jun 2026. It is voluntary and gives providers and deployers practical steps for AI Act transparency duties applying from 2 Aug 2026: label deepfakes and AI-generated or manipulated text on matters of public interest, and tell users when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot. The page also links a resource titled 'EU Icons for labelling AI-generated content'.
facts.source_title: Commission publishes Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content

facts.statement: FTC 'Operation AI Comply' (25 Sep 2024): five actions against deceptive AI claims. DoNotPay ('world's first robot lawyer'): proposed settlement requires a $193,000 payment and bars unsupported claims that it can replace professional services; Ascend Ecom (alleged consumer losses of at least $25M), Ecommerce Empire Builders and FBA Machine (alleged losses over $15.9M) were halted by courts over 'AI-powered' passive-income or earnings claims. Lesson: any 'AI-powered', 'replaces a lawyer/expert' or earnings claim needs substantiation in claims.md before use.
facts.source_title: FTC Announces Crackdown on Deceptive AI Claims and Schemes

facts.statement: In Operation AI Comply (25 Sep 2024) the FTC charged Rytr, whose AI writing assistant had a 'Testimonial & Review' feature generating detailed reviews likely to be false, with violating the FTC Act. The proposed order bars Rytr from advertising or selling services designed to generate consumer reviews or testimonials (3-2 vote, Commissioners Holyoak and Ferguson dissenting). Never use AI to draft reviews or testimonials attributed to customers; only publish real, consented customer words.
facts.source_title: FTC Announces Crackdown on Deceptive AI Claims and Schemes

facts.statement: FTC Endorsement Guides update (29 Jun 2023): 'endorsements' now covers fake reviews, virtual influencers and social media tags; new principle against procuring, suppressing, boosting or editing reviews to distort opinion; guidance on incentivised and employee reviews and fake negative reviews of competitors; a definition of 'clear and conspicuous'; and a platform's built-in disclosure tool may not be adequate. Advertisers, endorsers and intermediaries can all be liable.
facts.source_title: FTC Announces Updated Advertising Guides to Combat Deceptive Reviews and Endorsements

facts.statement: FTC endorsement FAQ disclosure rules: '#ad', 'Ad:' or 'ad' at the start of a post are about equal; 'Sponsored by XYZ' beats 'Sponsored'; disclosures in the middle or end of a post are easier to miss. Match the medium: visual endorsements need at least a visual disclosure, spoken ones an audible one, and both together is best; on TikTok superimpose large on-screen text. Livestreams need repeated or continuous disclosure. Add your own disclosure even when using a platform's paid-partnership tool.
facts.source_title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking

facts.statement: Colorado SB26-189 (Automated Decision-Making Technology), signed 14 May 2026, repeals and reenacts the consumer protection provisions of SB 24-205. Deployers must give clear and conspicuous notice at the point of interaction with a covered ADMT and, within 30 days after a consequential decision with an adverse outcome, a plain-language description of the ADMT's role. 1 Jan 2027 is the start date for developer technical documentation duties. The Attorney General enforces through the Colorado Consumer Protection Act (no new private right of action); before 1 Jan 2030 the AG must give 60 days' notice and an opportunity to cure where cure is possible.
facts.source_title: SB26-189 Automated Decision-Making Technology

facts.statement: UK DMCC Act banned practice on reviews (in force 6 Apr 2025; CMA guidance CMA208, 4 Apr 2025): it is automatically unfair to submit or commission fake reviews or reviews that conceal an incentive, and to publish reviews or review-derived information (star ratings) in a misleading way. 'Commissioning' includes incentivising by any means, and it applies to influencers, content creators and journalists too. Incentivised reviews are allowed only if the incentive is apparent.
facts.source_title: Fake reviews (CMA208)

facts.statement: CMA208: any trader that publishes consumer reviews (own site, marketplace, social, review platform) has a positive duty to take reasonable and proportionate steps to prevent and remove banned reviews. Expected steps: a published plain-English policy prohibiting fake and concealed-incentive reviews, an evidence-led risk assessment reviewed over time, detection and removal processes, and not steering customers to complain instead of reviewing or suppressing negative reviews.
facts.source_title: CMA208 Fake reviews guidance (PDF)

facts.statement: Since 6 Apr 2025 the CMA can decide consumer-law infringements itself and fine up to 10% of global turnover (5% plus daily penalties for breaching undertakings; 1% for information failures). The DMCC regime explicitly bans fake reviews and drip pricing (showing an initial price then adding fees during purchase). Show all mandatory fees upfront in UK prices and ads.
facts.source_title: CMA to boost consumer and business confidence as new consumer protection regime comes into force

facts.statement: UK CAP/ASA position (29 May 2025): there is no blanket UK legal requirement to disclose AI use in ads; existing CAP and BCAP rules apply however content is generated, edited or targeted. Ask (1) would the audience be misled without disclosure, and (2) does the disclosure clarify or contradict the message. An AI image showing a product effect that does not match real-world results is likely misleading and a disclosure alone will not fix it; making clear that a deepfake is for comedy, or that an influencer is AI-generated, may negate an otherwise misleading impression. Minor post-production edits have long been used without always being disclosed, but context still matters.
facts.source_title: Disclosure of AI in Advertising: Striking the Balance Between Creativity and Responsibility

facts.statement: WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation, 5 Oct 2023) adds four Level AA criteria that matter for landing pages and checkout: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (sticky headers, cookie banners and chat widgets must not fully hide the focused element), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (offer a single-pointer alternative to sliders and drag), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) of 24x24 CSS px or enough spacing, and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (no memorising or transcribing codes without an alternative such as paste or password managers).
facts.source_title: What's New in WCAG 2.2

facts.statement: WCAG 2.2 also adds two Level A criteria: 3.2.6 Consistent Help (help links, chat or contact details repeated across pages stay in the same relative order) and 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (information already entered in a process, such as a shipping address, is auto-filled or selectable instead of re-typed). Success criterion 4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete and removed. The AAA additions (e.g. 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: 2 CSS px perimeter, 3:1 contrast) are optional targets.
facts.source_title: What's New in WCAG 2.2

facts.statement: US DOJ ADA Title II rule (Apr 2024) requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. An Interim Final Rule published 20 Apr 2026 extended compliance by about a year: 26 Apr 2027 for entities with 50,000+ population, 26 Apr 2028 for smaller entities and special districts. It binds public entities, not private businesses, but it is the clearest US federal signal that WCAG 2.1 AA is the benchmark; vendors selling to governments need it.
facts.source_title: Fact Sheet: New Rule on the Accessibility of Web Content and Mobile Apps Provided by State and Local Governments

facts.statement: Search Console's Core Web Vitals report uses CrUX field data and judges each URL group at the 75th percentile of visits. Bands: LCP good <=2.5 s, poor >4 s; INP good <=200 ms, poor >500 ms; CLS good <=0.1, poor >0.25. A group's status is its worst metric (poor CLS + good INP = poor), similar pages are grouped, low-data groups fall back to the origin, and mobile and desktop are rated separately. Speed gates should check p75 field data on mobile, not lab scores alone.
facts.source_title: Core Web Vitals report - Search Console Help

facts.statement: European Accessibility Act scope per Your Europe (checked 12 Jul 2026): requirements apply to products and services placed on the market after 28 Jun 2025, including online shops, ticketing platforms and banking services. Service businesses with fewer than 10 employees and under EUR 2 million turnover are exempt; self-service terminals in use before 28 Jun 2025 may continue up to 20 years. Any business can claim disproportionate burden only with evidence, reviewed every 5 years. Check whether the operator is a microenterprise before scoping an EAA audit.
facts.source_title: Services, goods and their digital accessibility - Your Europe

facts.statement: Baymard's documented average online cart abandonment rate is 70.22%, averaged across 50 studies (page updated 22 Sep 2025). Use about 70% as the default baseline when no store data exists, and measure the store's own rate before claiming improvement.
facts.source_title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics - Baymard Institute

facts.statement: Baymard reasons US shoppers abandoned during checkout (excluding 'just browsing'): extra costs such as shipping, tax or fees 40%; slow delivery 20%; didn't trust the site with card details 19%; account creation required 18%; too long or complicated checkout 17%; site errors or crashes 17%; unsatisfactory return policy 13%; total cost not shown upfront 12%; card declined 10%; too few payment methods 9%. Prioritise upfront total cost, guest checkout and trust signals.
facts.source_title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics - Baymard Institute

facts.statement: Baymard: the average US checkout shows 23.48 form elements by default (14.88 form fields), while an ideal flow can be as short as 12-14 elements (7-8 fields). Count the store's default checkout elements and cut toward 12-14 by merging name fields, hiding company and address line 2 behind links, and defaulting billing to shipping address.
facts.source_title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics - Baymard Institute

facts.statement: Baymard estimates that fixing solvable checkout design issues could raise a large e-commerce site's conversion rate by 35.26%, which on $738B of combined US and EU e-commerce sales equals about $260B in recoverable orders. Treat this as an upper bound for large sites, not a forecast for one test.
facts.source_title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics - Baymard Institute

facts.statement: Baymard's Cart & Checkout benchmark of 344 top-grossing US and EU e-commerce sites rates 65% 'mediocre' or worse; only 2% are 'good' and none 'perfect'. The research behind its 110+ checkout guidelines comes from 4,400+ moderated usability sessions and 12 quantitative studies with 20,240 participants. Even big brands' checkouts usually have fixable issues, so audit before assuming the checkout is fine.
facts.source_title: Checkout Usability - Baymard Institute

facts.statement: NN/g (Jakob Nielsen, 5 May 2008), from Weinreich et al.'s browser log study (25 users, 45,237 page views): on an average page visit users have time to read at most 28% of the words and more likely about 20%; each extra 100 words adds only about 4.4 seconds of visit time. Limits: a 2008 study with 25 above-average participants, many university employees, so treat it as directional. Front-load the offer and proof in headings, bullets and the first sentence of each section; don't rely on long body copy being read.
facts.source_title: How Little Do Users Read? - Nielsen Norman Group

facts.statement: NN/g eyetracking study (2018): users spent about 57% of page-viewing time above the fold (down from 80% in 2010) and about 74% within the first two screenfuls; about 81% falls within the first three screenfuls. Attention drops sharply after the fold, though people scroll when they have a reason. Put the value proposition and primary CTA in the first screen and avoid false floors. Limit: eyetracking of the tested pages, not a rule for every page type.
facts.source_title: Scrolling and Attention - Nielsen Norman Group

facts.statement: Google Merchant Center required product attributes: id (max 50 chars), title (max 150) or structured_title, description (max 5,000) or structured_description, link on the verified domain, image_link, availability (in_stock, out_of_stock, preorder, backorder; availability_date required for preorder), price with ISO 4217 currency, brand for new products (except movies, books, music), mpn only when no GTIN, and condition for used or refurbished items. Apparel and variants also need item_group_id, color, size, gender and age_group in some countries.
facts.source_title: Product data specification - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Merchant Center image rules: show the product accurately with no promotional text, watermarks, borders or placeholders; no upscaled images or thumbnails; JPEG, WebP, PNG, non-animated GIF, BMP or TIFF; crawlable by Googlebot-image; up to 10 additional_image_link images. AI-generated images must keep their AI metadata (e.g. IPTC DigitalSourceType). A minimum size of 500 x 500 px for all product images is enforced from 31 Jan 2027, so re-export small images now.
facts.source_title: Product data specification - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Merchant Center identifiers: submit gtin whenever the manufacturer assigned one (max 14 digits, no dashes or spaces); identifier_exists defaults to yes and should be set to no only when the product truly lacks identifiers for its category. Setting it to no for a product that has valid identifiers can get the product disapproved. ISBN-10 is deprecated; convert to ISBN-13.
facts.source_title: Product data specification - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Merchant Center energy labels: energy efficiency class attributes now apply only to products targeting Switzerland, Norway or the UK; EU energy label data must be sent through the certification attribute. Smartphones and tablets came under EU energy label rules from 20 Jun 2025, and tumble dryers were rescaled from 1 Jul 2025. Feeds for EU appliance or phone sellers must carry certification data.
facts.source_title: Product data specification - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Google merchant listing structured data (pages where the product can be bought) requires Product name, image and offers, with price (or priceSpecification.price) and priceCurrency; if shippingDetails is used it needs deliveryTime, shippingDestination and shippingRate. Recommended: availability, hasMerchantReturnPolicy, itemCondition, shippingDetails, gtin, brand.name, sku, aggregateRating and review. Add these to every product page template, not only the feed.
facts.source_title: Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data - Google Search Central

facts.statement: Merchant listing vs product snippet markup: merchant listings require an Offer (product snippets also accept AggregateOffer) because the merchant must be the seller, and they require a price greater than zero. Use product snippet markup for editorial review or comparison pages, and merchant listing markup only on pages where shoppers can buy from you.
facts.source_title: Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data - Google Search Central

facts.statement: Organization-level return policy markup: nest MerchantReturnPolicy under Organization or OnlineStore via hasMerchantReturnPolicy on one page (e.g. the returns page), not every page. Required: either applicableCountry (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, up to 50) plus returnPolicyCategory (with merchantReturnDays for a finite window), or merchantReturnLink. Recommended: returnFees, returnMethod, refundType, restockingFee, and returnPolicySeasonalOverride for holiday windows.
facts.source_title: Return policy (MerchantReturnPolicy) structured data - Google Search Central

facts.statement: Google applies return policy sources from strongest to weakest: Content API for Shopping return settings, then Merchant Center or Search Console settings, then product-level merchant listing markup, then organization-level markup. If both markup and Search Console settings exist, Google uses only Search Console. Fix return policy errors where the strongest source lives, or markup changes will have no effect.
facts.source_title: Return policy (MerchantReturnPolicy) structured data - Google Search Central

facts.statement: Google free listings show products at no cost on the Shopping tab, Search (rich results, Popular Products, Shopping Knowledge Panel), Images and Lens, YouTube (limited countries), Maps, Gemini and Business Profile; free local listings need an opt-in. They are usually on by default (Admin access needed to change them) and work alongside paid ads. Check free listings status before spending on Shopping ads for a new store.
facts.source_title: About free listings - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Free listings requirements: follow Google's free listing policies, add return policy information (Merchant Center recommended), and configure shipping settings or the shipping attribute, which is mandatory in many countries including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan and India. Keep product data consistent with the store; appearance is not guaranteed and depends on data quality.
facts.source_title: About free listings - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Merchant API (v1) is the redesign of the Content API for Shopping, split into sub-APIs such as accounts/v1, products_v1 (write via productInputs), inventories/v1 (local and regional) and reports_v1. Resources use path names like accounts/123/products/en~US~sku123; multiple primary and supplemental data sources are supported; push notifications replace polling; product and merchant reviews can be uploaded; gRPC is the default with REST supported.
facts.source_title: Merchant API overview - Google for Developers

facts.statement: EU General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (Commission factsheet, 1 Jul 2023): in force 12 Jun 2023 and applicable to businesses from 13 Dec 2024, covering non-food consumer products sold offline or online. All covered products must carry information on an economic operator responsible for them located in the EU, who also acts as the contact point for consumers and market surveillance authorities. Recalls require direct contact and standardised notices, with an effective, timely and cost-free remedy; businesses communicate with authorities through the EU Safety Business Gateway; online marketplaces have specific product safety requirements.
facts.source_title: The new General Product Safety Regulation - factsheet

facts.statement: GA4 standard event collection limits: event names max 40 characters; 25 parameters per event (ecommerce events can add up to 27 item-level custom parameters); parameter names 40 chars and values 100 chars (page_title 300, page_referrer 420, page_location 1,000); 25 user properties (names 24, values 36 chars); app streams max 500 distinct event names per user, web streams unlimited. Character limits do not rise with GA4 360, so keep tracking-plan names short.
facts.source_title: Event collection limits - Analytics Help

facts.statement: GA4 standard property configuration limits: 50 event-scoped custom dimensions, 25 user-scoped custom dimensions, 50 event-scoped custom metrics, 30 key events, 100 audiences, 50 custom insights, 200 explorations per user (500 shared), 400 Ads links, and 10M events per exploration query. Analytics blocks new items once a limit is reached, so budget custom dimensions in the tracking plan and archive unused ones.
facts.source_title: [GA4] Configuration limits - Analytics Help

facts.statement: GA4 data retention: standard properties can keep user- and event-level data 2 or 14 months; 360 can keep event data 2, 14, 26, 38 or 50 months (user-level 2 or 14). Retention affects only explorations and funnel reports, not standard aggregated reports. Age, gender and interest data is always 2 months. Set 14 months at setup, keep 'reset on new activity' on, and export to BigQuery for longer history needed by cohort or MMM work.
facts.source_title: [GA4] Data retention - Analytics Help

facts.statement: Consent mode v2 adds ad_user_data and ad_personalization to ad_storage and analytics_storage. To keep measurement, ad personalisation and remarketing for EEA users, advertisers must collect consent under Google's EU user consent policy and send these signals with Google tags, including Google Analytics data used in Google Ads, Search Ads 360 and Display & Video 360. Certified CMPs update automatically; a self-built banner must implement v2. Blocking Google tags until banner interaction can prevent Google verifying consent and may cause data loss. Check status in the conversion diagnostics tab.
facts.source_title: Updates to consent mode for traffic in European Economic Area (EEA) - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: From March 2024, Customer Match data for EEA users must carry both consent fields (ad_user_data and ad_personalization, Google Ads API v15 Consent object) set to GRANTED. DENIED returns an error and UNSPECIFIED counts as missing consent, so that data can't be used for ad personalisation. Lists uploaded before March 2024 keep working only with the Google services they were already used with, until they expire or are removed.
facts.source_title: FAQs About the EU user consent policy for Customer Match upload partners - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Basic vs advanced consent mode: basic blocks Google tags until the user interacts with the banner and sends nothing (not even consent state) if consent is denied, so Ads conversion modelling uses a general model. Advanced loads tags with consent defaulted to denied and sends cookieless pings, enabling an advertiser-specific model once a data threshold is met. Choose per the company's legal position; advanced recovers more modelled conversions.
facts.source_title: Consent mode overview - Google Tag Platform

facts.statement: Consent mode implementation: call gtag('consent','default',...) on every page before any config or event command, since out-of-order code breaks defaults. Use wait_for_update (e.g. 500 ms) when the CMP loads asynchronously; set region-specific defaults with ISO 3166-2 codes (US-CA overrides US; a default without region covers everyone else); send gtag('consent','update',...) as soon as the user chooses and persist the choice in a first-party cookie.
facts.source_title: Implement consent mode - Google Tag Platform

facts.statement: Google retired most Privacy Sandbox technologies (17 Oct 2025, low adoption): Attribution Reporting API (Chrome and Android), Protected Audience, Topics, Private Aggregation and Shared Storage, IP Protection, Related Website Sets, SelectURL, On-Device Personalization, Protected App Signals and SDK Runtime. CHIPS, FedCM and Private State Tokens stay. Don't build measurement or targeting plans on Sandbox APIs; rely on first-party data, consented server-side events and modelling.
facts.source_title: Update on Plans for Privacy Sandbox Technologies

facts.statement: Third-party cookies in Chrome (22 Apr 2025): Google will keep its current approach of letting users choose third-party cookie settings in Chrome's Privacy and Security settings and will not roll out a new standalone prompt, so third-party cookies are not being phased out by Chrome. Incognito already blocks them by default. Plan for partial loss anyway (Safari, Firefox, Incognito, user opt-outs) through first-party and server-side measurement.
facts.source_title: Next steps for Privacy Sandbox and tracking protections in Chrome

facts.statement: Meta Pixel + Conversions API deduplication: Meta recommends a redundant setup sending the same events from browser and server. Give each event the same id in both (Pixel eventID as the 4th fbq argument = server event_id) and the same event name; Meta keeps one, generally the first received. Dedup only works within 48 hours of the first event with that id. The fallback (same event_name plus fbp and/or external_id) works only when the browser event arrives first.
facts.source_title: Handling Duplicate Pixel and Conversions API Events - Meta for Developers

facts.statement: Server-side Google Tag Manager runs a server container you control: clients (built-in GA4 and Measurement Protocol) claim incoming requests and turn them into events, then sandboxed tags with permissions forward data to vendors. You decide what data leaves and where it goes; Google recommends serving the container from a first-party subdomain before production traffic. Host on your own Google Cloud project or manually elsewhere. It does not remove consent obligations.
facts.source_title: An introduction to server-side tagging - Google Tag Manager

facts.statement: GA4 Measurement Protocol sends server-to-server and offline events over HTTP, but it is meant to augment gtag, Tag Manager or Firebase collection, not replace it; a tagging method must already be in place. Join events to users with client_id (web) or app_instance_id (app), include session_id within 24 hours to attach session geo and device data, and test payloads against the validation server first.
facts.source_title: Measurement Protocol (Google Analytics 4)

facts.statement: Apple App Review Guidelines 3.1.1(a) and 3.1.3: apps on the United States storefront may include buttons, external links or other calls to action pointing to purchase methods other than in-app purchase, and need no entitlement to do so. In every other storefront this stays prohibited outside the specific StoreKit External Purchase Link entitlements. Show web-checkout CTAs only in US builds or metadata.
facts.source_title: App Review Guidelines - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple SDK and OS minimums: since 28 Apr 2026, apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS 26 SDK; since 9 Sep 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps must target iOS 13 or later. Builds from older toolchains are rejected at upload, so check the build chain before any launch date.
facts.source_title: Upcoming Requirements - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple privacy manifests: a privacy manifest describes the privacy practices of third-party code in one standard format, and Xcode combines the manifests of all third-party SDKs into one report to help create accurate Privacy Nutrition Labels. For SDKs on Apple's list (e.g. Firebase, FBSDKCoreKit, OneSignal, Flutter, Alamofire), a privacy manifest is required when a new app includes one or an update adds one; signatures are also required when a listed SDK is used as a binary dependency.
facts.source_title: Third-party SDK requirements - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple EU terms: from 1 Oct 2026 all EU developers are on one business model (Attachment 14 of the Developer Program License Agreement). Commission: Apple IAP 26% (reduced 15%); alternative in-app payment processing 20% (10%); out-of-app offers via actionable link 15% (10%), only on sales within 7 days of the tap; apps outside the App Store pay a 5% Core Technology Commission, replacing the per-install Core Technology Fee. Reduced rates cover Small Business Program members and subscriptions after year one.
facts.source_title: Update on apps distributed in the European Union - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple EU payment rules (from 1 Oct 2026): payment options offered (IAP, alternative processing, web links) must stay available for 12 months; alternative payment transactions are reported monthly within 15 days after month end; developers collect and remit tax on alternative processing. Kids category apps need a parental gate and may not link to web purchases; under-13s get a gate and no out-of-app offers; 13-17 need a gate for both.
facts.source_title: Update on apps distributed in the European Union - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple EU alternative distribution: alternative app marketplaces and Web Distribution are enabled in App Store Connect and pay the 5% Core Technology Commission. Eligibility needs at least one of: a moderate Dun & Bradstreet financial-stability score, being publicly traded (or owned by such a company), venture funding from an established firm, an audit by a licensed accountant, an approved government, education or nonprofit fee waiver, a USD 1,000,000 stand-by letter of credit, or one million first-year installs worldwide. No EU legal entity is needed.
facts.source_title: Update on apps distributed in the European Union - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple and the EU Digital Services Act: since 17 Feb 2025, apps without verified trader status in App Store Connect are removed from the EU App Store until it is provided and verified; app updates have required it since 16 Oct 2024. Set trader status with business contact details before any EU launch.
facts.source_title: Upcoming Requirements - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Apple custom product pages: up to 70 extra versions of the App Store page per app, each with its own screenshots, app previews and promotional text per localisation. Pages can be assigned keywords so they show in organic search for those terms (each keyword combination unique to one page), can carry a deep link (iOS/iPadOS 18+), are reviewed without an app update, and can be the destination of Apple Ads on Today, Search and results. Build one page per ad angle or audience.
facts.source_title: Custom product pages - App Store - Apple Developer

facts.statement: Google Play in the US (after the Ninth Circuit upheld the Epic injunction on 12 Sep 2025): since 29 Oct 2025 Google no longer stops developers from telling US users about pricing or availability outside Play, linking to downloads or transactions, or using non-Play billing, and doesn't require price parity. The external content links and alternative billing programs started 9 Dec 2025. Since 22 Jul 2026, US listings are shared with third-party US Android app stores unless the developer opted out.
facts.source_title: An update regarding Google Play's policies for developers serving users in the US - Play Console Help

facts.statement: Google Play US alternative billing fees apply from 1 Oct 2026 (authorised US transactions must be reported within 24 hours): 10% on a developer's first $1M annual earnings; above that, 10% on auto-renewing subscriptions and, on other digital purchases, 20% for new installs (first install or first update from Google Play on or after 30 Jun 2026) or 25% for existing ones; for Play Games Level Up or Apps Experience program members, 10% on subscriptions and 15% (new installs) or 20% (existing installs) on other digital purchases.
facts.source_title: Offering an alternative billing system for users in the United States - Play Console Help

facts.statement: Android developer verification: from 30 Sep 2026, verification protections apply to users on certified Android 7+ devices in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand installing apps from participating stores, so apps must come from registered, verified developers; global expansion to all apps follows from 2027. Google Play auto-registers about 99% of apps; register the rest in Play Console, or in the Android Developer Console if you distribute only outside Play. Hobbyists can share with up to 20 devices without ID; power users get an 'advanced flow' to install unverified apps.
facts.source_title: Android developer verification - Android Developers

facts.statement: On 24 Mar 2026 OpenAI said 'the initial version of Instant Checkout did not offer the level of flexibility that we aspire to provide', so merchants may use their own checkout experiences while OpenAI focuses on product discovery, extending the Agentic Commerce Protocol toward discovery. Plan ChatGPT shopping as feed quality plus your own checkout, not in-chat payment.
facts.source_title: Powering Product Discovery in ChatGPT

facts.statement: OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol docs: 'OpenAI is not the merchant of record in the Agentic Commerce Protocol' - merchants bring their own PSP; for each one-time delegated payment request OpenAI sets a maximum chargeable amount and an expiry, the PSP returns a payment token and OpenAI passes it to the merchant (Stripe's Shared Payment Token is the first compatible implementation). Per OpenAI's commerce docs, product feed onboarding is currently available to approved partners; feeds can be delivered by SFTP, file upload or hosted URL, and the file guide recommends a full snapshot refreshed at least daily.
facts.source_title: Agentic Commerce Protocol - Key concepts and Get started

facts.statement: Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2, announced 16 Sep 2025) uses cryptographically signed 'Mandates' as proof of what the user approved: an Intent Mandate records the user's instructions and, for delegated tasks, rules such as price limits and timing; a Cart Mandate locks in the exact items and price when the user approves a cart. Together they form a non-repudiable audit trail from intent to cart to payment. AP2 extends A2A and MCP, supports cards, bank transfers and stablecoins (A2A x402 extension with Coinbase, the Ethereum Foundation and MetaMask), and was developed with 60+ payments and technology companies.
facts.source_title: Announcing Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)

facts.statement: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol (14 Oct 2025, built with Cloudflare) lets merchants tell approved AI shopping agents from bad bots: agents sign requests with agent-specific cryptographic signatures based on HTTP Message Signatures and aligned with Web Bot Auth, carrying Agent Intent, Consumer Recognition and optional Payment Information. It supports agent-driven guest and logged-in checkout with minimal site changes. Available via Visa Developer Center and GitHub; initial specs cover the Visa network only. Do not let bot defenses block signed agents.
facts.source_title: Visa Introduces Trusted Agent Protocol: An Ecosystem-Led Framework for AI Commerce

facts.statement: Mastercard said on 10 Sep 2025 that all U.S. Mastercard cardholders would be enabled for Mastercard Agent Pay by the 2025 holiday season, with a global rollout to follow shortly after; Citi and U.S. Bank cardholders were first to trial it. It also launched an Agent Toolkit that exposes Mastercard API docs to AI tools through an MCP server, and is working with the FIDO Alliance's Payments Working Group on standards for agentic payments. The release states plans only; completion of the rollout is not confirmed.
facts.source_title: Mastercard unveils new tools and collaborations to power smarter, safer agentic commerce

facts.statement: The Universal Commerce Protocol (ucp.dev) is an open standard for agents, platforms and businesses, with specification, SDKs and reference implementations on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. Co-developers listed include Google, Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, Stripe, Booking.com and Marriott; Visa, Mastercard and PayPal are listed as endorsers. Capabilities are catalog search and lookup, cart building, identity linking (OAuth 2.0), checkout and order management; it runs over REST and JSON-RPC with support for AP2, A2A and MCP. Businesses remain merchant of record. A lodging spec is in draft and food ordering is coming soon.
facts.source_title: Universal Commerce Protocol

facts.statement: Microsoft launched Copilot Checkout on 8 Jan 2026 in the U.S. on Copilot.com: shoppers buy inside the Copilot chat and the merchant stays merchant of record, keeping the customer data and relationship. Shopify merchants are enrolled automatically after an opt-out window and manage it in Shopify admin; PayPal and Stripe merchants apply via a form. Merchant Center is not required to sell, but its feeds can inform organic Copilot results. Microsoft plans to extend it to Bing, MSN and Edge. Check the Shopify admin setting before a merchant is enrolled by default.
facts.source_title: Conversations that Convert: Copilot Checkout and Brand Agents

facts.statement: Microsoft Brand Agents (Jan 2026) are on-site AI shopping assistants in the brand's voice that answer product, shipping and returns questions, compare options, surface checkout links and suggest upsells. Available to Shopify merchants: install Microsoft Clarity and join the waitlist; results appear in Clarity comparing agent-assisted and organic sessions. Microsoft cites one merchant with over 3x higher conversion in assisted sessions and internal Aug 2025 data of 53% more purchases within 30 minutes for Copilot-assisted journeys; treat these as vendor claims.
facts.source_title: Conversations that Convert: Copilot Checkout and Brand Agents

facts.statement: Google's agentic checkout (13 Nov 2025): a shopper tracks a product with size, color and a maximum price; when the price falls within budget and the merchant is eligible, Google can buy it on the merchant's site with Google Pay, only after the user confirms purchase and shipping details. Rolling out in Search including AI Mode with eligible U.S. merchants such as Wayfair, Chewy, Quince and select Shopify merchants. Keep prices, variants and availability in the feed exact, because the agent buys at the price the feed shows.
facts.source_title: Google Shopping launches agentic checkout and more AI shopping tools

facts.statement: Google's 'Let Google Call' (announced 13 Nov 2025, U.S.) phones nearby stores about stock, price and promotions for 'near me' product searches (toys, health and beauty, electronics) and sends the answers by email or text. Per Google Business Profile Help, businesses can opt out by verifying the profile and turning off options under Business Profile settings > Advanced settings > 'Google automated calls and text messages', or by telling the caller to stop; the help page says calls are available in the U.S. in all states except Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana and Nebraska. Brief store staff so price and promo answers match the site.
facts.source_title: About automated calls and texts from Google to your business - Google Business Profile Help

facts.statement: At I/O (19 May 2026) Google said Search would widen agentic booking to local experiences and services, showing live price and availability and linking to the chosen provider, and for categories like home repair, beauty and pet care Google can call businesses for the user; both were due for everyone in the U.S. in summer 2026. Background 'information agents' that monitor the web 24/7 and can take actions launch first for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Gemini 3.5 Flash became the default AI Mode model globally.
facts.source_title: Google Search's I/O 2026 updates: AI agents and more

facts.statement: The current Model Context Protocol specification is version 2026-07-28 (JSON-RPC 2.0; hosts, clients, servers). Servers offer resources, prompts and tools; clients can offer elicitation; tasks, MCP Apps (inline UI) and Skills over MCP are opt-in extensions. Security principles: users must consent to all data access and operations, hosts must get explicit consent before invoking any tool, tools are treated as arbitrary code execution, and tool annotations are untrusted unless from a trusted server. MCP cannot enforce these; the host must.
facts.source_title: Model Context Protocol Specification

facts.statement: MCP security best practices: token passthrough is forbidden - servers MUST NOT accept tokens not issued for them; proxy servers with static client IDs MUST store per-client consent, validate exact redirect URIs and use single-use state values; clients MUST show the full command and get explicit approval before a one-click local server install, and should sandbox it; state handles are not authentication; request minimal scopes and step up on demand, never wildcard scopes. Use these as the audit list before adding any marketing connector.
facts.source_title: MCP Security Best Practices

facts.statement: On 9 Dec 2025 Anthropic donated the Model Context Protocol to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a directed fund under the Linux Foundation co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI, with support from Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare and Bloomberg; goose and AGENTS.md are fellow founding projects. MCP's governance model and maintainers stay the same. Anthropic cited 10,000+ active public MCP servers and adoption by ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and VS Code, so one MCP server reaches most major AI clients.
facts.source_title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation

facts.statement: The C2PA Technical Specification (Content Credentials) is at version 2.5, listed as October 2026. A C2PA Manifest combines assertions, a claim and a claim signature. Soft bindings (such as fingerprints or invisible watermarks) let a manifest be recovered if metadata is stripped. Keep Content Credentials on AI-generated ad and social assets through export.
facts.source_title: C2PA Technical Specification 2.5

facts.statement: Google SynthID embeds invisible watermarks in AI images and video (designed to survive cropping, filters, frame-rate changes and lossy compression), watermarks in audio from Lyria and NotebookLM, and text watermarking of Gemini app output. The public SynthID Detector portal checks for watermarks from Google and partners including OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao. Assume Google-generated creative is detectable as AI and disclose it where platforms or law require.
facts.source_title: SynthID - Google DeepMind

facts.statement: Meta labels AI images on Facebook, Instagram and Threads when it detects industry-standard indicators of AI generation, including C2PA or IPTC metadata and invisible watermarks (from Google, OpenAI, Microsoft, Adobe, Midjourney, Shutterstock tools). Users must disclose organic posts with photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio that was digitally created or altered, and Meta may apply penalties if they don't; content that could materially deceive the public on an important matter may get a more prominent label.
facts.source_title: Labeling AI-Generated Images on Facebook, Instagram and Threads

facts.statement: Meta labels ads 'AI info' when they are fully created or materially edited with Meta's generative AI creative features; minor edits like resizing or color correction get no label. The label usually sits in the ad's three-dot menu, but when the image includes an AI-generated photorealistic human it appears next to 'Sponsored' at the top of the ad. Meta is rolling this out gradually. Expect visible labels on ads with AI people and test whether they change CTR before scaling AI-human creative.
facts.source_title: How AI-generated images in ads are identified and labeled on Meta

facts.statement: Meta's policy for social issue, election and political ads requires advertisers to disclose when third-party generative AI was used to create or alter a photorealistic image or video or realistic-sounding audio. From 1 Jun 2026 Meta also uses automated detection to find AI-created or edited ad media and adds an 'AI Info' label in 'About this ad'. Undisclosed ads are rejected and repeated failure can bring penalties against the advertiser. Tick the disclosure on every AI-touched issue ad.
facts.source_title: Ads about Social Issues, Elections or Politics - Meta Transparency Center

facts.statement: Google Ads Political content policy (updated July 2024): election advertisers must disclose synthetic or digitally altered content that inauthentically depicts real or realistic-looking people or events by ticking 'Altered or synthetic content' in campaign settings. Google auto-generates the in-ad disclosure for mobile feeds, mobile Shorts and in-stream ads; for all other formats the advertiser must add a clear, conspicuous disclosure such as 'This audio was computer generated'.
facts.source_title: Update to our policy on Disclosure requirements for synthetic content (July 2024)

facts.statement: TikTok ad policy (updated April 2026): significantly edited or AI-generated media is allowed only with the AIGC label or your own clear disclaimer, caption, watermark or sticker. 'Significant' includes fully AI-generated images, video or audio, showing a main subject doing something they didn't, and voice-cloning someone to say what they didn't; adjusting lighting or colour, removing or modifying backgrounds and denoising are minor. When unsure, label it. Undisclosed AI content gets the ad rejected or restricted. Using a public figure's likeness without permission, such as a false endorsement, is not allowed.
facts.source_title: TikTok ads policy - Misleading and false content

facts.statement: YouTube requires creators to set 'AI use' at upload for realistic AI-generated or meaningfully altered content: a real person saying or doing what they didn't, altered footage of real events or places, realistic scenes that never happened, or AI music as the main focus. Not needed for clearly unrealistic or animated content, minor edits, or AI used only for scripts, titles, thumbnails or ideas. YouTube may auto-label via its own tools or C2PA metadata.
