On AI, 68% are willing to receive and trust AI-personalised offers, but 49% are frustrated by chatbots that fail to solve queries and 33% suspect AI recommendations are biased. EY's advice: pair technology with trained staff and fix friction points rather than replace people.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: consumers return to physical stores for personal service even as AI and tech revolutionize online shopping

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index (survey of 22,000 consumers in 28 countries, Sept-Oct 2023): consumer trust in AI fell within months. Trust in AI product visualisation fell from 67% to 59% from April 2023, in AI-personalised recommendations from 66% to 58%, and in AI answers to questions from 62% to 56%. 71% were delaying some purchases until sales events. EY's guidance is to use AI openly for clearer price and quality comparisons and to keep an easy route to a human in AI service.
facts.source_title: EY: Can AI revolutionise your Black Friday sales and boost consumer spending

facts.statement: BCG digital B2B sales study (Aug 23, 2017; 723 European and global companies): 19% were beginners, 48% intermediate, 23% mature and 11% champions in digital sales. Planned digital sales investment over five years rose with maturity, from about 4% of revenue (beginners) to about 8% (champions). Self-classified maturity, so treat it as a benchmark of the period. Use: place a prospect or client on this four-stage ladder before proposing digital sales investment.
facts.source_title: Bringing Your Digital B2B Sales Up to Speed (BCG)

facts.statement: In BCG's 2017 digital B2B sales study (723 companies), champions had EBITDA more than 3 percentage points above beginners. Champions shared seven traits: heavy investment, digital-skills training, strong data tools, deep customer insight, digitized processes, integrated channels, and coordination that avoids channel conflict. Correlation in a company survey, not proof of cause. Use: turn the seven traits into an audit checklist for a sales organization's digital readiness.
facts.source_title: Bringing Your Digital B2B Sales Up to Speed (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Five Selling Secrets of Today's Digital B2B Leaders' (Apr 5, 2016; study of a dozen cloud-era B2B sales leaders): start with the customer journey, track each prospect from cookie to customer, stop cold calling in favor of scored inbound leads, make high-volume inside sales the main channel, and grow through customer success. Use: use the five secrets as the skeleton of a modern B2B sales-motion redesign brief.
facts.source_title: Five Selling Secrets of Today's Digital B2B Leaders (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 2016 digital B2B leaders article (sample: about 12 firms; figures are BCG estimates or cited third-party data): properly scored leads convert at two to three times the rate of cold leads; inbound leads cost about half of outbound; customer success teams may take up to 25% of sales spend and can lift existing-customer sales by up to 30%. Use: cite as directional ranges, never as guaranteed lift, when justifying lead scoring or a success team.
facts.source_title: Five Selling Secrets of Today's Digital B2B Leaders (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Building an Integrated Marketing and Sales Engine for B2B' (Jul 2, 2018; based on client work and 50+ executive interviews): firms that integrate marketing and sales may see 15-30% better marketing efficiency and a two- to threefold gain in lead conversion (authors' experience, not a controlled study). Benchmark: if sales accepts under about 50% of marketing-qualified leads, the leads are probably not valuable. Use: set a shared lead-acceptance target and review it jointly each month.
facts.source_title: Building an Integrated Marketing and Sales Engine for B2B (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Building Bionic Capabilities for B2B Marketing' (Mar 8, 2021) benchmarked 268 companies in seven B2B sectors using traffic data from May 2019 to Apr 2020. It says leaders running demand centers see 20-50% lower cost per lead, a 10-20% improvement in lead-to-close cycle time and 2-8x lead-to-close conversion (BCG experience, no sample stated). Cases: Salesforce, Hilti, Thermo Fisher Scientific. Use: frame demand-center proposals with these ranges as estimates to validate in a pilot.
facts.source_title: Building Bionic Capabilities for B2B Marketing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 2021 B2B marketing piece cites third-party data (Demandbase and Adobe surveys, samples not stated): about 82% of B2B website visitors are not potential customers, 97% leave without filling a form, and sales acts on roughly half of online leads. It also cites CES/Google: 57% of the buying process happens online. Use: set conversion and follow-up targets against this leak, and prioritize lead routing and visitor identification before buying more traffic.
facts.source_title: Building Bionic Capabilities for B2B Marketing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Creating a Digital-First Hybrid Sales Model' (Jun 17, 2021) names five imperatives: build omnichannel experiences, shift field reps to hybrid interactions, expand inside sales, focus on long-term relationships beyond the first sale, and integrate marketing and sales operations. It also floats a revenue-operations leadership role and regional sales 'minihubs'. Use: map a client's coverage model against the five imperatives to find the biggest gap.
facts.source_title: There's No Going Back to the Old B2B Sales Model (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG hybrid sales cases (Jun 2021, anonymized clients): a Fortune 100 B2B services firm with 500+ reps doubled its close rate in three months after redesigning the digital journey and incentives; a global services firm moved digital leads (about 1% converted) to about 200 inside reps and raised conversion roughly tenfold, over $100M added ARR. BCG-reported, not independently audited. Use: use as precedent for piloting inside sales on digital leads, with a control group.
facts.source_title: There's No Going Back to the Old B2B Sales Model (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG survey of 50+ large companies moving field sales to inside sales (Jun 2021): 78% cited keeping employee motivation and morale as a challenge and 58% worried about missing on-the-job training for remote staff. Executive opinion data. BCG adds that incentives paid per transaction must be rebuilt around customer-centric goals. Use: pair any inside-sales shift with a training and incentive redesign, not only a channel change.
facts.source_title: There's No Going Back to the Old B2B Sales Model (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Empowering the Marketing Function in B2B Sales' (Dec 15, 2023): B2B buyers increasingly behave like consumers, wanting self-service and third-party information; it cites Forrester that 64% of business buyers are Millennials or Gen Z (sample not stated). Firms with demand centers integrating marketing, sales and service get better leads and conversion. Three steps: shared data and metrics, wider data for lead quality, SLAs between the functions. Use: write SLA-based marketing-to-sales handoffs.
facts.source_title: Empowering the Marketing Function in B2B Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'An Overdue Upgrade for B2B Go-to-Market Functions' (Sep 5, 2024; tech-company benchmark, sample not stated): the average tech firm needs about six months to publish a long-form asset, top decile about six weeks. Most firms run one or two growth tests per quarter, leaders about 20 per month. 52% of B2B marketers name marketing-sales misalignment as a barrier; only 16% use marketing data in real time. Use: benchmark content cycle time and test cadence in audits.
facts.source_title: An Overdue Upgrade for B2B Go-to-Market Functions (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'demand squads' (Sep 5, 2024): small cross-functional teams of marketing, sales and customer success, each owning one 'hero metric' and working in two- to three-week test sprints. Client results (BCG-reported): a tech firm scaled 16 growth use cases for 15-30% one-year revenue gains; an insurer ran 30+ initiatives, tripled broker yield, added over $250M annual premiums. Use: propose a squad with one hero metric and a sprint backlog for growth work.
facts.source_title: An Overdue Upgrade for B2B Go-to-Market Functions (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How B2B Marketplaces Are Rewriting the Rules of Trade' (Jun 4, 2024): global B2B e-commerce reached about $23.4 trillion in 2023 (Statista, AgileIntel); over 50% of SMBs plan more online procurement; marketplace commissions run about 8% (B2B electronics) to 20% (clothing, PPE); operators cite 5-7% extra EBITDA margin. Marketplaces grow about 7x faster than other e-commerce (Digital Commerce 360). Use: size a marketplace channel option with these ranges.
facts.source_title: How B2B Marketplaces Are Rewriting the Rules of Trade (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG B2B marketplace research (Jun 2024): about half of buyers prefer manufacturer-run marketplaces, about 30% are indifferent, and 10-20% prefer general-purpose ones (survey sample not stated). Top 10% of sellers generate over 80% of third-party sales; buyers use only two or three platforms per category, so few winners. Success needs selective seller onboarding and B2B features such as quoting and ERP links. Use: advise a curated, specialized marketplace and seller-quality gates.
facts.source_title: How B2B Marketplaces Are Rewriting the Rules of Trade (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Why B2B Software Firms Need a Go-to-Market Reset' (Feb 17, 2026): buyers move from 3-7 year software refresh cycles to continuous evaluation and want fast proof of value; it cites G2 that 57% of buyers expect positive ROI within three months. Usually only one or two vendors reach the proof-of-concept stage, and BCG outlines four POC models from demos to customer-sandbox trials. Use: build a POC offer and time-to-value story into B2B software sales plays.
facts.source_title: Why B2B Software Firms Need a Go-to-Market Reset (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's 2025 IT-buyer survey, cited in its Feb 2026 software go-to-market article (sample not stated): 45% of IT buyers plan to raise AI spend within 12 months and 46% plan to widen their AI supplier roster. BCG proposes new roles (AI sales specialists, field CTOs, outcome managers, GTM engineers, forward-deployed engineers) and notes that many vendors now set account-executive targets on adoption, not only bookings. Use: redesign roles and quotas around adoption.
facts.source_title: Why B2B Software Firms Need a Go-to-Market Reset (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Get Your B2B Sales Team Ready for the Power of Generative AI' (Sep 11, 2023): four GenAI personas for sellers (sales assistant, data scientist, personal marketer, sales coach), plus a readiness check on Potential, People, Policies and Platforms. BCG estimates GenAI could double rep productivity and cross-sell rates, an estimate rather than a measured result. Its SuccessDNA tool is said to raise the share of reps beating quota by 30%. Use: scope seller-assist agents by these four personas.
facts.source_title: Get Your B2B Sales Team Ready for the Power of Generative AI (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'GenAI and the Path to Profit in B2B Sales' (Jan 2, 2024) sets a three-horizon path: augment and automate current tasks; reimagine workflows such as configure-price-quote, outreach and RFP responses; then drive transformational change to sales motions and operating model. Start with high-value, low-friction use cases, build pilot-measure-scale capacity, and set an end-state vision. Use: sequence AI sales initiatives across the three horizons and tag each use case.
facts.source_title: GenAI and the Path to Profit in B2B Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG research cited in 'GenAI and the Path to Profit in B2B Sales' (Jan 2, 2024; sample not stated): over 75% of sales organizations had invested in AI and analytics but only 20% fully adopted it; 66% of reps expect GenAI to raise productivity, 51% say reskilling is needed, and over 70% of sales leaders plan to invest. Executive and seller opinion data. Use: plan adoption, training and change effort, not only tool purchase.
facts.source_title: GenAI and the Path to Profit in B2B Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with AWS and Salesforce, 'How to Accelerate the GenAI Revolution in Sales' (Sep 16, 2024): AWS account teams using GenAI summaries saved on average 35 minutes of meeting prep and generated 4.9% higher pipeline value. BCG's 10-20-70 rule puts about 10% of effort on algorithms, 20% on data and technology, and 70% on people and processes; about 10% of firms scaled a GenAI application enterprise-wide. Use: budget most AI sales work for adoption and process change.
facts.source_title: How to Accelerate the GenAI Revolution in Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'GenAI Lets Telecom B2B Sales Teams Get Back to Selling' (Sep 16, 2024): citing a Salesforce study, reps spend 72% of their time on non-selling tasks. BCG says combining generative and predictive AI has the potential to raise EBITDA by more than 40% (a potential, not a measured result). It names CRM updates and call summaries as automatable, describes a Salesforce pilot that qualifies RFPs, and sketches AI-priced cross-sell only as a scenario. Use: automate admin first.
facts.source_title: GenAI Lets Telecom B2B Sales Teams Get Back to Selling (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The Unified Theory of Strategic Pricing' (Aug 29, 2023; Izaret and Sinha): the Strategic Pricing Hexagon joins cost, competition and customer value into seven pricing 'games': value, uniform, cost, power, custom, choice and dynamic. Buyer and seller concentration plus offer complexity decide which game fits, and each game has a lead function. Conceptual, no statistical data. Use: classify a client's pricing game before recommending tactics.
facts.source_title: The Unified Theory of Strategic Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Raising the Bar in Industrial Goods Pricing' (Feb 21, 2025; survey of 400 industrial goods firms from BCG's 2024 Pricing Maturity Assessment): almost half of top 'pricing innovators' widened margins by over 10 percentage points in two years while gaining share; only 22% of firms in the power pricing game can model competitor responses; 33% still price in Excel. Use: benchmark a B2B client's pricing maturity against these shares.
facts.source_title: Raising the Bar in Industrial Goods Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG industrial pricing recommendations (Feb 21, 2025): link management strategy to daily price decisions, match capabilities to your pricing game (power, custom or value), invest in data assets with GenAI for contract terms, own the core price-setting logic rather than rely on third-party tools, and staff a technical pricing team. A strategic team for $1B+ firms costs about $1.5M-$3M per year. Use: use as a capability roadmap when scoping a pricing function.
facts.source_title: Raising the Bar in Industrial Goods Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Five Trends Will Define the Future of Pricing' (Jan 30, 2025): AI and GenAI, price volatility, dynamic pricing, sustainability and fairness. Dynamic pricing needs a clear value story and human oversight of algorithms. Based on over 350 BCG GenAI projects, only firms that fix process, people and culture, not just technology, gain profit. Fairness is read differently across cultures. Use: add a fairness and human-oversight check to any dynamic price proposal.
facts.source_title: Five Trends Will Define the Future of Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Rethinking B2B Software Pricing in the Agentic AI Era' (Aug 13, 2025) lists five emerging models: usage by resources, per agent, usage by interactions, outcome by jobs completed, and outcome by financial result. Fold agentic features that neither finish a job nor differentiate into the core product; run agentic pricing in parallel with seats and track seat compression. Use: pick a pricing model by how well value can be defined and attributed.
facts.source_title: Rethinking B2B Software Pricing in the Agentic AI Era (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Aug 2025 software pricing article, mixed sources and samples not stated: BCG IT-buyer survey says 40% of buyers cut software spend mainly by reducing seats, 48% plan more AI spend, and 91% want only partly autonomous agents; ICONIQ 2025 says 68% of vendors charge separately for AI or reserve it for premium tiers; a16z buyers: 47% struggle to define measurable outcomes. Use: prepare outcome definitions and cost-predictability answers before proposing outcome pricing.
facts.source_title: Rethinking B2B Software Pricing in the Agentic AI Era (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Debunking the Myths of B2B Dynamic Pricing' (Nov 20, 2020; anonymized clients): an MRO distributor moved list-price setting to a dynamic engine in 12 months for about $40M near-term profit; a petrochemical wholesaler gained 100-250 basis points of margin; a building-materials distributor with hundreds of thousands of SKUs raised EBIT margin by 100 bps; an automaker's incentive efficiency rose 10%. Use: counter objections that dynamic pricing needs perfect data or fast markets.
facts.source_title: Debunking the Myths of B2B Dynamic Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Overcoming Retail Complexity with AI-Powered Pricing' (Apr 16, 2024): retailers adopting AI pricing report 5-10% higher gross profit (BCG-reported, no sample stated). Pricing decisions split into strategic (category roles, price zones), hygienic (item relationships, rounding) and dynamic (real-time competitor moves) layers, enabled by a central pricing team, frequent read-and-react cycles and an integrated data platform. Use: structure retail pricing work in these three layers.
facts.source_title: Overcoming Retail Complexity with AI-Powered Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How Companies Can Make Dynamic Pricing Fairer for Customers' (page shows an update date of May 6, 2024; advisory, no data): learn how customers differ in perceived value, make sure price changes come with a matching gain in value so they are not seen as unfair, and use data and tools while keeping the pricing decision with people. Dynamic pricing is drawing criticism as it reaches everyday purchases. Use: require a customer-facing fairness rationale in any variable-price offer.
facts.source_title: How Companies Can Make Dynamic Pricing Fairer for Customers (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Beyond the Black Box in Pricing' (Sep 9, 2021; Robinson and Garcia Escudero) proposes 'smart pricing authority', built on business intelligence, negotiating agility and pricing authority, as a blend of three prevailing models (decentralized sales-led, centralized scientific, tech-enabled sales discretion). It separately cites a telco with revenue leakage of up to 550 bps and a typical 400-800 bps margin opportunity at that maturity (BCG experience, not compared). Use: design deal-desk guardrails around the three pillars.
facts.source_title: Beyond the Black Box in Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Transformed by the Power of Pricing' (Jun 16, 2015): a seven-step pricing enablement journey built on a learn-do-teach skills model. BCG experience: companies upgrading pricing capability often gain 2-8% annual revenue, nearly all to profit. The composite case: discounts varied over 200%, a pilot raised price realization 5%, and about $150M run-rate EBIT on $4B revenue followed. Composite, illustrative. Use: cite the 2-8% as a BCG experience range only.
facts.source_title: Transformed by the Power of Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG pricing maturity curve (Apr 13, 2018, private-equity due diligence article): five levels, reactive, foundational, analytic, strategic and dynamic, drawn partly from a BCG and Professional Pricing Society assessment of 300+ corporations. Most PE targets sit at foundational. A 3-4 week pricing diligence found 150-400 bps of EBITDA upside; pricing change typically takes 6-18 months. Use: place a client on the curve and quote the timeline honestly.
facts.source_title: Evaluating Pricing in Due Diligence for Value Creation (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Five Pricing Moves for CPG in a Cost-of-Living Crisis' (Jan 3, 2023): a September 2022 survey of over 1,400 pricing decision makers (ten sectors, four regions) found about 60% of the CPG firms surveyed had raised prices several times in 18 months. BCG says differentiated, portfolio-based increases have at least twice the profit impact of blanket cost-driven ones (BCG's observation, not a survey figure) and that AI tools can add over 300 bps of EBITDA in the highest-leverage pricing areas. Use: recommend segmented, not blanket, price moves.
facts.source_title: Five Pricing Moves for CPG in a Cost-of-Living Crisis (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How Machinery and Automation Companies Can Lead in Commercial Excellence' (Apr 26, 2024; survey of 20+ machinery and automation firms): companies at advanced maturity show 15-20% higher revenue, 3-5% better EBIT margin and nearly double sales productivity than basic ones, but only about 20% reach that level. Framework spans marketing, sales, pricing, service, strategy and enablers. Small, self-assessed sample. Use: score a client on these commercial excellence dimensions.
facts.source_title: How Machinery and Automation Companies Can Lead in Commercial Excellence (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Uniting CPG Marketing and Sales' (Jan 23, 2025): in a BCG survey of CPG marketing leaders (sample not stated), 75% named omnichannel investment allocation and activation as top challenges, and 68% of those cited silos. From client work, a combined operating model can lift revenue 3-6% and return on marketing investment 30%. Four principles: cross-functional representation, consistent process, clear governance, aligned incentives. Use: apply the four principles when merging marketing and sales planning.
facts.source_title: Uniting CPG Marketing and Sales for Collaboration and Growth (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG medtech commercial model study (Jun 16, 2021): based on a survey of 8,500+ commercial employees, 200+ senior-leader interviews and a 150-business benchmark. Remote reps deliver two to three times the productivity per rep of field reps, at 75-100 calls a week versus 15-20 in-person visits. A European company approaching 300 remote reps saw long-tail accounts grow twice as fast as core segments in early tests. BCG-reported. Use: consider a blended remote-plus-field model for long-tail accounts.
facts.source_title: The Rise of the Next Generation of Medtech Milkmen (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Rule of 40 Lessons from the Top Performers in Software' (May 20, 2025; 107 private B2B SaaS companies benchmarked with seven growth equity funds): companies with a dedicated renewals team, account managers for upsell and customer success managers for renewals, had median gross revenue retention 4 points higher. 54% moved GRR by under 2 points in a year. Spending more on sales and marketing while go-to-market was inefficient produced a negative Rule of 40. Use: assign clear renewal ownership before adding acquisition spend.
facts.source_title: Rule of 40 Lessons from the Top Performers in Software (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Rule of 40 study (May 2025; 107 SaaS firms) groups companies into archetypes by gross retention and deal size: keepers (high GRR, low ACV), transactional (GRR under 80%) and leaky buckets (low GRR, high ACV). Leaky buckets had low win rates and high sales spend, suggesting expansion beyond the ideal customer profile. Fixes: renewal playbook, churn early-warning alerts, time-to-value focus. Use: diagnose a SaaS client's archetype before choosing between acquisition and retention.
facts.source_title: Rule of 40 Lessons from the Top Performers in Software (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG X survey of 109 B2B SaaS firms, mostly European (Apr 19, 2023): average CAC payback 11 months, with 84% under 18 months; average annual customer churn 8%, about 16% in analytics and martech/adtech and 5% in fintech. Fastest growers spend about 25-30% of revenue on go-to-market, mostly sales. Sample skews to Germany (56%). Use: use these as SaaS sanity benchmarks, noting the European skew.
facts.source_title: Tech Is Cooling Off. B2B SaaS Is Not. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG survey of 109 B2B SaaS firms (Apr 2023): firms with advanced lead scoring grew 75% faster and those using sales automation 89% faster than peers (association, not cause). Word-of-mouth was the top lead source at 34%, ahead of paid search at 18%. Field and inside sales suit contracts around $100,000 a year or more; smaller deals fit self-serve. Use: match sales channel to contract size and invest in lead scoring and referral programs.
facts.source_title: Tech Is Cooling Off. B2B SaaS Is Not. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Tech Comes Out on Top. Can It Stay There?' (Mar 10, 2022): its sample of 113 tech companies across 33 industries is the basis for the finding that net revenue retention is one of the most prominent contributors to SaaS valuation multiples and total shareholder return. It describes a customer-success mindset that uses data and AI-based intelligence. No NRR figures are given on the page. Use: lead retention business cases with NRR as the investor-relevant metric.
facts.source_title: Tech Comes Out on Top. Can It Stay There? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Your Indirect Sales Need Your Direct Attention' (May 29, 2019): five rules for tech vendors managing channels: embrace as-a-service without dropping traditional models, optimize incentives, modernize partner relationships (including a 'hard deck' of direct accounts), strengthen enablement, and reassess channel support, keeping field reps channel-neutral in pay. Based on authors' experience. Use: audit a partner program against these five rules.
facts.source_title: Your Indirect Sales Need Your Direct Attention (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG indirect sales article (May 29, 2019; authors' experience, no sample): distributors and resellers typically drive 70% or more of a tech vendor's revenue; BCG estimates only 10-15% of traditional resellers will invest in and succeed at a cloud business. Recommendations: initially move 10-20% of incentive dollars to cloud, require measurable gains within three to six months from partners on improvement plans, and ideally answer special-pricing requests within two to four hours. Use: apply as 2019 rules of thumb in partner program design.
facts.source_title: Your Indirect Sales Need Your Direct Attention (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Adopting an Ecosystem-First Mindset in Software' (Nov 10, 2022): five strategies for partner programs: judge partners by business model and outcomes rather than labels, attract and support partners in stages, simplify programs with tailored incentives, set clear roles for co-selling and lead routing, and build ecosystem culture and tools. A 2021 buyer survey found 68% see systems integrators as orchestrators (sample not stated). Building takes 12-18 months. Use: design partner incentives by business model.
facts.source_title: Adopting an Ecosystem-First Mindset in Software (BCG)

facts.statement: Christensen, Cook and Hall (HBR, Dec 2005, 'Marketing Malpractice'): about 30,000 consumer products launch each year and over 90% fail. The authors argue that fundamental marketing paradigms, namely the techniques used to segment markets, build brands and understand customers, are broken; P&G's A.G. Lafley is quoted agreeing. The page does not state the sample or method behind the 90% figure. Use: do not size a launch or choose a segment from demographic averages; test the job the customer is hiring the product to do.
facts.source_title: Marketing Malpractice: The Cause and the Cure (HBR)

facts.statement: HBS Working Knowledge excerpt of the Christensen-Cook-Hall milk shake study (16 Jan 2006): about 40% of a fast-food chain's milk shakes were bought in the early morning, usually by solo commuters who bought nothing else, to make a long, boring drive more interesting and stave off hunger until about 10 a.m. At other times, parents bought shakes with meals to placate their children, a different job. Observation count is not reported. Use: segment by job and moment of purchase, then write one offer per job.
facts.source_title: What Customers Want from Your Products (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Keller's 'The Brand Report Card' (HBR, Jan-Feb 2000) grades a brand against ten characteristics shared by the strongest brands, to audit brand equity and decide where to invest. The hbr.org page shows only the opening (brand equity is a priority in every industry; strong brands bring loyalty and profit); the ten-characteristic framing comes from the HBR store listing and secondary summaries. Use: run it as a periodic brand audit and fix the weakest trait before adding media spend.
facts.source_title: The Brand Report Card (HBR, Kevin Lane Keller)

facts.statement: Rust, Zeithaml and Lemon (HBR, Sep 2004, 'Customer-Centered Brand Management'): most managers already see growth in customer lifetime value as a priority. Retention, cross-selling and broader offerings each add to customer equity, and winning new customers costs far more than keeping current ones. The page summary gives no numbers. Use: judge brand work by its effect on customer-level lifetime value, retention and cross-sell, not by awareness alone.
facts.source_title: Customer-Centered Brand Management (HBR)

facts.statement: Dawar and Bagga (HBR, Jun 2015) map brands on two 0-10 scores: centrality (how typical of the category) and distinctiveness, giving four quadrants: aspirational (high on both), mainstream, peripheral, unconventional. Bubble size shows sales or price. Test categories were US cars and beer; scoring method details are in the full article. Use: place your brand and two rivals on the map before choosing whether to reinforce category fit or push difference.
facts.source_title: A Better Way to Map Brand Strategy (HBR)

facts.statement: Dawar and Bagga (HBR, Jun 2015), US cars and beer: aspirational brands held about 30% of car unit sales and 62% of beer sales; unconventional brands held 2-4%. A one-point rise in distinctiveness was associated with about $12,900 higher average car price and $2.59 higher price per 12-pack of beer, but with about 144,000 fewer cars and 8 million fewer barrels sold a year. Two categories only. Use: distinctiveness tends to buy price at the cost of volume; set the goal before briefing creative.
facts.source_title: A Better Way to Map Brand Strategy (HBR)

facts.statement: Hollis (HBR.org, 25 Oct 2013; Nigel Hollis of Millward Brown): cites Millward Brown research that brands with a meaningful difference command a price premium 13% higher than weaker category alternatives. The article gives no sample, method or category list. Use: treat 13% as a rough indication of the value of distinctiveness, not a forecast; test price headroom with your own buyers.
facts.source_title: Marketing's Mission: Make it Meaningfully Different (HBR.org)

facts.statement: Martin, Schwarz and Turner (HBR, Jan-Feb 2024, 'The Right Way to Build Your Brand'): the best ad campaigns make a memorable, valuable and deliverable promise to customers. The visible summary gives no sample or numbers. Use: before approving a campaign, check its single promise against those three tests and cut anything that fails one.
facts.source_title: The Right Way to Build Your Brand (HBR)

facts.statement: Kronthal-Sacco and Whelan (HBR, 24 Oct 2025) cite Edelman's 2025 Brand Trust report: 64% of respondents buy, choose or avoid brands based on their beliefs about what is going on in society, and about half assume the worst when brands stay silent on issues. Sample size is not stated on the page; consumer opinion data. Use: take a social stance only where it fits the brand's role, and keep messages consistent.
facts.source_title: What Consumers Really Want Brands to Do About Social Issues (HBR)

facts.statement: Rodriguez-Vila and Bharadwaj (HBR, Sep-Oct 2017, 'Competing on Social Purpose'): consumers increasingly expect brands to offer a social purpose beyond function, and brands use it to steer communications, product innovation and investment in causes. The authors warn that missteps are common and costly; examples include Airbnb, Tecate and Vicks India. The page gives no numbers. Use: tie any purpose claim to a concrete product or investment action, and pre-test the risk of backlash.
facts.source_title: Competing on Social Purpose (HBR)

facts.statement: Cornfield (HBR.org, 20 May 2021, Accenture Interactive) separates three levels of purpose: company (its role in the world), brand (its role in customers' lives) and customer (the needs and outcomes that bring buyers to the company). He reports that Bank of the West, after it stopped funding industries such as fracking, coal and tobacco in 2018, saw 37% new customer growth over eight months, per its CMO (company-reported, no sample). Use: write the customer-purpose statement first and design experiences around it.
facts.source_title: Recognizing Your Customer's Purpose is Key to Growth (HBR)

facts.statement: Magids, Zorfas and Leemon (HBR, Nov 2015, 'The New Science of Customer Emotions'): the authors (Motista, a consulting vendor, and CEB) report that targeting emotionally connected segments lifted a Millennial credit card's usage by 70% and new accounts by 40%, turned a cleaner brand's share losses into double-digit growth, and more than tripled an apparel retailer's same-store sales growth. Cases are the authors' own, unaudited; sample not stated. Use: map emotional motivators to segments and test one before a full rollout.
facts.source_title: The New Science of Customer Emotions (HBR)

facts.statement: Edelman (HBR, Dec 2010, 'Branding in the Digital Age'): online media have changed how consumers engage with brands, which alters the economics of marketing and makes many traditional marketing strategies and structures obsolete. The page shows only the summary; the consumer-decision-journey model and budget advice come from secondary descriptions. Use: allocate budget by journey stage, not by media type, and measure the touchpoints that influence choice.
facts.source_title: Branding in the Digital Age: You're Spending Your Money in All the Wrong Places (HBR)

facts.statement: Rawson, Duncan and Jones, McKinsey partners (HBR, Sep 2013, 'The Truth About Customer Experience'): measuring satisfaction at individual touchpoints can give a falsely rosy picture of how customers feel about the company; the authors say to manage the end-to-end journey instead. The page gives no sample or figures. Use: add a journey-level score (for example intent to renew or recommend) beside every touchpoint score.
facts.source_title: The Truth About Customer Experience (HBR)

facts.statement: Dawar (HBR, May-Jun 2018, 'Marketing in the Age of Alexa'): predicts AI assistants will soon be people's main route to information, products and services, which will change how companies attract and keep customers. The page summary is cut off and gives no data. Use: plan for being chosen by an agent, with clean product data, reviews and structured facts, not just persuasion of a human reader.
facts.source_title: Marketing in the Age of Alexa (HBR)

facts.statement: Duffek, Eisingerich and Merlo (HBR, 8 Dec 2025) cite influencer marketing as a $24 billion industry, with 88% of consumers saying authenticity matters, nearly half believing most influencers are fake, and over a third thinking influencers misrepresent themselves and products. Figures come from other studies; sample and dates are not stated on the page. Consumer opinion data. Use: vet creators for fit and disclosure, and expect lower trust in large-reach, high-frequency promoters.
facts.source_title: How to Do Influencer Marketing That Customers Actually Trust (HBR)

facts.statement: Karp, Fu and Friis (HBR.org, 22 May 2024): content creators change how established firms innovate through three effects: they raise demand for niche, highly specialized products, accelerate product life cycles, and change what customers consider valuable by altering how people search for and use products. The page gives no sample or numbers (summary only). Use: treat creators as a source of demand signals for niche variants and plan faster offer refresh cycles.
facts.source_title: How Your Business Should Tap into the Creator Economy (HBR)

facts.statement: Zhang and Cheng (HBS Working Knowledge, 26 Oct 2022; 'Reputation Burning' working paper): across 850+ beauty and lifestyle YouTube influencers and 85,000+ videos over one year starting in 2019, about 7% of videos were sponsored, and each sponsored video cost the creator about 0.2% of subscribers within three days. A rough estimate puts the lost value at about $10,000 over an average six-year career. Audiences were less critical of lesser-known brands. Use: brief creators on fewer, better-fit sponsorships.
facts.source_title: How Paid Promos Take the Shine Off YouTube Stars (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Gerdeman, HBS Working Knowledge (18 Sep 2017), drawing on Deighton, Gupta, Avery and John and The CMO Survey 2017: social media rose from 3.5% of marketing budgets in 2009 to 10.5% in Feb 2017, and 43% of respondents could not show its business impact. Gupta's research found Facebook likes lead to nothing in terms of purchases. Respondent count not stated. Use: judge social by sales effect, not likes.
facts.source_title: 'Likes' Lead to Nothing and Other Hard-Learned Lessons of Social Media Marketing (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Luca and Dai (HBS Working Knowledge, 13 Feb 2017): in a Yelp field experiment, about 7,210 of 18,295 eligible restaurants were randomly given free ad packages from August to October 2015. Yelp page views rose 24.6%, map requests 18%, calls 13%, website clicks 9% and reviews 5%. All effects dropped to zero once the ads ended. Established brands gained less. Use: treat paid ads for small local businesses as rented demand, and measure lift with a holdout.
facts.source_title: Paid Search Ads Pay Off for Lesser-Known Restaurants (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Ascarza and Padilla (HBS Working Knowledge, 9 Dec 2019): using four years of first-purchase data on 13,000+ customers of an international beauty retailer in six markets, buyers who bought more items in their first basket or bought new releases tended to be repeat, high-value customers; discount and holiday buyers tended to be one-time. The retailer's email would have been 39.7% more effective if targeted this way. Single retailer. Use: score new customers on their first order and steer retention spend to the likely repeaters.
facts.source_title: Identify Great Customers from Their First Purchase (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: MacKay, Miller, Doepper and Stiebale (HBS Working Knowledge, 5 May 2022), Nielsen scanner and panel data on about 14.4 million products in 133 US categories: markups rose about 25% between 2006 and 2019 and consumers were about 30% less price-sensitive, with coupon redemptions falling from 2.6 billion (2006) to 1.3 billion (2019). Falling costs were the main driver. Packaged goods only. Use: test price increases before assuming demand is elastic, especially for favoured brands.
facts.source_title: Why Companies Raise Their Prices: Because They Can (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Ofek (HBS Working Knowledge, 7 May 2026, article by Kara Baskin): seniors' share of US consumer spending grew from 14% in 2005 to 22% in 2022; repurchase rates are 40% for ages 18-39, 65% for ages 60-74 and 70% for 75 and over; older people are seven times more likely than younger people to be portrayed negatively in ads. A 2023 BCG study puts the spending of 870 million people aged 50-70 at about $7 trillion a year. Use: stop defaulting to youth targeting; test older-adult segments for loyalty-led growth.
facts.source_title: What Brands Get Wrong About the Over-65 Market (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: De Freitas and Ofek (HBS case 525-021, Oct 2024, rev. Feb 2025; Working Knowledge 24 Jul 2025) review brand AI experiments. Google (Gemini images), Levi's (AI models), Lego (AI images) and Intuit (TurboTax assistant) faced backlash when AI clashed with the brand promise or only cut cost. Orange, Nike and Ikea did better by tying AI to a brand-relevant purpose. The case lists 13 failures; no statistical sample. Use: before any AI-made brand asset, check it against the core brand promise and keep a human in the loop.
facts.source_title: What Google, Lego, and Other Brands Know About the Promise and Peril of AI (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Lakkaraju and Kumar (HBS Working Knowledge, 27 Jun 2024, article by Ben Rand): in a fictitious set of 10 coffee machines queried about 200 times, adding a machine-generated 'strategic text string' to the product pages of 2 products made them rank higher in about 40% of experiments, sometimes first, with no change in about 60%. Small lab test, not real shoppers. The researchers warn of unfair competition. Use: expect LLM answers to be gameable; invest in clear, accurate product facts and monitor rivals.
facts.source_title: Gen AI Marketing: How Some 'Gibberish' Code Can Give Products an Edge (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Brand, Israeli and Ngwe (HBS Working Knowledge, 30 May 2023): GPT-3 prompted as simulated shoppers gave price and brand-switching answers consistent with economic theory (higher income, higher price tolerance; Colgate's price rise shifted buyers to Crest). Its value of fluoride was $3.40 against $3.27 in a human study. Wine and yogurt answers deviated from theory. Studies usually cost over $20,000 and take 3-6 months versus under 15 minutes. Use: use synthetic respondents only to pre-screen ideas; confirm with real buyers.
facts.source_title: Can AI Predict Whether Shoppers Would Pick Crest or Colgate? (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Zhang and Narayandas (HBS Working Knowledge, 27 May 2025; forthcoming Management Science): in a randomized field test with 138 support agents and 256,934 chats at a meal-delivery firm (Dec 2020-Nov 2021), AI reply suggestions cut response time 22% and raised customer sentiment 0.45 points on a 5-point scale. Less experienced agents gained most (time down 70%, sentiment up 1.63). Gains were smaller on repeat complaints. One company. Use: give AI suggestions to newer service staff first, and keep humans on hard repeat cases.
facts.source_title: When AI Chatbots Help People Act More Human (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'The growth triple play: Creativity, analytics, and purpose' (2021; survey of more than 860 executives worldwide): only about 7 percent of companies combine creativity, analytics and purpose. Those that use all three grew about 2.3 times faster on average than companies using none of the three, and about 2.7 times faster in the pandemic period. The link is correlational, not proof of cause. Use: score a growth plan on all three at once instead of funding one.
facts.source_title: The growth triple play: Creativity, analytics, and purpose (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey growth triple play (2021; 860+ executives; growth data for 2018-19): companies using all three of creativity, analytics and purpose averaged annual growth above 12 percent. Figures for companies with only one or two of the three could not be confirmed here. Correlational. Use: report which of the three a campaign or team is still missing.
facts.source_title: The growth triple play: Creativity, analytics, and purpose (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'Next best experience: How AI can power every customer interaction' (2025): a capability that gives each customer the right interaction at the right time and place, built on data analytics, machine-learning predictive models, recommendation engines and gen AI content. McKinsey's own estimate is satisfaction up 15 to 20 percent, revenue up 5 to 8 percent and cost to serve down 20 to 30 percent; no sample or method was confirmed. Use: design lifecycle programmes as decision engines, not campaign calendars.
facts.source_title: Next best experience: How AI can power every customer interaction (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'Reinventing marketing workflows with agentic AI' (around June 2026): says agentic AI may eventually power some 60 percent of tasks across the marketing process, and cites 10 to 30 percent revenue growth from hyperpersonalized marketing for organisations that rebuild workflows around agents. These are McKinsey projections, not measured results. Use: redesign whole workflows around agents with a human owner for brand and strategy.
facts.source_title: Reinventing marketing workflows with agentic AI (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'From anxiety to advantage: A marketing organization that thrives with AI' (June 2026; survey of more than 500 marketers plus senior-leader interviews, opinion data): coverage reports fewer than 10 percent of companies see real business value from AI in marketing. Use: measure AI by finished workflows and outcomes, not by tool usage.
facts.source_title: From anxiety to advantage: A marketing organization that thrives with AI (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'From anxiety to advantage' (June 2026; survey of more than 500 marketers, opinion data): about 86 percent of marketers are excited about AI while 57 percent feel anxious about its implications. Use: pair every AI rollout with a clear statement of what it frees people to do.
facts.source_title: From anxiety to advantage: A marketing organization that thrives with AI (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'Unlocking profitable B2B growth through gen AI' (2024): in a B2B Pulse survey, 19 percent of respondents were already implementing gen AI for B2B buying and selling. In one client case, an industrial materials distributor that used gen AI to personalise outreach reported over $1 billion of new opportunities and a 10 percent pipeline increase. Single client case, not a benchmark. Use: start with account prioritisation and outreach, and test against a control.
facts.source_title: Unlocking profitable B2B growth through gen AI (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'AI-powered marketing and sales reach new heights with generative AI' (May 2023): McKinsey states that firms investing in AI see a revenue uplift of 3 to 15 percent and a sales ROI uplift of 10 to 20 percent. These are McKinsey's research claims with no sample or method confirmed, and pre-date most gen AI deployments. Use: set a modest uplift range as a hypothesis and verify it with a controlled test.
facts.source_title: AI-powered marketing and sales reach new heights with generative AI (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'A better way to build a brand: The community flywheel' (2022): brands that get the flywheel spinning show more than 75 percent of their brand content coming from users, and secondary reports cite an online conversion rate above 4 percent. McKinsey credits Gymshark and Drunk Elephant with pioneering the approach and describes Traeger's community of over a million people. Use: start with one agile team working from community ideas.
facts.source_title: A better way to build a brand: The community flywheel (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey 'Courageous growth: Six strategies for continuous growth outperformance' (October 2023; study of more than 4,000 global companies): on average about 80 percent of reported growth comes from companies' core businesses, and the strategies include expanding into adjacent businesses only where the firm has a right to win. Use: fund core productivity first and screen new bets for right to win.
facts.source_title: Courageous growth: Six strategies for continuous growth outperformance (McKinsey)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence survey, January 2025 (n=1,263 senior commercial executives, opinion data): 54% beat their 2024 revenue growth targets, 14% met them and about a third missed. Winners (2024 revenue growth above the upper quartile for their sector and region, plus positive gross margin growth) grew about twice the average rate of their industries. Use: benchmark growth plans against the winner profile, not the industry average.
facts.source_title: The B2B Growth Divide: What Sets Winners Apart (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence survey, January 2025 (n=1,263 executives, opinion data): 82% of companies say they run sales plays but only 21% realize their full value. Firms running a genuine Sales Play System grew 2.2 times faster than the average of firms without one. Use: define each play with target, message, offer, owner and KPI, and load it into the CRM.
facts.source_title: The B2B Growth Divide: What Sets Winners Apart (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence survey, January 2025 (n=1,263 executives, opinion data): over 90% have scaled at least one AI use case, and 57% of those that scaled say AI exceeded expectations. Winners run 4.5 use cases on average versus 3.3 for laggards. Roughly a quarter of sales and marketing AI pilots failed, and 35% of laggards that completed rep-automation pilots stopped pursuing them. Use: scale breadth of use cases and kill pilots with no owner.
facts.source_title: Parsing How Winners Use AI (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence survey, January 2025 (n=1,263, opinion data): slightly over half of commercial organizations lack adequate data and technology foundations for AI; incomplete or low-quality data is the top challenge. Firms following four or more AI best practices report about 12% cost efficiency versus 5% for firms following none. Wholesale banking: 72% expect gen AI to reshape business but only 24% feel equipped. Tech firms that reimagine selling can see 30% or better win-rate gains. Use: fix data hygiene before adding tools.
facts.source_title: Parsing How Winners Use AI (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Longitudinal Survey, January 2026 (n=1,125 leaders, 18 industries, opinion data): 87% say markets change faster than before and 91% are confident of hitting 2026 targets, yet last year 86% were confident and only 58% made it. Share missing revenue targets rose from 33% in 2023 to 42% in 2025. Pricing pressure ranks as the top concern. Winners grew 1.6 times faster than average in 2025. Use: discount executive confidence in plans and stress-test targets.
facts.source_title: Volatility Isn't the Storm. It's the Climate (Bain B2B Growth Agenda 2026)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Longitudinal Survey, January 2026 (n=1,125, opinion data): companies with a clear, consistently understood value proposition grew about 1.6 times faster than average (19% versus 12% revenue growth in 2025), yet only 4% rate their proposition strong. 49% say the root problem is the core product, not messaging. 40% of winners track proposition relevance versus 26% of laggards. Use: audit differentiation before rewriting copy, and review the proposition on a schedule.
facts.source_title: Unclear Value Propositions Stall Growth (Bain B2B Growth Agenda 2026)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Longitudinal Survey, January 2026 (n=1,125, opinion data): revenue growth rises with the number of programmatic sales-play practices, from about 1.2 times average with one to 1.9 times with four or more. Laggards see price negotiation as the decisive moment in winning customers, while winners focus earlier on experience and digital support. Nearly one in five laggards has no formal account prioritization model. Use: shift effort upstream of the price conversation and prioritize accounts with data.
facts.source_title: B2B Growth Masters' Formula for Repeatably Capturing New Customers (Bain, 2026)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Longitudinal Survey, January 2026 (n=1,125, opinion data): brand perception was the touchpoint most often named as influencing whether customers are won, kept or expanded, ranking ahead of price, fulfillment and rep responsiveness. Data-supported account models (firmographic or spend-based) are used by 94% of winners and 81% of laggards; only 6% of winners rely on relationship-led prioritization. Use: treat brand as a commercial lever and score accounts on data, not rep opinion.
facts.source_title: B2B Growth Masters' Formula for Repeatably Capturing New Customers (Bain, 2026)

facts.statement: Bain, The New Sales Productivity Equation (January 2026 survey, n=1,125 executives, opinion data): tech sales hiring grew 18% over 2017-2022 and now runs under 1% a year as spend shifts to automation and AI. 60% of winners say frontline managers focus on oversight and performance versus 42% of laggards; about two-thirds of winners use templated coaching versus roughly 55% of laggards. Bain cites its own experience that coaching can lift revenue 20%. Use: invest in manager coaching before adding headcount.
facts.source_title: The New Sales Productivity Equation (Bain B2B Growth Agenda 2026)

facts.statement: Bain, The New Sales Productivity Equation (2026): 49% of surveyed leaders say enablement centers on new hires while only 29% emphasize tenured sellers. A global tech company that retrained over 200 sales managers raised weekly or biweekly pipeline reviews from 56% to 75% and quarterly development talks with sellers from 30% to 50%. Single case, results self-reported by Bain. Use: extend enablement to experienced reps and measure manager cadence as a KPI.
facts.source_title: The New Sales Productivity Equation (Bain B2B Growth Agenda 2026)

facts.statement: Bain, AI Won't Transform Your Go-to-Market Until You Transform the Work (March 30, 2026; January 2026 survey of 1,125 sales and marketing leaders, opinion data): over 90% experiment with AI but few see meaningful productivity gains. Winners report about twice the AI-attributed revenue growth and 1.8x the cost efficiency of laggards. About 60% say data or technology is not ready; laggards more often report shared or undefined ownership. Use: assign one accountable owner and a cross-functional team before launching AI in go-to-market.
facts.source_title: AI Won't Transform Your Go-to-Market Until You Transform the Work (Bain, 2026)

facts.statement: Bain 2026 B2B Growth Agenda, AI go-to-market piece (survey of 1,125 leaders; use-case figures are Bain-reported gains, not a controlled average): targeting AI delivered about 50% more high-quality leads; marketing content about 40% more top-of-funnel leads with 40-70% less human time; AI pricing tools 4-8% revenue growth; RFP response generation automated about 50% of tasks. Use: prioritize use cases by these ranges, then verify with own incrementality tests.
facts.source_title: AI Won't Transform Your Go-to-Market Until You Transform the Work (Bain, 2026)

facts.statement: Bain, The Rise of the Super Seller (undated marketing page; survey of more than 1,100 sales and marketing leaders): a building-materials manufacturer that scaled an AI quoting tool cut quote turnaround days 90% and raised win rates 10 points, and the page names 20+ AI-assisted workflows per seller per week as the threshold for genuine daily use. Self-reported by Bain. Use: set a usage threshold per seller and prove a tool on one workflow first.
facts.source_title: The Rise of the Super Seller (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Where Have All the Sales Reps Gone? (January 14, 2026; headcount data for 20 software and tech companies plus US labor statistics): sales rep hiring slowed from steady growth through 2022 to about 2% or less, and inside sales shrank 3-7% a year in 2023-2025. Bain expects AI to let each rep cover roughly 1.2-1.7 times the book of business, and urges treating hiring as a lagging indicator. Use: plan capacity around AI-leveraged coverage rather than headcount ratios.
facts.source_title: Where Have All the Sales Reps Gone? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, AI in sales (Technology Report 2025, September 23, 2025; no survey sample stated): Bain advises starting with one or two high-impact front-of-funnel use cases such as prospecting and lead generation, expects more capable agentic sales tools within 6 to 18 months, and warns that layering AI on existing workflows yields only micro-productivity gains. Successful programs have sustained C-level sponsorship and a dedicated implementation team with targets. Use: redesign the selling journey first, then automate it.
facts.source_title: AI Is Transforming Productivity, but Sales Remains a New Frontier (Bain Technology Report 2025)

facts.statement: Bain, State of the Art of Agentic AI Transformation (Technology Report 2025, September 23, 2025): four levels of AI in the enterprise: information retrieval copilots, single-task agents, cross-system workflow orchestration, and multi-agent constellations (still largely theoretical). Tech-forward firms that scaled levels 1-2 in 2023-2024 gained 10-25% EBITDA per Bain. Leaders set top-down goals, assign general managers, redesign whole workflows and clean data. Use: place each marketing or sales agent on the ladder and move one level at a time.
facts.source_title: State of the Art of Agentic AI Transformation (Bain Technology Report 2025)

facts.statement: Bain, Will Agentic AI Disrupt SaaS? (September 23, 2025): a two-axis scenario grid scoring how far AI can automate user tasks and how deeply it penetrates a SaaS workflow, giving four outcomes: core strongholds (AI enhances SaaS), open doors (spend compresses), gold mines (AI outshines SaaS) and battlegrounds (AI cannibalizes SaaS). It argues seat pricing fits poorly when AI does the work, and urges experiments with charging for results. Use: classify a product or competitor on the grid before setting pricing and packaging.
facts.source_title: Will Agentic AI Disrupt SaaS? (Bain Technology Report 2025)

facts.statement: Bain, agentic AI SaaS opportunity (May 2026; Bain estimates, not survey data): the US opportunity is about $100 billion, vendors capture roughly $4-6 billion, and sales is the largest function at about $20 billion. Share of workflow tasks agents could automate: customer support and R&D 40-60%, finance and HR 35-45%, sales and IT 30-40%, legal 20-30%. Pricing is moving from per-seat toward outcome and usage models. Use: size the agent opportunity in sales as a task share, not total replacement.
facts.source_title: The $100-Billion SaaS Opportunity Hiding in Cross-System Labor (Bain Technology Report 2026)

facts.statement: Bain Generative AI Survey, Q3 2025 (n=197 executives; earlier waves about 184-199; opinion data): 74% rank AI in their top three priorities versus 60% a year earlier. About 80% of use cases met or exceeded expectations, yet only about 23% of respondents tie AI to higher revenue or lower cost. Sales, marketing and knowledge work are in a second tier where roughly one-fifth to one-third of use cases are scaling; agentic workflow users were twice as likely to exceed goals. Use: tie each AI use case to a revenue or cost metric.
facts.source_title: Executive Survey: AI Moves from Pilots to Production (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Per-Seat Software Pricing Isn't Dead (October 9, 2025; analysis of 30+ SaaS vendors adding gen AI, AI-natives excluded): about 35% raised per-seat prices and bundled AI into tiers, about 65% added an AI meter on top of seats, and none had moved fully to usage or outcome pricing. Example of transition friction: a $40,000 AI agent replacing an $80,000 rep means the buyer pays both during evaluation, a 50% jump. Use: offer delayed payment or performance guarantees when selling a replacement-priced product.
facts.source_title: Per-Seat Software Pricing Isn't Dead, but New Models Are Gaining Steam (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, AI Pricing: A Reality Check (August 10, 2026; public list prices of about 200 B2B SaaS firms captured June 2026): among AI meters, roughly 55% are output-based, 35% effort-based and 10% outcome-based. About four in five AI pricing models are capacity models with fixed allotments that do not roll over. Outcome pricing works mainly in customer support, where results are observable and contractible; one in five AI-natives still leans on seats. Use: choose the meter by how measurable the result is.
facts.source_title: AI Pricing: A Reality Check on Effort, Usage, and Outcomes (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, AI-Enhanced Pricing Can Boost Revenue Growth (September 24, 2024; survey of more than 1,000 commercial executives): top-quartile revenue growers use several gen AI use cases in sales and marketing about twice as often as bottom-quartile firms. Firms with data-driven pricing guidance win deals at a rate 12 points higher, and their reps are almost twice as likely to be confident of realizing price increases. Case potentials only: a theme park operator could add 4-8% revenue and an energy company could cut contract churn 5-10%. Not measured results.
facts.source_title: AI-Enhanced Pricing Can Boost Revenue Growth (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Harnessing Pricing Power (Global Private Equity Report 2020, February 24, 2020; Bain survey of 1,700+ B2B leaders): about 85% of management teams think pricing can improve, yet only about 15% have effective pricing tools and dashboards and about 13% have effective frontline incentives. Bain says building pricing capability can add roughly 200-600 basis points to profit. A training provider case suggested 5-20% price rises lifting first-year EBITDA 7-12%. Use: audit tools and incentives, the two thinnest capabilities, first.
facts.source_title: Harnessing Pricing Power to Create Lasting Value (Bain Global Private Equity Report 2020)

facts.statement: Bain, Is Pricing Killing Your Profits? (Kermisch and Burns, June 13, 2018; survey of 1,700+ companies self-rating 42 pricing capabilities): dedicated pricing software is associated with 2.5 times stronger pricing outcomes, yet only 26% use it. Bain cases: a North American manufacturer raised prices about 4% and lifted EBITDA 7 points; an industrial goods maker that rebalanced rep incentives raised prices 7%, adding 95 bps to a 350 bp margin gain; a specialty chemicals producer raised EBIT 35% within two years. Use: pay reps on realized price.
facts.source_title: Is Pricing Killing Your Profits? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Secret to B2B Pricing in a Digital World (Burns and Murphy, August 1, 2018; Bain executive pricing survey, sample not stated): about half of companies use some dynamic pricing, and firms with sound pricing decisions have better tools and data, though executives agreed tools cannot replace skills and a strong sales team. One enterprise tech firm that gave reps real-time guidance cut discounts 300-400 basis points in six months. Use: pair price guidance with rep coaching.
facts.source_title: The Secret to B2B Pricing in a Digital World (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, How the Best B2B Sales Groups Motivate Smart Pricing (Justin Murphy, July 23, 2018; global survey of 1,700 B2B companies): nearly 70% of leaders in share growth and pricing outcomes excel on two dimensions of discipline. They run a structured escalation path for nonstandard deals including a plan for quarter-end surges, tie rep pay to realized price, and give reps deal-specific price recommendations from customer size, industry, purchase history and competitors. Use: build an approval path and price-based comp into the deal desk.
facts.source_title: How the Best B2B Sales Groups Motivate Smart Pricing Behavior (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Clearing the Roadblocks to Better B2B Pricing (December 10, 2014; analysis of dozens of B2B firms plus a survey of 400+ purchasing executives): a 1% gain in realized price raises operating profit about 8%, roughly double the effect of a 1% gain in share, variable cost or fixed-cost utilization. Even in raw materials, buyers would pay about 4.2% more for quality and 3.1% for dependable delivery, and 88% would pay at least 2.5% more to avoid switching suppliers. Use: lead price tests with reliability and switching-cost value.
facts.source_title: Clearing the Roadblocks to Better B2B Pricing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Clearing the Roadblocks to Better B2B Pricing (December 2014): splits pricing into price setting (target price waterfall from list to net to final) and price getting (enforcing targets deal by deal). It rebuts five limiting beliefs: products are commodities, disruptive models cannot be answered, negotiations cannot be constrained, legacy channel discounts are required, list prices do not matter. One executive should own company-wide pricing. Use: structure pricing reviews as setting versus getting and assign a single owner.
facts.source_title: Clearing the Roadblocks to Better B2B Pricing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, How B2B Firms Can Price with Confidence as Inflation Rises (July 7, 2021, from HBR.org; Bain survey of 400+ industrial companies): midsize firms under $5 billion in revenue were less confident than large firms about using pricing to handle inflation, responding to market change and equipping frontline staff to decide prices. Most business leaders see inflation-driven increases as fair, but customers give little credit for increases pushed through months late. Use: communicate cost-driven increases early and equip reps with a script.
facts.source_title: How B2B Firms Can Price with Confidence as Inflation Rises (Bain, via HBR.org)

facts.statement: Bain, The Pricing Is Right (September 24, 2019; survey of nearly 1,100 consumer companies on 40 pricing capabilities): 78% say pricing could improve; about 15% are top performers (strong pricing plus market share growth). Winners lead on five capabilities: value-linked pricing, product mix, promotion discipline, price perception and dynamic pricing. Bain estimates at least 20% of promotional spend adds little incremental sales or hurts profit. Use: audit promotions for the dead 20% before adding discounts.
facts.source_title: The Pricing Is Right: Lessons from Top-Performing Consumer Companies (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Perception Beats Reality in Pricing (December 14, 2016; Bain and ROI Consultancy survey of almost 2,200 consumers in Atlanta and Washington DC covering eight grocery chains): shoppers often credit retailers with more or less price competitiveness than shelf prices justify. Indirect tactics such as signage and private label can shape price image as well as or better than list cuts. A European apparel retailer's across-the-board cuts missed the expected gains until it clarified price communications and reduced price points. Use: test price-image signals before cutting price.
facts.source_title: Perception Beats Reality in Pricing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Why Software Companies' Customer Success Is Failing (Technology Report 2024, September 25, 2024; Bain software and buyer surveys, sample not stated): net revenue retention fell at 75% of software companies even though nearly 60% raised customer success spend. Nearly two-thirds of customers say post-sale needs are only moderately met or worse. Buyers rank technical implementation help first; vendors rank it sixth, and buyers prefer a technical primary contact. Use: staff onboarding with technical help before adding relationship managers.
facts.source_title: Why Software Companies' Customer Success Is Failing (Bain Technology Report 2024)

facts.statement: Bain Customer Success Practitioner Survey, August 2025 (n=235; Bain article December 17, 2025; opinion data): net revenue retention keeps slipping despite more customer success hiring. About seven in ten leaders have not meaningfully adopted AI, and CSMs spend roughly 65% of their time on tasks AI could automate. Bain advises redesigning two or three related processes from scratch, not bolting AI onto old steps, and retiring legacy tools. Use: automate low-value CSM work to free time for expansion conversations.
facts.source_title: Customer Success at a Crossroads: Evolve with AI or Fade Away (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Radical Thought: Infuse Account Planning with the Customer's Perspective (July 11, 2022): only about 22% of B2B companies consistently measure and act on customer experience. A tech firm's promoters renewed about 10 points more than detractors. Bain groups accounts into four sets: underserved advocates, accounts at risk, selective fixes and big fans, instead of ranking by size or share of wallet alone. Use: add NPS or sentiment to account scoring and route advocates to referral asks.
facts.source_title: Radical Thought: Infuse Account Planning with the Customer's Perspective (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Is That Customer Worth Your Time? (Burns and Schottland, June 13, 2018; survey of 870 B2B executives): fewer than 20% have a quantified view of total market opportunity and untapped customer potential, and fewer than a quarter run an account process that flags actions like cross-sell. Firms doing these well gain more than twice the market share. At a distributor, rep time correlated with share of wallet, so it raised target-account conversations two to three times. Use: allocate coverage by growth potential.
facts.source_title: Is That Customer Worth Your Time? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Next-Generation Key Account Management (September 25, 2019; consumer-goods client experience, no survey sample): large accounts can be 40-80% of a branded supplier's revenue in some developed markets, and European buying alliances were projected to reach nearly 70% of grocery revenue by 2025. Leaders model the customer's economics as carefully as their own, tailor plans to each account's strategy and run cross-functional agile teams. Use: build joint account plans around the customer's profit pool.
facts.source_title: Next-Generation Key Account Management (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Take Your Indirect Channel to Full Potential (undated page; Bain consulting experience, no sample): almost half of industrial companies rely on indirect channels. Three common blockers: unclear channel roles, thin partner support such as weak screening and account planning, and an operating model that undervalues channels. Bain advises mapping profit pools by segment, reviewing partners regularly on performance versus targets, all-in cost to serve and customer experience, and building trust through transparency. Use: define partner tiers and account-ownership rules.
facts.source_title: Take Your Indirect Channel to Full Potential (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Do Your B2B Customers Promote Your Business? (February 12, 2014; survey of 290 B2B executives in 11 countries plus cases): B2B promoters (9-10) have a lifetime value 3 to 12 times that of detractors (0-6), loyalty leaders grow 4-8 points faster than their market, and 68% of executives said customers were less loyal than before. Intuit's new-client service program made accountants 49% more likely to renew. Use: track relationship NPS across buyers and users, and fund programs that move it.
facts.source_title: Do Your B2B Customers Promote Your Business? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Bought Not Sold (press release October 8, 2015; survey of nearly 400 marketing and sales executives at tech and industrial firms, opinion data): nearly 90% feel unprepared for digitally savvy B2B buyers; only 12% feel well prepared. Websites often fail to show how products solve problems and portfolios are too large for reps to explain. Leaders build relevant content, an integrated view of customer behavior and tailored experiences across the buying process. Use: lead with problem-solution content and simplify the portfolio story.
facts.source_title: Bought Not Sold: executives feel ill-prepared for digitally savvy buyers (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain, Mastering the New Reality of Sales (April 9, 2014; survey of 550 US B2B sales executives, opinion data): about 60% say offers are not consistently matched to target segments, only about 40% say reps clearly understand what sets the firm apart, only 35% report strong marketing-sales alignment, and about three-quarters made major tech investments but under a third saw clear gains. Use: fix segment-offer fit and rep differentiation messaging before buying more sales technology.
facts.source_title: Mastering the New Reality of Sales (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, The Sales Playbook of Successful B2B Teams (HBR.org, August 25, 2021; Bain survey of 167 companies, industries not stated): about 62% said returns on sales technology fell short of expectations, and many use CRM only for basic workflow. A global tech firm used data-driven sales plays, tracked which worked, scaled winners, retired weak ones and held weekly cross-functional playbook meetings, then beat its post-merger growth expectations. Use: review plays weekly and retire those without pipeline.
facts.source_title: The Sales Playbook of Successful B2B Teams (Bain, via HBR.org)

facts.statement: Bain, It's 10 AM, Do You Know What Your Sales Reps Are Doing? (HBR.org, March 10, 2017; calendar and email metadata analysis at three B2B firms, no overall sample): at a supplies firm reps spent under a fifth of time with customers, and moving to inside sales at about 55% of the cost saved roughly $40 million a year. Top performers spent about four more hours weekly with customers, were about 50% more likely to hold weekly pipeline reviews and about 25% more likely to cross-sell. Use: measure real time use and coach in weekly reviews.
facts.source_title: It's 10 AM. Do You Know What Your Sales Reps Are Doing? (Bain, via HBR.org)

facts.statement: Bain, The Ingredients of Strong Revenue Growth in B2B Software (April 8, 2024; Bain and Google survey of about 1,100 sales and marketing executives at US software and cloud firms, opinion data): revenue leaders put about 50% more budget and 80% more staff hours into digital marketing experiments than laggards. Firms using AI across use cases report a 16% average lift in conversion; high-growth firms are 2-3 times likelier to track intent and account engagement. Use: fund an experiment budget and add intent signals to the measurement stack.
facts.source_title: The Ingredients of Strong Revenue Growth in B2B Software (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Virtual Selling Has Become Simply Selling (April 2, 2021; Bain and Dynata global survey, sample not stated): 92% of B2B buyers prefer virtual sales interactions, up 17 points from May 2020, and 79% of sellers rate virtual selling effective versus 54% then. About 80% of buyers set specifications before contacting a rep and about 35% already prefer a vendor. A renewal-focused prescriptive play lifted renewals 10-20% at one firm. Use: win buyers before rep contact and keep digital self-serve paths.
facts.source_title: Virtual Selling Has Become Simply Selling (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, The One-Two Punch: Virtual Selling and Sales Playbooks (Technology Report 2020, October 2020): reps at sustainably growing firms were 50% more likely to have consistent weekly meetings with their managers, focused on deal strategy and coaching. In one survey, 55% said reps would be demoralized or might quit if forced into a mostly virtual model, while 25% would be excited. Half of surveyed sales transactions already happened virtually. Use: pair channel shifts with manager coaching and rep change management.
facts.source_title: The One-Two Punch: Virtual Selling and Sales Playbooks (Bain Technology Report 2020)

facts.statement: Bain, How to Grab Tech Buyers at Hello (Technology Report 2021, September 20, 2021; Bain surveys with Dynata, Google and Salesforce, samples not stated): about 80% of buyers fix criteria and shortlist before talking to sales, most want to initiate contact on their timing, and winning B2B firms were 2.7 times likelier to excel across sales-play elements. About 60% of CRM deployments miss ROI expectations; winners run 11+ marketing and sales apps versus under 8 for laggards. Use: invest in digital presence at shortlist stage and integrate the stack.
facts.source_title: How to Grab Tech Buyers at Hello and Never Say Goodbye (Bain Technology Report 2021)

facts.statement: Bain, Your Next Customer Will Find You Using AI (April 7, 2026; Bain survey of 1,500 US consumers, September 2025; analysis of about 500 million citations; B2B part is qualitative with no sample): 44% of online buyers start mostly in an LLM or split search between AI tools and traditional engines, and 89% of unbranded prompts were answered from third-party sources. SMB buyers reportedly build vendor shortlists in LLMs, then validate on sites, reviews and YouTube. Use: earn third-party mentions and review coverage, not only own-site content.
facts.source_title: Your Next Customer Will Find You Using AI. Now What? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, How Digital Natives Are Changing B2B Purchasing (HBR.org, March 14, 2018, citing Merit, Google and Forrester studies): roughly three-quarters of 20-35-year-olds take part in company purchase decisions, over 70% of buyer searches start with a generic query not a brand, and younger buyers rank search, vendor sites and peers above salespeople. Digital natives prefer brief visual content. Secondary data cited by Bain. Use: build non-brand category content and short visual assets.
facts.source_title: How Digital Natives Are Changing B2B Purchasing (Bain, via HBR.org)

facts.statement: Bain with Twitter, B2B Marketers: All the Right Moves in All the Wrong Places (September 22, 2020; survey of 279 US tech buyers and 121 marketers): buyers trust peers, customers and industry sources about twice as much as advertisements, and marketers underrate junior colleagues' influence. Over 50% of buyers say manager-level staff shape purchases, near 80% for directors below VP. Winning marketers (revenue up 10%+, share up 3+ points over two years) understood buyers better. Use: seed peer communities and content for junior influencers.
facts.source_title: B2B Marketers: All the Right Moves in All the Wrong Places (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with Twitter, It Takes a Community to Buy a B2B Product (March 9, 2021; survey of 279 US buyers and 121 marketers): nearly 80% of junior IT staff significantly influence purchases and spend about 57% of their research time on community sources such as peers, reviews and forums. Marketers spend only about 16% of budget on community building; winning marketers spend about 1.4 times more than others. Use: raise community and review budget share toward the winner level and test impact.
facts.source_title: It Takes a Community to Buy a B2B Product (Bain)

facts.statement: Dixon and Adamson of the Corporate Executive Board opened a four-part HBR series on 30 Sep 2011 with 'Selling Is Not About Relationships'. It introduced the Challenger sales research, which argues that top sellers teach, tailor and take control of the conversation rather than lean on rapport alone. The HBR page shows only the byline and teaser; the sample size and the 40% and 7% shares of star reps come from secondary write-ups, conflict with other CEB figures, and are not used here. Use: coach scripts toward commercial insight and controlled conversations.
facts.source_title: Selling Is Not About Relationships (HBR, Dixon and Adamson)

facts.statement: Adamson, Dixon and Toman (HBR, July-August 2012) argue that classic solution selling, where reps uncover needs and then sell a bundled answer, is losing value because procurement teams and outside purchasing consultants armed with data can now define solutions themselves. Use: qualify the internal champion who can drive consensus, not just the friendliest contact.
facts.source_title: The End of Solution Sales (HBR)
