facts.statement: Kotler, Rackham and Krishnaswamy (HBR, July-August 2006) describe friction between sales and marketing: each blames the other for poor results, sales sees marketing as out of touch with customers, marketing sees sales as fixed on single accounts, and each undervalues the other. They urge moving from coexistence to working together to create value. Use: set shared definitions, handoffs and joint metrics between the two teams first.
facts.source_title: Ending the War Between Sales and Marketing (HBR)

facts.statement: Toman, Adamson and Gomez (HBR, March-April 2017) report that B2B buying has become harder for the buyer: unlimited information, a growing set of stakeholders and rising pressure leave buyers uncertain and stressed. Many sellers still assume the buyer is in control, informed and clear about needs. Their advice is to make buying easier, not to push more information. Use: build buyer-enablement content that reduces confusion and helps a group agree.
facts.source_title: The New B2B Sales Imperative (HBR)

facts.statement: Schmidt, Adamson and Bird of CEB (HBR, March 2015) found that sellers rarely meet a lone decision maker, even at a 50-person customer. Authority usually sits with a group whose members hold different roles and each can veto, which makes agreement slow for both sides. Use: map every role with veto power in an account and plan messages for each, rather than chasing one executive.
facts.source_title: Making the Consensus Sale (HBR)

facts.statement: HBR's March 2015 data visual from the CEB research reports an average of 5.4 people who must formally approve a B2B purchase, with the chance of closing falling sharply as the number of decision makers grows. Sample and industry mix are not stated on the page, and the figure dates from 2015. Use: treat a deal with many approvers as lower probability and plan multi-threaded engagement.
facts.source_title: Group Size Matters (HBR data visual)

facts.statement: Adamson, a Gartner executive, writes in HBR (Jan-Feb 2022) that B2B customers spend only about 17% of the purchase process in conversation with potential suppliers, and most of the rest on independent research. The page does not state the sample. Use: put decision-useful content where buyers research alone, because most of the journey happens without a seller present.
facts.source_title: Sensemaking for Sales (HBR)

facts.statement: The Sensemaking for Sales piece (Adamson, Gartner, HBR Jan-Feb 2022) draws on Gartner research that surveyed 1,100 B2B customers: those who report overwhelming amounts of information are 54% less likely to make a high-quality, low-regret purchase (premium price, large scope). The truncated HBR page itself did not show the figure; it comes from Gartner's own version of the article. Use: curate and compare information for buyers instead of adding volume.
facts.source_title: Sensemaking for Sales (HBR)

facts.statement: Dixon and McKenna (HBR, 24 June 2022) cite a study of more than 2.5 million recorded sales conversations and report that between 40% and 60% of deals are lost to customers who express intent to buy but never act. They argue indecision is a main source of lost deals. Use: add a no-decision risk check to forecasts and coach reps to reduce buyer uncertainty.
facts.source_title: Stop Losing Sales to Customer Indecision (HBR)

facts.statement: A Bain and Google survey of 1,208 people at US companies involved in buying products and services such as software, cloud hosting and industrial equipment is written up in HBR by Bain authors Sherrard, Dave and MacGregor (20 Sep 2022). One example shows a vendor pursuing a contract with a current customer that chose a firm already on the buyer's 'day one' list. Use: aim to be on buyers' early lists.
facts.source_title: What B2Bs Need to Know About Their Buyers (HBR, Bain authors)

facts.statement: Adamson, Dixon and Toman (HBR, 9 Jan 2014) argue that firms run sales as a separate world with its own training, recruiting, pay plan and systems, all built to reward individual performance, and that this separation can hold back results as much as it helps. The page shows only the opening argument. Use: test team-based incentives and shared account planning rather than assuming individual quotas are optimal.
facts.source_title: Why Individuals No Longer Rule on Sales Teams (HBR)

facts.statement: HBR's Jan-Feb 2015 piece on discounting describes a vicious circle common in B2B sales: the customer threatens to switch to a competitor unless it gets a discount, the seller cuts the price hoping to hold firm next time, and the earlier discount makes holding firm harder. Use: set discount approval rules and ask for a give-back for each concession.
facts.source_title: The Downside of Discounts (HBR)

facts.statement: Holden (HBR, 10 June 2016) notes that suppliers label their most valuable customers strategic accounts, and those customers often push hard for cost savings after putting suppliers through rigorous procurement. He cites a study finding that salespeople feel more anxiety about the pricing discussion than any other stage of the sales cycle. Use: train reps to trade concessions for value (volume, term, access).
facts.source_title: Negotiating with Clients You Can't Afford to Lose (HBR)

facts.statement: Astray (HBR, 6 May 2026) argues sales teams often weaken their own position with long-time clients through early concessions and fragmented account management, rather than because clients are difficult. Her anchor case is an industrial manufacturer that left a multimillion-dollar project unpaid for three years while the seller kept delivering. The excerpt shows no sample. Use: audit unrequited concessions and payment status before renewing or extending scope.
facts.source_title: How Sales Teams Undercut Themselves with Longtime Clients (HBR)

facts.statement: Bertini, von Schuckmann and Kronrod (HBR, 31 Mar 2022) observe that firms treat price as an obstacle to the sale and use tactics from subtle to deceptive to reduce the friction, some of which hide the true cost from buyers, which the authors treat as a problem. The excerpt gives no numbers. Use: communicate full price transparently and test price-framing changes against trust and repeat purchase.
facts.source_title: Talking to Your Customers About Prices (HBR)

facts.statement: Shipilov (INSEAD, HBR, 16 July 2014) opens by asking how a seller facing many customer types can estimate buyers' willingness to pay: a better estimate makes a sale more likely and leaves less money on the table for the customer. The page shows only the introduction. Use: in negotiated B2B deals, treat offers and counter-offers as signals of willingness to pay and test them against price bands.
facts.source_title: The Benefits of Bargaining with Your Customers (HBR)

facts.statement: Evangelidis (ESADE, HBR, 24 Sep 2026) lays out three responses to rising costs: absorb them, raise the list price, or cut what the customer receives for the same price. The third, which he labels skimpflation, carries the greatest long-term risk. The excerpt shows no study sample. Use: prefer an openly communicated price rise to a hidden quality or size cut when modelling inflation responses.
facts.source_title: When Raising Prices Is Better Than Cutting Quality (HBR)

facts.statement: Pricing consultant Mohammed (HBR, 15 Oct 2026) opens by noting US consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September 2026 (up from the prior three months) and argues that simply passing costs through can drive customers away and cut total profit, so he lists ten alternative pricing moves. The list is not in the excerpt. Use: treat blanket price rises as one option and test alternatives such as packaging changes.
facts.source_title: 10 Pricing Strategies to Deal with Persistent Inflation (HBR)

facts.statement: Wise and May (HBR, 25 Aug 2026), practitioners rather than researchers, say many B2B firms have a value gap: the value they create exceeds what customers can see, and fast growth can hide it until sales slow or competitors erode margin. They urge leaders to make closing the gap an explicit decision and to help buyers measure and defend value. No data or sample is given. Use: build value quantification into proposals and renewal reviews.
facts.source_title: Do Your B2B Customers See the Value You Deliver? (HBR)

facts.statement: Miller (HEC Paris) and Zhang (Wharton) wrote 'Should Your Subscription Business Use Auto-Renew?' (HBR, 15 May 2026), drawing on a field experiment with more than 1.4 million readers. HEC's account of the underlying experiment says auto-renew looked better in the first months (roughly 20% higher subscription rate over four months) but the gap reversed by about a year, and auto-cancel produced 23% more total paid subscribers over the period. Use: test renewal defaults per segment against click-to-cancel rules.
facts.source_title: Should Your Subscription Business Use Auto-Renew? (HBR)

facts.statement: McCarthy (Emory) and Fader (Wharton) wrote in HBR on 19 Dec 2017 that US consumer subscription services had over 11 million subscribers in 2017, that more than 2,000 consumer subscription businesses existed, and that the industry had grown about 200% annually since 2011 (the growth figure is taken from a Fast Company link). Method not stated. Use: check cohort retention before leaning on growth numbers when judging subscription health.
facts.source_title: Subscription Businesses Are Booming. Here's How to Value Them (HBR)

facts.statement: Zoltners, Sinha and Lorimer (HBR, 22 Jun 2018) describe an enterprise software firm that moved from one-time custom sales to monthly SaaS subscriptions: account management absorbed more rep time, new-customer acquisition slowed and revenue growth slowed with it. The excerpt gives no figures. Use: when moving to subscriptions, split hunter and renewal roles and re-set quotas and compensation accordingly.
facts.source_title: What Subscription Business Models Mean for Sales Teams (HBR)

facts.statement: Cespedes (HBS senior lecturer) and van der Kooij (Winning By Design) argue in HBR (18 Apr 2023) that SaaS was the fastest-growing business model for tech entrepreneurs and investors until the SaaS capital index peaked in 2021 and then crashed, and that traditional sales models built around customer acquisition and funnel metrics fall short in subscription businesses. Use: add retention-oriented metrics to the sales scorecard.
facts.source_title: The Rebirth of Software as a Service (HBR)

facts.statement: Eisenmann (HBS), Parker and Van Alstyne (HBR, October 2006) describe two-sided markets, or platforms, that link two distinct user groups, such as credit cards (consumers and merchants) or operating systems (users and developers). The summary says such networks often enjoy significantly greater returns at scale than traditional value chains. Use: for marketplaces, measure cross-side network effects before setting fees.
facts.source_title: Strategies for Two-Sided Markets (HBR)

facts.statement: Eisenmann, Parker and Van Alstyne, 'Platform Envelopment', Strategic Management Journal 32(12), 2011: a provider in one platform market enters an adjacent market by combining its functionality with the target's in a multi-platform bundle, using overlap in users. The authors suggest incumbents sheltered by network effects and switching costs can be vulnerable. Use: watch adjacent platforms bundling your category and plan counter-bundles.
facts.source_title: Platform Envelopment (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Van Alstyne, Parker and Choudary (HBR, April 2016) argue that Porter's five forces describes pipeline businesses and that platforms compete on scale and orchestration instead. As evidence they cite 2007, when five phone makers (Nokia, Samsung, Motorola, Sony Ericsson, LG) held about 90% of global industry profit just before the iPhone arrived. Use: when a competitor is a platform, judge it on network effects and partners, not product features.
facts.source_title: Pipelines, Platforms, and the New Rules of Strategy (HBR)

facts.statement: Van Alstyne, Parker and Choudary (HBR, 31 Mar 2016) note that platform businesses such as Alibaba, Airbnb and Uber are hard to build, that many platforms struggle or fail (Apple and Google included), and that half a dozen key reasons trace back to managers misunderstanding how platforms operate and compete. The six reasons are not on the free page. Use: set and test participation rules before scaling a marketplace or partner program.
facts.source_title: 6 Reasons Platforms Fail (HBR)

facts.statement: Manzoor, Ascarza and Netzer (arXiv 2511.01181, submitted 3 Nov 2025) built an AI agent that decides when to stop a sales call, tested on calls from a large European telecommunications firm. It cut time spent on failed calls by 54% while keeping nearly all sales, and reallocating the saved time raised expected sales by up to 37%. Working paper, not peer reviewed. Use: pilot AI call-stopping for outbound time allocation.
facts.source_title: Learning When to Quit in Sales Conversations (Manzoor, Ascarza, Netzer)

facts.statement: Kaza, Chung and four co-authors (HBR, 15 Sep 2025) describe agentic AI in sales as autonomous agents that act as replicas of a firm's top sellers: they work continuously alongside human reps, find and nurture prospects, complete deals across channels, anticipate next steps, adapt to market shifts, connect with company systems and learn over time. No quantified results shown. Use: scope agent roles by funnel stage and keep human handoff rules.
facts.source_title: How Successful Sales Teams Are Embracing Agentic AI (HBR)

facts.statement: Chung and four co-authors (HBR, 4 Sep 2026) argue that agentic AI is erasing the divide between marketing and sales, yet most companies still deploy it separately in each function, missing an opportunity. They suggest it could finally make marketing-sales alignment achievable. No data or cases in the visible text. Use: design marketing and sales agents around shared customer data and clear handoff ownership.
facts.source_title: AI Is Blurring the Line Between Sales and Marketing (HBR)

facts.statement: Sinha, Shastri and Lorimer of ZS (HBR, 3 Sep 2024) propose AI assistants as rep coaches: rehearse pitches before key meetings, get feedback on tone, word choice and pacing, favour collaborative language, book the next meeting before ending the current one, and use customer data to spot cross-sell. The excerpt reports no productivity numbers. Use: pair a coaching tool with call-review checklists and measure win-rate change.
facts.source_title: Can AI Assistants Add Value to Your Sales Team? (HBR)

facts.statement: Harvard Law School's Program on Negotiation (Katie Shonk, 20 Jul 2020) defines BATNA as your best alternative to a negotiated agreement and calls it often your strongest source of power. It advises looking at the other side's BATNA too: if yours looks weak, consider what they would do without a deal; if both are weak, you may have room to push for better terms. Use: before quoting, state your BATNA and estimate the buyer's.
facts.source_title: BATNA in Negotiation: A Key Source of Power (PON, Harvard Law School)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Economics of Loyalty' (Markey and Reichheld, March 23, 2012): in its retail-banking profit model for affluent customers, a promoter is worth roughly $9,500 more to a bank than a detractor, and detractors have negative lifetime value. Promoters give their primary bank almost 45% more of their household deposit balances, buy about 25% more products, show attrition about a third of detractors' and make nearly seven times as many positive referrals. Banking-specific; sample not stated. Use: model promoter versus detractor value on your own cohorts before setting a loyalty or referral budget.
facts.source_title: Net Promoter System: The Economics of Loyalty (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Economics of Loyalty' (2012): more than 80% of positive referrals come from promoters and more than 80% of negative word of mouth from detractors. In Bain's North American banking study, relative NPS differences within a region explained most of the differences in retail deposit growth, and Philips business units leading on NPS grew a median 8 percentage points faster than competitors, while units trailing all rivals grew 5 points slower. Company data, correlational. Use: target referral asks and recovery effort by NPS segment; treat NPS leadership as a growth signal, not proof of cause.
facts.source_title: Net Promoter System: The Economics of Loyalty (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Introducing the Net Promoter System' (Markey and Reichheld, December 2011): a working NPS program needs four things: sorting customers into promoters, passives and detractors with a short survey; fast closed-loop processes to learn, recover and act; loyalty as a leadership priority; and employees treated as the route to customers. It names five elements: leadership commitment, a trusted metric, feedback and learning (inner loop for the front line, outer loop for structural fixes), an employee environment built around loyalty, and analytic infrastructure. Use: audit an NPS rollout against these five elements before blaming the survey.
facts.source_title: Introducing the Net Promoter System (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain's 2011 account of Net Promoter System adopters, company-reported and not independently audited: Schwab's stock fell from $40 to $6 in 2004, and four years later it had regained industry leadership with the share price tripled; American Express saw customer satisfaction rise and reported 50% lower employee attrition in its US service centres within three years; Rackspace's revenue run rate exceeded $1 billion by 2011. Bain adds that an industry's loyalty leader grows more than twice as fast as rivals on average. Use: cite as illustration only; many other factors were involved.
facts.source_title: Introducing the Net Promoter System (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, grocery loyalty (Caine, Barro and Koetter, November 2021; NPS Prism data, sample not stated): five US grocers (H-E-B, Costco, Wegmans, Aldi, Trader Joe's) have NPS nearly double the industry average. Promoters spend about $132 a month on groceries versus about $71 for detractors, and promoters send roughly 35% of grocery spend to the store versus 20% for detractors. Customers of the top five leaders give nearly three times as many positive referrals as customers of a low-NPS rival. Use: size the revenue gap between promoters and detractors when building the case for a loyalty or CX investment.
facts.source_title: Happier Shoppers, Higher Spending: The Value of Loyalty in Grocery (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain NPS Prism for grocery launch (press release, October 6, 2021): a benchmark of more than 50,000 shoppers, 40-plus grocers and 25 journeys put H-E-B first on relationship NPS at 65, Costco at 55 among warehouse clubs, Aldi at 55 among discounters and Amazon at 46 among online-only grocers. H-E-B drew two to three times the share of wallet of low-NPS rivals. Unfriendly staff interactions cost 110 NPS points versus 45 points when staff could not be found quickly. Use: weight service-recovery and human-touch fixes by their NPS penalty, not by complaint volume.
facts.source_title: Bain & Company launches NPS Prism for grocery (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Love, Love Me Do' (Darnell, Leibovitz and Caine, February 4, 2022): of the companies on the Glassdoor top-100 list, 11 are also tracked by NPS Prism, and all but one of those have strong customer NPS. In a survey of more than 50,000 grocery customers, a customer looking for an item who met knowledgeable staff scored 87 NPS points higher, moving from negative to positive. Bain also says NPS leaders post returns nearly three times the overall market. Overlap analysis, not causal. Use: pair employee-experience metrics with customer NPS in CX scorecards.
facts.source_title: Love, Love Me Do: New Data Proves the Value of Customer Love (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain NPS Prism US Benchmarks (press release, February 21, 2024): a double-blind survey covering more than 1,000 companies in 10 industries (respondent count not stated) named leaders including USAA (insurance), Lexus (auto), SRP (utilities), H-E-B (grocery), Sherwin-Williams (home improvement) and YouTube TV. Drivers differ by sector: ease of use in payments, proactive pricing communication in utilities, simple plans in mobile, and knowledgeable staff in home improvement, where leaders had 25% more customers citing staff interactions. Use: pick the loyalty driver that matters in the client's sector rather than a generic CX list.
facts.source_title: NPS Prism reveals America's customer loyalty leaders (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain Digital Transactions Survey (December 2024; about 1,800 US customers, 1,796 weighted, plus 80 interviews; reported January 2026): 67% of recent digital transactions had no issues; the 33% with notable issues scored NPS -31, an 88-point drop from the 57 of issue-free ones. Ease of navigation was the top experience driver (71%), then fast loading and glitch-free function. Mobile scored NPS 43 against 33 for desktop; 78% prefer to transact online. Use: prioritise fixing the failure rate of key digital journeys before adding features or promotions.
facts.source_title: Digital Experience Is Where Customer Loyalty Begins or Ends (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Digital Experience Diagnostic (reported with the December 2024 Digital Transactions Survey, nearly 1,800 US customers; article dated January 2026): a scoring method of about 25 criteria across four dimensions: functional, usable, valuable and delightful. In the survey, 41% of users reported positive experiences with AI and agentic AI models, but over half saw no perceived benefit. Health-insurer sites averaged about 19 minutes a visit with NPS 17, versus NPS 62 for department stores. Use: grade a signup or checkout flow on the four dimensions and add AI only where it removes effort.
facts.source_title: Digital Experience Is Where Customer Loyalty Begins or Ends (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain retail banking study (press release November 18, 2019; tenth annual edition with Dynata, more than 131,000 consumers in 22 countries): at a major US bank, credit card applications finished entirely on digital channels scored NPS 50, while those pushed to a human channel scored 8, a 42-point fall. Digital accounted for 18% to 60% of product purchases by country. Bain argues right-first-time digital tasks cost less and build loyalty. Use: design the digital path to complete simple tasks without handoff; offer human help for high-stakes ones.
facts.source_title: Seamless digital experience the key to retaining banking customers (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain, Customer Behavior and Loyalty in Banking, Global Edition 2023 (March 30, 2023; Dynata survey of 29,805 consumers in 11 countries): consumers who opened an account digitally at the first attempt scored 103 NPS points higher than those whose attempt failed and who moved elsewhere. Consumers who strongly agreed their bank interacts based on knowing them scored 123 points higher than those who strongly disagreed. More than 70% were interested in sharing banking data for personalised offers. Use: treat onboarding success and recognised-customer treatment as the top loyalty levers.
facts.source_title: Customer Behavior and Loyalty in Banking: Global Edition 2023 (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Customer Engagement Is Banking's New Battleground' (September 21, 2026; NPS Prism, 2025 interaction samples of 98,674 customers versus 43,043 in 2021): in NPS Prism Q1 2025 data (N=44,395), only 36% of customers say their engagement needs are met and 41% say they are not, against 62% to 65% whose experience and brand needs are met. Weekly interaction ranges roughly 24% to 49% across 16 banks. Digital challengers lead on weekly check-ins at 83%, though traditional banks are closing the frequency gap. Use: engineer low-effort check-in moments, not only transactions.
facts.source_title: Customer Engagement Is Banking's New Battleground (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, loyalty in insurance (Naujoks, O'Neill, Schwedel and others, April 12, 2024; Dynata-powered, ten years of Bain insurance loyalty studies, sample not stated): insurer NPS rose by roughly 10 to 30 points in most countries over the decade, and consumers rated insurers on 33 value elements that separate products from commodities. Digital self-service adoption doubled or quintupled depending on country; one Asian provider reported a 50% gain in adviser productivity from gen AI. Use: for low-engagement categories, add value elements and self-service rather than point-based rewards alone.
facts.source_title: After Years of Customer Loyalty Programs in Insurance, What Works, and What's Next? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'US Department Stores' (Cheris, De La Rocha, Rigby and Thakarar, July 23, 2024; double-blind NPS research with ROI Rocket): sales of North American department-store retail groups fell at a 6% compound annual rate from 2018 to 2023. In women's clothing, department stores held four of the top ten NPS places in 2018 and one (eighth) in 2023, and US department stores scored NPS -7 among 18-to-24-year-olds. Detractors cited assortment (23%) and high prices (22%) as primary reasons. Use: segment NPS by age cohort, since an average can hide collapsing loyalty among younger buyers.
facts.source_title: US Department Stores: It's Time for a New Day One (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'A New Prescription for US Pharmacy' (April 23, 2025): in NPS Prism's US Pharmacy survey (Q2 2024, n=5,669), customers were more satisfied with independent pharmacies, grocers and mass merchants than with other pharmacy types, and Bain expects that gap to widen. Customers still value their relationship with the pharmacist and the reliability of the in-store experience, such as collecting prescriptions right after a doctor visit. In Bain's most likely scenario, grocers and mass merchants grow from about 30% of retail pharmacy to around 40% by 2029 (projection). Use: in health retail, lead with pharmacist relationship and in-store reliability.
facts.source_title: A New Prescription for US Pharmacy (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Beyond Sales Lift: How Rewards Build Valuable Customers' (June 18, 2026; with Fetch Rewards, 92 partners: 73 CPG brands and 19 grocery and general-merchandise retailers, Q2 2024 to Q4 2025, randomised treatment and control): rewards raised first-time customer acquisition by 22% versus control. Net return on initial reward spend averaged 7.2 times per CPG brand (insurgent brands 2.7x to 11.8x). Reward-first buyers were 18% more likely to repurchase within the next two quarters than organic purchasers. Partner-platform data. Use: judge rewards by net value against a holdout, not by redemption counts.
facts.source_title: Beyond Sales Lift: How Rewards Build Valuable Customers (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain and Fetch Rewards (June 18, 2026; 19 retailers in a 92-partner, 21-month randomised study): across retailers, rewards produced an 8.4% sales uplift over 12 months, driven by shopping frequency about 11% higher than control, with spend per trip flat at roughly $43 (grocers) and $52 (general merchandise). Rewards expanded the active base by 3.9% for general merchandisers and 9.8% for grocers; for CPG brands the 12-month sales uplift was 20.7%. Use: expect loyalty rewards to move frequency and retention, not basket size, and set targets accordingly.
facts.source_title: Beyond Sales Lift: How Rewards Build Valuable Customers (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Power of Delivering Elements of Value in Consumer Products' (Gadiesh, Almquist, Meacham and Apps, November 27, 2019; Dynata survey of over 10,000 US consumers, 7 categories, nearly 75 brands): a brand counts as delivering an element when at least 40% of respondents rate it 8 or higher on a 0-10 scale. From 2015 to 2018, brands delivering four or more elements grew revenue on average 10 times as fast as those delivering only two or three; those delivering one or none grew even less. Correlational. Use: score a brand against the elements and aim for four-plus, led by emotional or life-changing ones.
facts.source_title: The Power of Delivering Elements of Value in Consumer Products (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain's Elements of Value in consumer products (November 2019), company figures as reported by Bain: Unilever's 28 sustainable-living brands grew 69% faster than the rest of its portfolio and drove 75% of its growth; Danone's purpose-led brands grew about three times faster than its others; Dollar Shave Club delivered eight elements against one for Gillette and reached number three in US razors in about seven years. Bain adds that over 65% of consumers globally say they would pay more for sustainable products. Use: back purpose-led positioning with a measured set of delivered elements, not slogans.
facts.source_title: The Power of Delivering Elements of Value in Consumer Products (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain and Verlinvest on purpose-led brands (October 27, 2022; Bain consumer survey, 60 brands in eight categories, founder survey): over 70% of consumers said they would pay a 10% to 25% premium for sustainability, yet only 14% rank ESG as their top buying criterion. About 17% of today's purpose-led start-ups reach EUR 10 million in sales versus 10% of all start-ups. Founders cite consumer and distribution barriers (71%) as the main hurdle. Stated intent, not purchase. Use: lead with health, quality and price benefits; let purpose support the offer.
facts.source_title: Purpose-Led Brands Can Reshape the Consumer Goods Industry if They Can Scale (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Brand Accelerator (McRoskey, Blasberg and Apps, 'How Insurgent Brands Are Rewriting the Growth Playbook', May 30, 2018): building on Ehrenberg-Bass thinking that penetration drives growth, Bain targets three brand assets: memorability, shopper visibility and range productivity. Its research used IRI data for 90-plus FMCG categories, surveys of nearly 5,000 consumers across 10 categories and 57 brands, and insurgent interviews. Insurgents held about 2% share in 45 disrupted categories but took about 25% of 2012-2016 growth. Use: audit a brand on the three penetration assets before adding loyalty or niche tactics.
facts.source_title: How Insurgent Brands Are Rewriting the Growth Playbook (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 2026 US Insurgent Brands (tenth annual review, March 4, 2026; NielsenIQ-tracked channels, 113 brands with over $35M revenue and at least 10x category growth over five years): insurgents held under 2% of US share but captured about 36% of 2025 market growth while the market grew under 2%. Their volumes grew about 55%. Since 2017 nearly 400 brands qualified, 15 passed $1B, and about 25% were acquired. Bain projects insurgents could take up to 50% of growth over five years. Use: benchmark a challenger brand's trajectory and pitch against insurgent signals such as high protein and natural claims.
facts.source_title: 2026 US Insurgent Brands: Powering the Next Wave of Growth (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain insurgent-brand trend across editions: the 2018 work found insurgents took about 25% of 2012-2016 growth with about 2% share in 45 disrupted categories; the Expo West note (March 14, 2025) reports nearly 40% of growth on just 2% share, with 73 insurgents past $250M; the 2026 review reports about 36% of 2025 growth on under 2% share. The revenue floor in the definition rose from over $25M in the 2025 note to over $35M in 2026. Use: cite the 25% to 40% range with the definition, not a single figure.
facts.source_title: Expo West 2025: Winning Brands Ride on the Strongest Consumer Trends (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Consumer Products Report 2025 (February 12, 2025; executive survey September 2024, n=96; US and European consumer survey in October, size not stated): global CPG retail sales grew about 7.5% in 2024 versus 9.3% in 2023, with roughly three-quarters of 2024 growth likely from price; developed-market volumes were flat. US and EU prices were over 20% above Q1 2020 and about 80% of surveyed consumers said they were cutting spending. Insurgents captured about 40% of US consumer-products growth in the first half of 2024. Use: plan CPG messaging around value and volume recovery, not price-led growth.
facts.source_title: Consumer Products Report 2025: Reclaiming Relevance in the Gen AI Era (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Consumer Products Report 2025 (February 12, 2025; executive survey n=96, September 2024): 84% of non-tech executives rank gen AI a top-five priority versus 37% of CPG executives, and only 6% of CPG executives have a plan to create business value with AI. Bain estimates, from its client experience, that granular data-driven marketing, sales execution and revenue growth management can add 3 to 5 points of sales growth and 200 to 300 basis points of gross margin, and cutting SKU complexity can add 2 to 5 points of growth. Estimates, not measured averages. Use: put marketing-mix and complexity work ahead of AI pilots in CPG roadmaps.
facts.source_title: Consumer Products Report 2025: Reclaiming Relevance in the Gen AI Era (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Road Forward to Value Creation in Consumer Products' (June 19, 2026; sample not stated): up to 20% of large CPGs' revenue comes from 'zombie' brands and up to 30% could sit in twilight brands. Capability moves from better to best can add 3 to 5 points of sales growth. Companies that reimagine retail may open a revenue gap of about 15% over five years. Leaders report ideas launched five times faster, 10% to 15% ROI uplift on commercial spend, and L'Oreal reports 10% to 15% marketing productivity from its AI backbone (company-reported). Use: prune the long tail before funding brand growth.
facts.source_title: The Road Forward to Value Creation in Consumer Products (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Want to Lead in Consumer Products? Adapt to Retailing's New Reality' (October 29, 2026; builds on existing research, no new survey): Bain projects agentic commerce will influence about $1 trillion of US consumer spending by 2030, around 16% of US retail. A chart description shows beyond-trade profit rising from 10% of retailer profit in 2021 to 25% in 2024, and the text says US retail media spending hit $58.8 billion in 2025. Forecast and secondary-research content. Use: prepare retail-media and shopper-data offers for retailer negotiations.
facts.source_title: Want to Lead in Consumer Products? Adapt to Retailing's New Reality (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain 2025 US holiday forecast (press release September 9, 2025; Bain US consumer survey, sample size not stated on the page): Nov-Dec retail sales up 4% to more than $975B against a 10-year average of 5.2%. Nonstore growth slowed to 7% from 9-10%, in-store sales grow 2.75%, and 55% of shoppers said high prices will affect holiday budgets. Ten percent more consumers plan to shop Black Friday and Cyber Monday and 30% more are open to sponsored ads. Use: plan holiday promotions around price sensitivity and a stronger in-store share.
facts.source_title: US holiday retail sales to reach more than $975B (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain Black Friday 2025 forecast (October 13, 2025; six years of Pyxis credit-card data): about 9% of holiday retail sales were expected between Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the largest share Bain has recorded, with that window up about 11% against 4% for the season. Black Friday topped the season in five of six years, and 55% of consumers planned to shop the day after Thanksgiving, up from 51%. Over half said higher prices would shape spending. Use: weight promo calendars and ad budgets toward the Black Friday to Cyber Monday window, with early-bird offers to protect margin.
facts.source_title: Black Friday 2025 Sales Forecast (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain 2025 European holiday outlook (October 16, 2025; Bain forecasts, no survey sample stated): UK Nov-Dec retail sales were forecast to rise about 2.5% with inflation at 3.8%, so volumes would fall; France about 0.5% with inflation near 1% and a household savings rate around 19%; Germany 2.5% nominal, down from 3.9%, volumes flat. Use: when advising European retail brands, plan for flat or falling volumes and rely on mix, value messaging and retention rather than traffic growth.
facts.source_title: 2025 European Holiday Shopping Outlook (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain 2026 US holiday forecast (press release September 3, 2026; Consumer Lab survey of more than 1,100 consumers, fieldwork dates not stated): Nov-Dec sales to grow 4.5% nominal and pass $1 trillion for the first time, with inflation more than half the rise. Online grows about 9%, in-store 2.5%. 24% of online shoppers plan to start on AI platforms (17% in 2025), 60% on retail or brand sites (51%), and a further 13% on retailer AI agents. About 90% plan to use a major sale event. Use: make product data and pages readable by AI assistants before the holiday peak.
facts.source_title: US holiday retail sales set to exceed $1 trillion (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain Black Friday through Cyber Monday 2026 forecast (press release October 13, 2026; Pyxis credit-card data plus a US consumer survey, size not stated): the weekend is expected to top $85B, about 8.5% of holiday sales, growing 8.75% against 4.5% for the season. 64% plan to shop Black Friday (55% in 2025), 44% Cyber Monday (41%), and 70% one or both (64%). More than 90% plan to shop those days or another major sales event. Bain's Aaron Cheris says retailers using personalised promotions, can't-miss events and targeted campaigns will be well placed. Use: set peak-weekend targets on this higher intent, with personalised rather than blanket discounts.
facts.source_title: Black Friday through Cyber Monday weekend sales to surpass $85 billion (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain/Dynata Consumer Health Indexes (press release April 17, 2025; sample and method not stated): the upper-income outlook fell 11.8 points to 88.6, its sharpest drop except at the onset of Covid, and the overall outlook fell 5.3 points to 94.6; Bain ties the upper-income drop to stock-market losses amid tariff turmoil. Upper-income spending intentions rose 2.1 points, which Bain reads as buying ahead of tariffs. Upper-income consumers account for over half of discretionary spending. Use: watch the upper-income outlook as a leading signal for premium and discretionary demand.
facts.source_title: US consumer outlook readings plummet (Bain/Dynata Consumer Health Indexes)

facts.statement: Bain US Tariffs Survey (April 3, 2025; n=564, fielded just before the April 2 announcement): 66% expected tariffs to significantly raise the prices they pay, only about 15% had made purchasing changes, and only 23% named tariffs a top-three issue (the page lists inflation, illegal immigration and healthcare affordability as the top three). NPS Prism grocery data show 33% of shoppers say they will buy the cheapest brand, up from 27% in 2021. Use: expect price-switching to rise; defend with clear value elements and trial offers, not blanket discounts.
facts.source_title: Tariffs and the US Consumer: Where to Focus Amid the Noise (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'AI in Marketing: How Leaders Achieve Double the Revenue Impact' (September 30, 2026; April 2026 survey of 1,397 CMOs, CFOs and senior marketing and finance executives; 10th annual study; leaders defined by over 11% annual revenue growth plus a market-share criterion): only 6% of marketing organisations, leaders included, report significant performance impact from AI today. Leaders are 3.7 times more likely to fully redesign workflows, 1.8 times more likely to follow a centralised AI roadmap and 8.5 times more likely to run 100 or more experiments a month. Opinion data. Use: redesign workflows before layering on AI tools.
facts.source_title: AI in Marketing: How Leaders Achieve Double the Revenue Impact (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain 2026 marketing leaders-and-laggards study (April 2026, n=1,397 executives; published September 30, 2026): 47% of leaders call AI a core capability (35% a year earlier) versus 30% of laggards (8%). Over 40% of leaders put 11% or more of budget into AI, and they are twice as likely to put over 25% there. Leaders are 5.2 times more likely to focus on customer-centric use cases, and three times more likely to use AI insights for continuous channel spend reallocation. Nearly 70% adjust strategy and spend on AI insights versus 31% of laggards. Opinion data. Use: point AI at customer use cases and budget reallocation first.
facts.source_title: AI in Marketing: How Leaders Achieve Double the Revenue Impact (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain AI marketing leaders-and-laggards (press release June 16, 2025; about 1,200 senior marketing executives worldwide): leaders' median revenue growth was about six times competitors' on average spend only about 1.5 times higher, implying roughly four times the marketing ROI (Bain's derivation). Leaders were 10 times more likely to treat AI as a core capability, six times more likely to run 25-plus AI use cases, and eight times more likely to run 100-plus experiments a month. Executive survey; leaders are defined by growth, so causality is unproven. Use: set experiment volume and use-case count as leading indicators.
facts.source_title: AI raises the stakes in marketing (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Ready for Launch: How Gen AI Is Already Transforming Marketing' (Katzin, Beaudin and Waldron, May 23, 2023; survey of nearly 600 companies in 11 industries): 39% were using or evaluating gen AI to speed marketing-material development, among the top seven use cases. Bain lists uses in content creation, personalisation at scale, near-real-time testing, mining unstructured data for targeting and briefs, and service. It advises employee-facing pilots or human review before customer exposure; no productivity numbers given. Use: start with internal drafting and review-gated outputs, and track time saved yourself.
facts.source_title: Ready for Launch: How Gen AI Is Already Transforming Marketing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Marketing's New Middleman: AI Agents' (April 14, 2025; Bain-Dynata survey, December 2024, n=1,117 US consumers): brands will be reached directly, through AI intermediaries, or through traditional search. A cited vendor figure (Scrunch AI, not Bain's own) says over 90% of LLM content on non-branded queries comes from third-party sources. Bain's three steps: define metrics for traffic at stake, build scorecards for brand visibility in AI search, and run fast 'influence experiments' to reallocate resources. Use: build an AI-visibility scorecard and test earned-media changes.
facts.source_title: Marketing's New Middleman: AI Agents (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Survey, January 2025 (reported in 'Parsing How Winners Use AI', April 23, 2025; n=1,263 B2B commercial executives): over 90% had scaled at least one AI use case, and growth winners averaged 4.5 use cases versus 3.3 for laggards, with almost twice the cost efficiency per use case. Roughly a quarter of respondents' sales and marketing AI pilots failed, and slightly more than half say they lack adequate data and technology foundations. Separately, Bain cites a potential 30%-plus win-rate improvement from reimagining the sales process (a potential prize, not a survey result). Use: fix data foundations and redesign the process before scaling AI.
facts.source_title: Parsing How Winners Use AI (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain Generative AI Survey (published November 24, 2025; waves from Q4 2023 to Q3 2025, the latest n=197 executives): 74% rank AI a top-three strategic priority (60% a year earlier). Marketing and customer service sit in a second tier, where roughly a fifth to a third of use cases have moved from pilot to scale (about 32% for customer service), behind software development at 40%. Of the 59% meaningfully adopting, about 80% of use cases met or exceeded expectations, but only about 23% of all respondents tied AI to revenue or cost. Opinion data. Use: expect marketing AI to be mid-pack; require a measured revenue or cost result per use case.
facts.source_title: Executive Survey: AI Moves from Pilots to Production (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Barriers and Pathways to Sustainable Growth' (Zook and Allen, July 19, 2016; two executive surveys n=325 and n=377, about 100 interviews, a database of about 8,000 public companies): 85% of surveyed executives named internal obstacles as the barrier to profitable growth, including 94% of those running companies above $5 billion revenue. Executives' Founder's Mentality self-scores averaged 72.3 out of 100 at companies with $500 million revenue or less and 56.1 at $5 billion or more (perceptions). Excluding tech, founder-led S&P 500 firms outperformed others by 1.8 times from 1990 to 2014. Use: diagnose growth stalls as internal drift from the front line.
facts.source_title: Barriers and Pathways to Sustainable Growth: Harnessing the Power of the Founder's Mentality (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Founder's Mentality blog on customer advocacy (James Allen, December 17, 2015): front-line obsession shows in three ways, translating strategy into frontline routines, elevating the employees who deliver customer value, and frequent experiments by empowered staff. Case: at India's Oberoi Udaivilas, a front-office manager said staff try to say yes to guests 99% of the time (an aspiration, not a measured rate); employees get small sums to delight guests, and the Udaipur team meets monthly with each department reporting customer lessons. Single-company illustration. Use: give frontline teams a small discretionary budget and a monthly learning routine.
facts.source_title: The Elements of Founder's Mentality: Customer Advocacy (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'A New Prescription for US Pharmacy' (April 23, 2025): in NPS Prism's US Pharmacy survey (Q2 2024, n=5,669), customers were more satisfied with independent pharmacies, grocers and mass merchants than with other pharmacy types, and Bain expects that gap to widen. Customers still value the pharmacist relationship and in-store reliability, such as collecting prescriptions right after a doctor visit. Bain's most likely scenario has grocers and mass merchants rising from about 30% of retail pharmacy to around 40% by 2029 (projection). Use: lead with pharmacist relationship and in-store reliability.
facts.source_title: A New Prescription for US Pharmacy (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Black Friday through Cyber Monday 2026 forecast (press release October 13, 2026; Pyxis card data plus a US consumer survey, size not stated): the weekend should top $85B, about 8.5% of holiday sales, growing 8.75% against 4.5% for the season. 64% plan to shop Black Friday (55% in 2025), 44% Cyber Monday (41%), 70% one or both (64%); over 90% plan those days or another major sales event. Bain's Aaron Cheris says personalised promotions, can't-miss events and targeted campaigns will help. Use: set peak targets on this higher intent, with personalised offers over blanket discounts.
facts.source_title: Black Friday through Cyber Monday weekend sales to surpass $85 billion (Bain press release)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Your Next Customer Will Find You Using AI. Now What?' (April 7, 2026; Bain Generative AI US Consumer Survey, September 2025, n=1,500, plus ScrunchAI data on about 500 million citations): 44% of surveyed US online buyers mostly start in an LLM or split between AI and search, and half trust gen AI for initial research and comparisons. About 89% of unbranded prompts are answered with third-party sources (76% to 99% by topic). Bain urges more earned-media and reputation work and tracking share of voice and citation frequency per engine. Use: measure AI citations by prompt.
facts.source_title: Your Next Customer Will Find You Using AI. Now What? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Commercial Excellence Survey, January 2025 (reported in 'Parsing How Winners Use AI', April 23, 2025; n=1,263 B2B commercial executives): over 90% had scaled at least one AI use case; growth winners averaged 4.5 use cases versus 3.3 for laggards, with almost twice the cost efficiency per use case. Roughly a quarter of sales and marketing AI pilots failed, and slightly more than half lack adequate data and technology foundations. Bain also cites a potential 30%-plus win-rate gain from reimagining sales (a potential prize, not a survey result). Use: fix data foundations first.
facts.source_title: Parsing How Winners Use AI (Bain Commercial Excellence Agenda 2025)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Barriers and Pathways to Sustainable Growth' (Zook and Allen, July 19, 2016; surveys n=325 and n=377, about 100 interviews, about 8,000 public companies): 85% of executives named internal obstacles as the barrier to profitable growth, including 94% of those running companies above $5 billion revenue. Executives' Founder's Mentality scores averaged 72.3 out of 100 at companies with $500 million revenue or less and 56.1 at $5 billion or more (perceptions). Excluding tech, founder-led S&P 500 firms outperformed others 1.8 times, 1990-2014. Use: diagnose growth stalls as internal drift.
facts.source_title: Barriers and Pathways to Sustainable Growth: Harnessing the Power of the Founder's Mentality (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Founder's Mentality blog on customer advocacy (James Allen, December 17, 2015): front-line obsession shows in three ways: turning strategy into frontline routines, elevating employees who deliver customer value, and frequent experiments by empowered staff. Case: at India's Oberoi Udaivilas, a front-office manager said staff try to say yes to guests 99% of the time (an aspiration, not a measured rate); employees get small sums to delight guests, and the Udaipur team meets monthly to share customer lessons. Single-company illustration. Use: give frontline teams a small discretionary budget and a monthly learning routine.
facts.source_title: The Elements of Founder's Mentality: Customer Advocacy (Bain)

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse 2026, 'The surprising economics of B2B growth' (June 2026; tenth global edition, nearly 4,000 B2B decision makers in 13 countries, opinion data): among market leaders, defined as firms whose market share grew by more than 10 percent, 60 percent report double-digit revenue growth, against 21 percent of laggards. Leaders are more likely to pair hyper-personalisation with scaled gen AI and firm sales accountability. Use: set the B2B growth bar at share gain, not just revenue, and report leader-versus-laggard gaps to the CMO.
facts.source_title: The surprising economics of B2B growth: The new survival threshold and what it takes to thrive

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse 2026 (nearly 4,000 B2B decision makers, 13 countries, opinion data), as reported by The Drum: firms where sales owns account-based marketing sit in the top revenue-growth bands about 5 to 10 percentage points more often than firms with shared or marketing-led ABM. This is a correlation, not proof of cause, and it was seen only in secondary coverage. Use: name a sales owner for target accounts, with marketing supplying content and intent data.
facts.source_title: The surprising economics of B2B growth: The new survival threshold and what it takes to thrive

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse 2026 (nearly 4,000 B2B decision makers, 13 countries, opinion data): AI-enabled search, chatbots and large language models now rank among buyers' top five channels in the purchase journey, and 58 percent of buyers say they trust these tools to learn about products and services. Roughly a third of B2B firms still offer no online purchasing. Use: write supplier pages and proof so AI answers describe the product correctly, and close the e-commerce gap.
facts.source_title: The surprising economics of B2B growth: The new survival threshold and what it takes to thrive

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse, 'The multiplier effect: How B2B winners grow' (spring 2023; survey fielded December 2022, 3,800+ B2B decision makers, 13 countries, opinion data): the report names five winning strategies (e-commerce, omnichannel experience, hybrid sales teams with sales technology, hyperpersonalisation, marketplaces) and says firms combining them see a multiplier effect of 10 percent or more market-share growth. Use: plan them as one bundle and track share gain, not single-channel wins.
facts.source_title: B2B Pulse: The multiplier effect - How B2B winners grow

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse 2023, 'The multiplier effect' (December 2022 survey, 3,800+ B2B decision makers, 13 countries, opinion data): about 57 percent of market-share winners had hybrid sales teams, against about 40 percent of firms that lost share; 69 percent of share winners planned more sales investment against 36 percent of share losers. Firms that grew hybrid teams by over 10 percent were about 79 percent more likely to be share winners. Use: argue for blended inside and field coverage when asking for headcount.
facts.source_title: B2B Pulse: The multiplier effect - How B2B winners grow

facts.statement: McKinsey Global B2B Pulse 2022 edition (press release 23 Feb 2022; survey fielded December 2021, nearly 3,500 B2B decision makers in 12 markets, opinion data): about one in five (20 percent) said they would spend between $500,000 and $5 million in a single purchase through remote or self-serve channels. Use: do not assume large tickets require a face-to-face rep; offer a credible remote or self-serve path for high-value deals.
facts.source_title: B2B Pulse: The new B2B growth equation

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'B2B sales: Omnichannel everywhere, every time' (15 December 2021; B2B Pulse, opinion data): 94 percent of B2B decision makers rated the current omnichannel sales model as effective as or more effective than the pre-COVID-19 model, up from 65 percent in April 2020. Use: treat omnichannel as the default buying experience and retire pre-2020 'in-person is best' assumptions.
facts.source_title: B2B sales: Omnichannel everywhere, every time

facts.statement: McKinsey B2B Pulse, wave fielded 12 to 26 February 2021 (about 3,500 B2B decision makers, opinion data): respondents ranked e-commerce as an effective sales channel most often (41 percent), ahead of in-person (37 percent) and videoconference (31 percent), per a McKinsey slide deck and Statista. These are shares of respondents naming a channel, not revenue shares. Use: give online ordering its own conversion owner.
facts.source_title: Omnichannel in B2B sales: The new normal in a year that has been anything but

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'The B2B digital inflection point' (May 2020, first B2B decision-maker pulse during COVID-19, opinion data, sample not stated here): B2B companies judged digital interactions two to three times more important to their customers than traditional sales interactions, and a large share of respondents saw remote selling as as effective as before the crisis. This was the start of the Pulse trend line. Use: cite 2020 as the baseline when showing how far buyer channel preference has moved.
facts.source_title: The B2B digital inflection point: How sales have changed during COVID-19

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'Unlocking profitable B2B growth through gen AI' (2024, drawing on the B2B Pulse, opinion data, sample not stated in the sources reached): about 19 percent of respondents were already implementing gen AI use cases across B2B buying and selling and a further 23 percent were in the process of doing so. The article groups value into revenue generation, sales productivity and internal process streamlining. Use: benchmark any gen AI sales pilot against this early-adopter share and pick use cases from those three buckets.
facts.source_title: Unlocking profitable B2B growth through gen AI

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'Five ways B2B sales leaders can win with tech and AI' (2025; interviews with 70+ commercial leaders plus B2B Pulse data, opinion data): only about 20 percent of B2B sales leaders say they can point to a proven record of using technology consistently for outsized growth. Growth leaders use AI to find new pockets of growth, and the article also covers pricing (price optimisation, deal scoring) and seller talent development. Use: pick AI pilots with one named sales metric each.
facts.source_title: Five fundamental truths: How B2B winners keep growing

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'Five ways B2B sales leaders can win with tech and AI' (2025, from the B2B Pulse, opinion data): only about 20 percent of respondents say they have a proven record of using technology consistently for outsized growth. Leaders use AI to find growth pockets (micro-segments, cross-sell, churn risk), automate pricing, and cut admin such as lead routing and RFP drafts. McKinsey advises a portfolio of pilots tied to metrics like win rate and cycle time. Use: choose AI pilots with one named sales metric each.
facts.source_title: Five ways B2B sales leaders can win with tech and AI

facts.statement: Marn and Rosiello, 'Managing Price, Gaining Profit' (Harvard Business Review, Sept-Oct 1992, McKinsey authors; analysis of 2,463 companies): a 1 percent price improvement with volume held constant lifted operating profit by about 11.1 percent, versus 7.8 percent for 1 percent lower variable cost, 3.3 percent for 1 percent more volume and 2.3 percent for 1 percent lower fixed cost. The volume-constant assumption matters, and later McKinsey updates put the effect near 8 to 9 percent. Use: show price leakage in profit terms, with the no-volume-loss caveat stated.
facts.source_title: Managing Price, Gaining Profit

facts.statement: McKinsey, 'Using big data to make better pricing decisions' (2014): a 1 percent price rise with no volume loss was estimated to lift operating profit by about 8.7 percent, and up to 30 percent of the thousands of pricing decisions a firm makes each year fail to land the best price. McKinsey's answer is granular, transaction-level pricing data and analytics rather than average-price rules. Use: segment price tests to the transaction or customer level and audit which price decisions miss the right price.
facts.source_title: Using big data to make better pricing decisions

facts.statement: The CMO Survey (Duke Fuqua, Deloitte, AMA), July-August 2018 wave, 324 US marketing leaders (95.3% VP level or above) from a pool of 2,895: marketing was 7.3% of firm revenue overall, but 10.1% for B2C products, 8.9% B2C services, 7.1% B2B services and only 5.4% B2B products. Opinion data from a non-representative panel. Use: benchmark a budget against the right business model, never against one blended average.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: How does your marketing budget grow? (Aug 2018 wave)

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Aug 2018 wave (324 US marketing leaders): digital took 44% of marketing budgets, expected to reach 54% within five years; expected growth was +12.3% for digital advertising versus -1.2% for traditional advertising. Executives expected B2B services (+9.2%) and B2B products (+8.8%) to grow budgets faster than B2C. Opinion data. Use: treat the digital-share trend line as the baseline when judging channel-mix shifts in later editions.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: How does your marketing budget grow? (Aug 2018 wave)

facts.statement: CMO Survey, August 2019 edition (341 US marketing leaders, 95% VP level or above): marketing was a record 12% of firm budgets and 9.8% of revenue; budgets were expected to grow 8.7%. Marketing analytics rose from 4.6% of budgets in 2017 to 7.2%, with 11.6% expected within three years, yet only about 40% said they had the quantitative tools to show spending impact. Opinion data. Use: fund measurement capability alongside media, because the tooling gap was the stated constraint.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Top ten results, August 2019

facts.statement: CMO Survey, August 2019 wave (sample not stated in the Feb 2020 write-up): marketers reported a 27% increase in using AI and machine learning versus six months earlier and expected a 59% rise within three years. Top uses were content personalization and predictive analytics for customer insight (each 56.5%) and targeting customer decision-making (49.6%). Opinion data. Use: start AI pilots in personalization and prediction, where marketers reported actual adoption.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Smart marketing, how corporate marketers deploy AI

facts.statement: CMO Survey, August 2019 (341 US marketing leaders): marketers rated their customer-experience performance above competitors on only one of twelve activities, assuring customer experiences are compatible with the brand. The other eleven were rated on par with or below competitors. Self-rated opinion data. Use: audit journey integration and CX capability first, since brand consistency alone is not a differentiator.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Top ten results, August 2019

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2019 wave (323 leaders, fielded 8-29 January 2019): social media peaked at 13.8% of marketing budgets in Aug 2018 and fell to 11.4%, while executives predicted 19.7% in five years. Its contribution rating stayed near 3.1-3.3 of 7 across seven waves. In Aug 2018, 39.3% could not show social impact, 24.7% proved it quantitatively. Use: discount executive forecasts of social spend and tie each social budget to a measurable outcome.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Why social media performance lags even as spending soars

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2019 wave (sample not stated in the post): expected marketing hiring growth was 5.1%, down from 7.3% a year earlier. By model: B2B products 6.5%, B2B services 6.1%, B2C services 4.4%, B2C products 0.5%. Firms selling more than 10% online expected slightly negative hiring (-0.18%), versus 7% for firms with no online sales. Opinion data. Use: expect ecommerce-heavy firms to automate before hiring when sizing team plans.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing hiring slows, is a recession on the horizon

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2020 (265 US marketing leaders, 98% VP level or above): marketing budget growth 7.6% (from 8.7% in Aug 2019); marketing was 11.3% of firm budgets and 8.6% of revenue; digital spend was expected to grow 13% while traditional advertising was -0.4%. Customer-experience spend rose from 8.9% to 15.2% of marketing budgets, 20.6% expected in three years. Opinion data. Use: use these as the pre-pandemic baseline for budget and CX share.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Top ten results, February 2020

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2020 (265 leaders): social media was 13% of marketing budgets, expected at 21.5% in five years; outside agencies ran nearly a quarter of social activity; in-house social staff fell from 4.1 people (2014) to 3.1; perceived value was 3.4 of 7; 30% could prove social impact quantitatively, up from 18% in 2017. Opinion data. Use: pair any social budget increase with attribution capability, as proof rates were still under a third.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Top ten results, February 2020

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2020 (265 leaders): growth spending leaned on existing markets and offerings (54%), with diversification at 10.4%; 72% of growth investment was organic, versus partnerships 11.4%, acquisitions 11.3% and licensing 5.1%; internet sales were 13.5% of revenue. Opinion data. Use: default growth plans to penetration of current segments, and require evidence before funding diversification.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Top ten results, February 2020

facts.statement: CMO Survey special Covid-19 edition, June 2020 (sample not stated on the post): marketing reached 12.6% of firm budgets and 11.4% of firm revenues, both survey highs; 9% of marketing jobs were lost; planned hiring fell to -3.5%, the lowest in survey history; expected budget growth dropped from 7.6% to 1.6%; 62.3% said marketing became more important. Opinion data. Use: read record budget shares alongside the 1.6% growth expectation, not as proof of real budget growth.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Covid drives digital as marketers pivot into stronger and leaner roles

facts.statement: CMO Survey, June 2020 (sample not stated on the post): social share of marketing budgets jumped from 13.3% to 23.2% in four months (a survey peak); 84.2% used social for brand building and 54.3% for retention; 85% of marketers said customers were more open to their digital offerings and 60.8% had shifted resources to customer-facing digital interfaces. Opinion data. Use: treat crisis-era social shares as temporary, since later waves show them falling back.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Covid drives digital as marketers pivot into stronger and leaner roles

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2021 edition (26th; 356 marketing leaders): marketing jobs lost between Feb 2020 and Feb 2021 were 8.2%, jobs added 9.1%; 72.2% said marketing grew in importance. Top digital investments were website optimization (74%), digital media and search (65%), direct digital marketing (57%), data analytics (56%), martech (54%) and online experimentation (45%). Opinion data. Use: use this list as the order of digital priorities for a lean team.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing proves its mettle during pandemic, job growth follows

facts.statement: CMO Survey, August 2021 edition (27th; 282 leaders, 94.1% VP level or above): digital took 58% of marketing budgets; digital spend grew 15.8% in the prior year, 14.7% expected; overall marketing spend grew 5.2% with 13.4% projected. Companies in the nascent stage of digital transformation fell from 31.1% to 8.6%; 73% of marketing leaders were asked to lead transformation. Opinion data. Use: assume digital transformation is owned by marketing at most firms.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Digital marketing spending soars as marketers' roles reach higher echelons

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Aug 2021 (282 leaders): marketers reported more pressure from CEOs (59%) and CFOs (45%) to prove value; almost half of how marketing is evaluated came from sales impact and customer engagement; AI and machine-learning use for prediction and measurement was expected to triple within three years. Opinion data. Use: report marketing results in sales and engagement terms that CEOs and CFOs already judge by.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Digital marketing spending soars as marketers' roles reach higher echelons

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2022 edition (320 US marketing leaders): marketing was 11.7% of company budgets and 10.3% of revenue; digital took 57.1% of marketing budgets; spending growth of 13.6% was predicted over the next year; data-analytics spend grew nearly 40% in a year; hiring grew 12.2% with 10.5% expected. Opinion data. Use: treat 2021-22 as a peak-spend period when setting normal benchmarks.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey finds digital marketing spending soars, yet companies lag on climate and privacy

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2022 (320 leaders) on data: marketers expected first-party data use to rise 74.8% over two years, second-party 45.7%, third-party only 30.5%; 17.7% expected third-party use to decline, up from 11.4% in 2018. More than 90% did not believe consumers read or understand privacy disclosures. Opinion data. Use: prioritize first-party data capture and plain-language consent in every lead and lifecycle flow.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey finds digital marketing spending soars, yet companies lag on climate and privacy

facts.statement: CMO Survey, February 2022 (320 US marketing leaders): nearly 40% of companies took no climate-related marketing action; one third had climate goals; only 24.5% said customers would pay more for climate-friendly offers and 34% believed customers or partners would reward climate action. Opinion data from marketers, not consumers. Use: do not price a green claim as a premium unless first-hand customer evidence supports it.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey finds digital marketing spending soars, yet companies lag on climate and privacy

facts.statement: CMO Survey, September 2022 edition (29th; 273 leaders): marketing analytics reached an all-time high 8.9% of budgets and was used in nearly half of decisions (38% pre-pandemic); mobile was 13.7% and social 14-15% of budgets versus a June 2020 social peak of 23.2%; marketing teams grew 15.1% in the prior year with 7.3% expected. Opinion data. Use: expect analytics share to hold while pandemic-era mobile and social spikes normalize.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Return to normalcy, leading marketing in a post-Covid era

facts.statement: CMO Survey, 30th edition (reported March 2023; 314 leaders, 97% VP level or above): executives named talent as the top driver of future organic growth (40.1%), ahead of operating model (19.4%) and technology (13.5%). Brand spend was split about 40% long term and 60% short term versus an ideal 50/50, and brand investment growth slowed to 5.5% from 12%. Opinion data. Use: weight talent and brand-building in growth plans, not only tooling.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing spending and hiring growth slows amidst economic uncertainty

facts.statement: CMO Survey, 30th edition (reported March 2023; 314 leaders): digital spending growth slowed to 8.2% from 15%, overall marketing spend grew 2.9%, marketing was 12.3% of company budget; marketing team growth was 3.4% (2022 averaged 12-15%, long-run average since 2010 is 5.6%); social was 17% of budgets, mobile 19%. Opinion data. Use: use the 5.6% long-run hiring average as the normal-year yardstick.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing spending and hiring growth slows amidst economic uncertainty

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Fall 2023 edition (31st; 316 leaders, 96% VP level or above): marketing was 9.2% of revenue (10.9% in the prior wave) and 10.6% of company budgets; spend grew 2.6% with 7.2% expected; influencers were 5.9% of budgets, expected 12.2% in three years; marketers used experiments about 36% of the time and outsourced 20.2% of activities. Opinion data. Use: raise experiment cadence, since experiments ran in barely a third of decisions.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: New results from the Fall 2023 edition

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Fall 2023 (316 leaders): 94.1% of marketers had begun using AI within the previous three years and 60.4% within the past year. Reported effects were sales productivity +6.2%, customer satisfaction +7.0%, and marketing overhead -7.2%. Companies by digital-transformation phase: nascent 8.8%, emerging 54.2%, integrated 24.2%, institutionalized 12.8%. Self-reported opinion data. Use: treat AI gains as claimed, and verify with controlled tests before promising them.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: New results from the Fall 2023 edition

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2024 (32nd edition, reported 24 April 2024; 292 leaders, 94% VP level or above): 75.3% of companies used martech, taking 19.9% of marketing budget (30.9% expected in five years); only 56.4% of purchased tools were actually used, and realized payoffs ran 34% below expectations. Impact rated 4.7 of 7. Opinion data. Use: audit martech utilization before buying more tools.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketers spend on new technologies while battling usage and impact challenges

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2024 (292 leaders): generative AI powered about 7% of marketing activities; on large language models, 10% were actively using, 51% evaluating or piloting and 39% not yet. Reported AI effects were sales productivity +5.1%, customer satisfaction +6.1%, overhead -7.0%. Marketing was 10.1% of revenue and 10.2% of company budget; sustainability took 1.9% of marketing budget. Opinion data. Use: use 7% as the one-year-before baseline against the 15.1% reported in 2025.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketers spend on new technologies while battling usage and impact challenges

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Fall 2024 edition (33rd; fielded 4-25 September 2024; 260 leaders, 97% VP level or above): marketing spend grew 5.8% (2.5% before), 8.6% projected; digital grew 11.1%, 12.7% projected; traditional advertising +0.8%, the first positive reading in two years. Next-year growth expected in branding (7.0%), CRM (6.9%) and customer experience (5.6%). Opinion data. Use: treat the Fall 2024 rebound as short-lived, as 2025 growth fell to 3.3%.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing budget and job growth rebound

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Fall 2024 (260 leaders): marketers said the ideal brand budget is half long-term and half short-term, but actual spend was 31.2% long term and 68.8% short term. Firms spent 19.6% more on acquiring customers than retaining them. When profits fell short, 46% focused on cutting costs (33% on growing revenue), and marketing was an early cut target 44.6% of the time. Opinion data. Use: defend brand and retention budgets with the stated 50/50 ideal.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing budget and job growth rebound

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Fall 2024 (260 leaders): marketing headcount grew 5.3% (3.9% in Spring 2024); by model B2B services +7.6% and B2C products +5.3%; by industry education +25.3%, banking/finance/insurance +14.8%, healthcare +9.8%, while mining/construction fell 20%, retail/wholesale 5.8% and communications/media 4.9%. Opinion data. Use: size hiring plans against the sector, not the all-industry average.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing budget and job growth rebound

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2025 edition (34th; reported 1 April 2025; 281 leaders, 99% VP level or above): AI powered 17.2% of marketing efforts (44.2% projected within three years); generative AI reached 15.1% of activities versus 7.0% a year earlier. Reported effects: sales productivity +8.6%, customer satisfaction +8.5%, overhead -10.8%, all higher than the 2024 wave. Self-reported. Use: use 15% as the market norm for generative AI coverage when scoring AI maturity.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketers claim a broader role and increased influence amid pressures

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2025 (281 leaders): marketing was 9.4% of revenue (7.7% in 2024) and 11.4% of company budgets; spend grew 3.3% (5.8% in Fall 2024) and digital 7.3% (11.1%); forecasts were 8.9% overall and 11.9% digital growth. Social fell to 11.3% of budgets from 12.1%, with 13.3% expected within 12 months and 18.4% within five years. Opinion data. Use: treat executive forecasts of social share with caution.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketers claim a broader role and increased influence amid pressures

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2025 (281 leaders): reported pressure rose from CFOs (63%, from 52%), CEOs (61%, from 51%) and boards (50%, from 33%). Marketing headcount grew 5.4% in 2024, and full-time staff were 77.9% of expected hires, down from 82.5% in 2019, so more work shifts to contractors. Opinion data. Use: prepare CFO-grade business cases and plan for a flexible talent mix.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketers claim a broader role and increased influence amid pressures

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2026 (35th edition; 308 leaders, 97% VP level or above; post dated 31 March 2026): acquisition spend was 26% larger than retention spend, almost 60% of growth spending went to market penetration, and almost half of marketers were prioritizing loyalty of existing customers. When profits fell short, 53.1% focused on cutting costs and marketing was cut 45.4% of the time. Opinion data. Use: argue for retention funding with the cost-cutting data in hand.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing contracts under economic pressure despite growing value and AI gains

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2026 (308 leaders): no marketing-technology activity scored above 5 of 7 on performance, and the main barriers were organizational (budget, integration, bandwidth, talent). Training fell to 3.8% of marketing spend from a pre-pandemic high of 5.8%, and headcount growth fell by more than half versus the prior year. Opinion data. Use: invest in skills and integration before buying another tool.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing contracts under economic pressure despite growing value and AI gains

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2026 (308 leaders): 57.6% of firms were adding channels, led by digital (47.9%), social selling (38.8%), new face-to-face (30.3%) and retail media (23.6%). Marketers spent about 68% of their time managing the present and 32% preparing for the future. Capabilities were rated 5.9 of 7 in importance. Opinion data. Use: plan tests of new channels such as social selling and retail media with a resourcing plan attached.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing contracts under economic pressure despite growing value and AI gains

facts.statement: CMO Survey, Spring 2026 (308 leaders): nearly half of companies were raising or planning to raise prices that year, more than half of respondents were less optimistic than the prior quarter (highest since June 2020), and companies changing investment levels were cutting about four times as often as increasing. Opinion data from US marketers. Use: stress-test pricing and offer plans for price-sensitive buyers when peers are raising prices into a pessimistic market.
facts.source_title: The CMO Survey: Marketing contracts under economic pressure despite growing value and AI gains

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital personalization study (published 29 Sep 2026; fieldwork April 2026; blind surveys by Lawless Research of 1,000 US consumers and 480 US B2C brand leaders): 87% of brands rated their personalization good or excellent versus 29% of consumers; brands thought 62% of experiences were personalized while consumers felt 44% were. Consumers who prefer personalizing brands reported spending about 30% more. Use: measure personalization from the customer side, not self-assessment.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: Personalization research 2026

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital personalization study (published 29 Sep 2026; April 2026 fieldwork by Lawless Research; 1,000 US consumers, 480 US B2C brand leaders): high-maturity brands had stronger data governance, customer intelligence and content supply and were more likely to fund personalization over multiple years. Integration was the top scaling constraint (44%), and brands needed an average of 4.7 business days to act on new customer data. Brand-reported. Use: fix data governance and integration before adding personalization tools.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: Personalization research 2026

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital personalization study (April 2026 fieldwork; 1,000 US consumers, 480 US B2C brand leaders): 63% of consumers used AI search tools or assistants in the past year and 1 in 5 start their searches there. Among AI users, 32% bought a product AI recommended and 18% found a new brand that way. Consumer self-report. Use: prepare product and review content for AI-driven discovery now.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: Personalization research 2026
