facts.statement: Deloitte Digital B2C commerce research (published 15 July 2026; fieldwork Feb-Mar 2026; 550 US B2C senior managers at firms with 1,000+ staff and $100M+ revenue, and 1,000 US online shoppers aged 18-79): only about 1 in 4 brands believed they delivered excellent online shopping; consumers said experiences had not improved since the 2024 survey; 57% spent less in the prior year; 90% of those with consistently great experiences bought, recommended or engaged more. Use: prioritize consistency of basic commerce experience over novelty.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: B2C commerce research 2026

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital B2C commerce research (Feb-Mar 2026; 550 US B2C leaders, 1,000 US online shoppers): only 12% of companies used agentic AI extensively in commerce; commerce standouts were 6x as likely as low-maturity brands to do so, and 50% of standouts offered personalized site search. Personalization ranked as the top commerce investment priority for 2026. Brand self-report. Use: plan agentic features as a staged pilot and benchmark against the 12% norm.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: B2C commerce research 2026

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital's April 2024 guidance on generative AI in customer service (sample and method not stated on the page) frames three outcomes to pursue: improve efficiency, elevate experiences through emotionally resonant personalization for customers and agents, and focus on innovation that expands revenue. It advises assessing the existing technical foundation first and letting AI take documentation work so human agents handle complex cases. Use: scope service AI as human-plus-AI, starting with a foundation audit.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: Generative AI in customer service

facts.statement: Deloitte Global Marketing Trends 2021 (page dated 18 Oct 2020; 2,447 global consumers and 405 US executives from global companies) organized marketing into seven trends: Purpose, Agility, Human Experience, Trust, Participation, Fusion and Talent. The page says customer expectations of reliable solutions, values-matching purpose and a co-creator role grew during the disruption. Survey-based opinion data. Use: use the seven trends as a checklist when reviewing brand strategy.
facts.source_title: Deloitte: 2021 Global Marketing Trends

facts.statement: Deloitte Global Marketing Trends 2022 (released 9 Nov 2021): 1,099 global C-suite executives (about half CMOs), 11,500 consumers aged 18+ in 19 countries surveyed in May 2021, and 18 executive interviews. Its seven trends: purpose, inclusive marketing, creative engine, cookieless world, human-first data, hybrid experience, AI-enhanced service. It reports high-growth brands set diversity, equity and inclusion metrics more often than lower-growth peers. Use: use as a 2022 agenda for data trust and hybrid experience.
facts.source_title: Deloitte releases third annual Global Marketing Trends

facts.statement: Deloitte State of the Consumer Tracker, October 2026 edition (monthly survey of thousands of consumers in over a dozen countries; exact sample not stated): the global financial well-being index fell to 101.9 in September from 105.1 the month before; 36% said finances were worse than a year ago; 73% worried about rising everyday prices; 69% of US respondents made a splurge purchase in September versus 75% a year earlier. Consumer survey. Use: set promotional and premium messaging against these value-seeking signals.
facts.source_title: Deloitte: State of the Consumer Tracker

facts.statement: BCG 'Why Brand Marketing Matters' (Nov 9, 2021; survey of 330 large B2B companies across seven industries plus 25+ executive interviews) sorts brand marketers into four maturity levels: nascent, emerging, differentiating and amplifying. Top performers share six traits: strategy and value proposition, measurement, diverse skills, multi-channel activation, a cross-functional operating model and integrated technology. Use: self-score a brand against the six traits before setting a brand budget.
facts.source_title: Why Brand Marketing Matters (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG B2B brand survey (Nov 9, 2021; 330 large B2B companies, seven industries, executive opinion data): 64% of firms sit at the two lowest brand-maturity levels and 10% at the top. Companies with strong brands show a 74% higher return on brand marketing investment and 46% larger market share than those with weaker brands; amplifying firms assess about 50% more KPIs than nascent ones. Firms putting over half of brand spend into digital saw returns about 25% higher. One company's experiment showed roughly 640% brand ROMI over four years. Treat as association, not proof.
facts.source_title: Why Brand Marketing Matters (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Mindshare Matters. Now Marketers Can Measure It.' (May 30, 2024): brand strength tracks how tightly customers link their needs to a brand. Mindshare is costly to build and cheaper to maintain (an S-curve), is best targeted by demand space (a need, not a segment), and counts direct, indirect (word of mouth, usage) and paid exposure. BCG's First Fast Response (FFR) metric tracks it in near real time. Sample and method not stated. Use: plan brand spend by need-based demand space and track a leading consideration metric.
facts.source_title: Mindshare Matters. Now Marketers Can Measure It. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG mindshare article (May 30, 2024; sample and method not stated, so treat as vendor claims): marketing focused on a demand space lifted mindshare by 10 to 20 points on average, and targeted customers were up to five times more likely to name the brand first. BCG says a 1-point rise in its FFR metric can drive a 1.5 to 2 point conversion lift, and cites a relationship value above 0.8 between total perceived impressions and mindshare in its studies. Use: test demand-space targeting in a holdout before trusting these effect sizes.
facts.source_title: Mindshare Matters. Now Marketers Can Measure It. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Building Lasting Brand Equity in the Age of AI' (Dec 12, 2025; analysis of 2,400 consumers and 130 senior marketing leaders): cutting $1 of brand spend costs about $1.92 of later investment to win back lost share, up from $1.85 in 2022. Three in four marketers say brand cuts hurt more than five years ago. BCG says its FFR metric is 2.6x more responsive and 4x more predictive of future sales than unaided awareness. Use: use the $1.92 figure as a framing for cut decisions, not a forecast.
facts.source_title: Building Lasting Brand Equity in the Age of AI (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG brand-equity article (Dec 12, 2025; 2,400 consumers, 130 marketing leaders) names five practices of above-market brand returns: map what influences consumers across non-linear touchpoints; use precision to capture attention; build trust through authenticity (68% of consumers cite trust as the top purchase driver; trust ties to an 8-point FFR gain); judge brand with financial rigor alongside predictive metrics; and use GenAI, especially video, to tailor messages. Use: audit brand plans against the five practices and add a finance-agreed brand metric.
facts.source_title: Building Lasting Brand Equity in the Age of AI (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Brand Advocacy Index (Dec 2, 2013; survey of 32,000+ consumers in France, Germany, Spain, the UK and US across five product categories): the index asks about actual behavior, which BCG says removes the influence of cultural differences between countries. In many markets the biggest brands do not score highest on advocacy, and local drivers matter: Skoda ranked highest in Germany on advocacy, on the basis of high value for money. Use: measure advocacy as recommending behavior and benchmark by market, not by size.
facts.source_title: The Most Recommended Brands of 2013 (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Agentic Scenarios Every Marketer Must Prepare For' (Mar 25, 2026; sample not stated): two uncertainties, where influence will reside (social networks and human judgment vs algorithmic optimization) and how market power will be concentrated (a few platforms vs many agents), yield four scenarios: The Open Agentic Bazaar, Brand Resurgence Through Data Fortresses, The Super-App Embrace, and A Creator-Led Authenticity Revival. No-regret moves named: brand equity, answer engine optimization and marketing speed. Use: stress-test any channel plan against all four.
facts.source_title: Agentic Scenarios Every Marketer Must Prepare For (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How the Composable Shelf Reinvents Marketing' (Oct 20, 2026): a virtual reference layer above existing asset, content and offer systems that links desired customer actions to approved offers, content and rules so AI engines can assemble individualized interactions, with an action library of the behaviors the business wants. BCG says it has consistently seen three times the ROI and ten times the speed across retail, travel, banking and healthcare-services clients (sample not stated). Start with one customer behavior as the pilot.
facts.source_title: How the Composable Shelf Reinvents Marketing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'GenAI Promised a Creative Revolution' (Oct 1, 2025; survey of 251 global marketing leaders, opinion data): 92% are optimistic about GenAI's creative potential, yet only about a third use it end to end or regularly. Two-thirds of the best use cases are structured, templated content; under 5% rank video or animation use cases highly. A third cite weak prompting skills; one education firm cut content-production hours 30 to 40%. Use: start GenAI creative with templated formats and train prompting before attempting video.
facts.source_title: GenAI Promised a Creative Revolution. Can Marketers Deliver? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 2025 CMO survey article 'How CMOs Are Scaling GenAI in Turbulent Times' (Jun 2, 2025; annual survey of 200 CMOs fielded Apr-May, opinion data), beyond the headline optimism: scaled personalized offers often return about three times the returns of mass offers; fewer CMOs than last year reported significant efficiency gains; measurement ranked last when CMOs prioritized funds for digital customer experience and martech; and BCG says hiring GenAI talent in sufficient volume is not an option, so training existing teams is imperative. Use: fund incrementality measurement alongside GenAI.
facts.source_title: How CMOs Are Scaling GenAI in Turbulent Times (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG CMO survey 2026, 'Moving the Agentic Marketing Transformation from Illusion to Reality' (Jun 15, 2026; 300 CMOs plus 50 structured interviews, opinion data): tiers based on observed deployment, not ambition: Leaders 32%, Followers 26%, At-Risk 42%. It proposes a four-layer agentic stack: data, a brand intelligence layer, an agentic layer, and a unified user interface (single pane of glass). Use: place the team on the three tiers and build the brand-intelligence layer first.
facts.source_title: Moving the Agentic Marketing Transformation from Illusion to Reality (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG CMO survey (Jun 15, 2026; 300 CMOs, opinion data): 43% report marketing AI spend above $15 million this year, up from 28%; 31% of B2C and 20% of B2B CMOs report measurable revenue impact; 91% of B2C and 76% of B2B CMOs say no-click AI discovery is reshaping funnels; 94% say CEO expectations have risen. Engagement-based, non-survey figures: 20-30% cost savings and about 3x ROI. Use: set a revenue-impact target for AI, not only a cost target.
facts.source_title: Moving the Agentic Marketing Transformation from Illusion to Reality (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The Agentic Marketing Race Is On' (Nov 25, 2025; survey sample and method not stated): a focused 9-12 month roadmap in four steps: prove the power, build the foundation, scale what works, embed and evolve. BCG says agentic AI can triple marketing ROI, speed and volume, which often translates into 5-10% incremental top-line growth (plus 15-20% cost efficiencies). Data fragmentation is the top barrier CMOs cite to scaling GenAI, and first-party data is called the decisive factor. Use: sequence an AI program in four steps with one quick-win pilot.
facts.source_title: The Agentic Marketing Race Is On (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Art and Algorithms' (Nov 18, 2025; authors' experience with hundreds of CEOs, no formal survey) casts the AI-first CMO as a chief growth architect who owns data inputs, growth platforms and measurement models with the CTO. CEO diagnostic: can the CMO build the AI backbone with the CTO, develop people as much as platforms, go deep on execution, withstand silo resistance, and protect human creativity. Use: frame marketing-AI proposals as joint CMO-CTO work with named data owners.
facts.source_title: Art and Algorithms: What CEOs Should Look For in an AI-First CMO (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The AI-Forward CPG Marketing Organization' (Feb 12, 2026; survey of 100 senior marketing leaders at US and European CPG firms with $1B+ revenue, opinion data): only 13% say GenAI is widely used; nearly 70% have a chief growth officer or equivalent; nearly 60% are centralizing marketing while about half localize; nearly 60% are insourcing GenAI content and retail media planning. One firm saw 25-40% less time on key workflows. Use: expect marketing scope to widen to growth, and design hybrid global-local roles.
facts.source_title: The AI-Forward CPG Marketing Organization (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Why Most CEOs Are Failing Marketing's New Math Test' (Sep 29, 2026; cites 13,000 consumers in 12 markets and BCG's survey of 300 CMOs): five CEO questions: is AI used to spend less or grow more; is there a trusted way to measure impact (upper funnel on leading indicators, lower funnel on sales); are major processes reshaped end to end; is advantage built on knowledge rivals cannot copy; is spend aimed at the emerging customer journey or the known one. Purchase paths grew from about 5 touchpoints a decade ago to over 15. Use: answer all five in the annual plan.
facts.source_title: Why Most CEOs Are Failing Marketing's New Math Test (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG creator-marketing study 'The Power of Authenticity' (Oct 1, 2026; 940 marketers and influencer-agency professionals, opinion data): a $30B+ market growing 1.5x faster than overall marketing budgets; only 15% of marketers are high performers; nearly 70% have no dedicated team. BCG reports 19% lower CPA and 133% higher ROAS for brands that integrate creator marketing effectively (reported, not a controlled test). Among leading companies, 53% name ROI measurement the top challenge and only 6% use advanced attribution. Use: assign one owner and build full-funnel measurement for creators.
facts.source_title: The Power of Authenticity: How Leading Brands Are Pulling Ahead in Creator Marketing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG creator-marketing study (Oct 1, 2026; 940 marketers) lists eight practices: five process (continuous social listening for communities, pick creators for trust not reach, brief with freedom instead of rigid scripts, treat boosting as an investment, full-funnel measurement incl. AI search visibility) and three enablers (single accountable owner, always-on dedicated team, integrated agency model with strategy and measurement kept in-house). Standard mix models undervalue organic impact. Use: score the creator program on the eight practices.
facts.source_title: The Power of Authenticity: How Leading Brands Are Pulling Ahead in Creator Marketing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Measure To Grow' (India edition, Nov 15, 2021; maturity survey across five Indian industries, perspectives from about 20 advertisers and six measurement specialists; BCG and Meta named as industry advisors): digital's share of marketing budgets rose from 12% to 34% in under five years; only 5% of organizations have data good enough for key decisions; 70%+ underinvest in measurement. Firms focused on strategic measurement report up to 60% sales uplift, 10x ROAS and 25% gross-margin impact (self-reported, India only, platform-advised). Use: treat as upper bounds.
facts.source_title: Measure To Grow: Drive double-digit growth by measuring marketing right (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Want Consumer Insights Faster? AI Can Help' (May 29, 2026; respondent counts not stated): GenAI synthetic panels, personas that answer conjoint surveys, predicted real consumers' choices for a new beverage with 92% accuracy after fine-tuning. Use cases: concept screening, attribute selection, pricing and promotion tests. Risk tiers: low-risk decisions on synthetic data, medium with human research, high only as a secondary check. Known failure: respondents inferred the hypothesis and confirmed it. Use: calibrate synthetic panels against real buyers.
facts.source_title: Want Consumer Insights Faster? AI Can Help. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Global Consumers Have Moved On' (Aug 26, 2026; 13,000+ consumers in 12 markets covering about 49% of the world population, 13 categories, 100+ in-depth interviews, 1,000+ brands, opinion data): nearly a third of consumers have used AI in a purchase journey, roughly triple the level 18 months earlier; about 13% buy whatever AI recommends; AI introduced a new brand in roughly 63% of AI-assisted purchase journeys. Use: treat AI as a brand-discovery channel and test visibility in assistants.
facts.source_title: Global Consumers Have Moved On. Has Your Growth Strategy Caught Up? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG consumer survey (Aug 26, 2026; 13,000+ consumers, 12 markets): price decides whether a product is considered, but perceived value decides purchase; the article gives about 67% in its overview and nearly 70% in the body as unwilling to buy an affordable product lacking strong value, and only 14% of 1,000+ analyzed brands consistently win on value. 43% feel overwhelmed by information, over half fully trust no source, 20% completely trust AI, and 60% limit sensitive data shared with it. Use: lead with proof of value and third-party validation.
facts.source_title: Global Consumers Have Moved On. Has Your Growth Strategy Caught Up? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG consumer survey (Aug 26, 2026; 13,000+ consumers, 12 markets): about 30% of households in mature markets are single-person (the overview says one in three), up 6 points since 2010; they spend two to three times more per capita than multi-person homes, yet 50-70% of solo householders say products are not designed for them, and solo shoppers have roughly 30% fewer touchpoints. Nearly four in ten consumers are 'longevity seekers', up 4 points in a year. Use: test solo-household and longevity messaging as distinct segments.
facts.source_title: Global Consumers Have Moved On. Has Your Growth Strategy Caught Up? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'European Consumers Are Still Cutting Back' (Jun 9, 2026; third annual survey, 20,000+ consumers in 11 countries, fielded Apr 2-22, 2026, stated intent): economic pessimism 56% (54% in 2025); 53% worry daily about personal finances (40% in 2024); 63% buy only on discount or seek deals; 62% would switch brands for a better offer; brand reputation ranks only fifth among switching drivers. Only groceries and pet care had positive net spending. Use: lean on offer clarity and value proof; do not assume loyalty.
facts.source_title: European Consumers Are Still Cutting Back (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG European consumer survey (Jun 9, 2026; 20,000+ consumers, 11 countries, stated behavior): regular GenAI use for product discovery quadrupled since 2024 to 8%; general web search is flat to falling in every category; among Gen Z and Millennials 32% use Instagram and 27% TikTok to research fashion vs 11% and 6% of older consumers; 28% of younger consumers buy the same brand vs 44% of older. Stores lead final-purchase influence for 40%. Use: weight social and AI discovery for under-40 audiences.
facts.source_title: European Consumers Are Still Cutting Back (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The AI-Powered Holiday: What Retailers Need To Know for 2026' (Oct 20, 2026; survey sample not stated): 56% of consumers intend to shop with generative AI this Black Friday, up from 51% in 2025 and 35% in 2024; in 46% of purchases where AI plays a role, it introduces a brand the shopper would not otherwise have considered; nearly 70% will not buy an affordable product that does not feel like strong value. BCG recommends simple, no-strings offers over deep discounts buried in exclusions. Use: keep product data complete and machine-readable for AI shoppers.
facts.source_title: The AI-Powered Holiday: What Retailers Need To Know for 2026 (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How Retailers Can Reinvent the Digital Flywheel for Agentic Commerce' (Oct 21, 2026; survey of 50 of the top 300 retailers and 100 top brands, executive opinion data): 68% of retailers expect significant effect within two years; 81% of US and 53% of European consumers expect to use AI agents; only 4% would let an agent buy alone; agent referrals under 1% of visits in late 2025, about 5% by end-2026 projected. 91% fear losing the customer relationship. Use: track agent referral share and protect first-party data.
facts.source_title: How Retailers Can Reinvent the Digital Flywheel for Agentic Commerce (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG agentic-commerce flywheel study (Oct 21, 2026; 50 top retailers, 100 top brands): loyalty and personalization drive 11% of GMV on average (15% in the top quartile). Nearly half of retailers would honor loyalty benefits on agent-made purchases, but only 14% at full parity and 58% at a lower tier. Advice: share product, price and stock data with agents but keep customer identity and loyalty history in-house, and keep exclusive experiences on owned channels. Use: design loyalty perks agents can compare, plus owned-channel extras.
facts.source_title: How Retailers Can Reinvent the Digital Flywheel for Agentic Commerce (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The AI-First Retailer' (Nov 11, 2025; sample not stated) frames three retail strategies as AI platforms begin selling: the destination game (pull shoppers to owned channels), the evaluation game (win the AI agent's recommendation on price, delivery or fit) and a hybrid (sell through AI platforms while keeping the best promotions for owned apps; BCG cites Sephora selling through Instacart but saving its best promotions for its own app). Use: choose a game per category and optimize content for answer engines.
facts.source_title: The AI-First Retailer (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'How New Revenue Streams Are Transforming Traditional Retail' (Jun 25, 2025; retailer TSR review 2019-2024, sample not stated): top-quartile global retailers by revenue returned 16% five-year total shareholder return vs 9% for the industry, and approximately one third of this outperformance came from new revenue streams such as online marketplaces, retail media and data monetization. An effective loyalty program is described as critical for data capture. Association, not proof of cause. Use: treat loyalty data as an asset that funds retail media and offers.
facts.source_title: How New Revenue Streams Are Transforming Traditional Retail (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'The Rise of the B2C Specialty Marketplace' (Jun 13, 2024; survey of 1,500+ consumers in five countries plus Mirakl data): 70% of surveyed consumers prefer specialized marketplaces to everything-stores selling the same products at similar prices; commissions run 8-15% (25-30% in fashion); marketplaces contribute a 7-9% EBITDA margin, and advanced services such as retail media add 3-5 points; retail media can reach 60-70% of collected ad revenue as margin. BCG lists seven essential elements. Use: weigh a niche marketplace or retail-media listing against these margins.
facts.source_title: The Rise of the B2C Specialty Marketplace (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG and Altagamma True-Luxury Global Consumer Insight (press release Jul 8, 2025; sample size not stated): clients spending over EUR 50,000 a year are about 0.1% of clients but generate over 37% of luxury market spending; the page gives 60% and 65% as feeling overwhelmed by impersonal marketing; they get 40-50 communications a month; of nine brands they shop regularly, only two see them as high potential; about 70% of potential clients go unidentified because CRM and segmentation are too basic. Use: segment by value tier and cut message volume.
facts.source_title: True-Luxury Global Consumer Insights 2025 (BCG press release)

facts.statement: BCG and Altagamma True-Luxury Global Consumer Insights, 12th edition (Jul 7, 2026; more than 10,000 respondents, stated behavior): 70% walked away from a purchase because the price felt unjustified; logo visibility was the least important factor across all categories; among aspirational buyers 56% do not know or barely know the brands' creative directors; 15% of top-tier consumers stopped buying from a brand after a change in creative direction; top-tier share of spend rose from 14% to 24%. Use: sell craft and quality, not logos.
facts.source_title: Luxury Is Back on Track, With Healthier Foundations (And AI Is Here To Stay) (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG and Altagamma luxury study (Jul 7, 2026; more than 10,000 respondents): 87% use AI weekly and around 80% of those research luxury with it; net trust in AI is 29 points, roughly twice social media and influencers and below only a brand's own website (42 points). 83% would view a brand using AI positively or the same, and 77% would keep buying; resistance is concentrated almost entirely among boomers in Western markets. Use: start with AI for support and imagery and disclose it on campaigns and advisor messages.
facts.source_title: Luxury Is Back on Track, With Healthier Foundations (And AI Is Here To Stay) (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with WWD, 'How Gen Z and Gen Alpha Are Rewiring the Fashion Industry' (Oct 29, 2025; 9,000+ consumer responses, 50,000 social conversations, five executive interviews): consumers aged 28 and under are projected to be about 40% of the US fashion market over the next decade; they are experimental rather than brand-loyal; the key takeaways say 40% of younger consumers use AI to shop. BCG urges a self-reinforcing flywheel in a social-media-driven journey instead of a linear funnel. Use: replace funnel KPIs with a flywheel view for youth audiences.
facts.source_title: How Gen Z and Gen Alpha Are Rewiring the Fashion Industry (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with Vestiaire Collective, 'Resale's Next Chapter' (Oct 9, 2025; 7,800 resale-engaged consumers from Vestiaire's community, so skewed toward resale fans): secondhand is about 8% of fashion and luxury sales, growing about 10% a year and about three times faster than firsthand; 66% say resale helped them discover or first buy a brand (59% in 2022), and around 80% of Gen Z did so; affordability is a key reason for nearly 80% of buyers. Use: treat branded resale as an acquisition channel for new customers.
facts.source_title: Resale's Next Chapter (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Why Owning the Moment Wins in a Changing Alcohol Market' (May 28, 2026; BCG BevAlc consumer survey Oct 2025, N=2,768, a separate supplemental survey Nov 2025, N=505, and NielsenIQ US in-store data 2022-2025): the occasion of use is the most powerful driver of consumer choice, so brands should be built around occasions. RTD cocktails grew over 20% a year (CAGR 2022-2025); purpose-built brands above $10M in 2025 revenue hold about 80% of the segment; social media is Gen Z's main channel for finding new brands. Use: test occasion-led positioning.
facts.source_title: Why Owning the Moment Wins in a Changing Alcohol Market (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'Will AI Become the Best Car Sales Advisor?' (Sep 18, 2025; co-authored with OpenAI staff, sample not stated, projections): by 2030 over 40 million car-buying journeys a year will be meaningfully shaped by GenAI, first as a product advisor, then as a deal finder comparing cost of ownership and financing. BCG estimates fast OEMs could gain up to 20% of top line and slow ones lose up to 15%. Use: make brand and offer data legible to AI assistants before the deal-finder stage.
facts.source_title: Will AI Become the Best Car Sales Advisor? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG 'AI Was Made for RevOps' (Sep 4, 2025; authors' experience, no formal sample): three layers of AI in revenue operations: predictive (segmentation, churn, now a baseline), GenAI (outreach content, coaching, pipeline inspection, RFP and contract automation, account planning) and agentic (sales assistants, autonomous lead management, self-optimizing cadences). Firms report up to 20% faster RFP turnaround. Six prep steps: data and governance, standard processes, one platform, focus on value, continuous testing, people. Use: sequence RevOps AI predictive to GenAI to agentic.
facts.source_title: AI Was Made for RevOps (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG and The Consumer Goods Forum, 'AI in CPG and Retail' (Jun 24, 2026; 39 senior executives, a small opinion sample): 75% of CPGs are still piloting and 18% scale impact, vs 45% of retailers scaling; full AI scale-up could add roughly 220-350 bps EBIT for CPGs and 180-360 bps for retailers, though some is reinvested; more than half do not formally measure ROI of consumer AI. Use: set baseline and scale thresholds before any marketing AI pilot.
facts.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Most Innovative Companies 2025, 'In Disruptive Times, the Resilient Win' (Jun 26, 2025; 18 editions over about two decades): the share of firms calling themselves innovation leaders has fallen despite innovation being a near-universal priority; mentions of digital innovation on earnings calls doubled 2005-2024, and 25 serial innovators mention it nearly four times as often as peers. BCG expects agentic AI to speed innovation and reshape teams. Use: benchmark product and marketing innovation against digital fluency, not R&D spend.
facts.source_title: In Disruptive Times, the Resilient Win: Most Innovative Companies 2025 (BCG)

facts.statement: KPMG Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24 (81,725 customers, 821,824 evaluations, 2,726 brands, 21 countries): the share of organisations meeting customer expectations fell 4% in 2023, and only 2 of the 21 countries saw customer satisfaction rise. Use: when benchmarking a CX score, assume the market baseline is falling, so holding a score flat is a relative gain; report change against the market as well as the absolute level. Page is undated; January 2024 is inferred from its download link.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24

facts.statement: KPMG Global CEE 2023-24 named a different leader in almost every market: Apple in Singapore, first direct then Lush in the UK, Fielmann in Germany (top for a fourth straight year), H-E-B in the US, Amazon in Italy, Emirates in the UAE, Nike in Mexico and Vietnam, KBank in Thailand, MAIF in France. The leaders span banks, retail and hardware, so no single sector owns CX excellence. Use: pick CX role models by market and sector, not from a global list, when writing positioning or journey benchmarks.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24

facts.statement: KPMG Global CEE 2023-24, results by market: Expectations was the pillar that fell in Japan and in Germany; Resolution gave Japan its lowest average pillar scores; Personalisation was the top driver in Australia; Time and Effort was the strongest pillar in Slovakia; Thailand declined on every pillar. Use: before copying a CX playbook, test which of the six pillars actually moves loyalty in the target market and fund that one first.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24

facts.statement: KPMG Global CEE 2023-24, telecoms: industry CEE scores fell 3% in 2023 and only the Value pillar held up; of 129 telco brands studied, just 4 reached the top 10 of any of the 21 countries. A KPMG survey of US consumers (sample not stated) found 41% want lower costs for the same service. Use: in low-differentiation subscription categories, a price-and-value promise plus visible service recovery is the realistic route to stand out.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24

facts.statement: KPMG Global CEE 2023-24 on AI in CX: customers want technology that carries the brand's character with a human available when needed. Named examples include first direct's chatbot Dot, Lush's Marvin and American Express's generative assistant, plus claims triage by language processing at USAA. Italian and wider European consumers were wary of AI, and the EU AI Act may limit some uses; trust and data privacy were the main risks. Use: name and voice-design service bots, and always show a route to a person.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global Customer Experience Excellence 2023-24

facts.statement: KPMG Italy Customer Experience Excellence 2023 (seventh Italian edition; 5,000 consumers rating 220 brands, fielded June 2023): the CEE score fell 3.4%, from 7.57 to 7.31, in every sector; yet 69 companies climbed the ranking versus 53 in 2022. KPMG names a Personalization Paradox, the tension between privacy and demand for tailored service. Use: expect rising expectations to lower scores even when service improves; report rank movement alongside score.
facts.source_title: KPMG Italy: The Wow Normal, customer experience in the age of AI

facts.statement: KPMG UK Customer Experience Excellence 2023 (13,143 UK consumers, fieldwork 8 June to 3 July 2023, 376 brands; released 8 November 2023): the UK score fell from 7.37 to 7.09 and 64% of brands declined. Top five: first direct, Lush, American Express (up 27 places), John Lewis and Nationwide. Use: assume the market baseline is falling when reading a CX score, and model CX impact before approving service cuts.
facts.source_title: KPMG UK: Brands bet on AI as UK customer satisfaction levels slide in 2023

facts.statement: KPMG UK CEE 2023 sector change in score versus 2022: non-grocery retail -2%, financial services -2%, travel and hotels -3%, grocery -4%, restaurants and fast food -5%, telecoms -5%, public sector -5%, entertainment and leisure -7%, utilities -7%, logistics -8%. KPMG's AI adoption index put financial services first and the public sector first on responsible AI use, with talent and skills the main barrier. Use: compare a client's CX score with its own sector's decline, not the cross-sector average.
facts.source_title: KPMG UK: Brands bet on AI as UK customer satisfaction levels slide in 2023

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Spring/Summer 2025 (1,516 US consumers, nationally representative; released 24 April 2025): 79% expected tariffs to push prices up, 50% were cutting purchases, 49% were hunting deals, 39% of households reported lower income, and cuts were planned in 15 of 17 tracked categories (only groceries and autos rising). Fast-food visits were up 26% while casual dining was down 38%. Use: in a price-anxious market lead with value proof, bundles and trade-down options rather than premium cues.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer Pulse Survey, Summer 2025

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Spring/Summer 2025 (1,516 US consumers): 43% were uncomfortable with companies using generative AI to analyse their personal data, 34% comfortable, 23% neutral; financial incentives and user control eased concern. 27% now buy direct-to-consumer in personal care, apparel and food, and 56% say online ads do not influence them versus 44% more likely to buy after seeing ads. Use: pair personalisation with visible consent, control and a clear reward; do not assume ads move most buyers.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer Pulse Survey, Summer 2025

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Holiday 2025 (US consumers; released 29 September 2025): planned average holiday spend was $847, up 4.6% from $810, but households above $200,000 planned +9% while those under $50,000 planned -2%. 52% were seeking promotions more actively, 57% had noticed higher decoration prices, 38% planned dollar-store visits (up seven points), and spending on oneself rose 20% to $379. Use: split holiday offers by income tier; premium bundles for high-income, price-anchored deals for the rest.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer Pulse Survey, Holiday 2025

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Holiday 2025 (release of 29 September 2025; sample size not stated on that page): 41% used AI to research purchases and another 22% were interested, with use higher among Gen Z (56%) and Millennials (62%). About a third had bought after seeing content on YouTube and a third after content on Instagram (reported separately), and nearly 70% had bought after seeing something on Amazon. Use: treat AI answers and marketplace listings as discovery surfaces and keep product data and reviews strong there.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Americans chose to spend on themselves and travel this holiday season

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Summer 2026 (1,544 US consumers, fielded 27 February to 18 March 2026): 93% reported a higher cost of living and over 7 in 10 said their costs rose by more than 10%, up from 3 in 10 a year earlier. Planned travel spend was down 7% even though 60% still planned a trip; 38% of travellers were trading down; generative AI use for trip planning rose from 14% to 27% in two years. Use: expect trade-down and shorter, cheaper trips; test value-led offers and AI-visible travel content.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer Pulse Survey, Summer 2026

facts.statement: KPMG Consumer Pulse, Back-to-School 2026 (2,297 US consumers, fielded 29 May to 18 June 2026): average spend per child projected at $324 versus $294 a year earlier; among those spending more, 80% blamed higher prices, and 37% said they were financially worse off than last year versus 27% better off. The page also quotes a 6% rise, so treat the exact rate with care. Use: frame back-to-school offers around essentials and price protection; higher spend reflects inflation, not extra demand.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer Pulse Survey, Back-to-School 2026

facts.statement: KPMG Tariff Pulse Survey, February 2026 (300 US C-suite leaders at firms with $1B+ revenue, fielded February and March 2026): the share passing more than half of tariff costs to customers rose from 13% in May 2025 to 34%, and 55% planned further increases of up to 15% within six months. KPMG says tariffs are now embedded in standard pricing models. Use: when advising B2B or retail clients on pricing, assume cost pass-through is normalised and focus on value communication and segment-level price moves.
facts.source_title: KPMG: 2026 Tariff Survey

facts.statement: KPMG tariff pricing survey, September 2025 (300 US senior executives): 66% passed up to half of tariff costs to customers and 9% absorbed all; 42% planned rises up to 5% and 29% rises of 6-15% over six months; customer pushback was a key issue for 36%, up from 29% in May. 40% had added dynamic pricing in contracts, and 49% used AI for pricing and cost modelling, up from 41%. Use: pair any price rise with a pushback plan and contract clauses that allow indexed pricing.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Pricing agility in focus, US executives rethink strategies amid ongoing tariffs

facts.statement: KPMG tariff survey for consumer goods (300 US C-suite executives, fielded 22 May to 11 June 2025; the consumer-goods cut is about 30 respondents and the page footnotes disagree on that sector label, so treat as small-sample): 28% named price rises as their main response, 77% had passed up to half of tariff cost to consumers (73% across all sectors), 57% planned further increases versus 40% elsewhere, and 43% reported gross margin falls of 1-5%. Use: model volume loss from trade-down before approving price rises in consumer categories.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Consumer goods companies confront tariff turbulence

facts.statement: KPMG tariff survey for retail (300 US senior executives, 30 in retail, September 2025): 93% of retailers had passed up to 100% of cost increases to customers, with typical rises of 6-15%; 83% adjusted pricing or cost structures and 40% reported gross margin declines. Only 30% rated their tariff response effective, 37% neutral, 33% ineffective. Small sector sample. Use: treat retail pass-through as common but unproven; test elasticity by category rather than copying a blanket rise.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Retailers recalibrate to meet the tariff challenge

facts.statement: Accenture Business of Experience study (1,550+ executives, a quarter CEOs, 21 countries, 22 industries; collected November 2019 to January 2020, published 1 December 2020): firms that organise around experience for customers, employees and society say their profitability growth is at least six times that of peers. Leaders were twice as likely as others to turn customer data into action (55% vs 26%) and 61% had a clear view of the platforms they need versus 27%. Self-reported executive data. Use: cite as directional only; sell experience as a cross-functional programme.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Business of Experience research

facts.statement: Accenture Business of Experience (published 1 December 2020; 1,550+ executives): 77% of CEOs said they would fundamentally change how their company interacts with customers to drive growth, against 56% of COOs, 53% of chief strategy officers and 51% of CFOs. Accenture reads this as experience moving from a marketing topic to a CEO agenda. Executive opinion data. Use: when pitching CX programmes, secure a CEO or COO sponsor and tie the case to growth, not to marketing metrics.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Business of Experience research

facts.statement: Life centricity (Accenture, 18 October 2022; 1,700+ C-suite executives, 14 countries, 19 industries, fielded February to August 2022): an enterprise-wide growth approach that engages customers across their whole lives and adapts as priorities change. Accenture reports life-centric firms had revenue growth about nine points above laggards, were almost five times more likely to beat peers on customer lifetime value, and 3 times more likely on speed to market. Executive self-report. Use: organise segments by life moments, not products, and measure lifetime value.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Life centricity report, press release

facts.statement: Accenture Life Reimagined, 16th Global Consumer Pulse (25,444 consumers aged 18+ in 22 countries, online, December 2020 to February 2021; published 23 June 2021): 50% said they had reimagined their behaviours and values. Among those reimagined consumers, 68% would switch travel brands over weak health and safety, 57% would leave retailers lacking fast, flexible delivery, over half would switch brands without clear service contact options, and 76% were drawn to ethical sourcing. Use: make service access and delivery promises explicit in brand claims; they are switching triggers.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Consumer values and buying motivations have fundamentally changed

facts.statement: Accenture's five new buying factors (Life Reimagined, 2021, 25,444 consumers, 22 countries): beyond price and quality, choices now turn on health and safety, service and personal care, ease and convenience, product origin (sourcing, production, transport, environmental and community impact), and trust and reputation. Accenture says these once mattered mainly to Gen Z and Millennials and now matter across all ages. Use: audit a brand's proof for each factor, and add the weak ones to the message house and landing proof.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Consumer values and buying motivations have fundamentally changed

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2024 (survey of 15,227 people in 21 countries, August 2023; published 17 October 2023): cost-cutting through price rises, lower quality, more subscriptions and weaker service is straining brand relationships, and nearly half of customers feel less valued when they struggle to reach unhelpful service. 35% see app designs as indistinguishable across brands, nearly 40% of 18-24s. Use: guard service quality in cost programmes and invest in distinctive design and voice.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Life Trends 2024 forecasts a decade of continued transformative change

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2024 (15,227 people, 21 countries, August 2023; published 17 October 2023): 77% were familiar with conversational AI, with comfort using it at 42% for product recommendations, 44% for work tasks and 33% for health and wellness advice. Nearly a third said technology complicates life as much as it simplifies it; 31% said constant notifications control how they use personal tech, and a third were removing notifications. Use: keep push and notification cadence low and opt-in; do not assume AI product advice is accepted by most.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Life Trends 2024 forecasts a decade of continued transformative change

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2025 (24,295 people in 22 countries, July 2024; 16 October 2024): 62% said trust is an important factor when choosing which brands to engage with, over half question online content more than before, and 33% had faced a deepfake attack or scam in the past year. Trend one, Cost of Hesitations, urges brands to build beacons of trust into communications, commerce and products. Use: add verifiable proof, authenticity cues and scam-protection messages to high-stakes journeys.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Life Trends 2025 predicts new dynamics of trust

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2025 (Impatience Economy trend; 24,295 people in 22 countries, July 2024; release of 16 October 2024): three in four consumers wish companies would respond faster to their changing needs, and over half now prefer quick answers and guidance. Use: prioritise response speed and concise guidance in the funnel.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Life Trends 2025 predicts new dynamics of trust

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2026 (online survey of 25,000+ people in 23 countries, 800 executives in 7 countries, 100+ interviews; page undated, 2026 edition) names five trends: stability premium, human journeys, finding Neo (AI and human experience), good vibrations (play and well-being) and coming of age (the 40+ market). Use: use as a themes checklist for brand and campaign planning, and check each trend against the target segment before acting.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Life Trends 2026

facts.statement: Accenture Life Trends 2026 statistics (25,000+ consumers, 800 executives; fieldwork dates not stated): 31% of daily AI users say AI made them notice how similar brand messaging sounds; 77% want brands to create products for well-being and joy; 80% of executives say marketing must pivot to reflect older generations' influence; 82% call spotting subtle offline shifts in behaviour important. Use: test messaging for sameness against AI-written competitors, and add 55+ segments to targeting.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Life Trends 2026

facts.statement: Accenture, Customer service on the brink (published 13 March 2025; sample not stated): 87% say they are likely to avoid a brand after one bad experience, 35% distrust AI and fear lower service quality, and only 18% say technology significantly improved their service in the past year. 64% of executives are trading off cost efficiency against satisfaction. Use: set a floor on service quality in AI and cost programmes, and publish a human escalation route.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Customer service on the brink

facts.statement: Accenture, Customer service on the brink (13 March 2025; sample not stated): leading firms are 82% more likely to use gen AI to help agents resolve issues, 87% more likely to personalise digital channels, and organisations with the strongest service are 87% more likely to say service informs marketing strategy. Only 14% of executives regularly use data-driven insights to improve service. Use: feed service-contact themes into marketing messages and journeys, and start with agent-assist AI.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Customer service on the brink

facts.statement: Accenture, Me, my brand and AI (Consumer Pulse, 18,000 people in 14 countries, published 3 June 2025): 72% interact with gen AI, 83% of active users rely on it when choosing a product or service, 36% of them call it a good friend, and 34% of consumers would switch to brands that make them feel special. Brand advice: be the trusted guide, loyal companion and second self; move from personalisation to proactivity. Use: build emotional proof points and proactive service into lifecycle plans.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Me, my brand and AI

facts.statement: Accenture Consumer Pulse 2026 names four brand positions in agent-led markets (25,590 consumers, 16 countries, January 2026): create a consumer-trusted agent, partner with existing agents, build authority through verified claims, or act as fulfilment partner. Case: Oreo appeared in only 10% of AI chatbot cookie recommendations, so Mondelez is restructuring a $3.5 billion digital commerce effort around machine-readable product content. Use: choose one position per brand and make product data and claims machine-readable.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Talk to my AI agent

facts.statement: Accenture Consumer Pulse 2026 (25,590 consumers, 16 countries, 7-22 January 2026): openness to autonomous purchasing is highest for recurring services such as insurance, telecom and utilities (12.5%) and lowest for travel (7.0%); collaboration with an agent is 80-88% in every category. Delegation is highest when prompting a need and in negotiation, and lowest in payments. 43% put budget and value first when instructing agents. Use: prioritise agent-ready offers in recurring services and keep payments human-confirmed.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Talk to my AI agent

facts.statement: Accenture Consumer Pulse 2026 on loyalty and value (25,590 consumers, 16 countries): loyalty persists but is conditional and enforced by the agent; 56% would tell their agent which brands to consider; 26% of active gen AI users bought a pricier item because AI raised their confidence and say it grew their basket. When fulfilment falls short, consumers form one verdict on the whole experience. Use: protect fulfilment accuracy and recovery speed as brand assets, and use agent-visible proof to defend price.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Talk to my AI agent

facts.statement: Accenture, Agentic commerce: Make your brand unmissable (28 April 2026; consumer survey September 2025, simulation February 2026, executive survey January 2026; samples not stated): 90% of frequent AI users in North America would consider switching from a preferred brand if their assistant offered a better one, up to 45% of shoppers may move half of commerce into agent ecosystems within two years, and 25% of executives expect AI agents to be their top content audience in three years. Use: plan for agent audiences and test brand visibility in assistants.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Agentic commerce, make your brand unmissable

facts.statement: Accenture's agentic commerce playbook (28 April 2026) distinguishes horizontal agents (general, cross-category) from vertical ones (deep in one category), and two brand strategies: choice of agents (structure offers so agents can see and select them) and agent of choice (be the agent people and other agents turn to). It suggests operating KPIs: exceptions per thousand transactions, cost to serve, and how often agents choose or bypass the brand, governed by a cross-functional control tower. Use: add agent-selection rate to the marketing scorecard.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Agentic commerce, make your brand unmissable

facts.statement: Accenture Holiday Shopping 2026 (20th annual survey; 16,000+ shoppers in 10 countries including 4,048 in the US; fielded 13 August to 1 September; published 16 October 2026): average planned holiday spend is $737, up 12% (the page does not tie this figure to the US alone); 80% of US shoppers plan to spend the same or more versus 87% in 2025; 53% cite rising costs; 1 in 2 lean toward value and efficiency; over 50% start before October. Use: open holiday campaigns earlier and lead with value messaging.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Holiday Shopping 2026

facts.statement: Accenture Holiday Shopping 2026 (16,000+ shoppers, 10 countries; published 16 October 2026): 4 in 10 will use gen AI for holiday shopping, up from 3 in 10; top uses are deal-finding (39%), comparing options (31%) and picking the best retailer (30%). 3 in 5 US shoppers prefer retailer or brand AI tools to public platforms, and nearly 3 in 4 want agents to buy only from preferred or familiar brands. Shoppers would let an agent spend $102 without approval. Use: build owned AI shopping assistants and keep brand familiarity strong.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Holiday Shopping 2026

facts.statement: Accenture's total enterprise reinvention page (12 January 2024) describes a bank that delivered 16 million hyper-personalised offerings within three months after building a generative AI marketing solution; the client is unnamed and results are Accenture-reported. The page also cites a 183% rise in the rate of change facing businesses since 2019 (Pulse of Change Index) and says Reinventors among companies above $50bn revenue quadrupled in the past year. Use: cite as a vendor-reported case only; run a holdout test before promising similar lift.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Total enterprise reinvention

facts.statement: Accenture, Making reinvention real with gen AI (6 March 2025; 2,000+ client projects and surveys of 3,000+ C-level executives): 36% of executives have scaled gen AI solutions and only 13% report significant enterprise-level value. Winners were 2.9 times more likely to have a comprehensive data strategy, 4.5 times more likely to invest in agentic architecture, and had 2.5 times higher ROI with executive buy-in. Use: gate marketing and sales AI pilots on data readiness and executive sponsorship, not on tool choice.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Making reinvention real with gen AI

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 11th wave (EY page dated Nov 2022): EY sorts consumers into five tribes by first priority: affordability, planet, experience, health, society. Affordability-first and planet-first are tied as the largest tribes at about 25% of consumers worldwide; experience-first is the largest in Asia (28%); society-first is the smallest in most regions. 58% of planet-first consumers would pay more for sustainably produced goods. The page does not state sample size, markets or fieldwork dates. The tribes are EY's own survey construct. Use: segment by stated priority and test one message per tribe.
facts.source_title: EY: Five types of consumer that you need to understand

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 11th wave (Nov 2022): EY describes each tribe differently. Affordability-first consumers are frugal, prefer in-store shopping and are wary of sharing personal data. Experience-first consumers are the most open to digital tools such as social commerce. Health-first consumers are worried about grocery costs (61%). Society-first consumers value community and ethics, and 70% base purchases on a company's ethical behaviour. EY's takeaway: serve shared needs and tailor offers to each tribe's motivation. Use: match loyalty mechanics to the tribe rather than one programme for all.
facts.source_title: EY: Five types of consumer that you need to understand

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 12th edition (21,000 consumers, 27 markets, release 16 May 2023): affordability became the largest tribe at 35% (up 10 points since Oct 2022), health first rose to 24% from 17%, planet first fell to 16% from 25%. 55% said brands are no longer important, 74% had noticed shrinkflation, 49% planned to buy only essentials, and 66% would share data to get cheaper alternatives. Opinion data. Use: expect sustainability messaging to lose pull as cost worry rises; lead with value proof and honest pack-size communication.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: consumers losing trust and turning away from brands amid cost-of-living crisis

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 13th edition (EY Southeast Asia release, March 2024): among Southeast Asian consumers, 89% worry about living costs, 69% buy only essentials, 77% take part in big sales events and 71% delay purchases until the next one. 56% prefer shopping mostly online versus 4% mostly in store. Only 19% say they understand AI well and 29% trust AI-generated promotions. EY advises building trust in AI through data transparency. Use: label AI-made offers openly and plan promotion calendars around sale events.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: consumers in Southeast Asia learning to live with less

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 15th edition (20,235 consumers, 26 countries, Jan-Feb 2025; EY article 27 Mar 2025): EY splits consumers into 24% brand loyalists, 58% brand switchers and 18% brand agnostics. Gen Z has the highest switcher share (64%), making it the most exposed group. Only 12% strongly agree brand messaging reflects their needs and values. Opinion data. Use: size the switcher pool as the main battleground and test messages on Gen Z separately.
facts.source_title: EY: What it takes to maintain brand relevance in an era of endless choice

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 15th edition (20,235 consumers, 26 countries, Jan-Feb 2025): 78% have noticed shrinkflation and 77% changed purchasing when prices rose. Over 64% see more private label on shelves and 36% of those who try it do not plan to return to brands. 56% would leave a favourite brand if it were unavailable. 65% still call brands important. Opinion data. Use: guard availability and visible quality cues, since supply gaps hand buyers to rivals.
facts.source_title: EY: What it takes to maintain brand relevance in an era of endless choice

facts.statement: EY brand-relevance playbook from the 15th Future Consumer Index (EY article, 27 Mar 2025): five moves. Get pricing right with price-pack architecture; prioritise operational excellence including supply resilience and quality control; make innovation deliver real consumer value rather than marketing; build AI-driven visibility so brands appear in digital discovery; pursue strategic M&A in high-growth, high-margin categories. 48% of switchers would return for better taste, quality or performance, 36% for better value. Use: treat AI-discovery visibility and pack-price ladders as brand tasks.
facts.source_title: EY: What it takes to maintain brand relevance in an era of endless choice

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, Sept 2024 (1,200 large-company CEOs, 20 countries, July-Aug 2024, FT Longitude; EY article 4 Sep 2024): 36% named changing customer needs and expectations, and 38% named emerging technology including AI, as disruptive forces. Leveraging emerging technology for an innovation edge drew the highest response among priorities at 55%. Executive opinion survey. Use: treat customer-need tracking as a standing input to the growth plan.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook: How bolder CEOs take charge to shape their future with confidence

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, Oct 2023 (1,200 CEOs, fieldwork Sep-Oct 2023): 99% planned to invest in generative AI and 70% said they must act now to avoid giving rivals an edge. 92% had completed at least one of eight AI initiatives, but only 17% had completed more than half. 66% expected higher revenue growth in 2024. Executive opinion survey. Use: benchmark a client's AI marketing roadmap against this early shallow-adoption baseline when judging progress.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook: Is the AI buzz creating too much noise for CEOs?

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, May 2025 (1,200 CEOs, fieldwork Mar-Apr 2025): 54% had delayed a planned investment and 50% were very or extremely worried about tariffs hitting operations and sales. Among the top five tariff responses, passing costs to customers through price changes was the least selected. 71% said inflation remains a challenge. Executive opinion survey. Use: when drafting pricing advice under cost shocks, offer non-price levers first (sourcing, pack size, mix) and test price moves narrowly.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook: How do CEOs chart a path to growth

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, Sept 2025 (1,200 CEOs, fieldwork Aug 2025; article 18 Sep 2025): 72% see localisation as a lasting strategic shift, and nearly 75% are either localising or have localised part of their production. The CEO Confidence Index stands at 83, up from 76.5 in May 2025. Technology disruption and AI integration risk ranks as the top threat to financial targets. Executive opinion survey. Use: plan local offers and proof points as a default for global brands.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook: Does today's disruption provide the blueprint for tomorrow's growth

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, Jan 2026 (1,200 CEOs, 21 countries, fieldwork Nov-Dec 2025; article 20 Jan 2026): the top results CEOs want from transformation are operations and productivity (43%), customer engagement and retention (40%), product and process innovation (37%) and faster top-line growth (36%). 52% are in a significant transformation and 45% plan to begin one in 2026 (97% together). About 20% report AI returns well above expectations. Executive opinion survey. Use: frame retention work as a board-level growth priority.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook 2026: How do CEOs reimagine enterprises

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, May 2026 (1,200 CEOs, fieldwork Mar-Apr 2026, published 4 May 2026): customer service and experience is the area where CEOs most often report measurable enterprise-level AI impact (42%). About 80% are raising AI investment versus 2025, yet only 11% say AI impact is tied to financial reporting and reviewed regularly by senior management. Executive opinion survey. Use: start AI proof-of-value in customer experience and wire its results into the finance review cycle.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook: Can disciplined ambition unlock growth in a volatile global economy

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, Oct 2026 (1,200 CEOs, 21 countries): only 16% of CEOs have comprehensive, real-time visibility into AI costs and high confidence in returns. Almost a quarter say productivity gains are absorbed by complexity, regulation, risk and new work. 69% favour strengthening the core over disruption. AI-enabled tools (50%) and process redesign (46%) are the top productivity drivers. Executive opinion survey. Use: show AI cost against return in every AI pitch.
facts.source_title: EY-Parthenon CEO Outlook, October 2026

facts.statement: EY State of Consumer Products 2026 (850+ senior executives, 24 markets, companies from US$250m to US$20b+ revenue, 28 Jan to 18 Feb 2026, run by Oxford Economics): retail-sales growth of mega brands fell from 13.1% a year (2020-22) to 3.8% (2023-25), while small brands held steady near 8%. Mega brands' share change went from +2.6 to -1.2 points; small brands' from -0.3 to +1.9. Use: show clients that scale no longer protects share and that small, focused brands are taking it.
facts.source_title: EY State of Consumer Products 2026

facts.statement: EY Consumer Products Dynamics Research 2026 (850+ senior executives, 24 markets, 28 Jan to 18 Feb 2026, Oxford Economics; release 15 Sep 2026): 86% of consumer products CEOs say future advantage will rest on provable consumer superiority and value rather than brand scale alone. 73% say 2026 AI spend is up on 2025, but only 12% say AI impact is linked to financial reporting and regularly reviewed. Executive opinion survey. Use: replace brand-size claims in messaging with demonstrable product and value proof.
facts.source_title: EY report: consumer products companies can capture growth by turning supply transformation into faster actions

facts.statement: EY European CPG Operating Model Survey (350 decision-makers in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain and Sweden, June 2025, plus 30+ C-suite interviews; EY article 13 Oct 2025): 63% say current operating models fall short on speed and adaptability, and about 70% cite inability to keep pace with volatility as a transformation barrier. EY's advice has three dimensions (redesign for growth, faster working, leadership mindset) and five priorities, the first being to rewire marketing. Europe only. Use: check marketing-finance-sales handoffs before media spend.
facts.source_title: EY: Three ways CPG can create an operating model that reignites growth

facts.statement: EY webcast on consumer-products sales and marketing (URL dated 2026/05; presenters Jens Weng and Andrew Cosgrove): EY states that only 11% of CP companies see sales and marketing as a strong, unified growth engine (sample not stated). It argues AI makes an integrated function possible, with decision engines and agent-to-agent negotiation, but that operating model and governance matter as much as the technology. Use: set a joint sales-marketing scorecard before adding AI tools.
facts.source_title: EY webcast: How CP sales and marketing can reclaim brand relevance in an AI world

facts.statement: EY four 2030 AI scenarios for consumer products (EY article 16 Dec 2025): Transform (AI becomes the operating system), Growth (steady gains and smarter personalisation), Constraint (setbacks and regulation) and Collapse (AI concentrates in a few firms). EY pairs them with the NAVI lens (nonlinearity, acceleration, volatility, interconnectedness) and a six-step path from envision to scale. It cites its AI Pulse Survey: by late 2024, 54% of executives across industries said they were falling short as AI leaders. Use: stress-test AI personalisation plans against all four.
facts.source_title: EY: How to shape the future of AI in consumer products

facts.statement: EY and Asahi Europe & International (EY alliance page, undated): EY and Asahi co-designed an AI-enabled tool for revenue growth management and trade promotion optimisation, built on Microsoft Azure and integrating with SAP. By 2025 it had been adopted across five European markets, daily use was growing 60% year on year, and a Romanian sales team received a full analysis and recommendations on hundreds of promotions within 24 hours. Vendor-authored case, no independent audit. Use: model promotion-planning pilots on descriptive, prescriptive and predictive layers.
facts.source_title: EY: How AI-led transformation helped a major brewer grow

facts.statement: EY Global AI Sentiment Study, 2nd wave (18,152 people, 23 markets, EY Studio+, article 26 Mar 2026): in the past six months 10% used AI agents to buy products for them and 11% let AI refill carts and buy automatically. As hypotheticals, 36% would like AI to apply checkout discounts and 34% an assistant to settle service issues alone. Seven in ten agree human oversight stays essential, and nearly three-quarters fear they cannot tell real from fake. Opinion data. Use: build agent-readable offers and discount rules, and keep a visible human route.
facts.source_title: EY: As AI moves from advice to authority, who defines its limits?

facts.statement: PwC 2024 Trust Survey (US; fielded early 2024; reported as 548 business executives, 2,515 consumers and 2,039 employees; published March 2024): 90% of executives believe customers highly trust their company, but only 30% of consumers say so. The 60-point gap is wider than the 57 points in 2022 and 2023. In consumer markets 92% of executives claim high customer trust versus 32% of consumers. 'High trust' means 8-10 on a 10-point scale. Use: measure trust from the customer side and report the gap as a KPI.
facts.source_title: PwC's 2024 Trust Survey

facts.statement: PwC 2024 Trust Survey (US): only 39% of financial-services executives strongly agree their company has formal metrics to monitor stakeholder trust, below the 48% average across all executives. PwC notes many firms say they measure trust but the metrics are often subjective, and recommends a common set of formal trust metrics. Use: add a formal trust metric to brand dashboards before claiming trust as a differentiator.
facts.source_title: PwC's 2024 Trust Survey: customer trust in your sector

facts.statement: PwC 29th Global CEO Survey (4,454 CEOs in 95 countries and territories, fieldwork 30 Sep to 10 Nov 2025, published 19 Jan 2026): only 30% are very or extremely confident about revenue growth over the next 12 months, down from 38% a year earlier and 56% in 2022, a five-year low. Executive opinion. Use: expect tight growth budgets and justify new-segment bets with early revenue evidence.
facts.source_title: PwC's 29th Global CEO Survey

facts.statement: PwC 29th Global CEO Survey (4,454 CEOs, Sep-Nov 2025, published 19 Jan 2026): only 12% of CEOs said AI delivered both revenue and cost benefits, a further 33% saw a gain on just one of the two, and 56% reported no significant financial impact. Self-reported perception, not measured deployment. Use: when selling AI marketing, set a revenue or cost target and a baseline first, since most firms have not seen a return yet.
facts.source_title: PwC's 29th Global CEO Survey

facts.statement: PwC Voice of the Consumer 2025 (21,075 consumers, 28 countries and territories, Jan-Feb 2025; executive interviews May 2025): PwC pages put concern about ultra-processed foods or pesticides at roughly 60%, with some pages giving 62%, and one page says it ranks above price, nutrition and sustainability. In Ireland 71% were extremely or very concerned about food cost versus 60% in the other 28 countries. Opinion data, food-led. Use: back health and origin claims with proof.
facts.source_title: PwC Voice of the Consumer 2025

facts.statement: PwC Pulse Survey, CMO insight (survey fielded 15-22 May 2024 among 673 executives and board members at Fortune 1000 and private companies; CMO page 17 Jun 2024): nearly half (48%) are focusing on building customer trust through privacy and consent, and 76% of CMOs say complying with privacy regulations is a challenge. CMOs see AI as the lever for transforming the business model. Executive opinion survey. Use: put consent and data-use transparency into the plan as an owned trust task.
facts.source_title: PwC Pulse Survey: CMO findings

facts.statement: The Haier Road to Growth (Fischer, Lago and Liu, strategy+business, 27 Apr 2015): Haier has held the largest worldwide white-goods market share since 2011. Self-organising units of roughly 10-20 people carry profit-and-loss responsibility. The Tianzun air conditioner concept grew out of 30 million+ responses on QZone, Tencent and other platforms. A Haier executive says water-purifier sales rose fourfold after an online water-quality resource launched (unverified account). Use: copy the open-data-as-marketing move.
facts.source_title: strategy+business: The Haier Road to Growth

facts.statement: e.l.f. Beauty and rhode (Furman, Leinwand and Swetzoff, strategy+business, 19 Nov 2025): e.l.f. is a $1.3b business (FY25) with more than two dozen consecutive quarters of share gains, growing roughly four times the global beauty market, with gross margin above 70% (CEO statement). It has raised prices only three times in 21 years and announced the August increase months ahead on social channels, drawing a 98% positive response. rhode became a nine-figure brand in three years with ten products. CEO claims are self-reported. Use: announce price changes early and plainly.
facts.source_title: strategy+business: e.l.f. Beauty and rhode are giving the beauty business a makeover

facts.statement: e.l.f. Beauty and rhode marketing methods (strategy+business, 19 Nov 2025): both use social video such as get-ready-with-me and haul clips. e.l.f. says it was the first beauty brand on TikTok and also has a Twitch and Roblox presence. A rhode customer habit of mixing blush with a barrier cream led to a hybrid product. AI is used for automation, content and community, and leaders also analyse marketing ROI. A pop-up study found 60% of visitors had never bought rhode. Use: mine real customer usage habits for product ideas.
facts.source_title: strategy+business: e.l.f. Beauty and rhode are giving the beauty business a makeover

facts.statement: Mastering the connection between strategy and culture (David Lancefield, strategy+business, 22 Nov 2021): in an online poll of 300 executives, 56% said they develop strategy and culture together and 30% said strategy comes first. In the PwC 2021 Global Culture Survey (3,200 respondents), 81% agreed culture can be a source of strategic differentiation. The article proposes four actions: start in the right place, create a common language, explore the culture's potential, and clarify the strategy's expectations. Use: align brand promise with internal behaviours before external campaigns.
facts.source_title: strategy+business: Mastering the connection between strategy and culture

facts.statement: Focusing on missions (Daniel Gross interview with GreenShield CEO Zahid Salman, strategy+business, 1 Apr 2026): the CEO says gross revenue grew from about CA$2.3b in 2018 to $6.2b by end 2025, with eight acquisitions in 18 months after none in 65 years. GreenShield calls itself Canada's first payer-provider and is moving from a claims-time touchpoint to a regular engagement model; showing employers well-being gains should drive more investment. About 95% of claims submitted online are adjudicated automatically. CEO self-report. Use: show buyer-side outcomes in proof points.
facts.source_title: strategy+business: Focusing on missions

facts.statement: BCG, 'CEOs Need a Customer Experience Revolution' (2 Aug 2021; sample not stated): companies with the highest customer satisfaction scores delivered about twice the shareholder value over ten years versus companies at the average score. BCG adds that routine CX improvement gives roughly 5-7% a year, whereas real impact needs 30-50% step changes from zero-based redesign. Use: build the CX business case on shareholder value and step-change redesign, not on small survey-score lifts.
facts.source_title: CEOs Need a Customer Experience Revolution, Not an Evolution (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's 2021 CX article gives client examples (no sample): a retail bank that redesigned checkbook replenishment from scratch cut cost over 30% and cycle time over 75% and raised satisfaction 30 points; another bank ran 220 uncoordinated CX initiatives across 30 departments; a telco's targeted top-up messaging lifted top-up revenue 15%, and a separate action of calling customers with a discount offer cut churn 20%. Use: consolidate scattered CX projects into a few journey-based efforts tied to one business KPI.
facts.source_title: CEOs Need a Customer Experience Revolution, Not an Evolution (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Don't Just Improve Your Customer Experience. Future-Proof It' (15 Jun 2023), citing a 2022 BCG survey (sample not stated): CX leaders showed 55% higher five-year total shareholder return growth, 190% higher three-year revenue growth and 70% higher net promoter scores than peers. Use: quote these as BCG's leader-versus-peer gaps with the caveat that the sample is not published, and do not treat them as a guaranteed effect of CX spend.
facts.source_title: Don't Just Improve Your Customer Experience. Future-Proof It. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's five principles for future-proofing customer experience (June 2023): make things easy; stand out through technology, innovation and partnerships; build emotional bonds that create advocacy; look ahead and anticipate shifts in customer behaviour; embed purpose (sustainability and social impact) inside the experience rather than as an add-on. Use: audit a brand's CX plan against the five principles and name the weakest one as the next experiment.
facts.source_title: Don't Just Improve Your Customer Experience. Future-Proof It. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Keys to Making Sustainable Products Mainstream' (13 Sep 2022): survey of about 19,000 consumers in eight countries (US, Japan, Germany, France, Italy, China, India, Brazil), June-July 2022, 14 categories. Up to 80% say they think about sustainability when buying, yet only 1-7% report paying a premium; about 70% are sceptical of corporate sustainability claims and only 20% believe they personally make a difference. Consumer survey, stated intent. Use: never price a sustainability claim on stated intent; test real willingness to pay.
facts.source_title: Keys to Making Sustainable Products Mainstream (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's 2022 sustainable-products study (about 19,000 consumers, eight countries) finds at most 16% treat sustainability as a top purchase driver in its own right (only 7% in beverages), but up to 43% have related needs such as health or quality that sustainable options can meet. BCG advises locally relevant, fact-based claims, selling through related benefits, fixing real product trade-offs, and targeting the concerned in-between consumers. Use: lead copy with the health, quality or cost benefit and add sustainability as the supporting proof.
facts.source_title: Keys to Making Sustainable Products Mainstream (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Green Awakening' (4 Dec 2023): survey of 2,524 buyers (1,750 for cars in seven countries, 774 for washing machines in three), fielded in 2023 (the page says both October and Q3). 57% would definitely or probably consider net-zero production for their next purchase. About 47% of car buyers cap their willingness to pay at 3% in the US (lowest) and 9% in China (highest); about 55% of washing-machine buyers at 6% in Germany and 12% in China. Stated willingness only. Use: segment before pricing a green premium and quote market-specific ceilings.
facts.source_title: Green Awakening: Are Consumers Open to Paying More for Decarbonized Products? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'European Consumers Optimistic But Still Not Spending' (22 Oct 2024): survey of 7,000 people in Denmark, France, Germany, Sweden and the UK, 1-16 July 2024. 19% said they would pay a premium for a green product; close to four in ten think about sustainability occasionally or regularly, and it ranks below value, practicality and savings. Use: treat a green premium as a niche play, not a mass-market price lever.
facts.source_title: European Consumers Optimistic But Still Not Spending (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Capturing the Green Advantage for Consumer Companies' (20 Jan 2009; Global Green Consumer Survey, July 2008, about 9,000 adults in eight countries plus seven Chinese cities): about a third outside China would pay 5-10% more for green products with a direct benefit; awareness and choice, not price, were the top barriers; only 28% understood green certification symbols; independent consumer reports were the most trusted source and manufacturers ranked eighth of 13. Use: pair green claims with an independent third-party proof.
facts.source_title: Capturing the Green Advantage for Consumer Companies (BCG)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Customers Want Relationships, Not Just Easy Experiences' (23 Apr 2025; Qualtrics X4 2025 and Bain NPS Prism): over 75% of UK banking customers say the base experience meets their needs but only about 45% say their engagement and value-proposition needs are met; at least 45% of X4 Executive Forum attendees could not confidently defend the business impact of CX to their CFO.
