The article also argues that a 20-question survey reflects only about 5% or fewer of customers (rhetorical, not sourced). Use: link CX metrics to revenue, retention or profit.
facts.source_title: Customers Want Relationships, Not Just Easy Experiences (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Customer Loyalty Metrics That Matter Most for B2B Companies' (5 Nov 2025): a three-layer NPS design for B2B. Strategic NPS every 1-2 years rates the company against rivals by segment; relationship NPS annually collects feedback from key stakeholders in each account and prompts account follow-up; operational and journey NPS runs continuously on support, logistics hand-offs and joint projects. No sample or figures given. Use: set up all three layers instead of one annual score.
facts.source_title: The Customer Loyalty Metrics That Matter Most for B2B Companies (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Customer loyalty in the Middle East' (31 Oct 2013, originally in Trends; broader study across 12 countries, sample not stated): loyalty leaders grew at more than double the rate of competitors with costs about 15% lower, and only about one in ten companies in the decade qualified as sustained value creators. Companies overrate themselves: 80% believe they deliver a superior experience, only 8% of customers agree. Saudi banks are the regional example. Use: use the 80/8 gap to justify measuring customers directly.
facts.source_title: Customer loyalty in the Middle East (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Top 5 for 2025' retail piece (23 Jan 2025): loyalty-programme members purchase more often, spend more and have a higher share of wallet, but over a third of US online adults do not regularly participate in most programmes they join. Bain says Sephora Beauty Insiders report making 58% more purchases a year and spending more than twice as much as non-members, and command a 63% higher share of wallet per Bain's annual study with ROI Rocket. Use: design loyalty around active participation, not enrolment counts.
facts.source_title: Top 5 for 2025: Retailer Resolutions and Forecast for the New Year (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Consumer Lab 2026 ESG Survey, in the CEO Sustainability Guide (11 Sep 2026; 7,499 consumers in the US, UK, Italy, Brazil, Indonesia; 2025 edition 14,206 in eight countries): 85% worry about environmental sustainability (79% in 2025); 83% have three or more sustainable habits; consumers say they would pay 18% more for sustainability benefits and 24% more when health is added. Health is the top purchase criterion in every category. Stated intent. Use: pair sustainability with health in offers.
facts.source_title: For Consumers, Sustainability Isn't Gone, But It Is Changing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain's 2026 ESG survey (7,499 consumers, five countries) shows AI and apps now mediate sustainability choices: 68% struggle to name the lower-carbon product in a pair; 41% use product-information apps and 79% of them say it changed purchases; among AI users, 43% use it to find healthier products. Bain advises machine-readable, product-level data and labels that work for both shoppers and AI. Use: publish structured product-level proof, not only corporate sustainability messaging.
facts.source_title: For Consumers, Sustainability Isn't Gone, But It Is Changing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with NielsenIQ, 'How (Some) Big Brands Are Beating the Odds' (15 Jul 2026): of nearly 500 large US consumer brands, 71 outgrew their macro-category every year since 2022; in 2025 they held about 8% of share but delivered 44% of net growth. Winners gained velocity (7% a year), distribution (1.5 points) and price (3%), while peers leaned on price (2%). Winners' engagement was about 1.5x peers on Instagram and 9x on TikTok. Use: aim brand plans at velocity and distribution, not price alone.
facts.source_title: How (Some) Big Brands Are Beating the Odds (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Rewiring Demand Generation in the Age of AI Agents' (8 May 2026): Bain consumer surveys (the figure cites the Bain Generative AI US Consumer Survey, September 2025, n=1,500) find 44% of online buyers mostly start in an LLM or split between AI and search, and 64% have used or are open to using AI to complete a purchase. Bain estimates fully agentic commerce could reach $300-500 billion of US revenue, a projection rather than a measurement. Use: write product pages with checkable attributes and review-backed claims.
facts.source_title: Rewiring Demand Generation in the Age of AI Agents (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Why Consumers Choose an AI Chatbot over a Search Engine' (20 Mar 2026; Generative AI Consumer Survey, September 2025, n=1,500, mainly US): 56% mostly or always use search engines by default versus 16% chatbots, but only 42% of millennials and Gen Z use search engines that much, versus 76% of boomers. Chatbot top uses: simplifying complex topics (53%), step-by-step help (47%). 46% use AI overviews. Use: plan for a split journey, with younger segments discovering brands inside chatbots.
facts.source_title: Why Consumers Choose an AI Chatbot over a Search Engine (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain B2B IT Decision Maker Survey, July 2026 (n=207), reported 23 Oct 2026: the headline says most software buyers use AI to find vendors, and Bain warns that a vendor missing from AI's initial list may see its sales funnel shrink. The text gives no percentages. Opinion data. Use: check how AI assistants describe and rank your product for category queries, and fix the third-party sources they cite.
facts.source_title: Survey: Most Software Buyers Use AI to Find Vendors (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'How AI Rewrites the Rules of Brand Discoverability in Banking' (18 May 2026): analysis of 6,000 Australian consumer prompts (March 2026) and 100 tracked banking prompts, plus global data of over 1 billion citations (14 Sep-14 Oct 2025) across 10 models. AI answers draw on comparison websites, reviews and forums. Bain's research finds 36% would feel comfortable buying through an AI assistant from a brand they already trust (country not named). Use: monitor how AI describes the brand.
facts.source_title: How AI Rewrites the Rules of Brand Discoverability in Banking (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with Comite Colbert, luxury and AI (30 Jun 2026; April 2026 survey of 1,605 luxury buyers in France, US and China; 35 executives at 23 houses; about 9,000 real prompts in eight markets): 64% of Chinese and 54% of US buyers used AI on their last luxury purchase versus 27% in France; about 70% of luxury prompts name no brand; official brand sites were about 10% of cited sources for watches and 45% for jewellery; only 10% of houses rate their generative visibility as strong. Use: invest in third-party presence for unbranded queries.
facts.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Travel Operators Can't Just Watch as AI Reroutes the Customer Journey' (30 Sep 2026; Similarweb traffic for three to five operators per category; consumer sample not stated): AI-platform referrals roughly quadrupled for hotels and rentals between July 2025 and July 2026 but stayed under 1% of site traffic in every category; in the US 49% of AI travel users rely on it most or all of the time. Direct bookings held near 45% of prebooked spend since 2011. Use: make direct booking as easy as the AI route.
facts.source_title: Travel Operators Can't Just Watch as AI Reroutes the Customer Journey (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Zero-Click Playbook' (9 Jun 2026; Bain 2026 Marketing Leaders survey n=1,397; Bain GenAI US tracker): as AI search shrinks clicks, sponsorships should be judged with a three-tier framework covering brand impact, engagement and commercial outcomes, using test-and-control designs. 58% of surveyed CFOs distrust marketing metrics; consumers starting shopping on LLM platforms rose from 5% to 14% (Dec 2025 to report date). Use: prove brand-building spend with matched controls before defending budgets.
facts.source_title: The Zero-Click Playbook: How Sports Sponsorships Build Preference Before Search (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Raising the Odds on a Deal: Likelihood to Buy' (19 Jun 2026; NewtonX buyer survey Feb 2026, n=750, HCM and cloud data platforms): a roughly 10-question survey across the buying committee measuring five decision themes. Separately, Bain says research shows around 90% of buyers purchase from their 'Day 1 list' (vendors in mind at the start), without naming a source. Use: diagnose lost deals as visibility, value-story or hidden-strength problems before changing the pitch.
facts.source_title: Raising the Odds on a Deal: How Likelihood to Buy Rewires B2B Growth (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain Gaming Report 2026, 'Half Your Players Already Buy Direct' (18 Aug 2026; June 2026 survey of 5,339 gamers): 47% bought from a game's web store in the past year, about 83% know direct stores exist, and about 75% of the top 50 mobile games run web stores, up from 12% in 2019. Direct sales add 15-30% margin per transaction. Raising the web bonus from 10% to 30% barely moved preference; 84% of repeat direct buyers want personalised offers. Use: win D2C with personalisation and relationship, not bigger discounts.
facts.source_title: Game Distribution: Half Your Players Already Buy Direct (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Synthetic Customers Earn Their Stripes' (4 May 2026): a consumer technology company backtested digital twins against a prior large quantitative conjoint study used as ground truth, and the twins replicated about 90% of key outcomes. In a separate GLP-1 survey comparison, variance rose when questions were more ambiguous. Use: pre-screen concepts and messages with synthetic respondents, then confirm winners with real buyers.
facts.source_title: Synthetic Customers Earn Their Stripes (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'When AI Optimizes the Wrong Thing' (30 Mar 2026; opinion piece): automation tuned to cost or deflection can cut near-term cost while eroding customer value. Booking.com's customer service cost per reservation fell roughly 10% in a year while bookings grew at a double-digit rate (an early result). Bain says success should be measured by lower churn, greater share of wallet, better price realisation and higher cross-sell. Use: set care-automation goals on resolution and retention, not deflection.
facts.source_title: When AI Optimizes the Wrong Thing (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Roshn Saudi League 2025-26 season highlights (28 Sep 2026; objective data and modelling, no sample): Al-Nassr had 57 million followers versus a league average of 7 million, 83% stadium utilisation and 20,000 average attendance versus 7,800. League-wide online fan growth slowed to 3% from 5%, attendance fell 7%, and the top five clubs held nearly three-quarters of squad value. Use: when advising Saudi sports-linked brands, benchmark fan engagement against these club-level figures and note growth is slowing.
facts.source_title: Roshn Saudi League Season Highlights 2025-26 (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'How Marketing Leadership Changed over the Last Decade' (13 Oct 2026; Bain research comparing leaders with other marketers, sample not stated per edition): 2016 leaders were about 3x as likely to use data in decisions; 2019, 3.6x as likely to focus on consumer feedback and journey maps; 2021, 5.9x as likely to be agile; 2025, 8x as likely to run 100-plus experiments a month; 2026, 3.7x as likely to redesign workflows. Use: read the trend as moving from data to testing to rebuilt workflows.
facts.source_title: How Marketing Leadership Changed over the Last Decade (Bain)

facts.statement: McKinsey, Who wins when AI does the shopping? (28 Oct 2026): a consumer survey of about 21,000 people (reported as 11 markets, fielded June 2026) shows growing AI-driven shopping, and McKinsey says companies are not yet ready for it. A secondary digest reports that the share of US AI users who bought inside an AI tool rose from 10% to 17% in a year; this was not seen on McKinsey's own page. The 53% and 48% usage figures and the 56% versus 27% tool split could not be confirmed. Use: treat AI assistants as a discovery channel and audit how the brand appears in their answers.
facts.source_title: Who wins when AI does the shopping? New evidence on agentic commerce (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey and NielsenIQ (Feb 2023): analysis of five years of US retail sales data to June 2022, covering about 600,000 SKUs and roughly $400 billion in annual retail revenue, found products with ESG-related claims averaged 28% cumulative growth versus 20% for products without claims (28% and 20% as reported by a secondary summary). The authors say the link is correlation, not causation, and they did not verify the claims. Use: cite as correlation only, never as proof a claim lifts sales; keep any sustainability claim provable.
facts.source_title: Consumers care about sustainability—and back it up with their wallets (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey, Experience-led growth: a new way to create value (2023): its exhibit shows customer-experience leaders grew revenue at more than twice the rate of CX laggards between 2016 and 2021. The article is a consulting analysis, so treat it as an association, not proof that CX causes growth. Use: treat CX as a growth lever in the plan, but benchmark against your own churn and repeat-purchase data rather than quoting the 2x as a promise.
facts.source_title: Experience-led growth: A new way to create value (McKinsey)

facts.statement: McKinsey Quarterly, The CEO guide to customer experience (August 2016): argues that end-to-end customer journeys track business outcomes more closely than individual touchpoints do, since touchpoints can score well while the whole experience disappoints. Use: map and measure the two or three journeys that matter (for example sign-up to first value) and give each one an owner, rather than scoring every touchpoint.
facts.source_title: The CEO guide to customer experience (McKinsey Quarterly)

facts.statement: Gupta (HBS) and Lemmens, HBS Working Knowledge, 11 Nov 2013: ranking customers for retention offers by churn risk alone ignores value. A model weighing churn risk, spend, response to the offer and offer cost raised profit by 115% on average over standard targeting at an unnamed US wireless carrier (sample size not stated), at no extra implementation cost. Use: rank retention targets by expected profit lift, not churn score.
facts.source_title: A Smarter Way to Reduce Customer Defections (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: HBS Working Knowledge, 6 Jul 2020, on Gupta and Lemmens, 'Managing Churn to Maximize Profits' (Marketing Science): prioritising higher-spending customers beats ranking by leave-risk, and adding each customer's responsiveness to an offer lifts profit further. On a European TV-service dataset (sample size not stated) the theoretical gain was 180% with no added spend, only a changed targeting algorithm. Use: add value and responsiveness to every churn model brief.
facts.source_title: The Right Way to Manage Customer Churn for Maximum Profit (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: Yankelovich and Meer, HBR, Feb 2006, 'Rediscovering Market Segmentation': the authors say segmentation has narrowed into a tool serving advertising, and that psychographic profiling, often sold as segmentation, is largely a wasteful diversion. Its real aim is to find customers whose behaviour can be changed or whose needs are unmet. Only the summary page is visible. Use: tie each segmentation brief to the behaviour you want to change or the unmet need.
facts.source_title: Rediscovering Market Segmentation (HBR)

facts.statement: Zoltners, Lorimer and Sinha, HBR, Jul-Aug 2006: the authors argue that sales force structure should be adjusted as the business moves through its life cycle, since few firms think about how structure should change over time. Secondary excerpts name the stages as start-up, growth, maturity and decline. The page shows only the introduction. Use: revisit sales roles and coverage whenever the product stage changes.
facts.source_title: Match Your Sales Force Structure to Your Business Life Cycle (HBR)

facts.statement: Zoltners, Sinha and Lorimer, HBR, 11 Jul 2011: a distribution company pays reps only commission and lets them keep accounts permanently. Veterans earn heavily from legacy customers and act as order-takers, while newer reps cannot build a book, so annual turnover is 57%. Presented as an illustrative case, not a study; no recommendation visible on the page. Use: audit whether account ownership rules starve new-business effort.
facts.source_title: Is Your Sales Force Addicted to Incentives? (HBR)

facts.statement: Zoltners, Sinha and Lorimer, HBR, 13 Nov 2012: single quick fixes rarely repair a sales force because the problems are multi-dimensional. Leaders must decide between incremental, evolutionary improvement and wholesale transformation, even when results are good. No figures on the page. Use: before proposing a sales fix, state whether it is a fine-tune or a transformation and the evidence that justifies the scale.
facts.source_title: Improving Your Sales Force: Fine-tune or Transform? (HBR)

facts.statement: Zoltners, Sinha and Lorimer, HBR, 11 Jun 2013, on sales force turnover: in the article's exit-interview scenario, 32% of departing reps left mainly over their first-line manager, 27% over pay and 21% over lack of promotion. The page frames this as an illustrative scenario and gives no sample. Use: when diagnosing rep churn, check manager quality before changing pay.
facts.source_title: How to Make Sense of Sales Force Turnover (HBR)

facts.statement: Cespedes (HBS), HBR page dated 31 Oct 2014, 'Effective Strategies for Modern Sales': the page promotes a webinar arguing that selling touches every element of value creation, and offers a way to express strategy in terms field sales staff can act on, plus a framework for diagnosing the core levers of effective selling. It contains no statistics. Use: translate each strategy choice into rep behaviours, hiring criteria and review metrics.
facts.source_title: Effective Strategies for Modern Sales (HBR, Cespedes)

facts.statement: HBR, 24 Mar 2025 (Grewal, Satornino, Davenport, Guha): citing Salesforce's 9th State of Marketing survey of 5,000 global marketers (opinion data), implementing AI was their top priority. Reported company results, with sample and period not stated: Vanguard raised LinkedIn ad conversion 15% with gen AI; Unilever service agents cut response time 90%. Authors urge balancing automation, customisation and human oversight. Use: treat these as vendor-reported, run own holdouts.
facts.source_title: How Should Gen AI Fit into Your Marketing Strategy? (HBR)

facts.statement: Brand, Israeli (HBS) and Ngwe, HBR, 18 Jul 2025: the authors argue large language models can simulate how customers react to product concepts ('synthetic customers'), offering a faster, cheaper complement to slow, narrow traditional human research. Only the summary and introduction are visible. Use: use synthetic panels only to screen early concepts and validate with real buyers.
facts.source_title: Using Gen AI for Early-Stage Market Research (HBR)

facts.statement: Peruta (Syracuse), HBR, 3 Sep 2026: a study of 3,000 US consumers found people could not reliably tell AI-made video ads from human-made ones, yet human ads came out ahead on sales impact (about 14% in the short term) and brand equity (about 17% long term) on Ipsos indices; secondary coverage attributes the figures to the Ipsos and Syracuse Newhouse study of 20 ads. HBR page body is paywalled. Use: test AI ads for sales and brand lift before approving.
facts.source_title: Research: AI-Generated Ads Perform Worse Than Human-Made Ones (HBR)

facts.statement: Lyons, Oteh (Accenture Song) and Bellin (Accenture Research), HBR, 16 Jul 2026, 'Stop AI from Eroding Your Brand': the authors say firms with lower 'brand debt' are better placed, and that AI can speed up brand debt by amplifying inconsistent, impersonal or off-brand experiences. The HBR page excerpt does not define the term. Use: check brand consistency and governance before scaling AI content or agents.
facts.source_title: Stop AI from Eroding Your Brand (HBR)

facts.statement: Gale, Cian and Wathieu, HBR, 29 Jun 2026: when asked for running-shoe recommendations, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini surfaced the smaller brand Brooks reliably but Nike far less consistently (number of queries not stated). The authors say AI-mediated discovery makes traditional advantages such as awareness, storytelling and emotional appeal less decisive. Use: audit what assistants recommend in your category.
facts.source_title: How to Get AI to Surface Your Brand (HBR)

facts.statement: Acar and Schweidel, HBR Mar-Apr 2026: Pernod Ricard, with agency Jellyfish, studied how AI models described its brands and found that one popular model labelled mass-market Ballantine's whisky as a prestige product. The article says about two-thirds of Gen Z were using LLMs to research products by 2024. Use: run a periodic audit of what AI assistants say about the brand.
facts.source_title: Preparing Your Brand for Agentic AI (HBR)

facts.statement: Dubois (INSEAD) with Jellyfish authors, HBR, 4 Jun 2025: citing a Capgemini consumer survey of 12,000 people (opinion data), 58% used gen AI tools for product or service recommendations, up from 25% in 2023. Another cited study reports a 1,300% rise in AI-search referrals to US retail sites in the 2024 holiday season. Use: budget for AI-search visibility alongside classic SEO and treat referrals as a tracked channel.
facts.source_title: Forget What You Know About Search. Optimize Your Brand for LLMs (HBR)

facts.statement: Taite and Fernandez, HBR, 19 Oct 2026: an agentic marketing organisation has three layers, a machine-readable 'brand code' of brand, customer and product rules, execution agents, and an orchestration layer that escalates decisions needing human judgement. Costs and complexity often rise before efficiency gains arrive. No data or sample on the page. Use: write the brand code first and plan for a dip before gains.
facts.source_title: Your AI Marketing Transformation Will Get Harder Before It Gets Easier (HBR)

facts.statement: De Freitas (HBS), HBR Nov-Dec 2026, 'Your Chatbot Will Define Your Brand': as AI chatbots become customers' main interface with a company, relationship management shifts from a marketing challenge to a product design challenge. Only the summary and an opening anecdote are visible. Use: treat chatbot behaviour and tone as part of brand design.
facts.source_title: Your Chatbot Will Define Your Brand (HBR)

facts.statement: Acar, Klesse, Tuk and Zhang, HBR, 7 Jan 2025: neither making AI tools look more human nor stripping them of human traits is the best way to win users over; the authors recommend showing the human effort and expertise behind the tools. Sample and effect sizes are not on the page. Use: in AI-assisted customer touchpoints, disclose AI plainly and surface the human expertise behind it.
facts.source_title: Research: Consumers Don't Want AI to Seem Human (HBR)

facts.statement: Sprague, HBR May-Jun 2026, 'Data Privacy Is a Growth Strategy': researchers analysed 360 real-world company announcements about new or improved data-privacy measures. The HBR store listing says markets rewarded serious privacy practices, especially for firms with past breaches, and that brands with strong privacy reputations saw a 12.31% increase in customer patronage. Secondary write-ups describe the sample and metric differently, so treat the exact figure as listing-reported. Use: frame privacy as trust, not only compliance.
facts.source_title: Data Privacy Is a Growth Strategy (HBR)

facts.statement: Hollenbeck (UCLA) and Taylor (SMU), HBR, 28 Oct 2021: two years of purchase data from more than 10,000 customers of a top US retailer; the authors say it is unclear loyalty programs work. Search listing reports no spending effect for high past spenders but a rise near 50% for customers vulnerable to competitors. Context: the average consumer belongs to over 14 programs. Use: aim loyalty offers at at-risk customers, not already-loyal ones.
facts.source_title: How to Make Your Loyalty Program Pay Off (HBR)

facts.statement: Sun, Zhang and Zhang, HBR, 27 Jun 2022: loyalty members lose up to a third of the savings they could have earned because of redemption hurdles such as expiry dates and spend minimums. The article says most reward programs include some hurdle and discusses when hurdles can benefit both sides. Sample not stated on the page. Use: review expiry and minimum rules for friction before they cost goodwill.
facts.source_title: When and How to Build Hurdles into a Loyalty Program (HBR)

facts.statement: Bower, HBR May-Jun 2021, 'Why Customer Loyalty Programs Can Backfire': the article states that US loyalty programs account for more than 3.3 billion memberships. Only the summary is visible; the title signals that loyalty programs can backfire. Use: fix service recovery and operations before adding rewards.
facts.source_title: Why Customer Loyalty Programs Can Backfire (HBR)

facts.statement: Chung and Kalra (Rice), HBR, 12 Sep 2024: influencer posts that show the influencer's inner circle can boost engagement. The page's illustration: in one week David Beckham's photos with his father and wife drew about 1.3 million and 1.8 million likes, roughly three times a sponsored sunglasses ad (460,000) or a team-win post (360,000). Anecdote, not study data. Use: brief creators to keep sponsored posts personal.
facts.source_title: Research: For Influencers, Showing Your Inner Circle Can Boost Engagement (HBR)

facts.statement: Leung, Zhang, Gu, Li and Palmatier, HBR, 24 Nov 2022: the page states the influencer industry reached $16.4 billion in 2022 and that more than 75% of brands have a dedicated influencer budget. The article asks whether influencer marketing pays off. Use: measure ROI per post rather than assuming returns.
facts.source_title: Does Influencer Marketing Really Pay Off? (HBR)

facts.statement: Audrezet and de Kerviler, HBR, 1 Apr 2019: the article cites Statista data that up to 25.2% of US internet users blocked ads in 2018, which is why brands look to influencers to reach customers. Only the summary and introduction are visible. Use: build long-term creator relationships rather than one-off ad placements.
facts.source_title: How Brands Can Build Successful Relationships with Influencers (HBR)

facts.statement: Bhattacharya, Ghose and Burtch, HBR, 3 Jun 2026: the title reports research finding that consumers respond better to ads when they have more control over them; the experiment details are not visible. The article cites 70% of consumers finding digital ads annoying, 18% always using ad blockers for streaming and 37% of US consumers cancelling a subscription over ads. Use: test giving viewers a choice over ad timing or content.
facts.source_title: Research: When Consumers Have More Control Over Ads, They Respond Better (HBR)

facts.statement: Luo (Houston) and Ranjan (Monash), HBR, 31 Mar 2026: most advertisers still draw a simple radius around each store, which the article calls blunt, and advertisers spent at least $57 billion on location-targeted campaigns in 2025. An abstract listing says customers closer to a retailer than to its rival respond more strongly to ads, so competitor locations should be added to targeting logic. Use: test geofences that account for rival stores.
facts.source_title: A Better Strategy for Location-Based Advertising (HBR)

facts.statement: Miller and Hosanagar (Wharton), HBR, 8 Nov 2019, 'How Targeted Ads and Dynamic Pricing Can Perpetuate Bias': the authors study whether and how bias can arise when algorithms set the prices consumers pay or the discounts they see, noting personalisation is usually pitched as a win-win. The visible summary does not spell out the mechanism. Use: audit personalisation and discount models for disparate outcomes before launch.
facts.source_title: How Targeted Ads and Dynamic Pricing Can Perpetuate Bias (HBR)

facts.statement: Aaker and Joachimsthaler, California Management Review 42(4), Aug 2000: brand architecture is the organising structure of a brand portfolio, defining each brand's role and how brands relate. Their brand relationship spectrum helps strategists weigh subbrands, endorsed brands and alternatives, driven by market fragmentation and pressure to reuse existing brands. Category list not on the page. Use: set the role of each brand and product line before launching a name.
facts.source_title: The Brand Relationship Spectrum (California Management Review)

facts.statement: Reza, Ho, Ling, Shi and Calvert, HBR, 7 Jan 2021: free trials often fail to convert to paying customers, and customers acquired through trials can be considerably less valuable than others. The authors argue many campaigns focus on new customers instead of enticing existing customers to spend more. Sample and numbers not on the page. Use: measure trial cohorts by long-run value, and test trials aimed at existing customers.
facts.source_title: Don't Count on Free Trials to Win You Customers (HBR)

facts.statement: Kumar (HBS), HBR, May 2014, 'Making Freemium Work': freemium offers basic features free and charges for advanced functions, and is described as the leading startup model for web and app businesses. It works in B2B too (Box, Splunk, Yammer cited). Page shows only the introduction and no statistics; later benchmark claims seen in search summaries were not confirmed. Use: define which features stay free and what upgrade trigger converts users.
facts.source_title: Making 'Freemium' Work (HBR)

facts.statement: Cochrane (CMO, SAP Customer Experience), HBR, 13 Jun 2018: consumers expect personalised offers, which requires companies to collect large amounts of data; the piece argues marketers need transparent data practices to regain trust. Vendor-executive opinion piece with no study data visible. Use: explain data use plainly and give customers control over what is shared.
facts.source_title: To Regain Consumers' Trust, Marketers Need Transparent Data Practices (HBR)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Loyalty Programs Need Next-Generation Design' (30 May 2023; survey of about 3,045 US members of 60 programs in 10 industries, Q4 2022, representative of US adults; consumer survey): top-rated programs had up to 3x the share of highly engaged members and up to 5x the share of loyal members versus weaker programs, and captured on average 35 percentage points more of members' wallet. Use: set loyalty-programme targets against top-quartile engagement and wallet share, not the category average.
facts.source_title: Loyalty Programs Need Next-Generation Design (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG loyalty survey (May 2023; about 3,045 US members, 60 programs, Q4 2022; consumer survey): members belong to 14 programs on average; top paid programs score 24 points higher on loyalty and 33 higher on engagement than the average programme; over 60% of digitally inclined under-35s expect to join a new paid programme within a year. Share of very engaged members in grocery and mass retail ranges from 22% to 82%. Use: test a paid tier for young digital segments and benchmark engagement within category, since spread inside one industry is huge.
facts.source_title: Loyalty Programs Need Next-Generation Design (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG (May 2023, about 3,045 US programme members, Q4 2022): satisfaction with a loyalty programme is only weakly correlated with the return members get relative to their spend, so perceived value is not purely monetary. BCG calls personalization the leading tool for success in free programmes. Use: design rewards around relevance and non-monetary value, and do not justify a programme only by points-per-dollar.
facts.source_title: Loyalty Programs Need Next-Generation Design (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Loyalty Programs Are Growing, So Are Customer Expectations' (9 Dec 2024; second annual survey, over 10,000 consumers in nine countries, representative by age, gender, ethnicity and income; consumer survey): the average US consumer belongs to over 15 programmes (about 10% more than 2022) and Europeans to nine, yet since 2022 US engagement fell about 10% and loyalty about 20%. Over 35% plan to cancel some memberships within a year, above 50% of 18 to 34 year olds. Use: expect programme fatigue and prioritise fewer, more differentiated memberships.
facts.source_title: Loyalty Programs and Customer Expectations Are Growing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG loyalty survey (Dec 2024; over 10,000 consumers, nine countries; consumer survey): paid programmes (streaming, gaming, cards, news) show the strongest loyalty; 85% of US respondents rank points, cash back or promotions in their top five benefits versus 75% in Europe and 55% in Asia-Pacific, where partnership and exclusive benefits matter more. Under-35s prefer free content and personalised digital benefits, over-35s monetary ones. Leader-versus-laggard engagement gap is 4.3x in retail and 2.9x in airlines. Use: localise reward mix by region and age.
facts.source_title: Loyalty Programs and Customer Expectations Are Growing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Leveraging the Loyalty Margin' (21 Apr 2014; BCG research, sample not stated): among members of best-in-class programmes, nearly 50% reported more frequent visits and nearly 30% reported higher spending (self-reported). Across six retail programmes, incremental share ranged from 8% to 114%. BCG's example: with a 35% gross margin, a programme costing 3% of revenue breaks even at 10% incremental share. Old data. Use: compute break-even incremental share before launching or renewing a programme.
facts.source_title: Leveraging the Loyalty Margin: Rewards Programs That Work (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Web3 Opens New Paths to Customer Loyalty' (18 Jan 2023): in BCG's October 2022 membership study (sample not stated) up to 54% of consumers named utility and real-world benefits as a main reason to join a membership, while only 21% cited NFTs or other digital products. Cited third-party data: about two-thirds of US consumers prefer cash back to points. Use: lead any token or community membership with tangible utility, not with the technology.
facts.source_title: Web3 Opens New Paths to Customer Loyalty (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'How Generative AI Is Already Transforming Customer Service' (6 Jul 2023): the authors project 30% to 50% or more contact-centre productivity at scale (an estimate, not a measured result). A 2022 BCG survey of service leaders (sample not stated; survey of executives) found 95% expect customers to be served by an AI bot within three years. Cases: Octopus Energy reported AI-drafted emails scored 18% higher on happiness; JetBlue saved 73,000 agent hours in a quarter. Use: start with agent-assist drafting, and measure satisfaction against human-only replies.
facts.source_title: How Generative AI Is Already Transforming Customer Service (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Transforming Customer Service Operations with GenAI' (6 Sep 2024; client experience, no sample): the 10/20/70 rule puts 10% of effort on algorithms, 20% on data and technology and 70% on operating-model change. Manual quality assurance covers only 1% to 2% of cases while GenAI can cover up to 100%. Scaled use cases reached 15% to 30% productivity; leaders aim for up to 80%. Senior agents can spend 30% of time maintaining knowledge content. Use: budget most of any service-AI programme on process and roles.
facts.source_title: Transforming Customer Service Operations with GenAI (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Agentic AI Is the New Frontier in Customer Service Transformation' (3 Dec 2025; survey of 180 customer service leaders worldwide plus client work; survey of executives): only 28% reported measurable business value from generative AI in service so far; 98% call change management crucial but 50% name it the main barrier; 78% expect scaling within 24 months. Pioneers target 60%+ productivity gain and up to 30% higher lifetime value. Use: treat service-AI as a business-led change programme and report value, not pilot counts.
facts.source_title: Agentic AI Is the New Frontier in Customer Service Transformation (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG (3 Dec 2025, 180 service leaders): service optimisation runs through four stages, pre-empt, self-heal, self-help and support response. Agentic AI adds most value in the first two, yet most deployments start at the last. Five lessons: make adoption business-led, focus on measurable value, get data and the tech stack right, balance buy and build, and redesign processes instead of automating old workflows. Cited cases: one global tech firm halved time to resolution; a European energy provider raised satisfaction 18%. Use: aim agents at preventing contacts, not only answering them.
facts.source_title: Agentic AI Is the New Frontier in Customer Service Transformation (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'How AI Agents Are Opening the Golden Era of Customer Experience' (13 Jan 2025; no study sample, figures from company statements): Klarna reported its assistant did the work of 700 agents in month one, matched human satisfaction, cut repeat inquiries 25% and resolved issues in under 2 minutes versus 11 (company estimate of $40M profit in 2024, unaudited). BCG advises adding cost-to-serve as a KPI beside satisfaction. Use: track cost-to-serve and repeat-contact rate together with CSAT when evaluating AI support.
facts.source_title: How AI Agents Are Opening the Golden Era of Customer Experience (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with LinkedIn, 'B2B Marketing in a World Without Cookies' (24 Mar 2022; survey of 100+ senior marketing and IT executives at firms with $400M+ revenue, North America, July 2021, plus 20 interviews; survey of executives): 39% already saw negative effects of privacy changes, 56% expected them within a year, 62% thought at least a fifth of targeting data was at risk, and over three-quarters named an inadequate martech stack the top challenge. Use: invest in first-party data and martech gaps ahead of identifier loss.
facts.source_title: Marketing in a Cookieless Future for B2B Companies (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG B2B cookieless study (24 Mar 2022; 100+ executives surveyed, case results are BCG client experience): a health-care leader raised marketing ROI over 30% by using more first-party data and analytics; an industrial firm gained 20% from contextual first-party data; an enterprise tech firm doubled its marketing-to-sales qualified lead pass rate by re-building lead scoring with AI; a services firm halved lead cost by adding social data partners. BCG also reports mature marketing organisations gained 18 points of sales. Use: copy the data-then-scoring sequence for B2B lead quality.
facts.source_title: Marketing in a Cookieless Future for B2B Companies (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'How CMOs Can Lead Transformations in an Era of Change' (10 Jan 2024; survey of 190 companies, September 2022, plus 20+ marketing executive interviews; survey of executives): digital is 65% of marketing spend but only 25% of marketing staff are digital specialists. Only 27% of companies have a fully centralised marketing structure, 1% fully decentralised, the rest hybrid. 47% keep analytics and insights partly or fully outside marketing. Use: audit the digital skills gap and decide where analytics sits before redesigning the team.
facts.source_title: How CMOs Can Lead Transformations in an Era of Change (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG (10 Jan 2024; 190 companies surveyed September 2022; survey of executives): the share of companies doing marketing work in-house rose from 42% in 2008 to 78% in 2018; analytics, brand strategy, CRM and e-commerce are in-house at over 70% of firms, while paid media, creative and martech are the most outsourced. About 60% of firms agency pay is retainer, project or service fee; performance-based fees are less common. 85% use some agile working, 27% fully; one adopter cut campaign launch time up to 60%. Use: keep data-heavy work in-house and buy creative capacity.
facts.source_title: How CMOs Can Lead Transformations in an Era of Change (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'The Future of Marketing Is Here. Don't Blink.' (30 Nov 2018; 40 leading international marketers rated on a 1 to 4 digital-maturity scale): 83% could not link data across touchpoints, 68% lacked automation, 78% could not attribute value to single touchpoints, 80% had weak cross-functional coordination. Climbers reported cost savings up to 30% and revenue up to 20% higher. Brands that personalise see 6% to 10% revenue gains; in-house execution can in some cases save up to 50% of agency and content cost. Use: diagnose maturity on these four gaps.
facts.source_title: The Future of Marketing Is Here. Don't Blink. (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with Facebook, 'Marketing Measurement Done Right' (7 Oct 2019; survey of 100 US senior marketing executives managing nearly $20B in budgets plus 30+ hours of interviews; survey of executives): nearly nine in ten say they leave money unspent for lack of ability to know what works; about 25% measure incrementality for most activities and 9% can forecast it across channels; only 42% rate data quality sufficient. BCG says capability building can improve spending efficiency 20% to 40%. Use: prioritise incrementality tests and data quality before more channels.
facts.source_title: Marketing Measurement Done Right (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Marketing Measurement Done Right' (7 Oct 2019; 100 US marketing executives, about $20B budgets): three shifts build return-on-marketing-investment capability: break down barriers across finance and IT, adopt agile and experimentation, and tie incentives to ROMI. Models (marketing mix, multitouch) estimate incrementality and experiments calibrate them, yet only 60% of model users also run tests. Marketers whose metrics enter annual planning are far more confident in ROMI (about 75% versus 22%); building the toolkit takes two to three years. Use: calibrate models with holdout tests and link metrics to planning.
facts.source_title: Marketing Measurement Done Right (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'The End of Marketing Campaigns as We Know Them' (2 Jul 2026; no sample, early adopter results): in a mature agent-native model 70% to 80% of touchpoints move from planned campaigns to real-time next-best-action; legacy builds take 60 to 90 days and 20+ people. Adopters report cycle time down up to 80%, 60% fewer resources, 20% to 40% higher engagement and conversion; pods are 3 to 5 people. Agents pick action and channel from preapproved assets in high-frequency, low-stakes cases; humans keep objectives and budget. Use: set autonomy and escalation rules first.
facts.source_title: The End of Marketing Campaigns as We Know Them (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'What Really Shapes the Customer Experience' (10 Sep 2015; over 227,000 customers, 650 brands, eight countries, seven industries; consumer survey): top-scoring brands on the Brand Advocacy Index grew revenue on average 27 percentage points faster than the lowest-scoring. Four drivers shape advocacy: value for money, customer service, product satisfaction, emotional connection. Friends and family recommendations are roughly 4 to 5 times more influential than indirect sources. Use: track advocacy (actual recommending) beside NPS and weight emotional connection for leaders.
facts.source_title: What Really Shapes the Customer Experience (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Brand Advocacy study (10 Sep 2015; over 227,000 customers, 650 brands; consumer survey): in car insurance strong advocates buy 74% more products than strong critics; 39% of strong critics in retail banking considered leaving versus 3% of strong advocates (36% versus 4% in health insurance). 37% of former customers keep talking about a brand, nearly half negatively, and the most influential advocates are about 2% of a brand's community. Use: size advocacy and detractor programmes by their cross-sell and churn gap.
facts.source_title: What Really Shapes the Customer Experience (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Customer Journey Programs Are Hard to Get Right' (29 Jan 2020; no sample, practitioner experience): BCG says well-run programmes can deliver 20 to 40 points higher customer advocacy, 15% to 25% lower cost and 10% to 20% more revenue (potential outcomes, not guarantees). Its six failure causes include ambition without a plan, journeys defined too narrowly, work kept in silos, weak follow-through, pilots set up to fail and success measured too narrowly. Its eight practices include permanent journey teams and compensation tied to programme metrics. Use: define journey-level KPIs and fund permanent teams.
facts.source_title: Customer Journey Programs Are Hard to Get Right (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Center for Customer Insight, 'Demystifying Global Consumer Choice' (15 Dec 2020; over 15,000 consumers, six markets in phase one, 13 categories, 56 attitude statements; consumer survey): needs diverge by market, so one global strategy would not be wholly effective in any of the 13 categories. Age is the only demographic that significantly affects purchases; context can outweigh attitudes in high-frequency, low-cost categories such as beverages and snacks. Use: segment by occasion and localise propositions.
facts.source_title: Demystifying Global Consumer Choice (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG with Moloco, Consumer AI Disruption Index (21 Jan 2026; survey of 238 senior marketing leaders across 17 consumer verticals; survey of executives): 67% expect high AI-driven disruption of their vertical's consumer journey. Verticals are placed on AI disruption of discovery and service model versus relationship strength (organic-to-paid acquisition ratio, post-install loyalty, time on apps versus web), giving four archetypes: breached (e.g. travel, retail, news), undefended, contested, secured. Use: place the product in the grid and set loyalty and owned-channel priorities accordingly.
facts.source_title: Battle for the Interface: Introducing the Consumer AI Disruption Index (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Optimism in the Gulf States Points to the Region's Potential' (27 Nov 2019; first BCG GCC consumer survey, over 7,000 respondents in six countries, nationals and expatriates, in-person Jan to Feb 2019; consumer survey): 90% optimistic about the future. 75% of nationals say brands reflect who they are (83% in Saudi Arabia, 56% of expatriates); 79% think long-established brands are best, yet 46% prefer brands different from their parents'; 46% would likely drop a brand a friend disapproves of. Use: stress identity and peer proof in GCC brand messaging.
facts.source_title: Optimism in the Gulf States Points to the Region's Potential (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG GCC consumer survey (27 Nov 2019; over 7,000 respondents, six GCC countries, Jan to Feb 2019; consumer survey): over 70% bought online in the past year, yet online was only 4% of UAE retail then; about 2 in 5 online purchases were paid cash on delivery (62% among non-working consumers). Costly returns were the top complaint, about 1 in 5 doubted product authenticity, and the internet is a top-three purchase influence in most countries. Old data. Use: offer cash-on-delivery, easy returns and authenticity proof in GCC e-commerce.
facts.source_title: Optimism in the Gulf States Points to the Region's Potential (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'Are Consumers in the Gulf States Ready to Go Green?' (31 Jan 2021; survey of 6,000 adults in six GCC states, July 2020; consumer survey of stated intent): 71% understand climate change, and 80% to 95% by country say they would act or already do, but 39% call a sustainable lifestyle too expensive and around 30% cite too few options. Respondents would pay a premium of up to 20% to 30% on average for organic food. Use: pair green claims in the Gulf with visible value and availability, and avoid assuming a large premium.
facts.source_title: Are Consumers in the Gulf States Ready to Go Green? (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, 'The Saudi Consumer in 2026: Confident, but Disciplined' (23 Oct 2026; 2026 Consumer Sentiment Survey, 1,895 Saudi consumers, 11 categories, April 2026; stated intentions, not observed behaviour): only 31% of purchases involve a pre-chosen brand; value for money, functionality and price lead purchase drivers; local origin ranks last although about two-thirds say they seek local brands; 59% will pay more for better quality. 85% say a physical store matters to the decision. Use: win at the shelf and in-store, not only through brand pre-selection.
facts.source_title: The Saudi Consumer in 2026: Confident, but Disciplined (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Saudi consumer survey (23 Oct 2026; 1,895 consumers, April 2026; stated sentiment): 79% feel positive across eight sentiment measures versus 35% in 11 European markets (BCG EMESA survey of about 20,000); 66% would cut current spending to save more; 61% do not want brands to access their data while 46% accept it for personalization; 72% have moderate or higher trust in AI; 86% expect sustainable options to cost the same or less (14% pay a premium). Use: gate personalization on explicit value exchange and price sustainability at parity.
facts.source_title: The Saudi Consumer in 2026: Confident, but Disciplined (BCG)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Turning Rewards into Loyalty' (7 Feb 2017; qualitative, case examples, no sample): most of the thousands of rewards programmes do not build loyalty and some pay customers for behaviour they would show anyway. Five traits of effective programmes: informed (know lifetime value, test incrementality), targeted, experiential (status and experience over points), easy (simple, opt-in), responsive (collect feedback, fix failures). Customers asked for feedback were about 7% more likely to return within two months (Thanx data). Use: audit any loyalty programme against these five traits.
facts.source_title: Turning Rewards into Loyalty (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with Genesys, 'AI Is Lifting Service-Center Performance' (4 Feb 2019; no formal sample, large service operations in banking, insurance, health care, telecom and tech): predictive routing pairs each customer with the agent proven best for the issue instead of first-in-first-out. Rogers Communications cut average handle time 7% and raised retention almost 3%; a Western European mobile operator lifted first-contact resolution nearly 4% and NPS 4 points. Customers often tolerate longer waits than managers assume. Use: route by proven agent skill and test wait tolerance by channel.
facts.source_title: AI Is Lifting Service-Center Performance (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Generative AI's Potential to Improve Customer Experience' (13 Nov 2024; Bain survey of 714 US online shoppers, July 2024, plus interviews; consumer survey): 71% were not aware they had used generative AI in online shopping; 41% would be comfortable using a generative AI tool from a brand they trust; obvious errors (57%) and inaccurate product information (56%, very or extremely negative) are among the biggest negatives. Five principles: complement habits, look beyond chatbots, rethink data exchange, build trust through transparency, reimagine service. Use: prefer passive AI features with error correction over chat-first launches.
facts.source_title: Generative AI's Potential to Improve Customer Experience (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'How CMOs Can Get, and Keep, Their Marketing Mix Right' (7 Feb 2018; Bain research and client experience, no sample): marketing mix optimisation evolved from top-down aggregate models (1.0) to customer-level bottom-up models (2.0) to AI-driven decisions (3.0). Well-run MMO yields 10% to 25% cost efficiency; one failed bank project spent about 80% of budget just preparing data. Five conditions: strategic alignment, data access, balanced analytics (research plus tests), operational flexibility, analytic marketers. Use: fix data access and testing habits before buying modelling sophistication.
facts.source_title: How CMOs Can Get, and Keep, Their Marketing Mix Right (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain (7 Feb 2018, marketing mix optimisation brief): treat MMO as a venture-style investment portfolio, not a fixed project list; the article suggests, notionally and perhaps quarterly, about three insights, two tests and one scaled solution, with quarterly governance and priority setting by the senior executive team. Use: run measurement as a regular cycle with limited scaled changes per quarter, and log tests as experiments.
facts.source_title: How CMOs Can Get, and Keep, Their Marketing Mix Right (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with Google, 'The Measurement Advantage' (26 Mar 2019; survey of 622 marketing executives in the US, UK and Canada sorted into four maturity levels; survey of executives): the 100 most mature firms were about four times as likely as the 100 least mature to beat business goals, grow revenue and gain share. Leaders were 2.3x as likely to automate bids and budgets across channels in real time and nearly twice as likely to link measurement and ad platforms. Bain estimates 25% to 30% more first-year revenue per dollar from advanced measurement (2,250+ tests). Use: link measurement to bidding.
facts.source_title: The Measurement Advantage (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'The Measurement Advantage' (26 Mar 2019; Bain client cases, results as reported by Bain): McAfee formed cross-functional Agile teams on two-week sprints and cut paid search acquisition cost 35% and overall customer acquisition cost 22% within 90 days; Shinola reset automation rules and mapped its digital journey, growing nonbrand search revenue 209% in six months. Leaders were also 1.6x as likely to run Agile teams around segments or campaigns. Use: organise growth squads around a customer segment with shared metrics.
facts.source_title: The Measurement Advantage (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Can Marketing Experimentation Become Your Superpower?' (7 Feb 2023; no sample, company examples): Netflix runs over 1,000 marketing tests a year and Amazon over 2,000. Allianz used one region as control and found paid social lifted marketing effectiveness 25%. Coca-Cola found CTV was more effective once it passed roughly 25% of the digital video mix, with effectiveness holding until about 75%, and runs 50 to 100 experiments per quarter. Advice: tie tests to business goals, measure through to sales. Use: measure to sales with geo holdouts, not media metrics.
facts.source_title: Can Marketing Experimentation Become Your Superpower? (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Marketers' Agency Partnerships Are Strained. Now Comes AI' (11 Oct 2024; ANA data cited, Bain analysis): 92% of ANA member companies used external agencies in 2023 and 82% also had an in-house agency (78% in 2018). Bain estimates generative AI could affect 47% of marketing activities and save 24% of marketing labour time, and advises agency fees should drop by, say, 20%. Its self-test asks if an agency can turn requests around in under 12 hours. Use: renegotiate scope and fees around AI.
facts.source_title: Marketers' Agency Partnerships Are Strained. Now Comes AI (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'What Agency Consolidation Means for CMOs' (6 Feb 2026; agency share-price data to Dec 2025, no survey): after Omnicom's acquisition of IPG, the largest marketing services group is pushing outcome-based pricing, data and technology monetisation and proprietary media inventory. Four lock-in forms: workflow, data and identity, technology, marketing strategy and brand stewardship. Six CMO moves, including treating agency technology like enterprise software and shifting to outcome-based pricing. Use: keep data, identity and measurement portable in agency contracts.
facts.source_title: What Agency Consolidation Means for CMOs (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with Dynata, 'Insurgent Brands Deliver More Value to Consumers and Are Rewarded for It' (8 Mar 2022; over 13,000 US consumers, nearly 75 brands, 10 categories, 30 Elements of Value; consumer survey): insurgents hold 2% to 3% of share but take 25%+ of category growth; brands delivering four or more Elements of Value grew about 3x faster than those delivering one or none; top scorers on life-changing and global-impact elements grew nearly 5x faster than the lowest; under 5% of brands deliver those higher-order elements. Use: map which Elements of Value the brand owns and add higher-order ones.
facts.source_title: Insurgent Brands Deliver More Value to Consumers and Are Rewarded for It (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain (8 Mar 2022; 13,000+ US consumers, nearly 75 brands): insurgents strong on environmental, well-being and ethical Elements of Value grew at twice the rate of other insurgents, and emerging insurgents under $100M revenue score higher across the whole value pyramid than larger ones, suggesting value delivery is harder to keep as brands scale. Insurgents are defined as 10x category growth with at least $25M sales. Use: expect value-communication to erode with scale and re-audit the value pyramid at each size threshold.
facts.source_title: Insurgent Brands Deliver More Value to Consumers and Are Rewarded for It (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Middle East Consumer Products Report 2025' (16 Dec 2025; survey of 3,500 consumers, 20 CPG executive interviews, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Iraq; mixed consumer and executive opinion data): consumer sentiment averages 6.0 of 10 (Saudi 6.8, UAE 6.6, Egypt 5.0, Iraq 4.9); more than half of consumers have boycotted a brand over values misalignment, about three times the US or EU rate; about 37% lack time for daily essentials. Use: audit brand values and public stances carefully before entering MENA markets.
facts.source_title: Middle East Consumer Products Report 2025 (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, 'Middle East Consumer Products Report 2025' (16 Dec 2025; 3,500 consumers, 20 executives): UAE CPG volume grew about 6% against 1.7% globally; the MENA CPG market exceeds $450B, projected up to $650B by 2030. UAE e-commerce is 12% to 14% of retail, expected at 20% to 25% by 2030; Saudi e-grocery is expected at roughly 3% by end-2025 and 12% by 2030; about 42% of Saudi consumers use buy now, pay later. Projections are Bain's. Use: size GCC channel plans around e-grocery and BNPL.
facts.source_title: Middle East Consumer Products Report 2025 (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain with NielsenIQ, 'Profitable Growth in the Middle East in the New Normal' (25 Feb 2022; about 1.4 billion posts analysed, shopper samples not stated): about 69% of UAE and 63% of Saudi consumers will pay more for quality; about 46% of value-conscious UAE consumers always choose private label where possible; top meal-maker manufacturers lost nearly 5% value share to midsize and local players. Fixing availability gaps can bring up to 2 to 3 times market revenue growth. Old data. Use: protect quality and shelf availability against private label.
facts.source_title: How to Drive Profitable Growth in the Middle East in the New Normal (Bain)

facts.statement: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise 2026 (3,235 business and IT leaders, 24 countries, fielded Aug-Sep 2025; executive opinion data): realised AI benefits were productivity or efficiency 66%, better insight and decisions 53%, lower cost 40%, stronger customer relationships 38%, product innovation 20% and higher revenue 20%; 74% hope to grow revenue with AI later. Use: treat revenue and customer-relationship gains as stretch goals and report efficiency gains separately.
facts.source_title: Deloitte: The State of AI in the Enterprise, 2026 AI report

facts.statement: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise (3,235 leaders, 24 countries, Aug-Sep 2025; release 3 Mar 2026; executive opinion data): 25% say AI is transformative for their company, over twice the prior-year share; only 30% redesign key processes around AI and 37% use it at surface level; close to three quarters plan agentic AI within two years, yet only 21% of those report a mature agent governance model. Use: pair every marketing or sales agent rollout with process redesign and governance, not just tool licences.
facts.source_title: Deloitte press room: State of AI in the Enterprise

facts.statement: Deloitte 2025 Connected Consumer (3,524 US consumers, fielded Q2 2025, released 25 Sep 2025; self-report): 70% worry about data privacy and security; only 20% say providers are very clear about what data they collect and 27% are highly confident their data is protected; about 1 in 10 are very willing to share sensitive data; 48% say service benefits outweigh privacy worries, down from 58% in 2024. Use: state what data you collect and why, and ask only for data the next experience needs.
facts.source_title: Deloitte: As Generative AI Gains Ground, Consumers Choose the Innovators They Trust

facts.statement: Deloitte 2025 Connected Consumer (3,524 US consumers, Q2 2025; self-report): 53% use or experiment with generative AI and 82% of them worry about misuse (74% in 2024); about 4 in 10 regular users' households pay for gen AI tools. Consumers who rate providers strong on both innovation and data responsibility spend 62% more a year on devices and 26% more monthly on services than those who see providers lagging on both. Use: present data responsibility as a visible value proposition, not a legal footnote.
facts.source_title: Deloitte: As Generative AI Gains Ground, Consumers Choose the Innovators They Trust

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital 2025 Marketing Investment Trends (1,395 US marketing leaders; page dated 13 May 2025; self-reported survey): organisations that invest more in martech than in working media such as events, digital ads and sponsorships reported 18% greater sales lift from marketing and 7% greater overall revenue growth. At least 61% of marketing budgets are set from enterprise revenue or prior spend. Use: test whether data and stack investment beats extra media before adding spend, and argue for outcome-based budgets.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: 2025 marketing investment trends

facts.statement: Deloitte Canada perspective on agentic AI for CMOs (20 May 2026; thought leadership, no survey of its own): moving marketing to agentic AI means progressing from isolated prompting to single 'lonely' agents to coordinated orchestration. It rests on a documented context layer (strategy, workflows, brand taxonomy, data foundations) and early governance for brand integrity, IP, data compliance and cross-border risk. Few firms coordinate agents across marketing at scale. Use: write the context layer and human approval points before scaling any agent.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Canada: The agentic AI era is here. Where should CMOs focus right now?

facts.statement: Deloitte Digital Marketing Trends 2026 (26 Feb 2026) names five trends: AI as the marketing operating system, ROI accountability, trust and purpose as economic assets, fragmented algorithmic discovery, and rebuilt organisations. Its advice: automate chosen workflows end to end with human approval only at defined risk points, agree one ROI model with the CFO, fix or cut the bottom 20% of spend each quarter, and pick three must-win channels per segment. Consumer percentages on the page have no stated sample. Use: run a quarterly bottom-20% spend review.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Digital: Marketing Trends of 2026

facts.statement: Deloitte analysis of CMO profiles at the 28 largest US banks by assets, from LinkedIn and other public sources (article of 10 Nov 2025): fewer than half of the CMOs have an explicit growth remit. Deloitte sets out three operating models for where growth marketing sits: centralised (CMO office owns shared platforms and standards), hybrid (ownership shared with business lines) and hub and spoke (central strategy, local execution), which it calls probably the current state for many banks. Use: name an owner for growth and pick one of the three models explicitly for multi-unit or regulated clients.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Insights: Bank CMO agenda, driving growth in the AI age

facts.statement: Deloitte Global Marketing Trends 2023, Middle East edition (1,015 C-suite executives and brand leaders worldwide; page dated 31 Jan 2023; executive opinion data): CMOs are prioritising new technologies, expanding markets and customer personalisation to endure uncertain times. Processes and mindsets that encourage creativity, risk-taking and cross-functional collaboration are common among the high-growth brands surveyed. Use: cite as context for protecting personalisation and creative investment in a downturn, not as proof of cause.
facts.source_title: Deloitte Global Marketing Trends 2023

facts.statement: KPMG US 2026 Customer Advisory Research (300+ business leaders; page carries only a 2026 copyright, no publication date; executive opinion data): a KPMG partner says only 5% feel they are fully there on integration towards Total Experience. Named barriers are legacy platforms, fragmented data, complex architectures, siloed teams, misaligned incentives and under-invested change management. KPMG says leaders who align marketing, sales and service report measurable gains but gives no figures in the text. Use: audit the handoffs between marketing, sales and service before buying more AI tools.
facts.source_title: KPMG: 2026 survey, only 5% of executives say front-office integration is complete

facts.statement: KPMG Singapore article 'From CX to Total Experience' (linked to its Customer Experience Excellence Report 2025/26; page undated, no sample or numbers): Total Experience brings customer, employee and ecosystem interactions into one intelligent, adaptive system, and KPMG describes a shift from human-directed journey orchestration to autonomous experience orchestration enabled by agentic AI. It states that Personalisation and Integrity remain the key drivers of loyalty and advocacy. Use: structure a CX and AI roadmap around TX, but verify which driver matters in the client's market before funding it.
facts.source_title: KPMG: From CX to Total Experience, the rise of agentic AI

facts.statement: KPMG Global Tech Report 2026 (2,500 tech executives in 27 countries: 43% EMEA, 29% Asia-Pacific, 28% Americas; all firms above US$100m revenue; January 2026 per file path; executive opinion data): 88% say they are already embedding AI agents in workflows, products and value streams; talent shortages, tech debt and cost pressure hold plans back, and ROI judgments often rest on indirect benefits. Use: treat agent adoption as mainstream in large firms but require measured ROI before scaling a marketing or sales agent.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Global tech report 2026

facts.statement: EY State of Consumer Products 2026 (850+ consumer-products executives, 24 markets, Oxford Economics, fielded 28 Jan-18 Feb 2026; release 11 May 2026; opinion data): 47% expect influencing algorithmic product recommendations to be essential within five years but only 21% can do it today; 15% say integrated commercial data routinely drives decisions; governance and unclear decision rights are the top barrier (35%). EY warns of brands 'never being considered'. Use: audit how AI assistants and retail algorithms rank the client's products and name an owner.
facts.source_title: EY report: AI is reshaping consumer products selection, accelerating brand consideration risk

facts.statement: EY article 'Will the future of retail be led by humans or AI?' (11 Nov 2025; draws on the EY AI Sentiment Study and Future Consumer Index, samples not stated on the page; self-report): 82% consciously used AI in the past six months and 67% in a customer experience, yet only 29% base purchases on AI recommendations; 45% discover products through in-store displays versus 17% through online recommendations; 46% accept an AI shopping assistant. Use: keep physical and human touchpoints in discovery plans and do not over-credit AI recommendations.
facts.source_title: EY: Will the future of retail be led by humans or AI?

facts.statement: EY AI Sentiment Index, UK edition (15,000 people in 15 countries including 1,000 UK consumers; release 5 May 2026; self-report): 74% of UK respondents used AI in the past six months and 35% used it for customer support, but only 43% trust companies to manage AI-related data effectively and 14% would rely on fully autonomous, agent-led systems. Use: in UK work, offer a human option beside AI service and publish plain data-handling commitments.
facts.source_title: EY UK: AI adoption, trust and governance 2026

facts.statement: Accenture Song 'Marketing, the Maestro way' (1,150 cross-functional executives worldwide; 25 Sep 2023; self-reported, correlation only): only 9% of surveyed companies are finding success with the Maestro approach, which treats marketing as a coordinated effort across the company. Those companies report performing 1.8x better on speed to market and 1.6x better on customer lifetime value. Separately, strong collaboration between marketing and other functions is linked to up to 4% more revenue growth. Use: cite as directional support for cross-functional marketing governance, not proof of cause.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Marketing, the Maestro way

facts.statement: Accenture Song Maestro approach (from the 1,150-executive study of Sep 2023): the framework has four steps, See, Solve, Simplify and Scale. They run from seeing customers in new ways, through solving for layered customer journeys and simplifying operations, to scaling through data, technology and talent. Use: use the four steps as a maturity checklist in marketing operating-model reviews.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Marketing, the Maestro way

facts.statement: Accenture Interactive Personalization Pulse Check (8,000 consumers in 8 countries: US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Sweden, Italy, Spain; fielded Nov 2017; release 3 May 2018; self-report): 91% are more likely to shop with brands that recognise and remember them and offer relevant deals, and 48% had left a brand's site to buy elsewhere after a poorly curated experience, up from 40% a year earlier. Dated evidence. Use: use as long-run context for personalisation value; re-test with current data before quoting as a norm.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: widening gap between consumer expectations and reality in personalization

facts.statement: Accenture Interactive Personalization Pulse Check (8,000 consumers, 8 countries, Nov 2017; release 3 May 2018; self-report): 73% said no brand had ever contacted them in a way that felt too personalised; among the 27% who had, 64% were uncomfortable because they had not knowingly provided the data used. Accenture says brands tend to over-collect data when they should design the experience, and 75% would value a living 'style profile'. Use: only personalise from data the customer knowingly gave, and show where it came from.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: widening gap between consumer expectations and reality in personalization

facts.statement: BCG, How Net Revenue Management Boosts the Top and Bottom Line (18 Sep 2017): over the prior three years, price and mix, not volume, produced more than two-thirds of revenue growth at the top 50 global FMCG companies. Across client work (count not stated), over half of promotion spend added no profit for retailer or manufacturer, and rigorous net revenue management programs lifted EBIT by 2-5% of sales. Use: when sizing RGM upside, start with promotion ROI and mix, not list price.
facts.source_title: How Net Revenue Management Boosts the Top and Bottom Line (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG net revenue management (Sep 2017) rests on five levers: brand portfolio pricing, pack-price architecture, mix management, promotion management and trade terms management, supported by five enablers. BCG says most FMCG firms run revenue management as over 70% art and under 30% science, and that managing SKU mix alone can add about 1-2% in pricing improvement a year. Use: audit RGM against the five levers and rank gaps by promotion ROI first.
facts.source_title: How Net Revenue Management Boosts the Top and Bottom Line (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, Paying for Performance: Trade Spending for Profitable Growth (6 Sep 2012): benchmark of nine US consumer-products manufacturers found trade spend rose 3 points faster than revenue and 7 points faster than volume from 2008 to 2010; US trade spend exceeds $60bn a year (about $500bn globally, BCG estimate). No firm followed all ten best practices. Recommendations: back winners, measure return per account and event, pay retailers for performance, phase the change over years. Use: treat trade spend growth above sales growth as a red flag.
facts.source_title: Paying for Performance: Trade Spending for Profitable Growth (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, How to Build a Customer-Back CPG Company (11 Sep 2026) sets five steps: a North Star category story per customer, a cross-functional customer pod with one plan and one P&L per top retailer, shared KPIs and data loops, decision-support tech (AI and agents), and leadership/culture change. BCG says key account managers spend about 70% of time on internal prep versus a target of about 80% with customers, and that freed time could add 1-3 points of revenue (BCG estimates, no sample). Use: restructure key account coverage around joint plans with retailers and track time-with-customer.
facts.source_title: How to Build a Customer-Back CPG Company (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, How Price-Based Compensation Metrics Shape B2B Sales (10 Jun 2024): fewer than 10% of the sales incentive plans BCG reviewed (count not stated) include any price-based metric. Variable pay averages about 40% of total sales compensation, and an incentive metric typically needs at least 20% of target variable pay to influence behavior. Use: when critiquing a comp plan, check for a price or margin metric weighted at 20% or more.
facts.source_title: How Price-Based Compensation Metrics Shape B2B Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's design steps for price-based sales compensation (Jun 2024): align on the pricing behaviors to reward (high-value opportunities, strategic negotiation, better terms, upsell); choose metrics on price realization or margin; decide whether to assess final price position, price improvement or a hybrid; and set the metric's weight in the plan. BCG also suggests multipliers when reps secure favorable terms such as prepayment. Use: checklist for drafting an incentive plan with a pricing component.
facts.source_title: How Price-Based Compensation Metrics Shape B2B Sales (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, Six Keys to Customer Success (Roberge and Andersen, 7 Oct 2019), drawing on BCG studies of leading SaaS firms (counts not stated): (1) focus on customer success as the function's primary purpose, (2) use leading indicators for accountability, (3) create a tight engagement model, (4) act on real-time value and usage data, (5) design the function to cover the whole customer base, (6) hire peers as CSMs. Use: structure customer success coverage and CSM pay around renewal, expansion and adoption.
facts.source_title: Six Keys to Customer Success (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG Six Keys to Customer Success (Oct 2019; BCG and BCG-Gainsight studies, counts not stated): customer lifetime value runs over 25 times first-year value; renewal and expansion rates are the most common bases for CSM bonuses, and almost half of the Gainsight-study firms also paid on adoption. Examples of leading indicators: HubSpot flagged churn risk for customers using under 5 of 20 features in 60 days; Slack tracked 2,000 team messages. Use: define a similar early-usage threshold for each product and alert on it.
facts.source_title: Six Keys to Customer Success (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, The $2T Opportunity to Boost Sales and Lower Costs with RevTech (1 Aug 2022): BCG estimates 30-50% of typical sales budgets are wasted on inefficient processes and sizes lost potential at about $2 trillion. Evidence is case-based, not a survey: a SaaS firm with 2,500 sellers reported 97% forecast accuracy and 30% revenue growth after adopting Clari; a cybersecurity firm using 6sense raised pipeline conversion 500%. Single-company results. Use: justify RevTech spend with forecast and conversion metrics, not vendor claims.
facts.source_title: The $2T Opportunity to Boost Sales and Lower Costs with RevTech (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, Three Steps to Creating Value from B2B Discounts (15 Dec 2015): discounts often reach 30% or more of list-price sales, and BCG says about 80% of B2B firms are fixed or flexible discounters whose discounts are not tied to value. Value-based discounting can lift EBIT by 1-4 points within 18 months. Steps: design discounts around sources of value, set simple guidelines (one discount type per source of value), and enforce in the field with training, near-real-time monitoring, escalation and incentives tied to net price. Use: tie each discount to a customer behavior worth buying.
facts.source_title: Three Steps to Creating Value from B2B Discounts (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, Inflation Is Forcing B2B CEOs to Rethink Pricing (25 Jan 2022), citing its pricing maturity assessment survey (sample not stated): about 33% of companies still reprice only annually or twice a year, and only 25% pass on more than 80% of input-cost increases on time. US intermediate processed-goods producer prices rose 24.4% in 2021. Use: benchmark a client's repricing cadence and pass-through rate against these figures.
facts.source_title: Inflation Is Forcing B2B CEOs to Rethink Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG's inflation pricing advice (Jan 2022) is grouped as act faster, enforce discipline and make nuanced price changes, and says to build advantages in information, strategy and sales preparation. It also suggests temporary price escalators for cost pass-through. Use: draft a pass-through and escalator policy before sales teams face customer pushback.
facts.source_title: Inflation Is Forcing B2B CEOs to Rethink Pricing (BCG)

facts.statement: BCG, Why AI in B2B Pricing Isn't Plug and Play (8 May 2026): a distributor with about $1bn revenue deployed an AI pricing agent analyzing customer-level elasticity across thousands of SKUs and gained 2 margin points, which BCG attributes to sales teams trusting and using real-time recommendations rather than efficiency gains. BCG's experience puts sustained pricing effectiveness at about 70% change management, 20% tools, 10% algorithm. Use: budget most of a pricing-AI rollout for adoption.
facts.source_title: Why AI in B2B Pricing Isn't Plug and Play (BCG)

facts.statement: Bain, How Leaders Get the Most Out of Their Salesforce (20 Mar 2011): from 25 successful sales transformations, six TOPS tools emerged; Bain has seen companies raise profitability by as much as 25% over sustained periods, with the full boost typically arriving over two to three years. Adding trained support staff for lead qualification, outbound selling and deal closing can return as much as 30% of a rep's day. A European business services firm that revamped pay and expanded its bonus pool added 14% of operating profit in year one. Use: audit rep time on non-selling work before changing headcount.
facts.source_title: How Leaders Get the Most Out of Their Salesforce (Bain)
