facts.statement: Bain, Revving Up Sales ROI for a Downturn (3 Apr 2020; client examples, no survey sample): at a major technology hardware company A-quality reps were 30% more productive than B-quality reps; a leading software company cut negotiated discounts by three to four percentage points; a manufacturer cut total selling costs 10% with no reduction in revenue growth. Use: when productivity lags, look at rep quality mix and discount discipline first.
facts.source_title: Revving Up Sales ROI for a Downturn (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Why Consumer Product Companies Need to Solve Revenue Growth Management (undated page, text refers to 2022; Bain interviews and research, sample not stated): over 80% of CP CEOs interviewed are dissatisfied with RGM results; about 50% of promotional sales cannibalize non-promoted sales and about 80% of promo spend adds nothing to category growth; about 70% of SKUs add complexity for under 5% of revenue; 10-30% of profit may be at risk. Use: open an RGM diagnostic with these tests (cannibalization, SKU tail, promo ROI).
facts.source_title: Why Consumer Product Companies Need to Solve Revenue Growth Management (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Revenue Growth Management Helps CPGs Battle Inflation (Caldarelli and Mologni, 10 Jan 2023; no sample): five moves: seize the leadership moment by defending the shared profit pool with new KPIs; make bold moves, starting with stopping value leakage and a zero-based redesign beyond price; transform the organization with cross-functional work, scenario planning and KPI-linked incentives; elevate the retailer relationship by creating joint value while protecting category value; focus on strategic markets, especially Europe. Use: frame an RGM reset around profit-pool defense.
facts.source_title: Revenue Growth Management Helps CPGs Battle Inflation (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Unlimited Partners (12 May 2020): Bain's database tracks over 300,000 tech channel partners, and 64% are emerging or small firms by revenue, so many are exposed to sustained financial shocks. Bain advises vendors to check partner health, redefine engagement (events online, faster digital tools), fill technology gaps in the ecosystem and set near-term actions by partner role; it also suggests relief such as payment terms or discounts and pandemic-relevant training. Use: in a downturn, protect partner viability.
facts.source_title: Unlimited Partners (Bain)

facts.statement: Bain, Better Matchmaking with B2B Channel Partners (Depeyrot, 7 Aug 2019): Bain's database holds estimated bookings and technical capabilities for about 200,000 channel partners by country. A technology OEM used it to decide which partners deserved more attention and resources, and Bain says experience shows it can unlock 5-10% channel revenue growth (vendor claim). A linked Bain brief teaser says SaaS vendors prefer partners with advanced capabilities, such as customer success that encourages renewals. Use: rank partners by capability and potential before allocating funds.
facts.source_title: Better Matchmaking with B2B Channel Partners (Bain)

facts.statement: Deloitte CFO Signals, 3Q 2025 (published 15 Oct 2025; 200 North American CFOs at firms with $1bn+ revenue, fielded 3-17 Sep 2025; opinion data): 86% expect pricing to matter more to financial performance in the next 12 months; 50% name competitive pressure and 34% trade policy as the top pricing factor; barriers to fast repricing are missing data (55%), no cohesive strategy (54%), weak tools (50%); yet 81% call their pricing process mature. Use: expect buyers to be re-pricing; show pricing-tool and governance gaps behind self-rated maturity.
facts.source_title: North American CFO Signals 3Q 2025 (Deloitte)

facts.statement: Deloitte, Revenue Growth Management Strategy (consumer products; undated, 2024 file path; sample not stated): citing its 2025 Consumer Products Industry Outlook, 62% of respondents said RGM capabilities would play a major role in their success in the year ahead. Deloitte says RGM focus is shifting from price toward promotions, assortment, trade terms and price-pack architecture as pricing gains fade and inflation eases (opinion data). Use: when price headroom is gone, prioritize promotion, assortment and pack levers.
facts.source_title: Revenue Growth Management Strategy (Deloitte)

facts.statement: Deloitte Sales and Commercial Transformation (consumer products, undated page), vendor-reported client results without named clients or samples: 3-5% more sales opportunities from targeted pricing and promotion, a 6% operating profit lift from redesigning route to market, and $100M of trade funds reallocated after removing inefficient spend. Deloitte's benchmark study says retail and CPG partners want to collaborate 1.2 to 2 times more than today. Use: treat as directional upside ranges, not guaranteed outcomes.
facts.source_title: Sales and Commercial Transformation Solution (Deloitte)

facts.statement: Deloitte, Generative AI in Wholesale Distribution (undated, likely 2025; Deloitte analysis, method not stated): applying GenAI to sales enablement, quote generation, order entry and post-sales support could add 75-100 basis points of EBIT for the average wholesale distributor; sales and service labor is typically 5-7% of expenses. Deloitte lists five enablement use cases (strategy support, collateral, personalized learning, call-note synthesis, next-best-action) without quantified results. Use: scope sales-enablement AI around quoting and order entry first.
facts.source_title: Generative AI in Wholesale Distribution (Deloitte)

facts.statement: KPMG US life sciences sales leader pulse survey (2022; 100 commercial and sales leaders split evenly across biotech/pharma, health IT, medical devices; opinion data), reported on a KPMG article (page undated, URL 2023): leading organizations average 40% more commercial operations headcount, 44% lower cost per seller and 42% higher productivity per seller than laggards. Over 90% of leaders have high-quality internal data; 74% rank customer intelligence the most important sales operations function. Use: fund sales ops and data quality before adding reps.
facts.source_title: The key levers for ROI and revenue growth (KPMG)

facts.statement: KPMG Sales Leader Pulse Survey (2022; 100 life-sciences commercial leaders; opinion data), article undated (URL 2023): 70% moved to a hybrid in-person/digital sales model and 87% expect the changes to stay; leaders raised budgets 33% in year one and 25% in year two; all said tech spend paid back. Later, 95% rated data and analytics very important, 81% AI, 82% staff training; AI spend rose 13 points while CRM upgrades fell 10. Use: pair data, AI and training investment instead of CRM-only upgrades.
facts.source_title: Targeted investments in the front office delivered revenue growth (KPMG)

facts.statement: KPMG Pricing and Commercial Strategy (page undated, 2026 copyright): KPMG frames pricing work with four questions: pricing strategy (which customer segments, how offerings fit), price setting (what a product is worth to each segment; cost, competition and value), price execution (linking pricing to sales processes, discount leakage), and embedment (sustaining prices through people, governance and data). KPMG claims 3-8% return on sales in incremental impact, typically within 3-12 months, with quick wins of 50-100 bps (vendor claim, no sample). Use: scope pricing and discount governance reviews with the four questions.
facts.source_title: Pricing and commercial strategy (KPMG)

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon 2023 Private Equity B2B Pricing Study (31 May 2023; PE-backed B2B firms in North America, Europe, Asia; respondent count not stated): firms that raised prices most had invested 25% more in data analytics and 48% more in pricing tools; high-growth firms raised prices 10.5% in 2022 versus 2.6% for low-growth. High-growth firms were 37% less likely to let salespeople control pricing. Of firms raising prices over 5% in 2022, 95% grew over 5%. Use: centralize price authority in a commercial or pricing team and fund tools.
facts.source_title: 2023 Private Equity B2B Pricing Study (EY)

facts.statement: EY field-force behavioral benchmarking (page undated; EY data over 13 years, 1,000+ organizations, 120,000+ customer-facing roles, life sciences focus): high-performing reps were twice as likely to beat sales-versus-target and sold 10% more than peers; high-performing managers up to 2.2 times more likely to lead teams to target. Where the program was used, over 35% of new hires reached the top quartile in year one versus under 10% otherwise, and onboarding time fell about 40%. Vendor-reported. Use: build coaching and onboarding around observed top-performer behaviors.
facts.source_title: Field-force Behavioral Benchmarking Services (EY)

facts.statement: EY-Parthenon 2025 PE Pricing Report (page undated; survey of global PE funds, sample not stated; opinion data): managers least exposed to unforeseen risk looked at pricing 55% of the time, versus 35% for the most exposed. Use: make pricing review a standing agenda item rather than a reaction to margin pressure.
facts.source_title: 2025 EY-Parthenon PE Pricing Report (EY)

facts.statement: Accenture study of B2B customer experience (28 Sep 2017; 1,350 sales, service and marketing executives in 10 countries, 16 industries, fielded May 2017; opinion data): 97% say indirect channels are critical, but only 21% have total control of their sales partner networks and 84% lack visibility into partner pipelines. Firms with integrated partner lead generation and coaching were 63% more likely to beat indirect revenue goals. Use: give partners shared pipeline visibility, lead flow and coaching.
facts.source_title: Growth at Stake as B2B Companies Lose Control Over Customer Experience (Accenture)

facts.statement: Accenture Interactive B2B buyer-seller research (11 Nov 2019; 748 buyers and 1,499 sellers, 10 countries, 16 industries, fielded Mar 2019; opinion data): 80% of frequent buyers expect to switch suppliers at least once within 24 months; 96% of service-focused leaders report higher profitability and 97% higher market share; 62% of laggard sellers invested in sales plays without salesperson support versus 48% of service-minded sellers. Use: involve sellers in designing sales plays and tie them to service outcomes.
facts.source_title: 80% of B2B Buyers Have Switched From Suppliers (Accenture)

facts.statement: HBS Working Knowledge (6 Jul 2015) on Chung and Narayandas's field experiment: 80 salespeople at water-purifier branches in four Indian cities, 14 weeks of schemes in 2013, weekly bonus of 500 rupees (about 27% of pay). Bonuses conditional on hitting a quota set 20% above typical sales lifted sales about 20%; unconditional bonuses framed as gifts lifted sales about 10%, mainly from high performers; bonuses handed over upfront cut performance about 8% on average. Small single-firm study. Use: attach incentives to a quota, never pay in advance.
facts.source_title: Money and Quotas Motivate the Sales Force Best (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: HBS Working Knowledge (22 Mar 2017) on Chung and Narayandas's quota-frequency experiment: 337 employees at a Swedish electronics retailer with 94 stores, 30 days in May 2015, daily quota versus existing monthly quota. Sales productivity rose 4.9% in aggregate and 18% for the weakest salespeople, but all salespeople shifted toward low-ticket items and high-margin sales fell. Use: short quota periods suit volume pushes; test them before use where margin or big-ticket mix matters.
facts.source_title: What's the Ideal Frequency for a Sales Quota? (HBS Working Knowledge)

facts.statement: HBR, Sales Teams Aren't Great at Forecasting. Here's How to Fix That (Bob Suh, 19 Mar 2019; essay, no sample; only the page summary was readable): argues the root causes of most forecast inaccuracies are human behavior, not faulty algorithms. The article's specific remedies were not confirmed. Use: treat forecast accuracy as a behavior and incentive problem, not only a tooling one.
facts.source_title: Sales Teams Aren't Great at Forecasting. Here's How to Fix That (HBR)

facts.statement: HBR, Setting Better Sales Goals with Analytics (Chung, Huber, Murthy, Sunku and Weber, 9 Jul 2019; sample not stated): says poorly set sales targets often fail to deliver expected benefits and can demoralize the sales force, and cites studies that revising compensation in line with market trends can have about a 50% greater impact on sales than advertising (presented as an example). Use: treat quota and pay design as a high-leverage lever and test it.
facts.source_title: Setting Better Sales Goals with Analytics (HBR)

facts.statement: HBR, How to Make Your Sales Forecasts More Accurate (Lou Shipley, HBS senior lecturer, 28 Aug 2019; essay, no sample): says consistently accurate forecasts are valuable but rare, mainly because sales and marketing are not aligned, calling alignment a prerequisite for forecast accuracy. Use: agree shared lead and stage definitions between marketing and sales before tuning the forecast model.
facts.source_title: How to Make Your Sales Forecasts More Accurate (HBR)

facts.statement: HBR, How to Really Motivate Salespeople (Doug Chung, April 2015 issue; only the summary was readable): says much advice on sales pay has come from theory and lab experiments, and that field studies over the past decade test these ideas in real business settings, challenging some conventional wisdom. Chung's field work on quotas and bonuses (see HBS Working Knowledge) supports quota-linked incentives. Use: test pay changes in a field pilot before rolling out.
facts.source_title: How to Really Motivate Salespeople (HBR)

facts.statement: Strategy& (PwC), Sales Effectiveness: The Overlooked Growth Engine (Dec 2025; page blocked with HTTP 403, confirmed via search-visible text and a companion PDF dated Dec 2025): frames sales effectiveness as four growth levers (retain, grow, acquire, enable) over five capability pillars (people, structure, process, technology, strategy), and warns that weakness in one lever pushes teams to overdeliver elsewhere. Use: map a sales diagnostic onto the levers-by-pillars grid to find the weakest cell.
facts.source_title: Sales Effectiveness: The Overlooked Growth Engine (Strategy&)

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 13th edition (22,000+ consumers, 28 countries, EY release 9 Nov 2023): 35% say they are increasingly willing to pay extra for brands they trust, up 10% from Feb 2022 (EY's wording; points versus percent is not specified). 54% plan to buy less overall, and 71% plan to hold some purchases for festive sales events versus 48% in Nov 2021. Consumer survey, stated intent. Use: back premium pricing with trust proof and plan promotions around sale peaks.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: consumers learning to live with less as climate change and cost of living reality hits home

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 13th edition (22,000+ consumers, 28 countries, 9 Nov 2023): 61% say private label helps them save and 64% say it meets their needs as well as branded goods, yet interest in private label had declined in every category. 61% plan to join Black Friday or Singles' Day sales (China 75%, Europe 54%, US 50%); online-only or mostly-online shopping rose 16 points. Consumer survey. Use: when benchmarking against private label, defend with quality proof and keep sale-event offers channel-specific.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: consumers learning to live with less as climate change and cost of living reality hits home

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 11th edition (21,000+ consumers, fielded 23 Sep to 14 Oct 2022, EY release 23 Dec 2022): the affordability-first and planet-first segments were each 25% of respondents; EY reported experience-first at 28% as the largest group in Asia (the page's comparison wording is unclear). 92% were concerned about their country's economy and 87% about personal finances. Consumer survey. Use: segment messages by priority, not demographics alone, and re-measure the mix each quarter.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index (11th edition) press release

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 11th edition (21,000+ consumers, Sep-Oct 2022): 52% were spending less on non-essentials, 42% planned less takeout and delivery, and 89% planned to spend less or no more on family this holiday season. Among affordability-first shoppers 59% bought only essentials; 48% of all respondents refused to share personal data for cheaper personalized alternatives. Consumer survey. Use: do not assume data-for-discount offers will work; test opt-in rates before building them into promotions.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index (11th edition) press release

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 10th edition (18,000 consumers, 24 countries, fielded 18 May to 7 Jun 2022, EY release 15 Aug 2022): 33% were trying new brands and 21% were switching to private label, which EY reads as about a third of a brand's addressable market at risk. 79% were worried about finances and 62% expected living costs to rise. Consumer survey. Use: treat price-pressure periods as brand-switching windows and defend with retention offers to at-risk segments.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: rising cost of living forces consumers to tighten grip on finances

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 10th edition (18,000 consumers, 24 markets, fielded 18 May to 7 Jun 2022, EY release 15 Aug 2022): consumers were putting affordability ahead of sustainability. 67% said the high price of sustainable goods deters them, yet negative beliefs eased: the share linking sustainable products with low quality fell from 67% (May 2021) to 58%, and distrust of manufacturers' sustainability claims from 59% to 51%. Consumer survey. Use: lead green claims with fair-price value and evidence; avoid premium-only positioning in downturns.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: rising cost of living forces consumers to tighten grip on finances

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 9th edition (18,000 consumers, 24 countries, fielded 28 Jan to 15 Feb 2022, EY release 29 Mar 2022): 52% said rising costs affect their buying (62% lower-income, 48% middle, 42% high income). Segment shares by first priority were Planet 26%, Affordability 24%, Experience 20%; experience priority had doubled since 2020. 42% planned to spend more on experiences and 36% would only visit stores with a great experience. Consumer survey. Use: weight offers toward experience value for high-income groups and price for low-income groups.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: rising costs dent post-pandemic hopes

facts.statement: EY Future Consumer Index, 9th edition (18,000 consumers, 24 countries, Jan-Feb 2022): 42% said they would buy only from brands whose values match their own (same share among Gen Z, 48% among millennials), and 56% would pay more attention to environmental impact, 52% to social impact. Opinion data, stated intent. Use: test values-led messaging with younger segments, but verify against actual purchase data before scaling.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index: rising costs dent post-pandemic hopes

facts.statement: EY Italia release on the Future Consumer Index (28 Apr 2022, Milan; over 17,000 people worldwide including 500 in Italy; edition and fieldwork not stated): 51% of Italian respondents said rising prices strain them, 46% expect to visit physical stores less often, and 31% intend to buy online what they used to buy in stores. Among those willing to spend on experiences missed during the pandemic, 50% would share data for a personalized experience. Consumer survey, Italy sub-sample. Use: treat data-for-personalization as an opt-in test.
facts.source_title: EY Future Consumer Index 2022 (EY Italia)

facts.statement: EY, 'Loyalty has outgrown the loyalty program' (EY Studio+, 3 Mar 2026; no statistics): argues loyalty is being reinvented around delivery and context, not rewards. Seven shifts include relief from effort, emotional awareness, portable identity, rewarding attention, and belonging. Three-step method: understand the human, build identity and decisioning enablers, then test small. Trust rests on permission and control; AI agents may soon choose brands for customers. Use: redesign loyalty around reduced effort and permissioned data; keep tests small and track emotional response.
facts.source_title: Loyalty has outgrown the loyalty program

facts.statement: EY loyalty ROI method (EY article 20 Dec 2024): members are often already better customers, so first remove selection bias with pre/post, difference-in-difference or test-versus-control designs. Then count direct costs (rewards, platform, operations) and indirect costs (compliance, points liability, data, support) against direct benefits (spend, frequency, basket, retention) and indirect ones (referrals, NPS, personalization data). Cites the 2024 EY Loyalty Market Study: 41% of loyalty leaders struggle to quantify impact (sample not stated). Use: never report loyalty ROI without a control group.
facts.source_title: How to unlock value from, measure and demonstrate loyalty program ROI

facts.statement: EY 2026 Loyalty Market Study, third edition (EY US page; undated, no sample or figures shown): programs still perform on enrolment and ROI, but churn is rising, customers use fewer programs and check rewards less often, and sentiment is turning neutral. Three customer groups define value differently: access and experiences, simplicity and time savings, clear immediate financial value; gaps versus 2025 became more visible. Use: segment loyalty offers by these three motives and simplify reward mechanics.
facts.source_title: 2026 EY Loyalty Market Study

facts.statement: EY 'Accelerating customer loyalty' (EY, 30 Aug 2024): five considerations to rebuild a loyalty program: orient teams around the whole journey, make trust the base with a cross-functional team, personalize from purchase and preference data plus community and purpose, lean on zero- and first-party data as cookies fade, and power it with omnichannel and AI. Quotes 79% saying programs affect repeat purchase and 80% buying more often after joining (sample not stated). Use: treat these shares as directional claims only.
facts.source_title: Accelerating customer loyalty: leveraging trust, technology and data

facts.statement: EY zero-party data article (4 Aug 2023): zero-party data is what consumers volunteer with clear terms of use. Four success factors: a privacy-first relationship, visible trust and transparency, an incentive structure that raises both volume and quality of shared data, and careful platform choice. Cites the EY-Parthenon 2022 Realizing Strategy Survey, where 75% of executives rated customer experience above traditional strategy elements (sample not stated). Use: design preference centers with a stated value exchange before collecting data.
facts.source_title: Zero-party: the next frontier in consumer data

facts.statement: EY 'How to get the most out of your marketing spend' (2 Dec 2025): budgets should be read as four linked pools (agency fees, media, martech/AI/data, people), because trimming one in isolation shifts cost into another. Four actions: review the whole marketing P&L, measure at strategic, tactical and operational levels, rethink every role and partner for AI, and invest to optimize. Cites Gartner that 24% of CMOs had enough 2024 budget (sample not stated). Use: reallocate across all four pools, not line by line.
facts.source_title: How to get the most out of your marketing spend

facts.statement: EY, 'The sameness trap' (15 Apr 2026): in hundreds of executive workshops with AI, unrelated teams produced near-identical snack concepts (earthy packaging, matcha, adaptogens). EY argues AI extrapolates the past, so differentiation comes from human taste. It proposes Human-AI-Human: define hypothesis and guardrails first, let AI draft, then humans challenge it. Qualitative; no sample statistics. Use: write the brand hypothesis before prompting AI, and have a reviewer argue against AI output.
facts.source_title: The sameness trap: the efficiency engine that erases your edge

facts.statement: EY, 'How AI is reshaping the future of marketing' (4 May 2026): four tenets: agents become the new front door, content is made at scale and read by machines, marketing runs as one continuous operating system, and empathy is the differentiator. Quoted figures (89% of marketers call personalization essential versus about 60% of customers feeling it; search volume down 25% by 2026) come from unnamed third parties, no samples. Use: define which decisions are automated, then govern brand voice for machine readers.
facts.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of marketing

facts.statement: EY, 'How to win in agentic commerce' (8 Jul 2026): AI agents will compare offers on structured facts (prices, availability, eligibility, policies), so differentiation that is not machine-readable is invisible. Choose a role (orchestrator, participant, platform partner), set autonomy per journey from recommend-only to full autonomy, and start with five moves: one authoritative source of commercial truth, policies as executable rules, governed read-only agent access, one or two P&L-tied pilots, and shaping agent preference. No sample data. Use: publish clean product, price and policy data.
facts.source_title: How to win in agentic commerce as AI agents decide and transact

facts.statement: EY on creative operations (24 Oct 2024): CMOs face more formats and personalization at flat cost. Three priorities: organize (shared services or agile pods, selected in-housing), upgrade tools (workflow automation, asset management, GenAI with human review and rights checks), and use creators, specialist agencies and user-generated content. Figures are third-party and unsampled (for example, 55% of marketers partly use GenAI, per Gartner 2023). Use: build a reuse-first asset library with rights tracking before scaling AI content.
facts.source_title: How CMOs can leverage the full potential of creative

facts.statement: EY, 'How AI is reshaping the future of sales' (Avis and Goonan, 6 Aug 2025): five tenets for sales: radically reduce complexity, unleash collaboration, personalized treatment per customer across channels, real-time product optimization from feedback, and use partner ecosystems. Four enterprise AI adoption levels run from no meaningful use (0) to AI embedded in culture and strategy (3). Cites Gartner: sellers with strong GenAI partnership skills are 3.7 times likelier to meet quota, yet only 7% have them (samples not stated). Use: rate each sales workflow against the four levels and fix data first.
facts.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of sales

facts.statement: EY Studio+ 'Revenue Drift Map' (18 Aug 2026): names five drifts in B2B revenue: pipeline, expansion, demand (research moving to AI-mediated discovery), decision (buying groups stalling), and model (pricing no longer matching AI value). Maps each by visible versus invisible and owned versus unowned. EY's analysis of 124 listed B2B companies in 21 sectors over 36 months reports net revenue retention falling from 106% (2022) to 101% (2025) and 40% of qualified pipeline ending in no decision. Use: assign an owner to each drift.
facts.source_title: Revenue optimization in a world of AI-powered buyers

facts.statement: EY Studio+ 'AI experience design' (Patricia Camden, 25 Aug 2026; no statistics): argues AI initiatives stall on user confidence rather than model capability, because people remain accountable for outcomes. Experience design moves upstream, to how recommendations are formed before users reach an interface. When reviewing AI output, people tend to approve everything because of volume or verify everything out of distrust, so expected productivity gains fail. Use: show customers and staff when and why AI decided.
facts.source_title: How AI is reshaping experience design

facts.statement: strategy+business, '10 Principles of Customer Strategy' (Strategy& authors Ripsam and Bouquet, 26 Sep 2016): ten principles, from mastering what is technically possible and knowing customers granularly to tying strategy to identity, targeting where you can win, treating customers as growing assets, seamless omnichannel, reorganizing around the customer, and matching culture. Survey of 161 executives (April 2016, from over 15,000 invited): 73% with customer-insight priority had the capability but 46% turned it into plans. Use: audit the insight-to-action gap.
facts.source_title: 10 Principles of Customer Strategy

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'How to deliver great customer experience at scale' (ActiveCampaign's chief customer officer, 7 Dec 2020): support cost should not grow in step with the customer base. Three pillars: engagement (self-service, communities with power users), expectations (a published menu of services with minimum service levels), and empowerment (journey-based options that raise lifetime value). Cited figures (96% would leave over bad CX; 93% of Peloton members renew monthly) are secondary with no samples. Use: publish service levels and invest in self-service before adding headcount.
facts.source_title: How to deliver great customer experience at scale

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Customer Loyalty Isn't What It Used to Be' (Medallia's Benjamin and Graham, 10 Oct 2016): shared online experiences make switching easy, so earned experience beats points. Four capabilities: see yourself as customers do, wire feedback into every decision, hold people accountable for customer behaviours, and innovate at scale. Medallia data cited: top-quartile NPS improvers ran seven times more tests than bottom-quartile (140+ programs); dealers sharing feedback with 20+ staff had about 15% higher sales. Vendor data. Use: widen who sees customer feedback.
facts.source_title: Customer Loyalty Isn't What It Used to Be

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'The untapped potential of B2B customer loyalty programs' (PwC US authors Rolston and Glick, 1 Jun 2021): apply B2C loyalty principles to B2B in five actions: segment business buyers, reward the behaviours you want, keep the design simple, lead with digital, and build the best experience. In a PwC customer survey (sample not stated) almost 60% of B2B customers had never felt special with a brand. A lawn-care supplier moved to performance-based incentives and reported 20% CAGR in independent channels. Use: reward growth behaviours, not volume.
facts.source_title: The untapped potential of B2B customer loyalty programs

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'The Marketer's Dilemma' (Strategy& authors Vollmer, Bennin and Bothun, 24 Oct 2016): channels multiplied but attention shrank, so the linear marketing value chain became a customer-centered ecosystem. Marketers need firsthand insight, integrated experiences, breakthrough content and ROI experiments. Cites a Duke Fuqua 2015 survey in which 61% of 288 CMOs felt pressure to prove marketing's value, and Coca-Cola's reported 70/20/10 split across proven, scaling and new bets. Use: set an explicit proven/scaling/experimental budget split.
facts.source_title: The Marketer's Dilemma

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Grow from Your Strengths' (Strategy& authors Adolph and Greenwood, 18 Aug 2015): capabilities-driven growth. Four approaches: in-market leverage with existing customers, near-market expansion into adjacencies, disruptive growth (rarer than executives assume), and capability development through M&A, innovation and operations. Warns of an adjacency trap when firms move into businesses where their strengths do not apply (the Sears and Dean Witter deal is the example). Reports capabilities-minded acquirers beating others by over 14 points of TSR. Use: sequence growth bets from in-market to adjacent.
facts.source_title: Grow from Your Strengths

facts.statement: Strategy& Fit for Growth Index (strategy+business, 'How Ready Are You for Growth?', 27 Aug 2013, Booz & Company): scores firms 1-5 on strategic clarity (50% weight), resource alignment (30%) and supportive organization (20%). Of 197 companies in 17 industries (Europe and North America), only 17% fell in the two strong archetypes, 'In the Game' or 'Ready for Growth'. Index scores tracked total shareholder return Aug 2010 to Jul 2012. Use: score a growth plan on clarity, resources and organization before adding spend.
facts.source_title: How Ready Are You for Growth?

facts.statement: Strategy& Fit for Growth transformation (Couto, Caglar and Plansky, strategy+business 10 Jan 2017, from their Wiley book): treat every cost as a choice, invest in a few differentiating capabilities and cut elsewhere. Three phases: case for change, design and dialogue (announce a savings target; the article's illustration is 20% of operating expense), and the new normal. Middle managers carry trust. Qualitative, no survey sample. Use: tie any cost cut to named capabilities being funded and brief managers first.
facts.source_title: Building trust while cutting costs

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'The four building blocks of transformation' (Kent, Lancefield and Reilly, 22 Oct 2018): lasting change comes from building a capacity for change, not one restructuring. Blocks: a strategic identity tied to distinctive capabilities, design for trust, master the pivot from sprint to scale, and treat legacy as an asset. Cases include Conagra shrinking from about $18bn to about $8bn as a focused brand company, with over $300m annual savings reported. Use: pilot small, then scale only proven ideas; tie each pilot to the identity.
facts.source_title: The four building blocks of transformation

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Why the Right Mix of Products, Customers, and Markets Is an Overlooked Profits Lever' (PwC US, Jones and McCue, 24 Jan 2017): profit varies widely by segment, and the article says some segments earn 10 to 100 times others. Three steps: map value with internal P&L, external profit-pool and future heat maps; chart a shortlist of value moves; set owners, milestones and KPIs. Its own example (profit 22M versus 31M on equal revenue) implies about 41%, not the stated 50%. Use: compute segment profit before setting growth targets.
facts.source_title: Why the Right Mix of Products, Customers, and Markets Is an Overlooked Profits Lever

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'How to Be a More Coherent Marketer' (Booz & Company, 29 May 2012): a survey of 350 marketing professionals (Booz, Korn/Ferry, ANA) found 50% rated five or more capabilities most important, and funding was the top barrier to building them (44%). The article sorts capabilities into right-to-play, right-to-compete and right-to-win, and urges funding only a few cross-functional right-to-win ones. Survey of practitioners, 2012 vintage. Use: rank marketing capabilities into the three tiers and cap the number funded.
facts.source_title: How to Be a More Coherent Marketer

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Growth Champions' (Landry, Tipping and Kumar, Booz Allen, 30 May 2006): the online Marketing Profiler, with more than 2,000 respondents, sorted marketing organizations into six types. Growth Champions, which take on growth work such as innovation and new business development, were about 9% of firms and 20% likelier than the other types to show superior revenue growth and profitability for their industry. CMOs averaged 23 months in role. Old, self-selected online survey. Use: widen marketing's remit to product and new-business decisions.
facts.source_title: Growth Champions

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Consumer companies must take leaps, not steps' (PwC's Ozturk and Kahn, 9 Oct 2020): citing PwC's Global Consumer Insights Survey (sample not stated), about 90% of online grocery shoppers planned to keep buying online after distancing ended, and before the pandemic 43% expected firms to be accountable for environmental impact. Five moves: steady prices through forecasting and price optimization, visible safety, digital shift, blended physical-digital stores, and what customers care about. Use: treat price stability as a trust signal.
facts.source_title: Consumer companies must take leaps, not steps

facts.statement: strategy+business blog, 'Reimagine your entire brand portfolio' (Strategy& authors Clausen and Egol, 7 Aug 2020): five actions for consumer goods after the pandemic shift: rethink product strategy, reprioritize the innovation portfolio, restructure the SKU range (keep, renovate or eliminate each item), redesign products for value through ingredients and packaging, and speed testing and commercialization. References PwC's return on experience (ROX) idea. No quantitative data. Use: run a keep-renovate-eliminate review of products against shifted needs.
facts.source_title: Reimagine your entire brand portfolio

facts.statement: strategy+business, 'Bring on the Super-CMO' by Steve Silver (20 May 2003, Booz & Company): marketing has shrunk into communications management. It contrasts 'Big M' leaders who manage the whole brand portfolio and work across functions with 'small m' communicators, and lists five skills for strategic marketers: spotting trends early, building plans that meet financial goals, mining customer motivation, directing agencies for consistent positioning, and building consensus. Opinion essay, no sample. Use: set a role profile for senior marketers around strategy skills.
facts.source_title: Bring on the Super-CMO

facts.statement: PwC 27th Annual Global CEO Survey (4,702 CEOs, 105 countries and territories, fielded 2 Oct to 10 Nov 2023, launched at Davos mid-Jan 2024): 45% of CEOs doubted their company would be viable in a decade on its current path, up from 39% a year earlier; 56% of CEOs at firms under US$100 million revenue said so (seen in secondary coverage only). Executive opinion data. Use: pair growth plans with a reinvention hypothesis.
facts.source_title: PwC 27th Annual Global CEO Survey

facts.statement: PwC 28th Annual Global CEO Survey (4,701 CEOs, 109 countries and territories, fielded 1 Oct to 8 Nov 2024, published Jan 2025): about 58% expected global economic growth to improve over 12 months, 42% said their company would not be viable beyond a decade on its current path (45% a year earlier, although PwC called the level consistent with prior years), and 42% planned to raise headcount by at least 5%. Executive opinion data via PwC pages and press. Use: treat reinvention pressure as persistent.
facts.source_title: PwC 2025 Global CEO Survey

facts.statement: PwC Future of Customer Experience Survey 2017/18 (about 15,000 consumers in 12 countries): 73% said a positive experience is among the key factors shaping their brand loyalty, and consumers said they would pay up to about a 16% price premium for great customer experience (the top figure, varying by product type). Consumer survey, old but widely cited. Confirmed via PwC press release text and press coverage; PwC pages blocked. Use: test experience-upgrade price premiums locally rather than assuming this ceiling.
facts.source_title: PwC press release: customer experience is everything

facts.statement: PwC Global Consumer Insights Pulse Survey (February 2023 edition; 9,180 consumers in 25 territories, fielded Dec 2022): 53% were holding back on non-essential spending and 15% had stopped it altogether. Other PwC regional releases combine these as 69% reducing spend, so check which framing a figure uses. Consumer survey. Confirmed via PwC Slovakia release text; PwC global page blocked. Use: model promotion elasticity per segment, not one average.
facts.source_title: PwC Consumer Insights Survey (Slovakia release)

facts.statement: KPMG UAE Customer Experience Excellence report, 2025 edition: Emirates ranked first with a CEE score of 8.81 (up 0.40) and NPS 68, Etihad Airways second at 8.60 (NPS 56), IKEA third at 8.35 (NPS 49). Emirates Islamic Bank climbed 42 places, Careem 32 and Daman 24. Consumer opinion data. Use: when benchmarking Gulf CX, set targets against the leaders' score-and-NPS pairing, not the market average.
facts.source_title: KPMG UAE: Customer Experience Excellence report (2025 edition)

facts.statement: KPMG UAE CEE 2025 press release (5 May 2025; 104 brands): integrity now ranks above personalisation as the strongest CX driver in the UAE, and empathy is still the area where brands are working to improve (KPMG calls it a key differentiator). UAE scores rose 1.5%. Travel and hospitality led, with average growth of 1.3% a year since 2017; financial services averaged 1.5% a year. Consumer opinion data. Use: lead UAE brand proof with fairness and after-sales reliability, then add personalisation and visible empathy.
facts.source_title: KPMG UAE: Humanizing AI is the new competitive edge for UAE brands

facts.statement: KPMG UAE CEE release (23 April 2024; 104 brands; sample not stated): Emirates ranked first for the third year running, followed by ADCB, Etihad Airways and IKEA. The CEE metric fell 3.8% across most markets and 1.5% in the UAE; KPMG links the fall to technology pushing customers into low-cost channels with little empathy or human contact. Air Arabia, HSBC and Deliveroo each gained 3% by cutting customer effort. Use: before shifting service to cheaper digital channels, keep a human escalation path and track customer effort.
facts.source_title: KPMG UAE: KPMG's annual CEE report (April 2024)

facts.statement: KPMG Germany CEE 2024 (over 7,000 German respondents rating 200+ brands in 11 industries, about 73,300 opinions): the German average CEE score was 7.43, back at its 2019 level after a 2023 fall. Automotive led at 7.77, retail 7.64, entertainment and media 7.53. The share of top performers more than doubled and low performers nearly halved. Consumer opinion data. Use: set German CX targets by sector, benchmarking automotive and retail near 7.6 to 7.8 and the cross-sector average near 7.4.
facts.source_title: KPMG Germany: Die Customer Experience Excellence Studie 2024

facts.statement: KPMG Germany CEE 2024 (7,000+ respondents, 200+ brands, 11 industries): integrity was the strongest driver of willingness to recommend a company, and personalisation the main driver of loyalty and repurchase. Automotive scored best on time and effort. Correlational consumer survey data. Use: build German referral mechanics on integrity proof and retention programmes on personalisation.
facts.source_title: KPMG Germany: Die Customer Experience Excellence Studie 2024

facts.statement: KPMG Japan CEE 2024 (page published 23 December 2024; sample not stated): the average Japan CEE score was 6.79, down 0.08, and all six pillars fell, most in personalisation, resolution and integrity. KPMG suggests the fall reflects a gap between what consumers want and what brands deliver; the widest gap between the top 10 and the rest is in meeting expectations. Consumer opinion data, translated from Japanese. Use: in Japan, closing the expectation gap (promises kept) is the first CX priority.
facts.source_title: KPMG Japan: 2024 Customer Experience Excellence (CEE) research

facts.statement: KPMG Japan CEE 2024 (23 December 2024): industry average scores were automotive 7.03 (first), entertainment and leisure 6.96, non-food retail 6.95; logistics fell from 6th to 9th. 42% of Japanese respondents said they would spend more on brands they see as ethical, a share that has risen with each survey. Opinion data, sample not stated. Use: in Japan, show verifiable ethics proof as a premium-pricing lever.
facts.source_title: KPMG Japan: 2024 Customer Experience Excellence (CEE) research

facts.statement: KPMG US CX analysis (5 June 2018; 7,500+ US consumers, 250 brands, 10 sectors; KPMG release via PR Newswire): the top 50 brands had 50% higher revenue growth than the bottom 50, and their EBITDA growth was more than three times higher. The top 10 began Navy Federal, USAA, Disney Parks, H-E-B, Calvin Klein; KPMG called Amazon the benchmark for personalisation and trust. Correlation, not proof of cause. Use: cite as directional support for CX investment cases, with that caveat.
facts.source_title: KPMG: Better customer experience means more revenue for companies (2018 US CEE)

facts.statement: KPMG UK CEE 2024 (27 November 2024; 13,053 UK consumers, 399 brands): the UK score history runs 7.08 in 2017, 7.45 in 2020, 7.09 in 2023 and 7.19 in 2024. Fidelity International rose 201 places to 56th and Netflix 106 to 57th; Klarna and Vinted entered the top 100. KPMG reports brands shifting from cost-cutting technology toward AI used to improve customer experience. Use: use 7.1 to 7.2 as the UK all-sector baseline.
facts.source_title: KPMG UK: AI adoption improves customer satisfaction scores

facts.statement: Accenture Interactive, 'Service is the New Sales' (11 November 2019; 748 B2B buyers and 1,499 sellers, 10 countries, 16 industries, fielded March 2019; sellers $25M+ revenue; opinion survey): Accenture reports 80% of frequent B2B buyers will switch supplier at least once within 24 months. 62% of laggard sellers invest in sales plays without salesperson support versus 48% of service-minded sellers; 69% of laggards cite board-level cultural resistance. Use: pair self-serve digital plays with named human follow-up in B2B funnels.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: 80% of B2B buyers have switched suppliers

facts.statement: Accenture 'Service is the New Sales' (November 2019; 748 buyers, 1,499 sellers; self-reported, correlational): service-focused leaders reported higher profitability (96%) and market share (97%); 51% of leaders use new technology platforms to remove service barriers versus 32% of laggards; 48% of leaders have fully integrated marketing across channels versus 19% of laggards; leaders are over 4 times likelier to have full senior buy-in. Accenture's message: digital and human selling are 'and', not 'or'. Use: align marketing and sales data and channels before adding more outreach.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: 80% of B2B buyers have switched suppliers

facts.statement: Accenture, 'Growth at stake as B2B companies lose control over customer experience' (28 September 2017; 1,350 B2B sales, service and marketing executives, 10 countries, 16 industries, mostly $1B+ firms, fielded May 2017; opinion survey): Accenture cites that 57% of the buying process is complete before a buyer contacts a rep, 61% of B2B transactions begin online and 90% of buyers never respond to cold outreach. 71% of executives say buyers want B2C-like experiences; 49% admit they fall short. Use: invest in content and self-serve evaluation, not volume outreach.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Growth at stake as B2B companies lose control over customer experience

facts.statement: Accenture B2B study (28 September 2017; 1,350 executives, 10 countries, 16 industries; opinion survey): 97% call indirect sales channels critical, yet 84% lack visibility into partners' opportunity pipelines and only 21% have total control over sales networks and customer experience. Firms with integrated partner lead generation and coaching were 63% likelier to exceed indirect revenue goals. Accenture advises moving from partner management to ecosystem orchestration with shared data and coaching. Use: give partners shared pipeline data, lead routing and coaching, not just price lists.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Growth at stake as B2B companies lose control over customer experience

facts.statement: Accenture Strategy B2B customer experience study (1 December 2015; 1,350+ B2B sales, service and customer executives, 10 countries, 16 industries, fielded February to March 2015; opinion survey): only 23% of firms ran truly effective CX programmes. These Leaders averaged 13% annual revenue growth, Strivers (57%) 6%, Laggards -1%. 66% believed new entrants offer better CX, and 32% felt well equipped (40% in 2014). Use: use as the historic base rate that CX leadership is rare in B2B, with self-reported growth figures.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Majority of B2B companies missing out on revenue growth due to poor CX

facts.statement: Accenture 2015 B2B CX study (1,350+ executives, fielded February to March 2015; self-reported): Leaders differed from Strivers in naming after-sales service the most important lifecycle point (61% vs 34%), putting 67% of CX budget into digital (41%), managing external partners vigorously (51% vs 29%), and believing digital investment brings competitive advantage (44% vs 23%). Leaders also kept funding traditional channels (39% vs 22% raising spend). Use: weight B2B retention work (after-sales service) alongside acquisition spend, and keep human channels funded.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Majority of B2B companies missing out on revenue growth due to poor CX

facts.statement: Accenture innovative CMOs study (27 March 2019; 935 CMOs and 564 CEOs, 12 countries, 17 industry groups, firms $500M+, fielded March to May 2018; opinion survey): the top 17% 'innovative' CMOs, who partner across the C-suite, lead on innovation and use emerging tech to predict behaviour, were associated with about 11% higher shareholder returns than peers. 90% of CEOs and CMOs expected marketing to change fundamentally within three years. Correlational. Use: position the marketing lead as a growth and innovation partner to sales and product.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Innovative CMOs are creating superior business value

facts.statement: Accenture CMO and CEO study (27 March 2019; 935 CMOs, 564 CEOs, 12 countries; opinion survey): 76% of CMOs said consumers expect more of a brand's purpose, and 70% of CEOs said companies with a bigger purpose achieve higher commercial success. Nearly a third (31%) of CEOs expected CMOs to drive growth using customer data and insight. Leading CMOs listed immersive experience designers, storytellers, growth hackers and futurologists among the roles their teams will need. Use: tie any purpose claim to a measurable proof point, not a slogan.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Innovative CMOs are creating superior business value

facts.statement: Accenture Song 'Marketing, the Maestro way' (25 September 2023; 1,150 cross-functional executives; self-reported, correlational): 66% of organisations say marketers are still scrambling for full control of the brand conversation, and Maestro companies are 33% more likely to say they have more control over their brand than ever. Use: pitch marketing as a cross-functional capability with shared metrics.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Marketing, the Maestro way

facts.statement: Accenture Song Maestro survey (1,150 executives, September 2023; self-reported): Maestro firms were 31% likelier to champion customer insights, 22% likelier to strongly agree they collect data from more channels than two years earlier, 19% likelier to report close marketing and HR collaboration, and 34% likelier to rate programming skills crucial for future marketing. Use: when scoping a marketing team, prioritise insight ownership, multichannel data collection and digital skills ahead of headcount for execution.
facts.source_title: Accenture Song: Marketing, the Maestro way

facts.statement: Accenture Interactive Personalization Pulse Check (3 May 2018; 8,000 consumers in 8 countries, fielded November 2017): 91% said they are likelier to shop with brands that recognise them, remember them and offer relevant recommendations. 48% had left a site and bought elsewhere because of poorly curated experience (40% a year earlier). 73% had never found a brand too personalised; of the 27% who had, 64% were uncomfortable because they had not knowingly given the data. Use: personalise from data customers knowingly provided.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: Widening gap between consumer expectations and reality in personalization

facts.statement: Accenture Personalization Pulse Check (3 May 2018; 8,000 consumers, 8 countries, fielded November 2017): location-triggered tactics were the most unwelcome. 41% found a text received while walking by a store creepy, 40% a mobile notification after passing a store, 35% social ads for items browsed on a brand site. 45% appreciated an apology email after a poor experience; 75% would value a living 'style profile' brands could use. Consumer opinion data. Use: ask permission for location triggers, and send apology messages after service failures.
facts.source_title: Accenture Interactive: Widening gap between consumer expectations and reality in personalization

facts.statement: Accenture Strategy, 'Seeing Beyond the Loyalty Illusion' (14 February 2017; Global Consumer Pulse, 25,426 consumers in 33 countries, fielded July and August 2016; US figures from 2,532 US respondents): 78% of US consumers were withdrawing loyalty earlier than before, 54% had switched a provider in the past year over poor service, 66% spend more with brands they love and 55% show loyalty by recommending. Accenture argued points schemes were wasting billions. Use: do not rely on points alone; fund service recovery and recommendation mechanics.
facts.source_title: Accenture Strategy: Organizations wasting billions on loyalty programs

facts.statement: Accenture's 'five languages of loyalty' (Seeing Beyond the Loyalty Illusion, 14 February 2017; 25,426 consumers, 33 countries): tokens of affection (personalised offers; 59% loyal), get to know me (privacy 85% and respect for time 81% as drivers), thrill seeker (co-creation 44%), if you like it I like it (brands friends use 42%), and hook me up (rewards exchangeable across providers 39%). Percentages are US shares citing each driver. Use: segment loyalty offers by motivation instead of one points scheme.
facts.source_title: Accenture Strategy: Organizations wasting billions on loyalty programs

facts.statement: Accenture frustrated-consumer study (18 December 2019; 20,736 consumers in 19 countries, online by Coleman Parkes, fielded January and February 2019): 42% were frustrated, and frustrated consumers were about three times likelier than satisfied ones to avoid a retailer or brand again. 47% of all would pay more for experiences that beat expectations (China 81%, US 31%, UK 28%); frustrated consumers 62% versus satisfied 36%. Use: treat recovery of frustrated customers as a revenue lever, and test willingness to pay by market.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Frustrated consumers three times more likely to avoid buying again

facts.statement: Accenture Pulse of Change, edition of 19 October 2026 (3,000 C-suite leaders and 3,000 non-C-suite employees, firms above $300M revenue, 19 industries, 21 countries, fielded July and August 2026; opinion survey): 75% of leaders plan to raise AI investment, 76% see AI as better for revenue growth than cost reduction, and 32% see signs of an AI bubble (51% in July) though 49% would keep investing. 71% expect domestic revenue growth versus 90% in January. Use: frame AI marketing and sales proposals around growth, with a bubble-proof payback case.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Pulse of Change (October 2026 edition)

facts.statement: Accenture Pulse of Change, October 2026 edition (3,000 leaders and 3,000 employees, fieldwork July and August 2026; opinion survey): 41% of leaders and 43% of employees use AI daily, but only 15% of leaders have redesigned end-to-end processes, 20% deploy agents across functions and 25% report widespread, sustained value. 53% expect measurable ROI within 12 months and 87% within 24. 69% watch AI operating costs ('tokenomics') more than a year ago. Use: budget AI marketing tools with run-cost tracking and a 12 to 24 month ROI test.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Pulse of Change (October 2026 edition)

facts.statement: Accenture Pulse of Change Index (12 January 2024; 3,400+ C-suite executives, 20 countries, 19 industries, fielded October and November 2023; opinion survey): 88% expected faster change in 2024, 76% saw generative AI as more opportunity than threat, 52% felt not fully prepared, and 72% were approaching investments more cautiously because of responsible-AI concerns. Technology rose from sixth to first among causes of disruption. Use: pair AI roadmaps with responsible-AI controls and readiness gaps, not tool lists.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Businesses anticipate unprecedented rate of change in 2024

facts.statement: Accenture (10 October 2024; 2,000 executives, 12 countries, 15 industries; opinion survey): 74% said gen AI and automation investments met or exceeded expectations; firms with fully modernised AI-led processes rose from 9% (2023) to 16% (2024); reinvention-ready firms reported 2.5 times revenue growth. Gen AI use cases already built: IT 75%, marketing 64%, customer service 59%, finance 58%. 61% said data is not ready and 64% struggle to change how they operate. Use: audit data readiness before launching marketing AI use cases.
facts.source_title: Accenture: Companies with AI-led processes outperform peers

facts.statement: Amazon Ads announced on 10 Mar 2026 that Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands prompts leave open beta (running since Nov 2025) and reach general availability in the US on 25 Mar 2026. From then they are billed inside your existing CPC bidding. Campaigns are enrolled automatically with no setup (authors and publishers excluded); a click may open a Rufus dialog or answer in place; single prompts can be paused in the Ads Console, and a Prompts report shows text, clicks, spend, ACOS and ROAS. Check spend on prompts after 25 Mar.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: Sponsored Products prompts and Sponsored Brands prompts

facts.statement: Amazon Ads (post of 11 Jun 2026): Rufus and Alexa+ were merged into one experience called Alexa for Shopping, and existing sponsored ads campaigns are automatically eligible to serve in its conversations and to be optimized as prompts, with no extra setup. Amazon cites Rufus use by over 300 million customers in 2025, and its own figures of nearly 20% of shoppers who engage with a prompt continuing the chat about that brand and a 6% conversion rise when prompts are added to a Sponsored Brands ad (vendor claims). Treat product detail content as ad input.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: What agentic shopping means for advertising

facts.statement: Amazon Ads page dated 29 Sep 2026: Branded Conversations launch in January 2027 for US endemic advertisers running Sponsored Brands (not author ads), starting with collections campaigns, which enroll automatically. A tap on a prompt opens a multi-turn, brand-informed chat inside Alexa for Shopping using your catalog and brand content. Only the conversation-starter prompt is billed per click; follow-up turns are free. Prepare accurate catalog and brand content before launch.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: Branded Conversations

facts.statement: Amazon's A+ Content page (undated): A+ needs a Professional selling account plus a Brand Representative or Reseller role on a Brand Registry brand (or generic catalog products); it is free and only applies to brand-owned ASINs; content goes through review. Basic A+ has images, text and comparison charts; Premium adds video, hotspots, carousels and Q&A. AI generation exists only for modules marked 'AI Ready'. Amazon claims up to 8% (Basic) and up to 20% (Premium) sales lifts from internal data with no date; treat as unproven.
facts.source_title: Amazon Seller: A+ Content

facts.statement: Walmart Connect post of 8 Apr 2026: advertisers can run Meta social campaigns self-serve from Walmart Connect's Ad Center with closed-loop measurement of online and in-store Walmart sales, using LiveRamp's clean room. TikTok self-serve was planned for the same half-year; closed-loop measurement already covers TikTok and Pinterest. An Add-to-Cart feature (up to 10 products from a social ad) is in beta for managed-serve clients only. Use it to tie social spend to Walmart sales.
facts.source_title: Walmart Connect: How we're expanding retail-powered social media

facts.statement: Instacart (6 Nov 2025): the Media Rating Council expanded Instacart's accreditation to ad placements on Carrot Ads, its white-label retail media tech. Covered metrics are impressions, clicks, click-through rate and viewable impressions, for Sponsored Product, Display, Shoppable Display and Shoppable Video ads on Instacart Marketplace and Carrot Ads partner sites and apps, more than 240 ecommerce partners at the time. Accreditation covers those four metrics, not sales attribution, so ask for the outcome methodology separately.
facts.source_title: Instacart Receives Expanded MRC Accreditation for Carrot Ads

facts.statement: IAB and IAB Europe finalised their In-Store Retail Media: Definitions and Measurement Standards on 3 Dec 2024, after two months of open feedback. They set shared definitions, measurement standards and guidelines for ad formats and store zones, and build on the IAB/MRC Retail Media Measurement Guidelines. The IAB page asks you to claim a free account to keep reading. Use its definitions when briefing a retailer's in-store screens so impressions and zones are counted the same way across retailers.
facts.source_title: IAB and IAB Europe: In-Store Retail Media Definitions and Measurement Standards

facts.statement: YouTube blog, 25 Mar 2026: the YouTube Shopping affiliate program opens to all YouTube Partner Program creators with at least 500 subscribers who meet the eligibility guidelines. They can tag products from partner brands in Shorts, long videos and Live, and viewers can shop on mobile or on TV. The post does not name countries; the Help page lists the supported ones. Brands can now brief far smaller creators for affiliate shopping tags.
facts.source_title: Earn earlier: expanding YouTube Shopping to creators with 500+ subscribers

facts.statement: YouTube Help on the Shopping affiliate program (undated): the channel must be in the Partner Program, in a supported country (the list includes the US, UK, Germany, Japan, India, Brazil and Mexico among others), not a music channel and not Made for Kids. Each participating brand or retailer sets commission rates and the attribution window per product. Commissions are paid through AdSense within 60 to 120 days after purchase, and a return reverses the commission. Automated redirects, click injection or cookie stuffing violate the terms. Plan cash flow around a 2 to 4 month payout lag.
facts.source_title: YouTube Shopping affiliate program overview & eligibility - YouTube Help

facts.statement: FTC Q&A on the Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465, effective 21 Oct 2024): it bans fake or bought reviews, incentives that require a particular sentiment, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled sites posing as independent, review suppression through threats or false accusations, and buying fake social indicators. Courts can impose civil penalties for knowing violations. A business that only hosts consumer reviews is exempt unless it wrote or bought them. Apply this to marketplace listings: no review gating or sentiment-conditioned incentives.
facts.source_title: FTC: The Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers

facts.statement: TikTok Shop US seller page: the referral fee rose to 6% of each qualified order from 1 Apr 2024 (some categories shown as 5% to 6%). On refunds, TikTok keeps a refund administration fee equal to 20% of the referral fee, capped at $5 per SKU type per refund since 15 May 2025; none applies to creator sample refunds or buyer cancellations before shipping that meet auto-cancel criteria. Add 6% plus refund-fee drag to unit economics, and recheck the Seller Center fee page, since the terms let TikTok change fees.
facts.source_title: TikTok Shop Referral Fee Updates (US)

facts.statement: TikTok Shop US AI-generated content rules (page dated '09/02/2026', format ambiguous): fully or significantly AI-made content, especially synthetic faces, voices or digital humans, must be disclosed by on-screen text, watermark, description note or the AI-generated toggle; official TikTok AI effects are auto-labelled. Banned uses: AI that changes the product's size, colour or features, shows effects it cannot deliver, uses someone's likeness without consent, or fakes doctor and expert personas. False disclosure is also a violation. Penalties range from removed product links to bans.
facts.source_title: TikTok Shop: AI-Generated Content Restrictions and Requirements

facts.statement: Google's Merchant Center product data spec update (14 Apr 2026): new product-level shipping attributes handling_cutoff_time and minimum_order_value, plus loyalty labels in shipping; an optional video_link attribute whose videos serve and face policy checks from 30 Jun 2026; and a 500x500 pixel minimum for image_link and additional_image_link, with warnings now and enforcement from 31 Jan 2027 (some smaller images are auto-optimised and flagged). Re-export any feed images under 500x500 before 31 Jan 2027.
facts.source_title: Merchant Center product data specification update 2026

facts.statement: Google Merchant Center Help (article dated 27 May 2026) announces 'AI performance insights' showing how products are discovered in AI Mode, AI Overviews in Search and the Gemini app: share of voice against similar brands, shopping funnel performance, popular product terms and attributes, and an attribute completeness score that flags products missing popular attributes. The page says it will roll out to the US, Canada, Australia, India and New Zealand 'in the coming months', so it is announced, not live, and the screenshots use simulated data. Fill missing attributes now so the score starts high.
facts.source_title: AI performance insights in Merchant Center - Google Merchant Center Help

facts.statement: Nielsen's US Gauge for August 2026 (5 weeks to 30 Aug, released 22 Oct 2026): streaming took 49.6% of TV time, cable 18.9% and broadcast 17.5%. YouTube set a platform record at 15.8% of TV and led all media distributors; Netflix was third at 7.7%; Disney streaming reached 4.8% (Disney overall 9.3%). Nielsen applies a one-time methodology adjustment from the September 2026 interval, so compare September onward with care. Put YouTube on TV in the CTV plan alongside Netflix and Disney.
facts.source_title: Nielsen: TV Viewing Cools Off in August 2026 Gauge

facts.statement: Amazon Ads (10 Sep 2025): advertisers using Amazon DSP get direct programmatic access to Netflix's ads plan inventory in 11 markets (US, UK, France, Spain, Mexico, Canada, Japan, Brazil, Italy, Germany, Australia), starting Q4 2025. This depends on buying through Amazon DSP.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads announces Netflix integration

facts.statement: Amazon's Prime Video ads page (figures updated Feb 2026, Amazon-internal) claims 315M+ monthly ad-supported viewers worldwide, with measurement windows that differ by market (12 months for the US, Canada and Germany, but only 3 months of 2024 for India and Japan). Kantar compared 15 Prime Video campaigns with 242 Kantar video campaigns (US, 2024): 2.3x ad awareness, 3x purchase intent. Buyers can order managed or self-service; formats include pre-roll, mid-roll and interactive. Do not compare reach claims across markets without noting the window.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: Prime Video ads

facts.statement: Google (22 Jan 2026): Demand Gen powers shoppable CTV, letting viewers browse and buy during YouTube ads on TV screens. Google says Demand Gen campaigns that include TV screens average 7% more conversions at the same ROI (Google internal experiment, global, 2025). Test it by adding TV screens to device targeting and running a holdout; the 7% is Google's own figure, not independent.
facts.source_title: Demand Gen Drop: January 2026

facts.statement: Google Ads Help on QR codes for CTV (undated; footer shows only 2026): QR codes are generated automatically on Demand Gen and Performance Max campaigns targeting CTV (skippable in-stream and Shorts), and via a 'show final URL as QR code on TV Screens' checkbox on YouTube Select video campaigns. They are not available on YouTube TV or Google TV inventory, and QR position and timing are fixed. Google advises avoiding embedding QR codes in the video file (a recommendation). Non-skippable ads are not supported in Demand Gen or Performance Max.
facts.source_title: About QR codes for Connected TV - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Walmart announced on 23 Jun 2026 that it will acquire Vibe.co, a self-serve CTV platform with direct supply integrations and 10,000+ advertisers (per Vibe), to join Walmart Connect and make CTV easier for small and mid-sized advertisers. Terms are undisclosed; closing needs Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance and is expected by the end of fiscal 2027. Walmart says Connect stays open to other publishers, SSPs and measurement providers. Until it closes, treat Vibe as an independent vendor.
facts.source_title: Walmart to Acquire Vibe.co to Expand Access to Connected TV Advertising

facts.statement: Walmart Connect (11 Jun 2026): Walmart's first-party audiences can be activated in Google Display & Video 360 for YouTube reach and awareness video campaigns, with measurement of how YouTube exposure contributes to Walmart omnichannel sales; more inventory types are to follow. The article says it is 'currently in a closed proof of concept phase and will become more widely available later', and advertisers must contact their Walmart Connect representative. Do not budget on it as a general availability product yet.
facts.source_title: Bringing Walmart Connect's first-party audiences and measurement to Google's Display & Video 360

facts.statement: IAB Tech Lab's ads.txt page (updated 14 Sep 2026) lists Ads.txt 1.1 (Aug 2022) as the current spec; it adds OWNERDOMAIN and MANAGERDOMAIN so buyers can link a publisher's ads.txt to sellers.json. App-ads.txt 1.0 extends ads.txt to apps distributed through mobile or connected TV app stores. For buyers: bid only on sellers listed as authorised in ads.txt or app-ads.txt, and check that the SSP publishes sellers.json. For your own sites, publish ads.txt with the owner domain.
facts.source_title: ads.txt - Authorized Digital Sellers - IAB Tech Lab

facts.statement: IAB Tech Lab CTV Programmatic Guide (the page shows no date, only a 2026 copyright; the guide is treated as undated, and the 7 Oct 2026 date below belongs to the separate sellers.json page): in CTV, ads.txt and app-ads.txt declare authorised sellers (the INVENTORYPARTNERDOMAIN value lets another domain be named an authorised seller); sellers.json plus the SupplyChain object let a buyer see the parties selling or reselling a bid request. The sellers.json page (last updated 7 Oct 2026) says SSPs and exchanges are expected to post their sellers.json files. For spoofed devices the guide describes manufacturer device attestation. Ask your DSP to report spend by final seller.
facts.source_title: CTV Programmatic Guide - IAB Tech Lab

facts.statement: ANA Programmatic Transparency Benchmark, Q1 2026 (released 27 May 2026; 86 participating marketers, 66 active; covers web, mobile and CTV, no CTV split): better advertisers turned 54.0% of programmatic spend into qualified impressions versus 32.1% for weaker ones, the widest gap yet; media quality losses were 19.0% versus 38.4%. Made-for-advertising exposure rose to 1.1% from 0.4% to 0.6% through 2025, with 'AI slop' flagged as a new subtype. Keep MFA and low-quality exclusion lists on and audit them quarterly.
facts.source_title: ANA Programmatic Transparency Benchmark Reveals Widening Gap Between Top and Bottom Advertisers

facts.statement: The Trade Desk press release of 6 Jan 2026 introduces OpenAds, a new auction environment for publishers and sellers that it calls direct, transparent and high-integrity, with first publishers AccuWeather, The Arena Group, BuzzFeed, the Guardian, Hearst Magazines, Hearst TV, Newsweek, People Inc. and Ziff Davis. The company said development and rollout would continue through 2026. It is a TTD-run path, so ask for reporting by path to see if it beats your current SSP routes.
facts.source_title: The Trade Desk Announces First Wave of OpenAds Publishing Partners

facts.statement: IAB's Attention Measurement Guidelines page (dated 11 Nov 2025) presents the final IAB/MRC guidelines, which the FAQ says define terminology, methodologies and disclosure requirements and include validation and auditing requirements for accreditation. The page treats attention as a complementary layer that adds context beyond delivery metrics such as viewability. Ask any vendor selling an attention metric whether it follows these guidelines and whether it is MRC-accredited before paying for it.
facts.source_title: IAB/MRC Attention Measurement Guidelines

facts.statement: Google Ads Help on AI Max experiments (undated): enable AI Max by Recommendations or via the Experiments page, which splits one campaign's traffic and budget between a control with AI Max off and a trial with it on. A campaign cannot be tested this way if it already has text customization on, targets the Display network, uses Portfolio Bidding, Shared Budgets or bidding exploration, or runs another experiment. Check these blockers first, otherwise the test cannot be created.
facts.source_title: About AI Max experiments - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Google Ads Help on ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode: existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns can serve there automatically, with no separate budget. Text and Shopping ads can appear; AI Max, broad match and PMax can match contextual AI responses, while exact and phrase match only match clearly commercial queries. You cannot target or opt out of AI Overviews or AI Mode separately; use negatives and brand exclusions. Stats arrive only in aggregate in standard reports. In-answer ads run in English in the US and about a dozen countries.
facts.source_title: About ads in AI-powered experiences in Google Search - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Google blog (30 Sep 2025): Performance Max asset reports can be segmented by devices, time, conversions and networks. Channel performance reporting adds a Cost toggle, ROI columns, account-level bulk download of channel reports, segmentation by conversion action and ad event type, and diagnostics such as limited serving from restrictive bid targets. Google said it was still rolling out channel performance reporting. Use channel reports to judge where PMax spends.
facts.source_title: Get more visibility in Performance Max with new asset and channel reporting improvements

facts.statement: Google Ads blog (30 Jul 2024): asset generation for images was rolling out in App and Display campaigns, extending beyond Performance Max; the image model is tuned on advertising performance data. Image editing (remove or add objects, extend backgrounds, change aspect ratio) launched globally in English only, with more languages promised later that year. The 'Asset' option in the Create menu also offers video creation. Generated images should still be reviewed for claims accuracy and AI-disclosure rules before they run.
facts.source_title: New reporting and genAI tools to boost creative results

facts.statement: Microsoft Advertising (21 Apr 2026): AI Max for Search opened as an open pilot in May with expanded query matching, asset personalization and URL routing, able to serve on Copilot Search, Copilot Answers and Bing; term, brand and messaging guardrails were 'soon'. Offer Highlights (such as free shipping, set in Merchant Center) run in Copilot for English-speaking retail markets; audience generation from a prompt is a closed pilot in the US and Canada. UCP-ready feeds are generally available in the US. Apply to the pilots through your account team.
facts.source_title: Win across all three eras of the web

facts.statement: Microsoft Advertising August 2026 product roundup (31 Aug 2026): AI Max for Search is generally available as an optional toggle. Performance Max gains uplift experiments that measure incremental conversions alongside Search, Shopping or Audience ads, search terms in the standard search term report, and age and gender include/exclude targeting (general availability 8 Sep). The Microsoft Advertising MCP server gives read-only access (open flight) for reports, audits and keyword research from Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude. Run an uplift experiment before scaling PMax.
facts.source_title: AI Max for Search and other product news for August 2026

facts.statement: HubSpot Credits page (undated, 2026 copyright): credits cost $0.010 each, sold in 1,000-credit packs for $10 or pay-as-you-go, and unused credits expire monthly. Per-action cost: customer agent 50 credits per resolution (messaging) or per voice minute, prospecting agent 100 credits per lead, knowledge base agent 200 credits per article, content agent 1,000 credits per piece (about $10). Included allotments vary by product and tier. Budget AI agents per outcome, and cap pay-as-you-go use.
facts.source_title: HubSpot Credits

facts.statement: Salesforce Agentforce pricing page (undated): Flex Credits cost $500 per 100,000; an Agentforce action uses 20 credits (about $0.10) and a voice action 30. Alternatives are $2 per conversation, an Agentforce User License at $5 per user per month (requires Flex Credits) and a Coworker licence at $50 per user per month. Max Edition includes 2.75M credits per org per year. The page says pricing is for information and may change. Compare cost per resolved task, not list price.
facts.source_title: Salesforce Agentforce Pricing

facts.statement: Canva Help Center (Magic Studio, undated, 2026 copyright): AI-created works may be used for personal and commercial purposes if the AI Product Terms are followed; between you and Canva, you own your AI content, though many jurisdictions including the US do not protect AI-created works, so exclusivity is uncertain. Do not prompt for known brands, characters or people, and get permission for recognisable people. Canva calls disclosing AI assistance best practice; the page does not mention indemnity. Check the AI Product Terms before client work.
facts.source_title: How to use Magic Studio safely and legally - Canva Help Center

facts.statement: Mailchimp Help on Write with AI (undated; copyright to 2026): the beta, powered by Intuit AI, helps you create or edit email content, including a quality check for spelling and grammar. It is included with the Standard plan or higher and needs a primary mailing address in Australia, Canada, the UK or the US. Content related to alcohol, tobacco, weapons, cannabis, vaping, health or financial advice is restricted, and you must review the generated suggestions and the Content Generator Beta additional terms before sending. The page reviewed states no usage quotas and does not say whether inputs train models.
facts.source_title: Use Write with AI to Create Content - Mailchimp

facts.statement: Klaviyo press release (24 Mar 2026): Composer, an agent that generates, optimises and recommends complete campaigns and flows from one prompt, and finds where flows lose customers, is in private beta ('nothing goes live without human approval'). Customer Agent gained retail skills (order tracking, returns and exchanges, subscription editing, loyalty lookup) and 'Agent Guidance' for voice, tone and escalation rules. The release gives no pricing. Join the waitlist, and keep human approval as the default on any AI-launched send.
facts.source_title: Klaviyo Expands AI Agents to Power the Autonomous B2C CRM
