facts.statement: Amazon Ads (22 Jun 2026): Responsive eCommerce Creative is open to all Amazon DSP advertisers. It can animate static product images, add seasonal elements, generate product-in-use videos and lifestyle images, reuse assets from past campaigns, Brand Stores or product pages, and create clickable product questions that, from July, run beyond Amazon and open a chat with Alexa for Shopping. In-Banner Video is US-only on third-party sites. Amazon cites up to +37% CTR and +26% conversion (its US 2026 study; vendor claim). Run it against a static baseline.
facts.source_title: How Amazon Ads creative tools help advertisers produce ads

facts.statement: Dawes (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report for the LinkedIn B2B Institute, May 2021): the '95-5 rule' is a rule of thumb from purchase frequency, not a precise law. If firms in a category switch provider about every five years, about 20% of buyers are in market over a year and about 5% in a quarter; at a two-year cycle it is about 50% a year and roughly 13% a quarter. Compute your own share from the category's interpurchase time. Use: set the in-market share from the purchase cycle before splitting budget between brand and activation.
facts.source_title: Advertising effectiveness and the 95-5 rule: most B2B buyers are not in the market right now (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Same Dawes report (Ehrenberg-Bass, May 2021; sample not stated on the page): many well-established B2B brands are linked to a given category entry point by only 20-30% of category buyers, and market leaders often reach about 50%; double-digit gains are described as a multi-year task. Advice: advertise to out-of-market buyers, spread spend across the year instead of one quarter, and track brand links to entry points as the mental availability measure. Use: set entry-point link-rate targets in years, not campaigns.
facts.source_title: Advertising effectiveness and the 95-5 rule (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report, July 2022): category entry points (CEPs) are the internal and external cues buyers use to retrieve brands from memory in a buying situation. Generate them with the 'W' prompts (when, where, while, with what, why, how feeling, with or for whom), then prioritise with three tests, the '3 Cs': credibility (can the brand deliver), competitiveness (how crowded is the mental space) and commonality (how often it occurs and its value). A long-short list of 5 to 8 is suggested. Use: run CEP elicitation before writing a messaging platform.
facts.source_title: Category Entry Points in a Business-to-Business (B2B) World (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass, July 2022), US business insurance survey (n=606) and 17 insurance products: brands with more linked category entry points had a lower likelihood of customers switching. The average slope was about -0.2, which the report reads as roughly 5% lower defection probability per extra linked entry point, significant in 16 of 17 products. In UK business banking (n=609) Barclays held 9.8% mental market share and 78% mental penetration. Use: treat entry-point breadth as a retention lever as well as an acquisition one.
facts.source_title: Category Entry Points in a Business-to-Business (B2B) World (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk, Dawes and Faghidno (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report for the LinkedIn B2B Institute, May 2021): the Double Jeopardy law says smaller brands suffer twice, with fewer buyers who are also slightly less loyal, so brand size (penetration) drives loyalty rather than the reverse. First reported in the 1960s (McPhee, 1963); the report shows it across B2B datasets including UK business banking and US business insurance, and concludes that sustainable growth comes mainly from acquiring customers. Use: do not plan growth on loyalty gains alone.
facts.source_title: The Double Jeopardy Law in B2B shows the way to grow (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute article on its LinkedIn B2B Institute study (Romaniuk, Dawes, Faghidno; 2021, sample sizes not stated on the page): in UK business banking, Barclays had 42% penetration of potential buyers, 27% of them solely loyal and 31% naming it their favourite; smaller Metro had 11% penetration, 3% solely loyal and 15% favourite. The article also says most B2B marketers believe growth comes from loyalty. Use: quote this as an illustration that big brands also have more loyal buyers.
facts.source_title: Customer acquisition is the only viable growth strategy in B2B (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report, May 2021) on the Duplication of Purchase law: brands share more customers with larger competitors, in proportion to the competitor's size. For 16 US business insurance products the sharing pattern correlated 93% with penetration; the same pattern appears in aviation fuel contracts and UK business banking switching. Sample sizes are not stated. The report concludes a brand's main competitors are the category's biggest brands regardless of positioning. Use: benchmark against category leaders, not look-alike niche rivals.
facts.source_title: How do B2B brands compete? (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report, May 2021): among 609 UK business banking and 616 US business insurance buyers (22 banks, 17 insurers), brand rejection averaged about 10% (banking 11%, insurance 7%), against a B2C median of 9% over 535 brands in 24 categories. In a subset of 12 B2B brands, even the best-known had more unaware potential customers than rejectors (the per-brand table is an image). The report concludes lack of brand awareness is a bigger barrier to acquisition than non-customer brand rejection, a finding from that 12-brand subset, not a general law. Use: prioritise reach and entry points over rebuttal messaging.
facts.source_title: Brand Rejection in B2B: Incidence, Reasons and Implications (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Romaniuk and Stocchi (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, Aug 2025): among 2,835 professional generative-AI users in 13 countries benchmarking 20 AI providers, average brand rejection was 6% and 90% of rejection levels were under 10%; the highest was 15%. Unfamiliarity was the most common stated reason (22%), while cost and bad press were each 3% or less. Unaware or no-opinion users outnumbered rejectors for every brand (ratio 1.3 to 3.9). Use: for AI products, build mental availability before rebutting objections.
facts.source_title: Buyer says no? The rejection of Generative AI brands in B2B (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Gelzinis, Kennedy, Beal, Hartnett and Sharp (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute; report to sponsors 2018, journal version online 21 Jun 2021): 70 brands in one Australian consumer goods category tracked over 20+ years, with 57 cases of all mass media stopped for a year or more. Sales index fell to 84 after one year (-16%), -25% after two and -36% after three. Smaller brands declined faster than medium and big brands; big brands (>1M units) appeared somewhat stable for 1-2 years. Of the growing and stable brands that resumed advertising, 5 of 10 kept their trend (2 of 5 growing, 3 of 5 stable); this is not all resuming brands. Use: model the cost of a media pause by brand size.
facts.source_title: What happens when brands stop advertising? (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: IPA blog by Hoad (13 Sep 2023) on Binet and Field's work: the 2013 report 'The Long and The Short of It' found an optimum brand-building to activation budget ratio of about 60:40, and the 2018 report 'Effectiveness in Context' found 62:38. The blog says the sweet spot stayed nearly constant across the reports. Use: use 60:40 as a starting prior and flex it, not as a fixed target.
facts.source_title: The next chapter for 'The Long and The Short of It' (IPA)

facts.statement: IPA blog (13 Sep 2023): 'Effectiveness in Context' found the share of short-term campaigns in the IPA Effectiveness Databank was rising, and effectiveness, measured as the number of very large business effects reported in IPA cases, fell as that share grew. The data predate COVID and the cost-of-living squeeze. The original 2013 report has been cited in more than 70 academic papers and textbooks. Use: when a plan is mostly activation, expect fewer very large effects; sanity-check with a long-term brand measure.
facts.source_title: The next chapter for 'The Long and The Short of It' (IPA)

facts.statement: Binet and Field, 5 Principles of Growth in B2B Marketing (LinkedIn B2B Institute; analysis of B2B cases in the IPA Databank 1998-2018, case count not stated; page undated, 2025 footer): (1) share of voice above share of market predicts growth; (2) balance brand and activation, recommended around 50/50 for B2B; (3) acquisition beats loyalty and broad reach grows most; (4) maximise mental availability, with fame ranking highest as an objective; (5) emotional messages work better long-term, rational ones short-term. Use: use 50/50 as the B2B starting split.
facts.source_title: The 5 Principles Of Growth In B2B Marketing (LinkedIn B2B Institute)

facts.statement: Nielsen (Marci, Oct 2017; vendor-reported), on a joint Nielsen Catalina Solutions and Nielsen study of TV and digital campaigns (number of campaigns and years not stated on the page): creative quality contributes as much to a brand's in-market success as all other factors combined; when creative is strong it drives up to 80% of in-market success on traditional TV and up to 89% on digital, and when creative is weak sales lift is weak and other media factors drive the result. Use: test creative quality before optimising targeting.
facts.source_title: Perspectives: Want a Successful Ad? Get Creative (Nielsen)

facts.statement: System1 (Test Your Ad page, 18 Jun 2025; vendor-reported): across 264 brands and 4,000+ ads, media investment alone (ESOV) predicts 27% of brand growth, and adding the System1 Star Rating raises that to 48%. The page says its database holds over 100,000 ads. No independent replication was found. Use: treat as a vendor claim; pair creative scoring with spend share, and hold out for validation.
facts.source_title: Test Your Ad: smarter ad analysis for campaigns that deliver (System1)

facts.statement: Kantar (BrandZ article, 7 Aug 2025; vendor-reported; Kantar BrandZ brand equity data combined with Kantar Worldpanel shopper behaviour, sample size not stated): brands that are 'Meaningfully Different' command five times the penetration of brands that are not. Just over half of the brands ranked in the 2006 BrandZ Global Top 100 remain on the list, and those that stayed had double the odds of strong emotive clarity. Use: add a meaningful-difference read to brand tracking, and note it is a Kantar model.
facts.source_title: A different route to growth (Kantar)

facts.statement: Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, reported at Mumbrella360 2024; Mumbrella article dated 24 May 2024, the Ehrenberg-Bass copy shows no date): the fame of a distinctive brand asset is the proportion of category buyers who think of the brand when they experience the asset. It should be measured unprompted, because prompting gives inflated fame scores, by up to about 20 percentage points. An asset meant to stand in for the brand name should score as close to 100% fame as possible. Use: measure logo, colour, sound and shape assets unprompted before dropping the brand name from creative.
facts.source_title: Mumbrella360: Ehrenberg-Bass Professor says 'you're poorly branding' (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: FTC business blog (24 Mar 2026): the Negative Option Rule, adopted in 1973, currently covers only prenotification plans such as product-of-the-month clubs. The FTC opened an advance notice of rulemaking asking whether to modernise it (enrolment and cancellation practices, costs and benefits); comments were due 13 Apr 2026 and are closed. Unfair or deceptive subscription practices are still pursued case by case under ROSCA, Section 5 of the FTC Act and the Telemarketing Sales Rule. Use: no federal click-to-cancel rule is in force; still design cancellation to match ROSCA.
facts.source_title: Do you have thoughts on negative option-related regulations? Share them with the FTC (FTC)

facts.statement: FTC Negative Option Rule page, checked 4 Nov 2026: the 2024 'click to cancel' final rule was announced 16 Oct 2024 and published 15 Nov 2024 as 16 CFR Part 425. A Federal Register notice of 12 Feb 2026 revised the Negative Option Rule and withdrew the CARS Rule, and the FTC announced an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on 11 Mar 2026, published 13 Mar 2026. As of this check no proposed or final replacement rule is listed (the latest rulemaking step is the ANPRM). Use: monitor this page; do not plan against the 2024 text; review in 60 days.
facts.source_title: Negative Option Rule (FTC legal library)

facts.statement: California Attorney General consumer alert (4 Sep 2025) on the amended Automatic Renewal Law, effective 1 Jul 2025: businesses need the consumer's express affirmative consent before charging auto-renewal or continuous-service terms. If a consumer enrolled online they must be able to cancel online at any time, with no obstructing or delaying steps, and the business must explain how to cancel and offer a toll-free number, email address or other easy method. Enforced by the AG and district and city attorneys. Use: audit every California-reachable trial for consent and online cancel.
facts.source_title: Attorney General Bonta Issues Consumer Alert on California's Automatic Renewal Law (CA AG)

facts.statement: California Attorney General alert (4 Sep 2025) on the amended Automatic Renewal Law (in effect 1 Jul 2025), notice timing: for plans with an initial term of a year or more, send a renewal notice 15 to 45 days before renewal; for free or discounted trials longer than 31 days, notice 3 to 21 days before the trial ends; for accepted fee changes, 7 to 30 days before the change; plus a yearly reminder through the enrolment channel naming the product, charge frequency and amount, and how to cancel. Use: build these into trial-end and renewal email schedules.
facts.source_title: Attorney General Bonta Issues Consumer Alert on California's Automatic Renewal Law (CA AG)

facts.statement: GOV.UK (published 19 Oct 2026): guidance on the UK consumer subscription contracts regime, which is Part 4 Chapter 2 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 together with the Consumer Subscription Contracts (Cancellation and Information) Regulations 2026, covering business-to-consumer subscription contracts. The detailed duties sit in a 77-page guidance PDF; the page itself does not give a start date. Use: have the UK subscription team read the PDF before any UK trial or auto-renewal launch.
facts.source_title: Subscription contracts (GOV.UK)

facts.statement: CMA blog by Cochrane (14 Oct 2026): the CMA says the new UK subscription contracts regime 'will come into force in January', with the government to publish secondary legislation and further guidance beforehand. The same post reports 20 direct-enforcement investigations in total, 7 cases settled since April 2026, over GBP 11.8 million in fines and over GBP 2.3 million in redress. Use: plan UK trial and renewal flows for a January start and confirm the exact date in the made regulations.
facts.source_title: Direct consumer enforcement: 18 months on (CMA blog)

facts.statement: Apple subscriptions page (App Store, undated, 2026 copyright): offer types are introductory (new subscribers), promotional (existing or lapsed, up to 10 per subscription), offer codes (one-time 18-digit or custom) and win-back offers. Each can be a free trial, pay-as-you-go discount or pay-up-front discount. A customer can redeem one introductory offer per subscription group. Use: put all trial and intro price tiers of one product in a single subscription group so a user gets one introductory offer.
facts.source_title: Auto-renewable subscriptions (Apple Developer)

facts.statement: Apple subscriptions page (App Store, undated, 2026 copyright): on a failed renewal Apple retries billing for 60 days, and developers can configure a billing grace period of 3, 16 or 28 days. The developer revenue share is 70% during the first year of a paid subscription and 85% after one year of paid service; free trials and renewal extensions do not count toward that year. Use: model trial-heavy cohorts at 70% net and use the grace period to cut involuntary churn.
facts.source_title: Auto-renewable subscriptions (Apple Developer)

facts.statement: Apple App Review Guidelines 3.1.2 (page undated): subscriptions must give ongoing value, run for at least seven days and work across the user's devices; users must receive what they paid for without extra tasks such as posting on social media or uploading contacts. Before asking someone to subscribe, the app must clearly describe what they get for the price, and apps that trick users into subscribing or bait and switch are removed. Free trials are set up in App Store Connect. Use: check paywalls against 3.1.2 before submission.
facts.source_title: App Review Guidelines (Apple Developer)

facts.statement: Google Play Console help on subscription offers (undated): a free trial must last between 3 days and 3 years. Offers must be communicated clearly in in-app promotions, stating terms, charges, billing frequency, cancellation steps and whether a subscription is required; benefit text cannot mention free trials or prices. Account hold starts after the grace period and by default runs 60 days minus the grace period, and shortening it can reduce recovered subscriptions. Use: set trial length inside 3 days to 3 years and keep default account hold.
facts.source_title: Create and manage subscriptions (Google Play Console Help)

facts.statement: Google Play Console help on subscription offers (undated): offer eligibility can be set to new customer acquisition, upgrade or developer determined (your own logic, for example second-chance trials or win-back). You can add up to 20 tags to base plans and offers to choose which offer to show when a user qualifies for several. Use: use developer-determined eligibility for win-back trials.
facts.source_title: Create and manage subscriptions (Google Play Console Help)

facts.statement: Stripe Billing docs, Trial Offer API (API version 2026-09-30): one object handles free, discounted-paid and upgrade trials and item-level trials, set as a trial price plus a post-trial price (for example 1 USD for the first week). Requires flexible billing mode; trial offers are not supported in Payment Links, pricing tables or most Checkout integrations; trial length cannot be changed after creation; trial items add nothing to MRR during the trial. Free (0 USD) trials show status trialing. Use: pick paid or discounted trials in Stripe to filter low-intent sign-ups.
facts.source_title: Configure trial offers on subscriptions (Stripe Docs)

facts.statement: RevenueCat, State of Subscription Apps 2026 (page undated, likely Mar 2026; 115,000+ apps, USD 16+ billion revenue, 1+ billion transactions, calendar 2025): median trial-to-paid conversion is 42.5% for 17-32 day trials, 37.4% for 5-9 day trials and 25.5% for trials of 4 days or less (top quartile 59.4%, 52.8%, 38.5%). By category the median is Travel 43.5%, Health and Fitness 37.7%, Gaming 25.0%, Photo and Video 22.2%. Apps are self-selected RevenueCat users. Use: test longer trials for high-consideration products.
facts.source_title: State of Subscription Apps 2026 (RevenueCat)

facts.statement: RevenueCat, State of Subscription Apps 2026 (115,000+ apps, calendar 2025, RevenueCat users only): median download-to-trial start within 30 days is 9.1% for Business apps, 6.9% Health and Fitness, 6.5% Education and Utilities, 4.4% Gaming, 4.1% Travel; by price tier 8.9% high, 5.4% mid, 4.4% low; by region North America 7.1%, Asia-Pacific 5.7%, Western Europe 5.0%. Most trial starts happen on day 0 (89.9% in Business, 82.1% Health and Fitness). Use: design the paywall and onboarding for the first session.
facts.source_title: State of Subscription Apps 2026 (RevenueCat)

facts.statement: RevenueCat, State of Subscription Apps 2026 (115,000+ apps, calendar 2025; vendor-reported, RevenueCat users only): the share of trial cancellations that happen on day 0 is 55.4% for 3-day trials, 39.8% for 7-day, 35.7% for 14-day and 31.1% for 30-day trials. Involuntary billing failures account for nearly a third of cancellations on Google Play versus 14% on the App Store, and AI-powered apps churn about 30% faster than non-AI apps. Use: prioritise payment recovery on Android and ship early value in the first session.
facts.source_title: State of Subscription Apps 2026 (RevenueCat)

facts.statement: FTC Endorsement Guides Q&A (Guides revised 2023; Q&A published 29 Jun 2023 per the FTC's resource listing and announcement; the Q&A page itself shows no date): an endorser must disclose a connection to the brand that a significant minority of viewers would not expect. Connections that generally count include payment, free products or trips, employment, family or friendship, and affiliate commissions. Endorsers who buy with their own money and have no connection generally need not disclose. Use: treat every affiliate link and gifted product as needing disclosure.
facts.source_title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (FTC)

facts.statement: FTC Endorsement Guides Q&A (Guides revised 2023): disclosures must be clear and conspicuous, close to the endorsement and hard to miss. A disclosure only in comments, a hyperlinked button or a video description is generally not enough; in video it should be in the video itself, ideally seen and heard, early, and repeated in long streams. Terms like 'Gifted', '#sponsored' or '#ambassador' can be unclear, while 'Ad', 'Paid ad' or 'Gifted by [brand]' are clearer. Platform disclosure tools do not replace the endorser's and brand's duty. Use: require on-video 'Ad' labels in creator briefs.
facts.source_title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (FTC)

facts.statement: FTC Endorsement Guides Q&A: advertisers are responsible for what endorsers say for them, and handing the work to an agency does not remove that. The FTC advises training endorsers, explaining permitted claims, requiring disclosures, monitoring posts, and pre-approving content, with monitoring continuing for a reasonable time after a contract ends. Tagging a brand is an endorsement but not itself a disclosure; likes and shares may need disclosure inside a paid campaign. Use: add training, pre-approval and a post-contract monitoring window to every creator contract.
facts.source_title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (FTC)

facts.statement: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465, in effect 21 Oct 2024): it bans writing, selling or buying fake or false reviews and testimonials, including celebrity ones the business knew or should have known were false; offering incentives conditioned on a positive or negative sentiment; and insider reviews that hide the relationship to the business, where disclosure must be clear and conspicuous. Simply paying or rewarding for reviews is not banned; the sentiment condition is. Use: pay for reviews only without any sentiment requirement, and disclose staff and partner reviews.
facts.source_title: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers (FTC)

facts.statement: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465, in effect 21 Oct 2024): it also bars review suppression, meaning knowingly false accusations against reviewers, intimidation or unfounded legal threats to stop or remove reviews, and buying or distributing fake social media indicators such as bot followers when the business knew or should have known they were fake. Courts can impose civil penalties for knowing violations. Use: vet creators for bought followers and never threaten critics.
facts.source_title: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers (FTC)

facts.statement: YouTube Help, paid product placements, sponsorships and endorsements (page undated, 2026 copyright): creators must declare paid promotion in YouTube Studio by selecting the paid promotion option in video details (the upload flow asks whether the video includes branded content). Selecting it adds a disclosure label that appears at the beginning of the video, and optional age and country restrictions can then be set. Creators and partners remain responsible for complying with applicable law; YouTube points to bodies including the FTC, ASA, DGCCRF, Medienanstalten and the KFTC. Use: brief every YouTube creator to tick the paid promotion setting.
facts.source_title: Add paid product placements, sponsorships and endorsements (YouTube Help)

facts.statement: TikTok Ads help, content disclosure setting for creators (page shows 'Last updated: April 2026'): creators must turn on the commercial content disclosure setting when promoting a brand, product or service, which shows a 'Paid partnership' or 'Commercial content' label. If TikTok detects undisclosed branded content, the creator is notified and can respond within 24 hours before the video becomes ineligible for the For You feed; only the original poster can appeal. Use: put the disclosure toggle in every TikTok brief and check within 24 hours of posting.
facts.source_title: About the Commercial Content Disclosure setting for creators (TikTok)

facts.statement: TikTok Ads help, content disclosure setting (page last updated April 2026; TikTok-reported): TikTok says an internal comparison of nearly 2 million videos, tested in Indonesia and Pakistan, found no performance difference between properly disclosed and undisclosed branded content, and that using the Paid partnership or Commercial content label does not affect how TikTok recommends content. Method details and study date are not given and the claim is not independently verified. Use: do not let creators skip disclosure on reach grounds; test it in own data.
facts.source_title: About the Commercial Content Disclosure setting for creators (TikTok)

facts.statement: Amazon Associates Program Operating Agreement (dated 15 Oct 2025): Associates must display the statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases' (Section 5), and the agreement term starts when you register or first use the Associates Site. Further rules sit in the Program Policies incorporated by reference. Use: add the exact statement to every page or post carrying Associates links, and review the Program Policies for channel limits.
facts.source_title: Associates Program Operating Agreement (Amazon)

facts.statement: Google Search Central, qualifying outbound links (page undated): mark paid and advertising links with rel='sponsored', which Google prefers, though nofollow is still accepted for them; use rel='ugc' for user-generated content and nofollow when neither fits. Values can be combined. Google generally does not follow such links, but the linked page may still be crawled if found elsewhere. The page does not mention affiliate links by name. Use: tag paid creator and partner links on owned pages with sponsored.
facts.source_title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (Google Search Central)

facts.statement: European Commission and national consumer authorities influencer sweep (fieldwork 2023, published Feb 2024): of 576 influencers screened across Member States, 97% (558) posted commercial content but only 20% (112) clearly said so, 38% (216) did not use platform labels such as Instagram's paid partnership toggle, and 62% were flagged for further investigation under national procedures. Use: assume EU regulators are actively checking creator disclosure; require platform labels plus a plain 'ad' marker.
facts.source_title: Sweeps (European Commission)

facts.statement: CMA blog (14 Oct 2026) on UK direct consumer enforcement, 18 months after the new powers: 20 investigations opened in total, six since April 2026; investigations into fake or misleading reviews at Autotrader, Feefo, Dignity, Just Eat and Pasta Evangelists are ongoing. Since April 2026, seven cases settled with over GBP 11.8 million in fines and over GBP 2.3 million in redress. The post does not mention influencers. Use: treat review platforms and review incentives as live UK enforcement risk when running creator or affiliate review programmes.
facts.source_title: Direct consumer enforcement: 18 months on (CMA blog)

facts.statement: European Parliament research service briefing on the Digital Fairness Act (updated 5 Oct 2026): the Commission's fitness check found problems with how influencer commercial communications are disclosed and unclear responsibilities among influencers, brands, agencies and platforms; consumer group BEUC calls for clearer labelling, and a Parliament resolution of September 2026 called for an EU code of conduct for influencers. The proposal itself is still pending (Q4 2026). Use: expect stricter EU influencer labelling rules and shared brand liability.
facts.source_title: Towards a digital fairness act (EPRS briefing)

facts.statement: Amazon's Rufus article (no publication date; it says Rufus was renamed Alexa for Shopping on 13 May 2026) lists: answers personalised from your Amazon activity (editable memory); 30- and 90-day price history with target-price alerts; Auto-buy for Prime members with free 24-hour cancellation; and Buy for Me, where Amazon buys from another merchant's site for branded searches. Amazon says 250M+ customers used Rufus 'this year' (year unstated; its 11 Jun 2026 ads post says 300M in 2025) and users are 60%+ more likely to buy (vendor claims). Keep price and brand pages consistent.
facts.source_title: Amazon Rufus: Amazon's AI shopping assistant gets smarter and more personal

facts.statement: Amazon's Sponsored Products page (undated; footnotes cite Amazon internal data, US, June 2026): CPC pricing with no monthly or upfront fee; the daily budget is averaged over the calendar month, so a month can reach 31 times the daily amount ($100 a day gives up to $3,100); budgets are not paced through the day, so a small budget can be spent early; ads show only for in-stock items eligible for the Featured Offer; adult, used, refurbished and closed-category items are excluded.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: Sponsored Products

facts.statement: The same Amazon Sponsored Products page headlines that video campaigns saw +67% CTR and +9% conversion rate (Amazon internal data, US, June 2026), but another section of the page describes only a +9% CTR uplift. Treat the video figures as an unreconciled vendor claim and test video against a static baseline before relying on them.
facts.source_title: Amazon Ads: Sponsored Products

facts.statement: IAB and MRC released draft Retail Media Measurement Guidelines for public comment on 13 Sep 2023 (comment period to 13 Oct 2023), covering audience measurement, in-store digital place-based measurement, ad delivery, viewability, incrementality, reporting and transparency. The IAB release cites a BWG Strategy survey of 200 retail media network buyers each spending $5M+ a year: 52% were funding RMNs by reallocating from other digital media. The page does not mention a final version. Ask each network which guideline items it meets before comparing ROAS.
facts.source_title: IAB and MRC release Retail Media Measurement Guidelines for public comment

facts.statement: Netflix Upfront 2026 post (13 May 2026): programmatic audience targeting on Amazon's DSP in all ad-supported markets by 1 Jun, Yahoo DSP in later months; Pause Ads and Live can be bought through preferred DSPs using dynamic ad insertion (summer in the US and Canada, other countries by end of 2026). The ads plan expands to 15 new countries from 2027 (including Poland, Sweden, Indonesia, Thailand). Snowflake and AWS clean rooms are integrated; Infosum is due by end of 2026. Netflix is testing AI agents that manage and buy ads.
facts.source_title: Netflix Upfront 2026: Get Closer

facts.statement: Netflix Ads Suite update (4 Mar 2026): Amazon Audiences (built from Amazon shopping, streaming and browsing signals) become available for programmatic Netflix buys through Amazon DSP, US first in Q2. Yahoo DSP deterministic audiences can be activated on Netflix deals. Netflix launched its own Conversion API for outcome proof; in early testing with Tinuiti, campaigns 'outperformed benchmarks by more than 75%' (vendor claim, no method). Send conversion events through the API to measure Netflix.
facts.source_title: Netflix Ads Suite Expands Capabilities

facts.statement: IAB Tech Lab CTV Programmatic Guide (undated page, 2026 copyright), buying mechanics: it describes OpenRTB 2.6 podded bidding (pod signals include ad sequence, total pod length and maximum ads per pod); its brand-suitability example tags content with Content Taxonomy 3.1 and has the DSP use the 'bcat' attribute to block ads; and it says an impression is flagged not viewable when the video is obscured, outside the active window or the TV is off (Open Measurement). Ask a CTV DSP whether it supports these before launch.
facts.source_title: CTV Programmatic Guide - IAB Tech Lab

facts.statement: Google (15 Apr 2026, updated 11 Jun 2026): Dynamic Search Ads are being upgraded to AI Max for Search. Voluntary upgrade tools began in mid-April; campaigns with Automatically Created Assets or campaign-level broad match are auto-upgraded from September 2026; the DSA sunset and automatic upgrades now begin in February 2027 (extended from the original plan). Use the upgrade tools and one-click experiments before the automatic move.
facts.source_title: Google's Dynamic Search Ads are upgrading to AI Max

facts.statement: Google's DSA-to-AI Max post: an upgrade mirrors the legacy setup, but the features switched on differ by campaign type. DSA campaigns get search term matching, text customization and Final URL expansion; ACA campaigns get search term matching and text customization; campaign-level broad match campaigns get search term matching. Google cites an average 7% more conversions or conversion value at similar CPA/ROAS for the full suite versus term matching alone (Google internal data, 2026, non-retail advertisers; vendor claim).
facts.source_title: Google's Dynamic Search Ads are upgrading to AI Max

facts.statement: Google Ads Help on AI Max setup (undated; footer shows only 2026): new Search campaigns have AI Max on by default and text customization enabled; Final URL expansion requires text customization. These features need conversion-based Smart Bidding to work well. Controls: brand exclusions (campaign), brand inclusions (campaign or ad group), URL exclusions (campaign; need text customization and Final URL expansion) and text guidelines for restricted terms and tone. With Final URL expansion on, pinned RSA assets are not used if a more relevant URL is chosen. Review these toggles on every new Search campaign.
facts.source_title: Set up AI Max for Search campaigns - Google Ads Help

facts.statement: Meta's Marketing API docs on the Advantage+ campaign experience (sales, app, leads), undated, versions v25.0 and v26.0: new Advantage+ shopping (ASC) and app (AAC) campaigns cannot be created from v25.0 (an FAQ line says v24.0, so the page is inconsistent); with v26.0 legacy ones are blocked from edits and those using existing_customer_budget_percentage are paused. The page gives no calendar dates. Plan the move before v26.0. Migration restarts the learning stage.
facts.source_title: Advantage+ Campaign Experience for Sales, App, and Leads - Meta for Developers

facts.statement: Meta's Advantage+ docs: a campaign counts as Advantage+ (sales, app or leads) only when Advantage+ audience, campaign-level budget and Advantage+ placement are all enabled. Any ad-set placement targeting or exclusions turns it off; account-level placement exclusions do not. Supported objectives are OUTCOME_SALES, APP_INSTALLS and OUTCOME_LEADS. Check each ad set before expecting Advantage+ behaviour.
facts.source_title: Advantage+ Campaign Experience for Sales, App, and Leads - Meta for Developers

facts.statement: Nenycz-Thiel and Romaniuk (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, B2B report, Nov 2025): physical availability means being easy to find and buy, with three parts: presence (being where buying happens), prominence (easy to find in physical, digital and mobile sales environments) and portfolio (products that fit current and future buyer needs). A survey of over 500 B2B marketers in the USA and UK found an average of 3.7 sales channels in use. Use: audit channel gaps against the category channel mix.
facts.source_title: Easy to Find: Being Where B2B Buying Happens (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: Same Nenycz-Thiel and Romaniuk report (Nov 2025): its 'covering revenue' approach says presence should match each channel's value contribution to category transactions. Example: if 30% of category revenue comes through brand websites, the brand should aim to earn about 30% of its own revenue there. Presented as an approach with an example, not a fixed rule. Use: compare brand channel revenue mix with category channel mix.
facts.source_title: Easy to Find: Being Where B2B Buying Happens (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)

facts.statement: FTC press release (25 Sep 2025): Amazon settled FTC Act and ROSCA claims over Prime enrolment and cancellation with a $1 billion civil penalty, the largest ever for an FTC rule violation, plus $1.5 billion in refunds for an estimated 35 million consumers. The order requires a clear button to decline Prime, disclosure of cost, charge dates, frequency and auto-renewal, and cancellation through the sign-up method, not difficult, costly or time-consuming. Only the third ROSCA civil penalty. Use: mirror these in trial and subscription flows.
facts.source_title: FTC Secures Historic $2.5 Billion Settlement Against Amazon (FTC)

facts.statement: European Parliament research service briefing on the Digital Fairness Act (updated 5 Oct 2026): the Commission proposal is expected in Q4 2026, with current information pointing to mid-November (not an official date); its form is not yet known. Existing EU directives give no general right to cancel an online subscription as easily as it was concluded. Use: expect EU easy-cancel rules; design for one-step cancel; re-check within 30 days.
facts.source_title: Towards a digital fairness act (EPRS briefing)

facts.statement: Same EPRS briefing (updated 5 Oct 2026): the Digital Fairness Act fitness-check public consultation (undated on the page) found 69% of respondents reported difficulties cancelling an online contract and 62% had a subscription renewed without a reminder. The separate July-October 2025 call for evidence is described only as showing differing views on whether new rules are needed. Use: cite as consultation-reported difficulty, not as a measured market rate.
facts.source_title: Towards a digital fairness act (EPRS briefing)

facts.statement: Stripe Docs on trial compliance (card network requirements, page undated): with customer emails enabled and the Stripe-hosted page option selected, Stripe sends a trial-end reminder 7 days before the trial ends, or as soon as the trial begins if it is shorter than 7 days, and the reminder includes the cancellation URL. If a statement descriptor is longer than 10 characters, text after the 10th is overwritten with '* TRIAL OVER' (22-character limit). Use: enable reminder emails.
facts.source_title: Manage compliance requirements for trials and promotions (Stripe Docs)

facts.statement: Stripe Docs, trial offers page (API version 2026-09-30): the customer.subscription.trial_will_end event fires 3 days before a trial ends by default. When a trial ends with no payment method, trial_settings.end_behavior.missing_payment_method can create an invoice (default), cancel the subscription or pause it. Use: choose pause or cancel for card-free trials.
facts.source_title: Configure trial offers on subscriptions (Stripe Docs)

facts.statement: Amazon Associates Program Policies (updated 14 Apr 2026): a session ends at the first of several events, including 24 hours after the click on a Special Link. For add-to-cart orders the item must be added within 89 days of the click (1-Click follows a separate condition). The product must ship, stream or download, and be paid for, within 180 days of purchase. Use: do not promise creators a 90-day cookie.
facts.source_title: Associates Program Policies (Amazon)

facts.statement: Amazon Associates Program Policies (updated 14 Apr 2026): Special Links may appear in email, SMS and social direct messages only where the recipient opted in, and may not be used in offline promotion (print, ebooks, mailings, oral solicitation). Influencers with a material connection must disclose it, for example with text such as '#Ad'. Use: check list opt-in and channel before adding Associates links.
facts.source_title: Associates Program Policies (Amazon)

facts.statement: Google Search spam policies, thin affiliation (page undated in the checked text; date is an unverified placeholder): affiliate pages whose descriptions and reviews are copied from the merchant, or pages spread across an affiliate network without added value, count as thin affiliation. Good practice: extra price information, original reviews, rigorous testing and ratings, and comparisons. General policy text says violating sites may rank lower or get a manual action. Use: require original testing from affiliates.
facts.source_title: Spam policies for Google web search (Google Search Central)

facts.statement: UK Advertising Standards Authority snapshot on travel influencer disclosure (7 May 2026): from a curated sample of 531 Instagram and TikTok posts shown to UK users in Nov 2025, adequate disclosure was 20%, attempted but inadequate 11% and no attempt 69%; the shares may refer to the ads identified in the sample, so check the denominator before quoting. 'PR', 'gifted' and 'hosted' were judged inadequate. Use: require 'Ad' or 'Paid partnership' on UK posts.
facts.source_title: Snapshot Report: Travel influencer disclosure (ASA)
